strings.collections.character_events.ange_lv1_ha: An Qi reorganized the three scattered remarks into one sentence.
——Epilogue: The next day, the nurse’s station.
Sakaguchi saw Angel again. She was underlining the shift notes and combining three scattered notes into one sentence. The bunny sticker was not folded this time.
Seeing Sakaguchi, she took the initiative to say hello.
"Good morning. Bed Six was in stable condition last night."
An Qi reorganized the three scattered remarks into one sentence.
Angel was still confirming the shift handover details after get off work.
Sakaguchi has finished his ward rounds and is preparing to leave the ward.
Next to the nurse's station, An Qi was holding the shift record and explaining the situation to the taking over nurse.
"Six beds need to pay attention to their eating tonight. I only ate less than half of my lunch. I didn't feel sick in the afternoon, but I didn't drink much water."
The taking over nurse marked the record.
"Okay, I understand. I'll do the rest."
"Also, when he says he feels discomfort in his abdomen, he will first say, 'Maybe I'm too sensitive.' You can ask more."
An Qi handed the record out and took it back.
"By the way, the family members brought it——"
"Dr. Sakaguchi. Are there any new medical orders for bed six?"
"No. What time do you get off work?"
She glanced at the clock on the wall.
"She's done it once. This is the second time."
Angel's ears are a little red.
"I missed some details the first time."
Sakaguchi took the record and looked at it.
The handwriting is neat, and several easily overlooked places are marked in different colors. There was a small rabbit sticker stuck to the corner of the paper, which she folded in half.
She realized that Sakaguchi had seen it, and subconsciously stretched out her hand to press the corner of the paper.
SakaguchiReturn the record to the relief nurse.
"I understand the situation of the six beds. If there are changes at night, please contact us according to the on-duty arrangements."
"When he says it's okay...it doesn't necessarily mean it's okay."
The taking over nurse shook the record in her hand.
"I remember it. He first said, 'Maybe I'm too sensitive,' so I asked one more question."
An Qi looked at her, then at Sakaguchi, and finally nodded.
——Transition: at the entrance of the hospital.
An Qi changed into casual clothes and came out, carrying a small bag on her shoulder that was much lighter than when working. When she saw Sakaguchi, her steps slowed down.
She looked down at her phone and the screen lit up.
"The next one is in seven minutes."
The two of them walked along the way to the station.
An Qi walked for a while and suddenly asked:
"Am I too long-winded in my shift handover?"
"Some things can be sorted out in advance. The one about six beds is worth talking about."
An Qi put her mobile phone into her bag, moved the corners of her mouth, and quickly returned to her normal appearance.
When she reached the intersection, she glanced at the bus stop and suddenly quickened her pace.
She had walked out and stopped again.
She trotted into the convenience store and the bell on the door rang.
Angel was still confirming the shift handover details after get off work.
strings.collections.character_events.ange_lv2_ex: On the day of surgery, she kept her promise to accompany the patient in.
——Epilogue A: The next day, the entrance to the surgical area.
The patient is brought to the surgical area. An Qi went up to her and told her name first.
"Let's check the information first. Then I'll accompany you in."
The patient looked at her and nodded.
When Sakaguchi passed by, he heard the patient whisper:
——Epilogue B: Resting place after the operation.
An Qi sat down and finally opened the cookies that she had never eaten. Sakaguchi comes in and pours water.
"When the patient went in, she was not as nervous as yesterday."
After she finished speaking, she added:
Angel squeezed the cookie bag loudly.
"I'm afraid she'll ask me something that I don't even know."
"Then I got busy and couldn't care less about it."
She lowered her head and picked out an unbroken cookie and handed it to Sakaguchi.

strings.collections.character_events.intro_doc_r: Give Me All the Facts First
The examination room is temporarily empty. The reports on the desk are stacked in date order, and the screen still shows the imaging she just finished checking.
A young woman doctor stands at the workstation. Her white coat is neat, her posture composed, and her striking features are matched by a seriousness that leaves little room for anyone to bluff.
Sakaguchi knocks twice at the door. She finishes writing the line in front of her before looking up and glancing at his name badge.
Dr. Sakaguchi Ryuji?
Yes. I’m Sakaguchi Ryuji, newly appointed here. It’s a pleasure to meet you. Sorry to interrupt.
Kaori Miyama. I mainly work in surgery, and I’m currently also responsible for emergency cases. I look forward to working with you.
Miyama gives him a slight nod and briefly shakes his hand. It is courteous, but she makes no attempt to extend the greeting into small talk.
The director mentioned your record. Your overseas training is impressive.
I’m grateful for the director’s trust. But a résumé is a résumé; I still have to start from the beginning when it comes to the work itself.
That’s a sensible thing to say. Patients don’t become easier to handle just because your résumé looks good.
That’s true.
Especially at the operating table. Your clinical judgment can’t be answered for by your résumé.
I understand. I hope we’ll have a chance to work together, Dr. Miyama.
We certainly will. When that happens, I’ll care more about what you do than where you studied.
That’s the fairest way to judge someone.
Miyama studies him for a moment, the corner of her mouth lifting slightly as if his answer is acceptable. She closes the report folder and finally gives him her full attention.
May I ask, Dr. Miyama—are you related to Professor Soichiro Miyama?
Miyama is about to put down the folder when her fingers pause. Her smile fades.
He’s my father.
I see. I read some of his papers while I was overseas. He is a highly respected surgeon and professor.
Thank you. My father’s research in that field is certainly worth studying.
I imagine he influenced your decision to go into surgery.
Of course. But if you’re wondering whether I’m capable, my father’s name won’t help me prove it.
I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to let your family name stand in for my judgment of you.
Good. I won’t spare you my own judgment just because the director praised you, either.
As it should be.
After all, when we work together in the operating room, neither of us can rely on a reputation to take responsibility for the other.
She opens the folder again, her expression returning to its earlier, orderly calm.

I trained at a medical school here in Japan, mainly in surgery, and now I also cover emergency cases. You spent years training overseas, so the clinical workflows you encountered must have been different. Would you tell me a little about how you approach a case?
Of course. What would you like to discuss, Dr. Miyama?

Suppose the emergency department sends over a case of abdominal pain, and the report says only, ‘Stable; recommend observation by surgery.’ Would you accept that conclusion at face value, Dr. Sakaguchi?
No. I’d first confirm when the symptoms began, when the tests were done, and what changed afterward. Without that, the word ‘stable’ has no basis.
Mm. At least you wouldn’t hear ‘stable’ and immediately relax.
How would you handle it, Dr. Miyama?

Start by laying out all the facts. When the pain began, when the tests were done, and what happened afterward; which risks have been ruled out, and which haven’t. If the information is incomplete, clarify it first. When it’s time to decide, don’t keep putting it off.
You don’t like leaving the judgment to the next shift.
What I don’t like is when everyone says ‘let’s wait and see’ even though someone needs to make a judgment. If surgery really is necessary, I’ll explain why and take responsibility for my decision.
Understood. It sounds like working with you will be quite a challenge, Dr. Miyama.
That depends on whether you can keep up. Next time we get a chance, I’ll see what you can do in the operating room.
Then I’ll answer with my performance.
It sounds like you set a rather high bar for new colleagues.
Good. I’d rather trust what I’ve seen with my own eyes, too.
For everyone. Myself included.
Sakaguchi is about to reply when the examination-room door suddenly swings open.
Operating Room Nurse
Dr. Miyama! The woman scheduled for your next operation got very agitated once she was on the table. She was crying and making a scene, saying she doesn’t want surgery and wants to cancel!
Miyama listens without even raising an eyebrow, then turns to the last page of the report in her hand.
Has her condition changed?
Operating Room Nurse
No! We rechecked the surgical indications today, and the team is ready. She’s just suddenly frightened and refusing to go through with it.

Give her a sedative and let her sleep. She signed the consent form, and the whole team is ready. She can’t just cancel like that... Besides, with her condition, she’s unlikely to survive without the operation.
Operating Room Nurse
Understood. I’ll notify the operating room.
The nurse turns and hurries away. Miyama closes the report and puts it back where it was.
That’s enough for now. I have an operation to perform.
Understood. Go ahead; sorry for taking up your time today.
No need to apologize. I’ll remember our conversation today. We’ll see how you perform from here on.
See you in the operating room next time, Dr. Sakaguchi.
She gives Sakaguchi a slight nod. The hem of her white coat sways as she walks, and in a moment she has left the examination room, heading for the operating area.

...What a decisive doctor.
Sakaguchi watches the way she went, then looks down at the hospital information in his hands. Kaori Miyama is certainly a name he’ll remember.

"Please don't use such exaggerated titles in the hospital. If a patient hears it, I might have to sign 'National Goddess Doctor' on the medical record tomorrow."
She coughed slightly and tried to regain her usual dignified tone.
"I did participate in a game character design audition. I thought it was a fun souvenir at first, but then... it became a bit bigger. Advertisements, interviews, invitations from agencies, all came."
The name sounds familiar...have you been to the draft before?
Wait... aren't you the "national goddess" Shiori Fujisaki?

A red-haired female doctor wearing a light yellow headband raised her head and nodded politely to Sakaguchi.
"Dr. Sakaguchi, right? First time meeting you. I am Shiori Fujisaki from the Department of General Internal Medicine."
Sakaguchi's hand that was already reaching for the consultation sheet stopped in mid-air. This name, this face, and the almost unchanged hair tie - suddenly overlapped with the images that covered TV and magazines many years ago.
Make an appointment to consult each other later

"It's normal for a surgeon to look at the lesion first. The point of medical consultation is to pull the camera back a little."
Shiori did not show off the conclusion, but only rearranged the symptoms, medications and previous examinations according to time.
"Beautiful individual data are reassuring, but patients are not a data table. If you have any cases in the future where the preoperative risks are uncertain, please come to me directly."
A red-haired internist was re-checking the pre-operative consultation form in the corridor of the ward.

strings.collections.character_events.intro_hikam: At the nurses' station, Hiroko is briefing an unfamiliar nurse. The woman neatly puts several handover sheets into a folder, then looks up at Sakaguchi as she hears footsteps.
“Doctor, perfect timing. Let me introduce someone.”
“This is Saeko Hikami. She's just transferred here and will be working in internal medicine.”
“Saeko Hikami. I look forward to working with you.”
She bows slightly, her voice steady. Rather than nervous, she seems to have already prepared everything she needs to say on her first day.
“Yes. Ms. Sugimura is showing me the wards and the duty schedule.”
“The paperwork is all done. We can teach her the rest as she works.”
Sakaguchi nods, then glances at Saeko again.
“Hikami... I heard you had another reason for coming here?”
Her expression does not change. Sakaguchi looks at Hiroko, who lowers her eyes and turns a page of the duty roster.
“Anyway, get used to the work first. We can talk about your situation later.”
This time, her answer comes quickly.
“That's how I waited last time, too.”
“They said I had an ulterior motive, a mysterious background, and probably a story coming later.”
“Then the series got axed, the setup never paid off, and all I could do was go play mahjong.”
“So, could you put my story on the schedule first this time?”
Hiroko pulls out a sheet of paper and hands it to her.
“I've put you on tomorrow's early shift first.”
Saeko takes the roster and studies it for a while, then checks the name on it once more.
“...At least I'm working as a nurse this time.”
strings.collections.character_events.intro_ishig: The nurses' station is busier this morning than Sakaguchi expected. Ren Nanase is checking the handover records when he hands her a surgery request awaiting confirmation.
“Nanase, isn't there still an opening in the operating room tomorrow morning? I wanted to ask whether we could move this operation up.”
“Let me check... Yes, there is time available in the operating room.”
“Not yet. That schedule only covers the operating rooms, not the nursing staff.”
She places the request on the nursing liaison folder.
“I'll have to ask the nursing department about this first.”
Ren nods and takes the request toward the office area inside the nurses' station.

Sakaguchi remains beside the desk at the nurses' station. Ren Nanase has left the frame with the request. The scene stays in the same location. After a brief silence, a cool female voice comes from behind him.
“Would you like me to explain why?”

Sakaguchi turns around.

The woman before him is tall and slender, with black hair. Her clothes are neat and practical, and the badge on her chest identifies her nursing management role. She carries two different staffing schedules and the request from a moment ago. Her face shows no particular displeasure, nor any inclination to make small talk.
Ishigami places the two schedules separately on the desk and sets the surgery request to one side.
She points to the other sheet.
“This is the nursing staff allocation schedule.”
“You were looking at the first one.”
“...I haven't checked the second one, that's true.”
“Then don't say it can already be scheduled.”
Sakaguchi looks down more closely. The available operating room slots do not neatly line up with the nurses' handover times.
“So all that's free here is the room.”
She stacks the schedules neatly again, her tone as level as before.
“Nurses don't automatically materialize in operating rooms.”
For a moment, Sakaguchi has no reply.
Ishigami does not hurry him or take the opportunity to lecture him. She simply points out the nursing handover on the schedule.
“During this period tomorrow morning, the wards need to complete handover. The afternoon circulating staff already have assignments, too.”
“What if we made a last-minute adjustment?”
“We can discuss it. First establish whose assignment changes and who takes over their original duties.”
“I only wanted the patient to wait one day less.”
Sakaguchi raises his head a little. But she has not agreed to the request.
“But saving the patient a day's wait cannot mean giving a nurse an extra shift.”
“I didn't mean to make them work overtime.”
“Intentions don't turn themselves into staffing schedules.”
Ishigami closes the schedules and looks at Sakaguchi.
“I'm not here to stop you from operating.”
“Doctors decide when an operation should be done. The nursing department confirms whether there are people who can safely take on the work.”
“Understood. How should I submit the request, then?”
Ishigami seems a little more satisfied with this question than with his earlier explanation.
“Send the nursing department the estimated duration, the scrub and circulating nurses required, and the postoperative handover requirements in advance.”
“If we can adjust the schedule, I'll agree. If we can't, I'll tell you why.”
“And if there really isn't a way to fit it in?”
“We find the next suitable time together.”
“This is a hospital. Doctors, nurses, and patients all need to be able to count on arrangements that work for them.”
Sakaguchi picks up the request again and turns to the nursing coordination section he had left blank.
“Then I'll fill this in properly first. I won't promise the patient a specific time before the nursing department confirms it.”
“From now on, I'll notify the nursing department first when adding an operation at short notice.”
“No need to wait until next time. Finish this one first.”
Sakaguchi cannot help smiling a little. Ishigami's expression does not change.
“Head Nurse Ishigami, I suspect I'll be troubling you quite often from now on.”
“If you fill in the information clearly, it isn't trouble.”
She picks up the nursing allocation schedule, preparing to leave.
“When the wards are busy, please don't discuss who is unwilling to work overtime in front of patients.”
“The nursing department will handle the coordination. All the patient needs to know is whether the hospital has made proper arrangements for her.”

Ishigami nods slightly and leaves the nurses' station with the schedules. She does not smile or add any polite pleasantries.

Sakaguchi looks at the unfinished request in his hand, picks up a pen, and fills in the estimated duration, staffing needs, and handover arrangements in the nursing coordination section.
strings.collections.character_events.intro_itsum: Young Nurse at the Nurses’ Station
A Proper Introduction at the Nurses’ Station
Sakaguchi enters the nurses’ station. Hiroko stands beside the work counter, checking ward handover records with a young nurse.
The nurse wears a neat white uniform, with no surgical cap or mask. Her red hair is uncovered, and she has a bright, open smile.
“Is that junior nurse you mentioned here?”
Hearing Hiroko, the young nurse sets down her pen and turns around.
“This is Sonoda Itsumi, a surgical nurse. She was my junior back in nursing school.”
“Hello! I’m Sonoda Itsumi. I finally get to say hello properly!”
Itsumi bows slightly with a smile. For a moment, Sakaguchi cannot connect this cheerful face with anyone he has seen in the corridors.
“Sakaguchi Ryuji. It’s nice to meet you.”
“Huh? Dr. Sakaguchi, you really don’t remember me?”
“We have! In the surgical corridor, I took a corner too quickly and almost ran into you.”
She raises both hands and mimics skidding to a hurried stop.
“And that other time, later on! I was pushing an instrument cart and dropped a tray. You held the cart steady and moved the empty tray for me.”
“Hehe, both times. Sorry—it seems the only things I’ve given you to remember are embarrassing moments.”
Sakaguchi looks at her uncovered red hair and remembers the eyes that looked at him from above a surgical mask on those two occasions.
“No wonder I didn’t recognize you. Both times, your cap and mask covered you completely.”
“Of course! I can’t exactly run around the surgical area with all this hair out!”
“She told me about the instrument tray. She made sure the recount and handover were done properly afterward.”
“Hiroko-senpai… Did you have to tell Dr. Sakaguchi that part, too?”
“Weren’t you the one who brought it up?”
Itsumi blinks, then breaks into laughter.
“But I really was happy that you stopped to help that day. I never got to thank you properly.”
“It was no trouble. You handled the follow-up with those instruments well yourself.”
“Thank you! That means a lot coming from you.”
“Now can you two finally get properly acquainted?”
“Yes! Dr. Sakaguchi, I hope we get to work together in surgery sometime! And if you need help on the ward, please feel free to call me.”
“Of course. I look forward to working with you, Nurse Sonoda.”
“Me too! At least today we finally got to talk without rushing past each other in a corridor.”
The printer hums and delivers another handover sheet. Itsumi turns to sort the paperwork, then gives Sakaguchi one more cheerful smile and nod.
A Proper Introduction at the Nurses’ Station

strings.collections.character_events.intro_kariy: The nurses' station is already busy this morning. Chizuru Ishigami is checking a stack of internship registration papers. An unfamiliar young woman stands in front of the desk.
The girl wears a neat nurse's uniform, but does not yet have a permanent staff name badge. Holding a notebook filled with sticky notes, she stands very straight, smiling but a little nervous.
Ishigami takes a neatly folded sheet of paper from the documents.
“Oh, that's some information I put together myself.”
“Staff nurses' pay, benefits, and comparisons with other hospitals...?”
“Yes! I spent ages researching it. Since I'm going to be an intern, I thought I should find out whether I might be able to stay afterward.”
“I have no objection to your researching pay and benefits. But this doesn't belong among the ward handover documents.”
“I-I'm sorry! I put it in the wrong place when I was sorting everything!”
She quickly takes the sheet back and slips it into her notebook. The handwriting and tables on it are clearly very neat.
Just then, Ryuji Sakaguchi enters the nurses' station.
“Dr. Sakaguchi, perfect timing. Let me introduce an intern who is starting today.”
The girl immediately turns toward Sakaguchi and bows carefully.
“It's nice to meet you! I'm Megumi Kariya, and I'm starting my internship here today. I look forward to working with you!”
“Hello, Kariya. You're certainly full of energy for your first day.”
“Of course! I've really been looking forward to this internship.”

“The internship begins on June first and lasts six months. The final assessment will be on December first. The nursing department will arrange your duties. Start by learning the daily routines in each department.”
“Yes! I've already read all the instructions you sent me.”
Hiroko Sugimura, who is sorting patient records nearby, looks up at her with a smile.
“I hear you're keen to work at our hospital after you graduate?”
“Yes. I've compared the offers, and the pay and benefits here are the best.”
She pauses, then hastily adds something.
“...I mean, there's so much I can learn here!”
“There's nothing wrong with what you said the first time.”
“It's perfectly normal to want to earn money through your own work.”
“That's a relief. I was worried that saying that on my first day would give everyone a bad impression of me.”
“My family needs the money, and I want to become independent sooner, too. If I'm going to study hard and work hard during my internship, of course I want a well-paying job afterward.”
“Sounds like you've really done your homework.”
“Then let's see how much homework you've done on nursing.”
The phone at the nurses' station rings. Hiroko is busy checking the handover documents. Megumi instinctively reaches for it, then stops and looks at Ishigami.
“Listen carefully to what the caller needs first. If you're unsure about something, leave the answer to the person responsible.”
Megumi picks up the phone. Her slightly embarrassed expression immediately turns serious.
“Hello, you've reached the nurses' station. This is Kariya speaking.”
“...All right. Take your time. I'll write it down.”
She opens her notebook and takes notes on a blank page, nodding gently as she listens.
“You'd like to confirm the time of your preoperative tests, is that right?”
“I'm not able to answer that myself yet. May I check with the nurse in charge and have her get back to you?”
The person on the other end says a little more.
“Yes, I understand you're worried. I'll make sure your question is passed on clearly. Please hold.”
She puts down the phone and hands her notes to Hiroko.
“Ms. Sugimura, this patient wants to confirm her preoperative test schedule. I've written down her name, ward, and question, but I don't know the exact time, so I couldn't just give her an answer.”
Hiroko takes the paper and glances over it.
“Thank you. These are very clear notes. I'll contact the nurse responsible.”
“Great! I'll take notes like this next time, too.”
“It's good that you took the initiative to check what you didn't know on the phone. But you don't need to rush to do everyone's work on your very first day.”
“Oh... am I getting ahead of myself?”
She quickly adds a line to her notebook.
Hiroko sets a rotation schedule in front of her.
“During your internship, you'll experience the work of different departments. You'll gradually learn the nursing routines on the wards, in outpatients, and in the operating room.”
At the words “operating room,” her pen suddenly stops.
“...I have to go to the operating room, too.”
“What's wrong? Don't you like operating rooms?”
“It's not that I don't like them. It's just... I've never actually stood beside someone having an operation.”
“I can look at all the pictures at school. But when I see it for real... I don't know how I'll react.”
She tries to keep smiling, but her fingers unconsciously tighten around the edge of her notebook.
“If I don't do well then, will it affect my internship assessment?”
“Your assessment is based on how you learn and work over these six months. It won't be decided by your first attempt alone.”
“If you really feel unwell, tell a senior nurse right away. Pushing yourself until you can't even look after yourself won't help the patient.”
She looks down, writes another line, then raises her head again.
“Then I'll keep studying ahead! I spent ages memorizing the operating room preparation procedure yesterday. I can't let that go to waste.”
“Being prepared is good. But once you're actually there, you also need to judge how you're coping.”
Just then, Ange Tonegawa enters the nurses' station carrying a neatly sorted stack of patient records.
“Ms. Ishigami, the ward records are all sorted. Is there anything else I can help with?”
“Good timing. Ange, show Kariya, who is starting today, the routes around the wards and the nurses' station.”
Ange turns to Megumi with a friendly smile.
“Hello, I'm Ange Tonegawa. If there's anything you're unsure about, you can ask me.”
“Hi! I'm Megumi Kariya. You look about my age.”
She suddenly notices Ange's permanent nurse's name badge.
“Yes, but I still have plenty to learn.”
She looks at Ange's badge for a moment, then smiles.
“Then I'll have to work hard to catch up with you. In six months, I want to wear a badge like that, too.”
“Then let's both do our best. Come with me and learn your way around the wards first.”
Megumi gathers her notebook and follows Ange toward the nurses' station exit. After a couple of steps, she turns back and bows earnestly to Sakaguchi, Hiroko, and Ishigami.
“I'm really looking forward to working with all of you, starting today!”
“There's no need to rush. Learn one thing at a time.”
“I know. But... I've already done the math.”
“If I can stay here, life will be a lot easier financially for both me and my family. I'm going to work hard for these six months to make that happen.”
She speaks with complete sincerity, then returns to her cheerful smile.
“Well then, I'd better get to work!”
Ange waits for her by the door. The two leave the nurses' station side by side.
Once outside, Megumi quietly glances through the rotation schedule.
“Ange... do you see blood very often in the operating room?”
“Yes. Of course you'll see blood in an operating room.”
She falls silent for a moment, then closes her notebook.
“It's all right. I'll focus on learning what I can today!”
She quickens her steps to catch up with Ange. Back in the nurses' station, the phone rings again amid the day's work.

strings.collections.character_events.intro_pharm: Behind the pharmacy window, a young woman is checking the medication register. She looks up and notices an unfamiliar male doctor at the entrance.
She is striking, with a bright, natural smile.
Oh, a new face! You must be a doctor who just joined the hospital, right?
That's right. I'm Ryuji Sakaguchi, from surgery. I came by today to get acquainted with the pharmacy department.
Welcome, welcome! I'm Manami Iimura, the pharmacist. I look forward to working with you!
Likewise. It's nice to meet you.
She speaks brightly, and her smile is lovely. Sakaguchi only meant to stop by and say hello, but her warmth makes him want to keep talking.
Ms. Iimura, is the pharmacy department usually busy? Is the workload hard?
Hehe, are you asking because you care about me, or are you checking whether our pharmacy slows down your surgery department?
The first one, of course. I'm new here, so I want to learn more about my colleagues' work.
I see. Dr. Sakaguchi is quite thoughtful, then.

Actually, we're a little different from an ordinary hospital's outpatient pharmacy. We don't dispense all that many prescriptions directly to outpatients. Most of our work is for inpatients, major treatments, and surgeries.
Sounds like I'll be asking you for help pretty often, then.
You bet. Preoperative medication, anesthesia-related drugs, things needed during surgery, and pain relief afterward... Once surgery gets busy, we don't get a moment's rest over here.
She smiles and points to the register in front of the service window.
But let me make one thing clear. You're in charge of operating, and I'm in charge of stopping you when you operate way out of line.
...Operating on a patient, or writing a prescription?
By the way, your surgery department's anesthesia arrangements are pretty interesting.
General anesthesia, local anesthesia, sometimes no anesthesia at all... In the end, it feels like the surgeon-in-charge decides everything with a single word.
Hehe, not really. It's just that when you surgeons make a decision, our pharmacy often ends up rushing around to keep up.
She pauses, then gives him a slightly sly smile.
But I am curious. For the same surgery, how different is the experience for a patient who's awake versus asleep?
Actually, I've been researching pain relief lately, too.
It's too early for that; I'm only exploring a few research directions. Especially when a patient stays awake, I wonder if there's a way to make the whole process less unpleasant.
Maybe one day I really will be able to help with one of your surgeries, Dr. Sakaguchi!
Then maybe sometime, if there's an opportunity, I could invite you to come see the operating room.
She freezes for a moment, then sticks out her tongue with a sheepish grin.
Oh, I'd rather have the nurses come here to pick up their medications. The operating room... I'm not quite brave enough to go in there yet.
So there are things Ms. Iimura isn't good at, after all.
Of course! I became a pharmacist specifically so I wouldn't have to stand beside an operating table all day!
She laughs and waves her hand.
So, I'll leave the surgery to you, Dr. Sakaguchi, and the medication to me!

“Yes, Ms. Sugimura! I’ve already checked this morning’s handover notes.”
“Shiori takes her work very seriously. Dr. Sakaguchi, you can count on her whenever you need a hand.”
“Big Sis Rumi, I can tell the doctor myself…”
Watching the two of them trade remarks, Sakaguchi couldn’t help smiling too.
“It looks like work is going to be lively from now on.”
“There’s certainly no shortage of that. I just hope they remember to do more than chat.”
“We take our work seriously too! Right, Shiori?”
“Well then, Dr. Sakaguchi, just ask whenever you need our help.”
“I’ll do my best too. I look forward to working with you!”
Rumi waved with a smile, while Shiori bowed politely to Sakaguchi. Then the two returned to organizing the paperwork at the nurses’ station.
Two Colleagues at the Nurses’ Station
strings.collections.character_events.intro_satsu: As Sakaguchi passes the nurses' station, he sees Hiroko Sugimura checking handover documents with a young nurse wearing black-framed glasses. The girl's voice is quiet, but she explains every item clearly.
“The patient in bed seven has completed all her preoperative tests. She says she doesn't want to cancel the operation. She just wants someone to tell her when they'll come to collect her.”
“Right. Then confirm the expected transfer time, too. Don't just write ‘explained.’”
“Yes, I've already asked the operating room. Once she heard the time, she finally put down that information leaflet.”
“Good. You remembered what the patient was actually worried about. That's more important than filling every box on the form.”
“Thank you. I still have a long way to go, though...”
“I've always looked up to you, Hiroko.”
“I want to be a nurse like you, someone who helps patients feel at ease.”
“Then start with today's handover. You're already doing well.”
Sakaguchi approaches the counter. Hiroko looks up, and Satsuki turns with her. The instant she sees who it is, the hand reaching for her glasses freezes in midair.
“Good morning, Hiroko. Do I confirm this transfer arrangement with you?”
“Yes, Doctor. Perfect timing—let me introduce you. This is Satsuki Orikawa. She's recently started working alongside me to learn the routines.”
“Satsuki, this is Dr. Ryuji Sakaguchi from surgery.”
“Hello, Orikawa. I heard your handover just now. Your notes were very clearly organized.”
“Th-thank you! N-no, I mean, I'm still... um...”
Satsuki's voice grows quieter and quieter. Instinctively, she moves half a step behind Hiroko, her fingers still gripping the handover folder tightly.
“Satsuki, put the file down for a moment. The doctor is only saying hello.”
“It's all right. If you have any questions about transfers or handovers, just ask me directly.”
“Of course. You don't have to pass everything through Hiroko.”
Only after making sure Sakaguchi is no longer looking her way does Satsuki slowly loosen her grip on the folder and bow her head to apologize to Hiroko.
“Hiroko... was I terribly rude just now?”
“You greeted the doctor, and you didn't hold up the handover. Your nerves were just a little too obvious.”
“Ugh... I know. I had it all ready in my head, but when I saw a male doctor coming toward me, I forgot everything.”
“You didn't forget what to say when you were talking about the patient.”
“Th-that's work. The patient is waiting. Of course I have to explain things clearly...”
As she says this, she looks down and leafs through the duty roster in her hands. Her fingertip pauses between the surgery and gynecology columns.
“I really did want to be a surgical nurse like you, Hiroko...”
“But I applied to gynecology after all.”
Hiroko looks at her, then at the ward information in her hand, as though she has finally realized they have been talking about different things from the start.

Satsuki abruptly raises her head, and her black-framed glasses slide a little down her nose. Holding the frames, she stares at Hiroko, clearly reconsidering what her department application actually meant.
strings.collections.character_events.intro_visit: Futaba Sakura finds patterns in the timing of psychological stimulation and physiological responses.
Ask her about her identity

"The stimulation hasn't started yet, where is the pain coming from?"
She pushed her glasses up a little.
"It's an expectation. She knows it's safe here, but her body doesn't believe it yet. The brain is also an organ, so don't keep pretending that it doesn't participate in medical treatment."
Take note of her research contact details

Futaba's eyes lit up for a moment, and her speaking speed suddenly increased.
"Yes. Fear, Pain, Dignity, Cooperation - not four unrelated slots. As long as you find the trigger point, your body will tell you how they are connected."
She paused and regained her composure.
"If there are any strange cases in the future, please remember to call me. The more incomprehensible the explanation, the better."
"This would explain many of the perioperative reactions."

"Futaba Sakura. I have PhDs in medicine and psychology. I am now studying how the mind changes the body, and how the body in turn changes the mind."
She glanced at Maya's device report.
"Maya confirms that the change is real. I am responsible for asking why it happened now. We are from the same batch."
Listen to her replay the record

The monitoring device again recorded a significant increase in heart rate after the last calibration. Maya Ibuki confirmed that there are no problems with the sensor and raw waveform.
The orange-haired woman standing on the other side of the screen did not look at the curve immediately, but fell back into the room to record.
"Is it pain?"

"Here."
She paused a second after the staff member said "Next phase begins."
"Heart rate, respiratory rate, finger muscle tension, all changed together in this order. The signal is real and not random."
There was no glitch in the guard signal, but Futaba noticed that the change happened exactly after a sentence.
The Body Still Doesn't Believe It
Maya Ibuki indicates that the abnormality comes from the monitoring link, not the patient.
Let's see how she judges first

The monitoring test bench in the imaging and inspection area suddenly and continuously alarmed. The blood oxygen curve on the screen dropped sharply, but the volunteer sitting next to him who was undergoing routine sampling still looked calm and breathed evenly.
A woman wearing thin-rimmed glasses raised her hand to stop the staff member who was about to change the oxygen mask.
Accept calibration report

Maya was startled for a moment, her eyes softened first, and then she nodded seriously.
"...Yes. You see the patient, and I see how the machine sees the patient. Both sides confirm so that neither side will be deceived."
She handed the calibration report to Sakaguchi.
"Please take good care of me in the future, Dr. Sakaguchi."
"Are you sure it's a problem with the machine?"

"Don't move the patient yet. The radial artery pulse, the probe on the other side, and the respiratory wave are all consistent. Only this channel is floating."
She brought up the original waveform and stacked the two timelines together.
"It's not that the person's condition suddenly deteriorated, it's that the sensor baseline and the system clock both deviated."
"Clinical judgment also requires knowing when a machine is lying."

"Maya Ibuki. Visiting research doctor, responsible for physiological monitoring, medical equipment and data quality."
She adjusted her glasses, as if she was worried that this list of job titles sounded too exaggerated.
"I don't do regular outpatient clinics, and I'm not a surgeon. When the operating room needs equipment support, I will go there."
introduce yourself to her

"You can't trust the machine just because of a beautiful curve, and you can't ignore the alarm just because the patient seems fine."
She replaced the calibration probe, and the abnormal values immediately returned to the normal range.
"Let independent sources corroborate each other. Only then can we be sure."
The monitoring test station repeatedly alarmed, but the visiting research doctor standing in front of the equipment asked everyone not to touch the patient.
The Wrong Waveform
strings.collections.character_events.itsumi_lv0_: After the Fifth Operation: Around the Corner
After the operation, Sakaguchi leaves the operating room and heads along the surgical corridor toward the changing area.
At the other end of the corridor, a young nurse approaches quickly with handover papers in her arms. A surgical cap covers all her hair and ears, and a tied surgical mask hides most of her face.
They both step around a parked cart at the corner and lightly bump shoulders. The nurse stops at once and steadies the papers in her arms.
“Oh! I’m so sorry! Are you all right?”
“I’m fine, too. I took that corner too fast. I’m really sorry!”
She bows her head in apology, then glances at the surgery schedule clipped to the top of her papers.
“Yes! They’re waiting for me over there. Sorry again—I’d better go!”
The young nurse gives him a quick wave and hurries toward another operating room.
Sakaguchi glances after her, then continues toward the changing area.
After the Fifth Operation: Around the Corner
After the Fifth Operation: Around the Corner
After the Tenth Operation: The Instrument Tray
Another operation has finished. As Sakaguchi enters the surgical corridor, a young nurse in a surgical cap and tied mask is wheeling a cart of used surgical instruments ahead of him.
As the cart rounds a corner, an instrument tray that was not sitting securely on the upper shelf suddenly slides toward the edge.
With a clatter, the tray hits the floor and several instruments scatter across the corridor.
The nurse stops the cart at once, steadies it, and checks that nobody nearby was struck.
“No, I’m not hurt. I didn’t make sure the tray was secure before turning…”
“Oh no… Now I’ll have to check everything again.”
“Really? Thank you so much! I was just wondering how long it would take to sort all this out alone.”
“But these instruments have just been used, so please don’t touch the ones on the floor. Could you hold the cart steady for me?”
“Sure. Should I move this empty tray out of the way?”
“Please set it beside the cart. I need to record the instruments that fell and send them through the proper collection process.”
Sakaguchi steadies the cart and sets the spare empty tray aside. The nurse puts on protective gloves, collects the used instruments according to procedure, and checks each item against the list.
She checks the last instrument and marks it off on her list.
“You kept the count thorough even after that scare. Nice work.”
“When you make a mistake, you’ve got to handle everything afterward properly.”
She looks up, and the bright smile returns to her eyes.
“Thank you! You really saved me a lot of trouble.”
“Take the next corner a little more slowly.”
“Yes! I’ll remember! Oh—the collection team is still waiting. I’d better get going!”
She gets the instrument cart rolling steadily again, gives Sakaguchi a grateful nod, and heads down the corridor.
After the Tenth Operation: The Instrument Tray
After the Tenth Operation: The Instrument Tray
After the Fifteenth Operation: Hiroko’s Invitation
After an operation, Sakaguchi leaves the surgical area and meets Sugimura Hiroko in the corridor, carrying handover documents.
“Dr. Sakaguchi, you’ve certainly been doing a lot of surgery lately.”
“I have. I’ve barely had time to take a break.”
“Hehe. Actually, there’s something I wanted to ask you.”
“A junior of mine from nursing school has been asking me about you lately.”
“She’s heard how active you’ve been in the operating rooms, and she’s wanted a chance to meet you properly.”
“She works in surgery. She says she’s run into you in the surgical area a few times, and that you helped her out.”
“Helped her out… That does ring a bell.”
“She’s been wanting to thank you herself, but every time she sees you, she’s rushing off to the next task.”
“When you have a moment, would you stop by the nurses’ station to meet her?”
“Of course. I’d like to meet your junior, too.”
“Thank you. I’m sure she’ll be delighted.”
Hiroko smiles, gathers up her documents, and continues with the handover. Sakaguchi keeps her invitation in mind.
After the Fifteenth Operation: Hiroko’s Invitation
After the Fifteenth Operation: Hiroko’s Invitation
strings.collections.character_events.manami_lv1_: “U-um… Nurses, you really don't have to wheel me in. I can walk on my own.”
“It's all right, we're almost there. Listen to the doctor once you're inside, okay?”
“Yes, I will. It's just… thinking about the operation makes me a little scared.”
“Don't worry. Someone will explain the preparations to you, one step at a time.”
“Good afternoon. Another patient heading into surgery?”
“Oh, Dr. Sakaguchi. It's a routine minor operation for Dr. Narumi today.”
“It doesn't look like anything particularly serious?”
“No, the operation itself is straightforward. Nothing needing special attention came up in the preoperative checks, either.”
“Excuse me… are you a doctor too?”
“Yes, although I'm not the surgeon today.”
“Oh, I see. Well… please look after me too.”
“She seems familiar… Have I seen her somewhere before?”
“Um… do I really have to tuck all my hair inside the surgical cap?”
“Of course. Here, let me fix it for you.”
“What's wrong? Stay still, we're just about to—”
“Dr. Sakaguchi! Don't go over there! Stay away!”
“The patient suddenly turned into someone else! She even overturned the instrument trolley!”
“Hey! Who just said they were going to strap me to that table?!”
“All of you, hold it! I'm not finished talking!”
“Don't go near her! Stay clear of the blade!”
“Another white coat! You're with them too, aren't you?!”
“Calm down! We're not trying to hurt you!”
“What do we do, what do we do…!”
“Don't provoke her. Get everyone over to the other side first.”
“If I'm right… there might be a way.”
“Ren! Miyuki! When she comes after me, run the other way!”
“Huh? Dr. Sakaguchi, what are you going to do?!”
“No time to explain! Dr. Narumi, please get everyone away from here!”
“Clear the corridor! Keep everyone else back—don't let her reach the patients!”
“Wh-what?! Why is a naked woman charging into the pharmacy with a scalpel?! Dr. Sakaguchi!!!”
“Iimura! Do you have anything that makes people sneeze?!”
“Is this really the time to talk about sneezing?! She has a knife!!”
“I know! That's why I'm telling you to hurry!”
“What the hell are you two talking about?!”
“Found it! Nasal reflex powder for research use!”
“But I have no idea whether it'll work on her!”
“What the hell! What are you trying to—”
“I was just in the operating room… How did this happen?!”
“…What I want to know is, what on earth just happened?!!”
“Dr. Narumi! Ren! Miyuki! It's all right now! Could you come here, please?”
“Oh dear! Don't just stand there! Put this around you!”
“Ooh… thank you. I'm sorry. Have I caused trouble for everyone…?”
“Let's leave the questions for now. Let her sit down and rest. I'll get a trolley ready.”
“It's a long story. Anyway, she's all right now.”
“All right. Let's not discuss it here.”
“Um… did I do something rude just now?”
“Someone will explain later. Just rest for now, okay?”
“As for the pharmacy… we'll arrange to have this cleaned up.”
“Miss Iimura. About what happened… thank you. If you hadn't found that powder, I don't know how I could have brought things under control.”
“Oh, there's no need to thank me.”
“How exactly did you come up with making her sneeze?”
“I don't believe for a second that you're some expert on nasal reflexes.”
“There was a girl in it who was usually very gentle. But whenever she sneezed, her hair changed color and she suddenly became very hot-tempered.”
“When I saw her hair turn from blue to blond, it suddenly came back to me.”
“When that woman was chasing us with a scalpel…”
“You gambled our lives on a plot from a manga?!”
“…There wasn't anything else I could do at the time.”
“What do you mean, nothing else you could do?!!”
“In all my time at this pharmacy, that's the first time anyone's rushed in demanding something to make someone sneeze!”
“I can hardly believe it actually worked myself.”
“…But when you called out to me back there, I honestly thought I was going to die of fright.”
“I'm sorry I dragged you into something so dangerous.”
“You really believed I could find something, didn't you?”
“Yes. You know what's in this pharmacy far better than I do.”
“I am Hoshimi Hospital's pharmacist, after all.”
“When you rushed in just now… didn't you call me 'Manami'?”
“I'm sorry. I was in such a hurry.”
“After all, we're comrades who survived a blond woman with a scalpel together!”
“But next time, please don't bring that sort of patient charging into my pharmacy!”
“Didn't you say you were a little afraid to go into the operating room?”
“Exactly. That's why I stay in the pharmacy.”
“Who knew trouble from the operating room would come running all the way here?!”
“If this happens again, remember to warn me in advance!”
“Can you even warn someone about this sort of thing in advance?”

Sakaguchi approaches from the other end of the corridor. Ren Nanase is wheeling a stretcher toward the operating room, with Miyuki Asakura beside it. A young blue-haired woman lies on it, already changed and prepared for surgery. A light-blue medical blanket covers her, leaving her shoulders and arms visible. Her light-blue surgical cap is slightly loose, and a few strands of long blue hair peek out around its edge. She is docile, but nervously clutches the blanket.
Lying on the stretcher, she gives Sakaguchi a small, earnest nod. He nods back.
When the stretcher stops outside the operating room, Launch turns to Ren beside her.
Ren bends down and carefully tucks the long blue strands into the surgical cap. Launch lies still and obedient, not daring to move a finger.
Miyuki Asakura wheels the stretcher into the operating room, followed by Ren Nanase. The doors slowly close. Sakaguchi continues down the corridor.
Before Sakaguchi has gone far, the faint clinking of instruments comes from inside the operating room.
CLATTER!! Metal instruments tumble to the floor one after another.
The operating room doors fly open. Ren Nanase, wearing a surgical cap and mask, rushes out first and nearly collides with Sakaguchi.
Miyuki Asakura runs out next, still clutching the clipboard she had no time to put down.
Narumi backs out through the doors, still trying to keep the other staff at a safe distance.
BANG! The operating room doors are flung open again.

A blond woman appears in the doorway. She has already changed and undergone her preoperative preparation, but her drape has slipped off in the confusion, leaving her naked and barefoot in the corridor. Her white disposable surgical cap is still on, though slightly askew; thick blond hair spills out from its edge and swings with her movements. She brandishes a scalpel taken from the instrument table, her face blazing with anger.
Everyone scrambles back against the corridor wall. Sakaguchi instinctively steps in front of the nurses, shielding them as they move aside.
Launch lunges a step forward. Sakaguchi and the nurses flatten themselves against the wall to dodge her.
Sakaguchi looks at her brilliant blond hair, then suddenly recalls the gentle blue-haired face he saw earlier.
Sakaguchi freezes for a moment, as if an utterly absurd possibility has just occurred to him.
Launch advances with the knife. The nurses retreat to one side of the corridor, but trolleys and corners hem them in, leaving less and less room to move.
Sakaguchi looks up and spots the pharmacy sign around the corner.
He glances at the blond woman, then at his colleagues trapped against the wall.
While Launch is shouting, Sakaguchi suddenly breaks away from the corner and runs toward the pharmacy.
She takes the bait and chases him. The two race around the corner, one after the other, while the nurses seize their chance to escape.
Manami Iimura is checking the medication register behind the dispensing window. She looks up at the sound of hurried footsteps.
Before she can ask anything, a naked blond woman bursts into the pharmacy behind Sakaguchi—with a scalpel in her hand.

There is no time to answer. As Launch swings her arm, Sakaguchi catches the wrist holding the blade and braces her upper arm with his other hand, pushing the scalpel away from Iimura. Launch struggles fiercely, and they stumble into the pharmacy counter.
Launch wrenches her arm a fraction free, and the blade scrapes the edge of the counter. Sakaguchi grits his teeth and pins her arm again.
Iimura goes pale with fright. She looks at the scalpel, then whips her head toward the medicine cabinet. Something changes in her eyes.
She hurries to the glass medicine cabinet against the wall and pulls it open. Her eyes scan a row of research supplies, and she quickly snatches up a small bottle.
Launch struggles again. Sakaguchi forces her knife hand out to the side, barely managing to keep some distance.
Iimura grips the small bottle and hurls it at a clear patch of floor near their feet.
A small amount of white powder bursts out of the bottle and drifts through the air around them.
She wrinkles her nose, its tip twitching slightly.
The sneeze drowns out every other sound.

Before Sakaguchi and Iimura's eyes, the woman's brilliant blond hair instantly changes back to soft blue. Her fierce expression disappears too. Her whole body relaxes, her surgical cap still in place. The scalpel slips from her hand and falls to the floor.
She looks from the sweat-soaked Sakaguchi to the pale-faced Iimura.
She looks down at her naked body, then at the surgical instruments scattered near her feet.
She hurriedly covers herself with her arms, her face turning bright red.
Sakaguchi finally exhales in relief. His legs weaken, and he nearly sinks to the floor.
Sakaguchi calls loudly into the corridor.
Ren Nanase cautiously peeks around the doorframe.

Seeing blue-haired Launch huddled in a corner of the pharmacy, flushed and covering herself, Ren freezes, then runs to fetch a clean blanket. She returns a moment later with it in her arms, but hesitates in the doorway, still shaken.
Ren finally approaches and drapes the clean blanket over Launch's shoulders.
Ren looks at the scattered glass, then at Launch's gentle, harmless face, unsure how to answer.
Narumi enters the pharmacy. Seeing that Launch is calm again, she finally lowers her guard.

After checking the patient's condition, Narumi arranges for Launch to return to the surgical area and resume sedation and the necessary preparations under the original preoperative plan, to keep her from becoming frightened and agitated again. The nurse on duty brings a sedative, checks it, and gives her the injection. Launch cooperates obediently, still utterly confused.
The staff escort Launch out, wrapped in her blanket. Before leaving, Narumi turns back and glances at the broken bottles covering the floor.
The voices in the corridor fade into the distance. The pharmacy is quiet once more.
The pharmacy staff have cleaned up the broken bottles and powder, and the glass medicine cabinet is closed again.
Iimura leans against the counter and lets out a long breath. Sakaguchi sits in a chair by the window, straightening his disheveled white coat.
Iimura stares at Sakaguchi and slowly blinks twice.
She is stunned for a few seconds, then suddenly clutches her stomach and bursts out laughing.
After laughing for a while, Iimura finally settles down a little. She looks at the floor where the staff have already removed the broken bottles, then back at Sakaguchi.
Iimura's smile fades. For a moment, a hint of surprise crosses her face, then she smiles again.
She raises a hand to tidy her mussed hair, then narrows her eyes as if something has just occurred to her.
With her hands behind her back, she leans forward slightly. The bright, mischievous smile she wore when they first met returns to her face.
The two of them can't help laughing together.
Sakaguchi has no answer. Iimura gives another little snort of laughter.
Smiling, Iimura goes back behind the counter and picks up the medication register again. She watches Sakaguchi leave the pharmacy.
That afternoon, a single sneeze nearly turned a routine operation at Hoshimi Hospital into a hospital-wide emergency.

The operation was later completed, and the patient recovered smoothly. Apart from having to check the inventory in both the instrument room and the pharmacy all over again, the hospital suffered no other losses.
Sakaguchi and Iimura, on the other hand, now shared an experience they would probably remember for the rest of their lives.
strings.collections.character_events.miyuki_lv1_: At the nurses' station, Asakura is gathering several handover sheets into a stack. Seeing Sakaguchi approach, she looks up and gives him a smiling nod.
“Doctor Sakaguchi, perfect timing. I'm halfway through sorting out today's handover sheets for the surgical department—”
A young nurse hurries over clutching two sheets of paper, nearly colliding with the counter.

“Ms. Asakura, we have a problem! The next operation has been moved forward. The operating room is pushing us to bring the patient over, but the ward is still preparing according to the original schedule!”
Asakura takes the papers, checks the dates, then compares the revision times on the two documents.
“This is the original schedule, and this one was just revised, correct? Has the ward received the update? How far along is the patient's preoperative preparation?”
“Yes. The operating room says they're all ready and keeps asking us to bring the patient. But I don't think the ward has received it yet... I haven't finished checking the preparations, either.”
“Huh? But they said they're already waiting...”
“They're waiting for a properly prepared patient, not that sheet of paper with a revised time on it.”
Her voice is calm, but her smile has disappeared. The young nurse instinctively straightens up.

“First, confirm the patient's identity, the procedure, and the handover status of the preoperative preparations with the ward. If something hasn't been confirmed, say so. Don't substitute ‘probably’ for confirmation.”
“I'll contact the operating room. You handle the ward and report back once you've checked. Don't call both sides at once; that'll only make things more confused.”
The young nurse takes the paperwork to the phone at the other end of the station. Asakura picks up the receiver on the desk and quickly dials.

“Hello, operating room? This is Asakura. About the patient whose operation was moved forward—the ward hasn't completed the updated handover checks. Yes, we can't transfer the patient yet. You can change the schedule, of course, but the ward needs to receive the same information.”
“I know you're waiting. But no amount of rushing turns something unconfirmed into something confirmed. We'll call back as soon as we've checked.”
Asakura hangs up and lays the two sheets side by side on the counter. Standing beside her, Sakaguchi watches as she marks the items that need to be checked again.
“Would you like me to explain the situation to the operating room?”
“No, this is a handover issue. Doctor Sakaguchi, could you pass me the latest record first? The one on the left.”
Sakaguchi hands her a sheet. She glances at it, realizes it's the old version, and immediately holds out her hand again.
“Not this one. The one with today's date.”

“Everything's checked! The patient's preparations still need a little more time, and the ward has explained the situation. The operating room has agreed to receive the patient at the reconfirmed time, too.”
“Good. Both sides have the same version of the schedule now?”
“Yes! The old one has been marked void, too.”
“Tell the next shift as well. Let's not go through this again this afternoon.”
“Of course. Thank you so much, Ms. Asakura! I had no idea whom to contact first.”
“Hehe. Next time, start by putting the two sheets side by side. Running fast doesn't always help. Running in the wrong direction is what really wears you out.”
The young nurse sighs in relief, bows to them both, and leaves with the organized paperwork.
“Ms. Asakura, you handled that very smoothly.”
“Oh dear. You've caught me bossing people around, Doctor Sakaguchi.”
“When we first met, you said you were a little nervous on your first day. I thought you weren't very familiar with hospital work, either.”
“I meant my first day at Hoshimi. It's not as though I only became a nurse today.”
“I see. The way you spoke just now sounded like someone who used to be in charge of quite a few people.”
“Hehe. You're very observant, Doctor. But let's talk about the past some other time, when we have the chance.”
“All right. Then I'll come to you first when I run into handover problems.”
“Of course. But I won't accept ‘it should be fine’ as an answer just because you're a doctor.”
“Yes, I've already seen that for myself.”
“Good. I look forward to working with you, Doctor Sakaguchi.”

wait for her reaction

“All right. Now that we’ve made it clear, you don’t get to pretend you never gave that answer.”
“I wasn’t planning to take it back.”
They stand quietly beneath a streetlamp for a while. Sakaguchi doesn’t start walking right away, and Sayaka doesn’t hurry him. She looks up at him, her eyes still holding a smile.
“What? Now that you’ve officially called me your girlfriend, all you can do is stand there looking at me?”
“I was thinking there might be one thing I still haven’t done.”
“Only just remembered? You’re not usually this slow at work.”

Sakaguchi moves closer. Sayaka doesn’t pull away; instead, she lifts her face slightly. He lowers his head and kisses her, and she naturally returns the kiss. After they part, she doesn’t immediately follow it with a joke as she usually would.
Sayaka lets out a soft breath, briefly looks away, then can’t help smiling again.
“…You were certainly quick about that. I was just thinking of something to say, and suddenly I forgot my lines.”
“It’s rare to see you at a loss for words.”
“Don’t get too pleased with yourself. I thought it was nice, so I wasn’t in a hurry to tease you.”
As she speaks, she takes half a step closer to Sakaguchi. Unlike before, there is no longer any need to explain the distance between them.
“…Well then, boyfriend. Walk me home today.”
“Can’t I? I’m not asking you to work my shift. I just want you to walk with me a little longer.”

Sayaka walks beside Sakaguchi. As they cross the road, the backs of their hands brush together, and she doesn’t move away. Neither makes a point of mentioning the word ‘girlfriend’ again along the way, yet they are already acting on that answer quite naturally.
At the intersection where they are about to part, Sayaka stops and turns back.
“Mm-hm. But don’t keep staring at me at work tomorrow.”
“Weren’t you the one who kept looking at me first?”
“I’m allowed to look at you. You’re not allowed to look at me.”
She deliberately puts on a stern face, but can’t hold it for even two seconds before she laughs.
“Mine. I’m kidding—look all you want. Just don’t miss anything in the chart you’re holding.”

“Dr. Sakaguchi, the patient’s preoperative preparations have been handed over. She’s still worried about having her arms secured. She just asked again whether she can pull her hands back under the blanket once she’s on the table.”

“Dr. Sakaguchi, I’ve finished checking the preoperative handover record. The patient has repeatedly asked whether she can adjust her hands herself once she’s on the table. I’ve noted her questions at the end as well.”

“Dr. Sakaguchi, the preoperative handover is complete. The patient keeps asking whether being on the operating table means she won’t be able to pull her hands back under the blanket. I’ve written down her question.”
Sakaguchi turns to the end of the handover record and checks the explanations and preparation arrangements.

“She’s asking whether she’ll still be free to move. Under the plan we’ve already agreed on, of course she can’t move around when she needs to be secured. Prepare her as planned. Tell her which step involves securing her and why, before she’s lying on the table fighting the nurse for the blanket.”

“She also asked me very quietly whether we’d have to lift the blanket to disinfect her skin. I told her, of course we do. What are we supposed to disinfect without lifting it? The look on her face was even better than when she heard about the scalpel.”
“You certainly didn’t mince words. Did she understand in the end?”

“She did, but she kept asking whether the blanket could stay on until the very last minute. I said we’d leave it as long as we could, but every area that needs preparing will still be prepared. Don’t worry, it’s all in the handover.”
“Then carry on according to this record. If she asks again, answer honestly. Don’t skip any of the preparations just because she’s scared.”
Sakaguchi hands back the checked record. When Sayaka takes it, she doesn’t look straight at the papers. Instead, she lets her eyes linger on Sakaguchi. The nurse handling the handover notices.

In the corridor near the operating department, Sakaguchi is checking a preoperative handover record. Sayaka stands beside him, holding the documents she has already put in order. The nurse handling the handover approaches, bringing along the questions the patient has been asking over and over.
