Sayaka waves to Sakaguchi, turns, and leaves. He watches her walk away. Only now does this day truly come to an end.
Before the end of the workday, Sayaka seems to have been watching Sakaguchi the whole time.
strings.collections.character_events.sayaka_lv4_: That Look from the Other Night
After returning to work on Monday, Sayaka catches Sakaguchi in the corridor.
That Look from the Other Night
On Sunday evening, Sayaka and Sakaguchi continue their proper date.
strings.collections.character_events.sayaka_week: “Aren't you worried I might get the wrong idea?”
“You can get a little bit of the wrong idea for now. Your number?”
Sakaguchi gives her his number. She quickly types it in and sends the first message.
Sakaguchi saves the contact on his phone. Sayaka leans over from beside the desk to peek at the screen.
“Hey, wait. You're not really saving me as 'Dr. Nanjo,' are you? It looks like a hospital mailing list.”
She answers so quickly that she gives herself pause. Their eyes meet; she glances away first, then smiles.
“...Don't actually change it yet. We're not that close.”
“It rolled off your tongue pretty easily just now.”
Can I message you at two in the morning?
“Just letting you know the option exists.”
“Oh, please. I'm just worried you'll actually change it, say it out loud at the hospital, and the whole nurses' station will know.”
“Sounds like you're more worried about them finding out.”
“Give that lot a scrap of gossip and they'll talk about it for three days. It's still too early for that.”
“I never said that. Whether you can message me outside work—why don't you try and find out?”
“So it depends on what I send.”
“Exactly. You can't expect me to come up with your first message for you.”
“Can I message you at two in the morning?”
“No boring messages at two in the morning. I have work the next day.”
“I can't promise I'll have the patience for questions in the middle of the night.”
“You send the first one. I'll be the judge.”
She slips her phone into her white coat pocket, takes two steps out, then looks back.
“Like... asking if I'm off work yet. That sort of thing.”
“Aren't you busy right up until the end of the day too?”
“That's why I want you to ask. All right, back to work.”
Sayaka leaves the office. For the first time, Sakaguchi has a contact on his phone he might use after work.
A workday morning. Sakaguchi has just put down a patient's chart when Sayaka knocks on his open office door, a consultation form in hand.
“Thanks. I've already seen you in two departments this morning. How come you're over here now?”
“I go wherever they need someone. All right, save your thanks. Sign here.”
She taps the last page with her pen. Clearly, she has already found the place for his signature.
“You look like you're here to collect a debt.”
Once Sakaguchi signs, she checks it and puts the papers away.
“For this one. You've probably got more to do today, but I'm not keeping track for you.”
She reaches the door, then stops as if something has just occurred to her.
“Your number. I wouldn't have any use for your phone.”
Sayaka opens her contacts and looks up at him.
After delivering the papers, Sayaka takes two steps toward the door—then stops.
strings.collections.character_events.serika_lv0_: In the afternoon corridor, a woman in a white coat hurries along, looking down at an imaging report.
“Hm? I don't think I've seen you before...”
“Excuse me. Could I have a moment?”
As though she hasn't heard him, she walks straight past Sakaguchi.
“...She really didn't hear a word, did she?”
“Were you calling Dr. Misono? That's Dr. Serika Misono from Radiology.”
“Her reports are always on time. As for the doctor herself... well, you just saw.”
The doctor has already disappeared around the end of the corridor. Thinking back, Sakaguchi realizes he never even had a chance to introduce himself.
In a corner of the staff lounge, Serika Misono studies a set of images alone. A drink sits close at hand, untouched.
“Dr. Misono, right? We met in the corridor. I'm Ryuji Sakaguchi from Surgery.”
“Are you the one handling imaging consultations for our department? I've been meaning to—”
“The report is in the system. Images, findings, conclusions. It's all there.”
“I just wanted to get to know a colleague.”
“If you need a further assessment, use the formal consultation process.”
“Surely I don't need a consultation form just to have a cup of tea?”
She has already ended the conversation. They are sitting face to face, yet the distance seems greater than it was in that corridor.
“Asakura, let me ask you about someone. Do you know Serika Misono in Radiology?”
“I do. We used to work together.”
“Is there a problem with Dr. Misono's reports?”
“No, not at all. They're thorough, and the annotations are clear. It's just that she won't talk to me.”
“Then perhaps she's already put everything she needs to say in her reports.”
“...Are you explaining her behavior, or laughing at me?”
“But she doesn't dislike doctors who take their work seriously. There are just some things she should be allowed to decide for herself whether to talk about.”
“What exactly happened between you two back then?”
“Doctor. That's a question for Dr. Misono, not me.”
“Sometimes she goes up to the rooftop for some air. If you really want to talk to her... think about what you want to ask first. Don't open with 'a cup of tea' again.”
“How do you even know about that?”
“This is the nurses' station. News travels faster than lab reports here.”
Asakura turns back to her work with a smile. Sakaguchi has learned nothing about the past, but he has found a more useful place to try than the consultation system.
The breeze on the rooftop is cooler than downstairs. Serika Misono stands alone by the railing, without an imaging report in her hands.
“You called to me in the corridor, and you came to see me in the lounge. I'm hardly going to forget that.”
“So you really did hear me last time.”
“If you're here to ask whether I want tea again, you can leave now.”
“No, it's work this time. I read your postoperative imaging report.”
“The one where you highlighted the vessel running near the surgical field. Just a few lines of text, but very detailed annotated images.”
“Whether Surgery actually looks at them is another matter.”
“I did. It would be easy to misidentify that vessel if you assumed it was in the usual position.”
“Since you noticed, don't get it wrong during surgery.”
“Come to think of it, don't postoperative scans at Hoshimi often look a little too perfect?”
“When I first came here, I thought someone had swapped the preoperative and postoperative labels.”
“I checked the records, the times, and the patient IDs again. Everything matched.”
“For the medical outcome, very good. For the radiologist's mental health, it's harder to say.”
At last, she turns her gaze toward Sakaguchi. This time she neither avoids him nor immediately ends the conversation.
“Serika Misono. You already know my name, but I should introduce myself properly.”
“Ryuji Sakaguchi, Surgery. If there's something in the images I don't understand, may I come and ask you directly?”
Serika looks away again, as though she has merely finished a brief consultation. But this time, at least, she hasn't treated Sakaguchi like empty air in the corridor.
strings.collections.character_events.serika_lv1_: 「Serika did not bring up the images first as she usually did. She moved an electronic document to the center of the screen, her fingertip resting on the final line.」
「Dr. Sakaguchi. Have you read these preoperative discussion minutes?」
「The ones sent out this morning? I haven't had a chance to read them closely yet.」
「She selected a line on the screen. Every word was clearly visible.」
「Following confirmation by Dr. Serika Misono of Radiology, the planned cholecystectomy may proceed as originally scheduled.」
「I'd like to know that too. Because I never said it.」
「I've read your report. You warned of a possible variant bile duct course and asked for it to be checked again during surgery.」
「The right posterior sectoral duct doesn't follow the usual anatomy. These images alone can't fully establish its relationship to the cystic duct.」
「What I wrote was, 'Biliary anatomy must be confirmed intraoperatively, with adjustment of the surgical strategy if necessary.'」
「How did that become 'proceed as originally scheduled' in the minutes?」
「She reached for the pen on the desk. Its tip almost touched the printed minutes, then stopped.」
「Radiology explains what we can see and what remains uncertain. Whether to operate, and how, are decisions for Surgery to make.」
「Serika finally looked up. Her voice was quiet, yet firmer than any refusal Sakaguchi had heard from her before.」
「I'll compare the original report with the meeting minutes first. We can't resolve this just by deleting a name.」
「...Suit yourself. Just don't let that sentence follow the patient into the operating room tomorrow.」
「Sayaka was clipping several sets of examination results together in order. Seeing Sakaguchi and Serika approach together, she greeted them with her usual smile.」
「Both of you came to see me? What's with the formal visit?」
「It's about yesterday's preoperative discussion minutes. Could you check the final paragraph with us?」
「Sakaguchi turned the screen toward her. Sayaka read it twice, her smile gradually fading.」
「What exactly does 'confirmation' in this sentence refer to?」
「I meant to write that Dr. Misono had confirmed the abnormal course on the images, so we could use that information to continue discussing the surgical plan.」
「When I condensed it into a summary, I cut out the first part. And... it changed the meaning completely.」
「You didn't just cut words. You changed who made the decision.」
「I remember the discussion being quite detailed. How did it end up like this?」
「Everyone was praising Dr. Misono's image annotations. I was so focused on making the conclusion clear that I ended up combining different people's opinions.」
「Dr. Mido said the report even marked where the variant bile duct might affect the operative field. It wasn't merely a nicely drawn duct.」
「Dr. Artoria said that with these warnings, Surgery should prepare contingency plans ahead of time, rather than waiting until the operation to improvise.」
「They both sounded so certain about her assessment that I conflated 'the imaging evaluation is thorough' with 'the surgical plan has been approved.'」
「They endorsed the report. They didn't authorize you to put my name on a stamp of approval for the procedure.」
「Sayaka pulled out the original report and turned straight to Serika's final comments. She made no further attempt to explain what she had been thinking.」
「I'll rewrite it. Imaging suggests a possible variant course of the right-sided bile ducts. Biliary anatomy must be verified intraoperatively. That is Dr. Misono's report opinion.」
「And imaging cannot replace intraoperative confirmation. You mustn't leave that out.」
「Right. The extent of surgery, the technique, and whether to change the plan if a variant is encountered must be confirmed by the operating surgeon. Those are the surgical team's decisions.」
「Write it that way. Please have the surgeon responsible for this operation review and confirm it again. Don't carry over the old version.」

「I'll send the correction to everyone who took part in the consultation and to the operating room now. I'll replace every printed preoperative handover sheet myself. The original will be retained with a correction record according to procedure.」
「Dr. Misono, I'm sorry. I turned your professional opinion into a promise you never made.」
「Correct the record first. The patient's operation is tomorrow.」
「I will. I'll check it again myself when it's done.」
「Serika watched her reopen the document without saying anything more. Yet as they left the office, her pace was a little slower than when they had arrived.」
「Only the soft clicks of the keyboard and mouse remained in the imaging room. Sakaguchi set a revised set of preoperative documents at the edge of the desk.」
「Sayaka has sent out the correction. The operating surgeon has also confirmed the revised plan. The operating room has the new version.」
「She knows where she went wrong, and she's willing to put it right herself.」
「I was too harsh with her earlier.」
「That sentence really couldn't stay. You weren't angry for no reason.」
「I didn't say I shouldn't have been angry.」
「She finally turned her chair. Her gaze settled on the corrected record and stayed there for a long time.」
「...I just hate people speaking for me. Especially once it's written into an official record.」
「Then we'll keep your exact words. What was said is one thing; who makes the decision is another.」
「No. The imaging opinion is still yours, and every warning you gave is still there. The section deciding how to perform the surgery bears the surgeon's name.」
「I don't want to erase your assessment. And I certainly don't want your name carrying responsibility that belongs to us.」
「Serika stacked the old and new records together. She did not reach for the pen again.」
「I can accept being wrong in my assessment. If there's evidence, I'll correct it. But words I never said... it's hard even to know where to begin correcting those.」
「At least this one has been put right. If it happens again, I'll ask you directly first.」
「I'll keep it in mind. I won't write, 'Following confirmation by Dr. Misono, Sakaguchi will never make another mistake.'」
「Serika paused. She lowered her eyes, the corners of her mouth lifting briefly before settling again.」
「...That isn't for me to confirm either.」
「True. I suspect that application would be sent back.」
「If you want to include my imaging opinion in a preoperative discussion, bring the original material. Ask me face-to-face about anything you're unsure of.」
「You're willing to take a little more part in preoperative discussions now?」
「I said imaging. Don't push your luck.」
「All right. I'll come straight to you about the images.」
「And tell Dr. Nanjo something for me. The corrected version is very clear.」
「...Next time she comes to ask about a scan.」
「I won't leave out a single one.」
「Serika turned back to the screen. This time, without waiting for Sakaguchi to ask, she brought up the next set of images.」
「Since you're here, take a look at this. I found a clearer slice of that vessel you asked about last time.」
「The monitor lit up. Serika shifted her chair a little to one side, making room for Sakaguchi to see the screen.」
strings.collections.character_events.serika_lv3_: 「A rare day off. Sakaguchi hadn't asked anyone out or made any serious plans. He simply wanted to get away from the hospital and wander for a while.」
「Without quite intending to, he took a train to Ochanomizu. Guitar, bass and amplifier signs lined almost every inch of the sloping street outside the station.」
「...I had no idea there were so many instrument shops around here.」
「In front of a shop window, a woman in a dark coat, her long hair falling over her shoulders, was looking up at a display rack.」
「Even without her white coat, Sakaguchi recognized her at once.」
「Serika's shoulders visibly stiffened. She turned, a flash of surprise crossing her eyes.」
「Nothing in particular. I came out for a walk on my own this Sunday and happened to end up here.」
「She glanced instinctively at the window, then looked away again. Rather than annoyed, she seemed unsure how to explain what she was doing here herself.」
「Are you out shopping too? Sorry for calling out so suddenly.」
「Then I won't keep you. See you at the hospital tomorrow.」
「Just as Sakaguchi was about to step away, a very quiet voice called from behind him.」
「Do you... have any other plans today?」
「No. I was just going to wander around on my own.」
「...If you don't mind, would you like to walk together?」
「Of course. Are you sure I won't be keeping you from anything?」
「There wasn't anything I absolutely had to do.」
「...And I'm not in a hurry to go home.」
「Once she said it, she seemed to feel she had been too candid, and looked away.」
「There's a cafe up ahead. Let's sit down for a while first.」
「Someone carrying an enormous instrument case passed the window. Serika glanced at them, then lifted her coffee, as though waiting for Sakaguchi to ask first.」
「I never expected to run into you here. I thought you spent your days off looking at scans at home too.」
「That's a relief. I almost asked if you were out buying a monitor.」
「...What kind of person do you think I am?」
「The corner of her mouth moved slightly, though her voice remained as calm as ever.」
「By the way, Mizuho's been recovering well. Thanks for making rounds with me.」
「Has she finally agreed to stay quietly in bed?」
「At least she isn't insisting she's braver than Chihaya anymore.」
「...Once you've had a rough time, you do learn a little.」
「They exchanged a smile. Their hospital talk came to a natural end there.」
「Last time, in the operating room, Chihaya brought up the light music club. She called me some kind of 'K-On! girl'...」
「Serika sighed softly, but even the rim of her cup couldn't hide the hint of a smile.」
「After I went home, for some reason, I started thinking about high school.」
「So you really did play bass in the light music club.」
「Didn't I already say that in front of Chihaya? We even played at the school festival.」
「Sorry. It's just hard to imagine you up on a stage.」
「...I wasn't born wearing a white coat, you know.」
「Fair point. How did your band sound back then?」
「We were decent. More people showed up at the school festival than we'd expected.」
「Of course. Before it was our turn, I kept flexing my fingers where no one could see.」
「But once the first song started, there was no room left to be nervous.」
「She looked down at her hands beside the cup and gently stretched her fingers a few times.」
「Passing through here today, I suddenly thought... maybe I could buy a bass and try again.」
「That sounds great. How about I help you choose one?」
「But I can help choose the color.」
「Serika looked at him and finally couldn't help laughing aloud.」
「At least if two basses sound exactly the same, I should be useful.」
「See? That's why I need an expert to set me straight.」
「...Let's go once we've finished these. We won't find a bass just by talking.」
「She drained the last of her coffee as she spoke. This time, she was the one to stand up first and wait for the other.」
「They entered the first instrument shop. Guitars and basses in different colors hung neatly along the wall, their metal strings catching fine glints of light.」
「Wow. There really are a lot of models.」
「Let's look around first. I don't know what the current models are like either.」
「...Have I already lost my right to help choose?」
「Serika answered dryly, but a faint smile appeared as she passed him.」
「In the second shop, she picked up a five-string bass, studied the fingerboard, then put it back.」
「Why does that one have an extra string?」
「It's a five-string bass. There are six-string ones too. Different playing needs call for different setups.」
「So more strings means it's more powerful?」
「...This isn't upgrading equipment in a game.」
「I saw you feeling the neck just now. What were you checking?」
「Whether the grip feels comfortable and whether it gets in the way when shifting positions. You can't tell from a photograph.」
「So choosing a bass is a little like choosing surgical instruments.」
「...Don't bring everything back to the operating room.」
「She turned her head and glanced at Sakaguchi.」
「As they stepped outside, Sakaguchi watched the young people passing with instruments on their backs, and something occurred to him.」
「Seriously, I'd really like to hear you play bass.」
「Have you ever picked out the bass in the music you usually listen to?」
「Exactly. Ninety-nine percent of people say they can't hear the bass.」
「But take it away, and then they can.」
「It's the sound that holds the whole song up. It doesn't always stand at the front demanding attention.」
「Isn't that a little unfair? When it's so important.」
「What's unfair about it? You don't play bass just to wait for praise.」
「...Though when someone really does notice it, it does make you a little happy.」
「Serika lowered her head and gently adjusted the cuff of her coat.」
「Then I'll listen properly from now on. At least I'll learn which part you're playing.」
「You'd better make sure it isn't the drums you're hearing first.」
「Serika laughed. This time, she didn't immediately hide her smile.」
「A little farther down the street, she suddenly stopped outside a third instrument shop, her gaze settling on a dark-colored four-string bass in the window.」
「...That one does look a bit like the one I used to play.」
「Serika stopped in front of the bass. It hung a little high. She looked up at it for a while and was about to ask a shop assistant to take it down.」
「Sakaguchi followed her gaze. When the assistant nodded that she could try it, he reached up first and carefully lifted the instrument from its rack.」
「She took it, supporting the body with a practiced movement. Her fingers slid along the neck, and she checked the length of the strap.」
「Still, if you expect a bass tryout to sound wonderful, you're very much mistaken.」
「Don't expect some brilliant solo, though. I just want to see how it feels. Bass on its own might be a little boring.」
「Then I'll try my best to keep quiet and just clap as hard as I can.」
「Serika plugged into the amplifier and gently plucked a few strings. She tilted her head to listen, adjusted the volume, then calmly played a few single notes.」
「She checked the fingerboard and began a short rhythmic pattern. At first she had to watch her fingertips; after a few bars, her shifts grew smoother and her right hand settled into her own beat.」
「Sakaguchi knew nothing about technique, but even he could see that her fingers were no longer hesitant. After several fluid movements, she even found a moment to look up at him.」
「The corners of Serika's mouth slowly lifted. She nodded gently to the rhythm, her hands still playing.」
「You don't even know what I'm playing, do you?」
「There was unmistakable laughter in the complaint. She looked at the fingerboard and decided to try another passage.」

「She switched to a faster, more complicated phrase. Her left hand crossed several positions in succession, her right plucking faster and faster; her relaxed expression gradually gave way to concentration.」
「In the latter half of the phrase, her left hand fell a fraction behind. She stopped at once, her fingers still hovering over the notes they had been about to press.」
「That last little section. I couldn't keep up with the tempo.」
「She returned her hand to the starting position and played it again from the beginning. Her fingers reached the same spot, and stopped again.」
「Because you have no idea how I wanted it to sound.」
「Serika didn't answer. Her gaze narrowed to the strings and fingerboard alone; the easy smile from a moment ago had vanished.」

「A third time, then a fourth. She grew more hurried with each attempt, her left hand always failing to keep pace with her right at the same point. Each time she stopped, she pressed her lips tightly together and moved her hand back to the start.」
「...I used to be able to do this.」
「It's been years since you last played, hasn't it? You don't always have to be so hard on yourself.」
「Serika's voice suddenly rose. Several customers nearby stopped what they were doing and all turned toward the trial area.」
「Serika froze, her lips slightly parted. She glanced at the customers who had turned, then looked at Sakaguchi.」
「She slowly took her hand away from the strings and turned the volume down. Her fingers hanging beside the bass finally stopped moving.」
「It's all right. I made it sound too easy just now too.」
「I didn't mean to snap at you.」
「Serika lowered her eyes and looked again at the bass in her arms. Her voice grew quiet.」
「It's only that I haven't practiced in a long time... What am I fighting so hard against?」
「She slipped off the strap, carefully returned the bass to the assistant and nodded her thanks. Sakaguchi said nothing more about trying it and followed her out.」
「After leaving the shop, they walked a little way in silence. Serika's steps gradually slowed.」
「I made a fool of myself back there.」
「Actually, I had a good time today.」
「But before that, it was the first time I'd ever seen you playing an instrument.」
「...And you saw me losing my temper when I couldn't play properly.」
「Yes. At least it proves you aren't calm every single moment.」
「Am I really that hard to approach at the hospital?」
「Serika gave a brief, helpless laugh. It was a little while before she spoke again.」
「Today, I thought that if I just picked up a bass, my fingers would remember on their own.」
「I couldn't hear where you went wrong later on. But I could see how happy you looked when you smiled at the beginning.」
「Serika looked at him. For once, that face that always seemed to weigh every word didn't immediately reach a judgment.」
「She let out a soft breath, her expression growing serious again.」
「Sakaguchi, I still need a little time to see whether I can be the person I used to be.」
「Thank you so much for keeping me company today.」
「By the way, how about we find somewhere to have dinner together?」
「Serika paused, as though she hadn't expected him to ask just then.」
「...Are you asking me on a date?」
「Serika didn't answer at once. She looked toward the end of the street, then back at Sakaguchi.」
「Actually... you've already spent a lot of time with me today.」
「Serika pressed her lips together briefly, but didn't look away.」
「So, Sakaguchi... would you give me a little more time?」
「She looked quietly at Sakaguchi, waiting for his answer.」
「Serika let out a small breath of relief. This smile was much more natural than the one at the cafe.」
「Then, see you at the hospital tomorrow.」
「Serika turned to leave. After a few steps, she looked back.」
「If you come to an instrument shop with me again...」
「First, your punishment is to go home and listen to K-On! songs until you can pick out the bass.」
strings.collections.character_events.serika_radi: Lv0, Part 1: A Shadow on Just One Slice
“Why didn't you identify this shadow as a lesion?”
“Because it disappears on another slice. Look at the entire series first. Don't just pick the scariest image.”
“...You make it sound like I came looking for something frightening.”
“You printed that screenshot and circled it three times in red.”
“That's called taking a suspicious finding seriously.”

strings.collections.character_events.takemi_lv0_: “Shh. Keep your voice down. She used to work at a top research institute.”
“But I've never seen her lead an operation…”
“I heard it isn't that she can't. The director just doesn't really let her.”
“Oh, Dr. Sakaguchi! …Nothing. Just talking about old times.”
“There's a surgeon here who isn't allowed to operate?”
“That's exactly why everyone keeps talking about it.”
Iwasaki closes the handover log and pulls Yoneda back into the nurses' station. The door stays ajar, but there is no more talk of the subject.
“Head Nurse Ishigami, are they really scrapping this one? It still looks pretty new.”
“If it can't be used, it can't go into surgery, no matter how new it looks. Confirm the number and hand it over to Equipment.”
“One of the senior nurses said this wasn't an ordinary mechanical failure…”
“…What happened here? Was it cut with a knife?”
“I heard that a doctor was operating once…”
“And cut so deep that she sliced through the leather on the operating table.”
“…She operated all the way down into the table?!”
“That's what I want to know! How deep do you have to cut to slice the table too?”
“Itsumi, have you finished confirming the transport?”
“Then don't hold up the work. Dr. Sakaguchi, this old table isn't on the usable equipment list.”
Ishigami covers it again. The operating table becomes a vague outline beneath the cloth, making a brief metallic scrape as it is wheeled away.
The Ghost in the Operating Room
“Huh… Satsuki, wasn't today's last operation already over?”
“Yes. The handover record here has been signed off.”
“Then… why is the light still on in there?”
Light falls on the empty operating table. A figure is bent over beside it, as though studying something closely.
“Wait. Let me check… There aren't any additional cases today.”
“L-let's get the doctor on duty first. Don't go in on your own.”
“What happened? Why are you two running?”
“In the operating room… There's no surgery, but someone's standing beside the table!”
“The last case has already been handed over. I checked the schedule.”
“Maybe the doctor on duty went in to check the equipment?”
“B-but… That shadow hadn't moved for such a long time…”
Only the reflection of the corridor lights remains in the glass. The operating room is so quiet that it seems the light was never on.
“So did I. …At least, the light was on.”
Sakaguchi looks toward the empty operating table again. There is nothing beneath the surgical light, yet somehow he doesn't want to keep looking inside.
The Ghost in the Operating Room
The Ghost in the Operating Room
“Why does that opening line sound so ominous?”
“Like we said this afternoon, that door behind the elevator lobby might lead to the basement. Let's have a look tonight.”
“Don't you want to know what you saw in the operating room last time?”
“Why do I have to come along?”
“With a doctor along, it feels more like an official hospital inspection.”
The farther down the stairs they go, the quieter it becomes. By the bottom, even the air conditioning upstairs is almost inaudible.
“…Does anyone really still use this place?”
“Look, the sign on that door says ‘Morgue.’”
“This place… I've really never been here before.”
The morgue is empty and silent. The floor is clean, the trolleys stand neatly against the wall, and there is no sense that anyone has lingered here.
“I heard it hasn't been used in years.”
“A hospital morgue going unused for so many years… That's quite something.”
“But standing here in the middle of the night doesn't make me happy about it at all…”
“Huh? Why is there another room here?”
“It certainly is. Looks like this is as far as we go today.”
“Th-then let's go back. Right now, please?”
The three turn back toward the stairs. Only the door remains at the end of the corridor, along with its cold, unyielding lock.
“By the way, did you know our hospital actually has a basement?”
“Of course it does. But I don't think I've been down there even once since I started here.”
“If I remember right, isn't the morgue down there?”
“The m-morgue?! Stop talking about it, aaah!!”
“Oh, come on. It's perfectly normal for a hospital to have a morgue, isn't it?”
“Normal, yes… But a morgue in the basement…”
“Still, now that you mention it… I've worked here so long, and I really don't think I've ever seen anyone take a body down there.”
“Huh? Isn't that a good thing? It means our doctors are amazing, and the patients all get well and go home.”
“You know that door behind the elevator lobby? I hear it leads to the basement.”
“None of us has been there anyway. How about taking a look after work today, when there aren't many people around?”
“Rumi, that basement research lab from the other night… Did you ask around about it?”
“I asked Itsumi. She said someone in the instrument room knows who uses it.”
“The doctor the director banned from leading operations.”
“…Huh?! The one who sliced up the operating table?!”
“Shh! Keep it down. I hear she used to be especially fond of operations that were… different from everyone else's.”
“Yes. Apparently she's especially interested in… what living bodies look like inside.”
“…Do you know what that doctor downstairs likes doing most?”
“Yes. I was startled when I heard it too.”
“But last time, that room downstairs was clearly locked!!”
“Then there must be evidence of vivisection hidden inside!!”
“…Aren't you two making this sound scarier and scarier?”
“This is the lounge, isn't it? I was just getting some water.”
“You came down there with us last time, Doctor. You saw that door too.”
“I did, but a locked door… means there's evidence of vivisection inside?”
“Doesn't that just make you more curious?”
Before taking a drink, Sakaguchi suddenly realizes that all the rumors he has heard over the past few days seem to point to the same doctor, one who has never shown her face.
After the operation, Sakaguchi leaves the operating room. An unfamiliar female doctor stands beside the corridor, holding a stack of records.
“The third one I've specifically stayed to watch all the way through.”
“Mm. I watched the previous two as well.”
“You've done quite a few operations without anesthesia, haven't you? I thought it was just a rumor, but you really do keep things under control reasonably well.”
“Are you interested in this sort of thing?”
“…If it gets the operation done, I'm willing to try.”
“Heh… So you have that sort of interest too.”
“Hold on. Shouldn't we introduce ourselves first?”
“Tae Takemi. Doctor. Usually in the basement research lab.”
“So you're the one everyone's been talking about…”
“I heard that during one of your operations… you even damaged the operating table.”
“They replaced the table afterward. Isn't that a good thing?”
“And… someone said they saw a strange figure in the operating room late at night.”
“It's quiet at night. Easier to think.”
“And the basement… The morgue is right next door. Doesn't that place frighten you a little?”
“What's frightening about it? That morgue hasn't been used once since I came to this hospital.”
“Mm. Taking up all that space for nothing.”
“Just how good are this hospital's doctors…?”
“I have another question. It might be a little rude.”
“I heard… your ultimate hobby is vivisection?”
“We're doctors! How can we do vivisection?!”
“Who says vivisection has to be fatal?”
“When I dissected a frog in middle-school biology, I finished all the observations, sewed it up and turned it over. It hopped away on its own.”
“…By the way, will you be doing another operation like that?”
“There should be more on the schedule.”
“Call me if you need an assistant.”
“Huh? But didn't you say the director won't let you lead operations?”
“She won't let me lead them. She never said I couldn't assist.”
“Asuka's rule. Take it up with her if you have a problem.”
“Come downstairs if you need anything. You know which door it is now, right?”
“…So that locked room from the other night is your office.”
“Mm. If you want to come in, just find me. Don't go wandering around with flashlights in the middle of the night.”
“It's quiet downstairs. You can hear people arriving very clearly.”

As though she has no interest in explaining further, she leaves with the records in her arms. Sakaguchi stands in the corridor, suddenly realizing that not one of the ghost stories he heard over the past few days has really been denied.
“…I have a feeling I've just met someone extraordinary.”

strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_aoi.d: “Of course. It would be nice to spend some time away from the hospital. I'd be happy to join you.”
“I really liked that painting. Not because it's famous, but because the longer I looked, the calmer I felt.”
“Our coffee is nearly cold. Have we really been talking that long? Let's find another place like this next time, shall we?”
“I felt so at ease today. It's lovely to talk at our own pace, without having to rush to a conclusion.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_aoi.i: “Sorry, I'd like to keep some time for myself this Sunday. Would you invite me another time?”
“A date? Of course! Just a moment, let me put this page of case notes away!”
“Did you see that fish? The way it reproduces is fascinating! ...Huh? You brought me to look at fish, not to give a lecture?”
“The sea breeze feels wonderful! If only I could take this feeling back to the examination room. Just kidding. Today I just want to have a little more fun!”
“Today was so much fun! There's so much outside the hospital worth studying—oh, I mean, worth enjoying!”
“No, no, there's still a problem I haven't figured out today! ...Ask me again next time. I promise I'll try not to bring my notes.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_artor: “I'll keep that afternoon free. Since this is a personal invitation, let's leave work schedules aside for now.”
“This meal suits my tastes perfectly. Taking the time to truly enjoy a dish is a luxury in itself, it seems.”
“A race to the bottom? I accept. But we'll check the slope and safety rules first. After that, don't expect me to go easy on you.”
“You've arranged everything very thoughtfully. Thank you for giving me such a rare, relaxing day.”
“I'm sorry, there are things I must finish today. If we can arrange it in advance next time, I'll give it serious consideration.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_asuka: “Sure. A Sunday without approval forms is a rare treat. Where would you like to take me?”
“Wow, that enormous aquarium window was beautiful! I thought I'd only look for a little while, but I couldn't bear to skip a single exhibit.”
“A cherry blossom landed on my shoulder... Don't brush it off just yet. Let me stand here a little longer, like any ordinary girl.”
“Today I finally got to be just Asuka, instead of the director. Spending an afternoon like this feels wonderful.”
“I'm really tied up today. I'm not just using the director's work as an excuse. Ask me again another time.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_emiko: “Fine. Send me the time and place. And don't be late.”
“That improvisation was beautiful. For once, there was a stretch of time when I wasn't thinking about my next operation at all.”
“This is a good restaurant. The timing of each course, the cooking, all just right... Your taste in venues is quite acceptable.”
“You haven't wasted my time today. That's high praise, coming from me.”
“I'm busy today. If I wanted to go, I'd say yes. Another time.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_minat: “Sure! What time shall we meet? ...Wait a moment, I'll put it on my calendar myself.”
“You still don't like much sugar in your coffee, right? You mentioned it last time. I'm much better at remembering people's preferences than my schedule.”
“Wasn't that dog by the river just like the one you told me about back home? Oh dear, I remember things like that, but I nearly forgot to check the time.”
“Today was so much fun. I remember all those little things we talked about, though I'll still have to write down when we're meeting next.”
“Oh, did I already agree to something this Sunday? Let me check... Sorry, I don't think I can this time.”
strings.collections.date_profiles.date_doc_rei.d: “Sure! I've been wanting to get out and do something. Got any good ideas?”
“Did you really guess how that movie would end? Come on, sit down and tell me everything. I've got plenty to say!”
“That fall of yours was spectacular! ...All right, I've had my laugh. I'll take it slow with you on the next run.”
“Haha, that was fun today. If you find anything else interesting, remember to invite me along.”

strings.collections.first_surgery_diagnosis_reac: She looks down at her abdomen.
“Oh no... I have been eating too much lately.”
She pinches her lower belly.
“I have a little bit of a tummy.”
“And now someone has to see it during surgery... This is so embarrassing.”
She falls silent for a long moment, then touches her lower belly.
“Since you are already opening me up...”
“Could you get rid of a little of the extra fat here while you are at it?”
She goes silent again for two seconds.
“...Never mind. Pretend I said nothing.”
She suddenly pulls her abdomen in tight.
A few seconds later, she realizes that makes no sense.
“...Would this make it easier to operate?”
She slowly lets out her breath.
“What am I even trying to help with...?”
Her face rapidly turns pale.
“I saw this in a movie once...”
She seems to be trying desperately to stop herself from thinking any further.
“You really will be able to see my intestines and everything, right?”
“No. The picture is already in my head.”
She goes completely still.
“Open surgery...”
Looking down at her abdomen, she traces a finger from her upper belly to her lower belly.
“How... long will the incision be?”
“You are not going to open my whole stomach, are you...?”
She nods, then suddenly seems to remember something.
“Wait.”
“...Where do you go in?”
“You are not going in through the nipple, are you...?”
The image in her own head clearly frightens her.
“...You have to cut my breast?”
She looks down at herself.
“You are not going to slice straight through the middle like a watermelon, are you...?”
“...No, at this size it would be more like a peach.”

She covers her face.
“What am I even thinking right now...?”
She stares down at her chest for a long moment.
“...Will both sides still be the same size afterward?”
Without thinking, she cups her breasts.
“Why have I never seriously compared them before?”
“Of course I only start worrying about this when I need surgery...”
Her face turns pale, yet the first thing she says is:
“If I had known, I would not have worn this bra today...”
She freezes as soon as the words leave her mouth.
“...No. Those things have absolutely nothing to do with each other.”
“Great. I really am scared senseless.”
She presses a hand to her chest without thinking.
“So... you really will see my heart?”
“It will be beating right in front of you...”
Her expression grows complicated.
“That feels so strange. Just imagining it is a little embarrassing.”
She makes herself sit up straight.
“It is all right.”
“I am not afraid.”
She nods with great conviction.
Three seconds later, she asks, “...Do you really have to saw through my breastbone?”
“I am sorry.”
“I know you just explained everything very clearly.”
She pauses.
“But it feels as if none of it stayed in my head.”
“All that is left is: ‘I am going to have surgery.’”
She is silent for a long time.
“It is not a figure of speech.”
“You really are going to operate on me.”
She looks at the doctor as though only now has she understood what all the previous explanations meant.
She keeps nodding with great seriousness.
“Yes, I understand.”
After several seconds of silence, she speaks in a small voice.
“Afterward, when I... do that, I will not be able to feel that something inside was moved before, will I?”

She immediately covers her face.
“Why was that the first thing I thought of...?”
Her face slowly turns red.
“So... you will see a place very deep inside me.”
She falls silent for a moment.
“Even my boyfriend could never see that far inside...”

The instant she says it, her whole body freezes.
“...Did I just say something really strange?”
She stares blankly for a moment.
“You will be able to see my ovaries too...”
“What do they actually look like again?”
“They do not really look like two grapes, do they...?”
She mutters under her breath, “Why am I thinking about this now?”
She places a hand over her lower abdomen.
“Your uterus is something you normally cannot feel at all.”
“Then suddenly someone tells you they have to open your abdomen and touch it.”
She is quiet for a moment.
“I do not know why. It suddenly feels so private.”
Her body visibly stiffens.
“The pelvis...”
Her voice grows quieter.
“Do you... go in from below?”

When she hears that this operation requires an abdominal incision, she still does not look relieved.
“...Why are both possibilities so frightening?”
She tries to nod, then seems to realize something.
“Once you are inside... you really can see my uterus, right?”
“Would you ever... take it out to look at it?”
Her face immediately turns red.
“I did not mean take it out for a tour!”
Without thinking, she raises both hands and makes a parting motion in front of her chest.
“It is not really like this, is it...?”
Looking at her own gesture only makes her face turn paler.
“Why did I have to demonstrate it to myself?”
She is clearly frightened already.
After a moment, she suddenly looks down at her chest.
“It will be obvious when I wear a low neckline afterward, right...?”
“At a time like this...”
“I am still thinking about clothes.”
She is trying to keep nodding, but suddenly stops.
“...Open-chest surgery.”
She touches her breastbone.
“When you say ‘open’...”
“You mean actually open it?”

The Grand OR opens with the fixed team configuration. Every role signs in on the electronic board; no vacancy is assumed to be something “someone else will cover.”

"So now you still think that the injection yesterday was the scariest?"

“Don’t act as if this was part of your plan!”

Erina lies back in bed, exhausted.
“...I made it.”

“The TV.”

“At least I didn’t miss this one.”

Erina closes her eyes.
“...For the moment.”

Erina jolts fully awake.
“Today?! My surgery is tomorrow!”
“Thank you. At least there’s one person here who remembers the time.”

Erina looks at Haruka, then at Sakaguchi.
“...I don’t feel reassured at all.”
Erina is taken to the OR holding area. Haruka checks Sunday’s staffing arrangements and realizes that the original first assistant is nowhere in the hospital.

“Dr. Minato.”
Megumi’s eyes, visible above her mask, land precisely on Haruka.
“Focus on the surgery. Don’t hold a baseball discussion with the patient.”

“You’re welcome.”
She pauses.
“She’s always like this. Her hands are steady, and her mouth never stops.”
Megumi has already confirmed the instruments and sterile workflow inside the operating room, and passes the next thing to be done into Haruka’s hands.

Megumi does not argue about the date. She simply completes the preoperative preparations one by one: an enema, skin preparation, changing clothes, then gathering all of Erina’s hair beneath the surgical cap. Every step is professional and efficient.

Megumi looks down to confirm the schedule.
“It says today—Sunday, at ten twenty.”

“It’s seven-thirty in the morning. Good morning, Ms. Kinjo. Your surgery is at ten twenty today.”
Megumi has already placed the chart and preparation checklist beside the bed.
Sakaguchi takes the first-assistant position. Haruka takes the scalpel and makes a clean, precise incision in Erina’s abdomen.

“All right, Ms. Erina. We’re going to the operating room now.”
Megumi starts pushing the stretcher, preparing to leave the ward.
Megumi walks in. The preoperative supplies in her hands are arranged in order. Her movements are brisk, and her voice is steady.
“The Giants? Do you prefer watching pitching duels or batting battles?”

Haruka thinks for a moment.
“Don’t worry. You’ll make it. The surgery will finish on schedule.”

“See? You’ll definitely make it.”
Haruka does not look up; her hands remain steady.

Sakaguchi changes out of his scrubs and returns to the corridor, where he finds Haruka, also changed and holding her bag.

“Dr. Sakaguchi, do you have plans for the rest of today?”

The TV is already tuned to the game.
Sakaguchi finishes the last of his postoperative notes, leaving only the commentary from the game in the room.

“I am focusing.”
She does not stop working.
“Here—ease the retraction a little.”

Haruka Minato pushes open the door, her eyes settling on Erina, already seated on the transport stretcher.
“Good morning. Erina, are you ready?”

Haruka catches Sakaguchi as he happens to pass through the corridor.
“Dr. Sakaguchi, are you free today?”

Erina stares at Sakaguchi for two seconds.
“What? Is he reliable? Can he really operate? Or is he just some random person wandering around the hospital on a Sunday??”

Haruka comes in afterward.
“Did you get to watch it?”

“Don’t worry.”
Haruka keeps her eyes on the operative field.
“I’ll get you there in time.”

Haruka smiles.
“No problem. We promise everything will go smoothly!”

Haruka’s voice tightens.
“I know. Keep breathing steadily. I’ll handle this.”
She steps up to the operative field, and her voice settles into a more serious tone.

“Haruka Minato. I’m the lead surgeon today.”
She glances toward the operating room.
“As for you—I’ve just decided that you’re the first assistant.”
“Perfect. The patient is awake for an open procedure, and we’re short a first assistant. I’m borrowing you for the morning.”
“That’s exactly why I came to find you. A first assistant usually doesn’t just happen to be in the operating room on a Sunday.”

Haruka buys two cans of coffee from a vending machine and hands one to Sakaguchi.

Haruka blinks and laughs as if nothing happened.

Sakaguchi is clearly not entirely convinced, but he does not press the question.

Sakaguchi occasionally adds a comment, and before long they are talking easily together.

Haruka steps back with a bright smile.
“Then I’ll see you in the operating room.”

“That’s enough for today. See you next time, Dr. Sakaguchi.”

She turns with a smile and walks away along the riverside path.

Haruka says with a bright smile:
“It’s such a nice day. Since you’re free too, Dr. Sakaguchi, shall we go for a walk together?”
“I may be a random person wandering around the hospital on a Sunday, but I know a little something about surgery.”
Sakaguchi looks at Haruka, then toward the operating room.
At two forty in the afternoon, Erina returns to her room. When the TV comes on, the baseball broadcast has not officially started yet.

Sakaguchi accepts the coffee and looks at her cautiously.
“You’re welcome. But... how did you manage to get the surgery date wrong?”

Sakaguchi looks at her.
“I did. Now... I don’t.”
The open cholecystectomy is completed successfully. Haruka makes the final checks, Megumi counts the instruments, and Sakaguchi assists with the handoff.

【Sunday Morning】
Erina Kinjo-Wang is still asleep.
