strings.collections.temporary_conditions.drowsin: Ask the assistant surgeon to keep calling to her and repeat instructions
“Look at me and stay awake. I will tell you, one sentence at a time, how far we have progressed.”
Ask the circulating nurse to continue observation and verbal stimulation
“I will keep watching her responses. Listen to my voice and slowly tell me your name and where you are.”
Continue the operation without interrupting the current task
The patient’s gaze drifts again, and she gives no answer to the last instruction.
Call to her personally and reassess consciousness and command following
“I can hear you... please keep telling me what comes next.”
“Doctor... my eyelids feel so heavy... I'm still awake, but I can hardly keep my eyes open...”
“...What did you just say? I'm sorry, I keep losing track of your voices...”
“I... can't hear clearly anymore... Don't let me drift off... Please, please keep calling to me...”
Ask the assistant surgeon to stabilize the patient and explain the situation
“I will maintain her position and explain what is happening. Slow your breathing; we will settle the nausea first.”
Ask the circulating nurse to prepare suction and a cool towel and reassure her
“Suction and a cool towel are ready. I am right here—breathe slowly, and do not force yourself to speak.”
Maintain the current pace and do not intervene yet
“Ugh... the nausea has not stopped... I cannot hold it much longer...”
Pause, reassure her personally, and adjust her position
“...That is better. Thank you for stopping first.”
“Doctor... I feel a little sick... My stomach keeps churning...”
“Ugh... I feel awful... I, I'm about to throw up. I can't control my body...”
“No... I'm really going to be sick... Please stop for a moment. I can't take it anymore...!”
strings.collections.time_events.basement_researc: ...Need something? If you just wanted to see the basement, you got a pretty good look from the doorway.
Put those files back where they were. They're not arranged the way Surgery does things.
The director wants me? ...If it's about the operating table, tell her I've heard enough about it.
strings.collections.time_events.clinic_chat_doc_: She mentions an easily missed detail from today’s clinic. They do not dissect the case, merely exchange a few thoughts.

Sayaka folds a complicated health-management chart into three columns and smiles. “Things we can handle, things that need consultation, and things we do not need to frighten ourselves about today. People work the same way.”
After hearing Sakaguchi’s assessment, Sayaka does not immediately agree. She gently points to a long-term medication he missed. “You look at the lesion. I’ll help you see the whole person.”
Sayaka takes the temporary consultation form. “I can cover ordinary difficulty. If it needs a genius, you will have to call an actual genius.”
strings.collections.time_events.clinic_chat_nurs: With the clinic briefly quiet, Hiroko and Sakaguchi exchange a few observations about the emotions of patients in the waiting room.
After arranging the examination-room supplies, Hiroko warns Sakaguchi that the next patient may be more anxious than the chart suggests.
She smiles and says that the ward and clinic move at completely different rhythms, but both begin by making the patient feel heard.
Moe carefully finishes checking the clinic record. Only when she looks up does she notice her glasses have slipped down her nose; she hurriedly adjusts them before continuing her report.
She pulls a small notebook covered in arrows from her pocket and solemnly announces that she has recorded every route in the hospital where one is most likely to get lost.
Worried that she missed a detail, Moe checks the same preparation twice. When she notices, she blushes and says that checking once too often is better than once too little.
She quietly tells him about a small incident in the clinic, then starts laughing halfway through her own story.
strings.collections.time_events.exam_chat_doc_re: She complains that the machine lagged by half a beat again, then asks whether Sakaguchi is adjusting. The conversation is brief, but feels more natural than silence.
strings.collections.time_events.imaging_chat_vis: Discuss Psychophysiological Data with Futaba Sakura

Futaba overlays the waveforms from before and after the patient heard the word ‘incision.’ “See? The signal is clean. The patient is not anxious for no reason. Her body is simply answering before her mouth does.”

Staring at a set of recovery data, she suddenly says, “Beautiful.” When she notices Sakaguchi looking, she adds, “I know the patient is still here. The data are beautiful precisely because they are hers.”

Futaba places Maya’s calibration report on the left and the interview notes on the right. “The machine proves the change is real; language tells us why it happened. Put them together and you have the complete case.”
Review Monitoring Data with Maya Ibuki

Maya enlarges two nearly overlapping waveforms. “The difference is small, but enough to show that this probe needs recalibration. Machines bear no malice. They only repeat an error with perfect diligence.”

She looks first at the bedside record, then at the equipment log. “Dr. Sakaguchi sees the patient. I see how the machine sees the patient. When those disagree, neither of us should rush to a conclusion.”
Maya closes the equipment report and adds softly, “I checked three times. It is not that I distrust you... the third check simply makes me feel safer.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_doc_: Chat with Narumi Jinguji
Narumi Jinguji asks over tea whether Sakaguchi has settled in, then shares a small trick she uses to keep her shifts organized.
Their conversation moves from today’s cases to the cafeteria’s new menu. Narumi listens closely, adding an occasional gentle comment.
Narumi gives Sakaguchi the seat by the window and reminds him not to forget to drink water when work gets busy.
Chat with Aqua Mizuki

Aqua Mizuki gestures toward the sofa a couple of times and says enthusiastically, “You know, feeling comfortable sitting on something is completely different from actually lying down on it!” Seeing Sakaguchi’s expression, she immediately laughs. “Don’t worry, I’m not planning to experiment on the lounge sofa.”

Aqua spends a while studying the buttons on the drinks machine. “Why are some options always in the most prominent positions? Could that affect what people choose?” Sakaguchi assumes she has thought of another new device, but she waves it off. “No! Let me study something that doesn’t need a paper written about it once in a while.”

She sits down with a few draft pages, rattles off three explanations, then rejects two of them herself. Seeing that Sakaguchi can’t keep up, Aqua laughs heartily. “It’s all right, I’m sorting out my thoughts. When I’m actually explaining things to a patient, of course I take it one sentence at a time!”
Chat with Artoria Pendragon

Artoria pushes a crooked chair back into place, clearing a path for Sakaguchi. “Of course, there is no need to line up in formation in the lounge.” She looks down at the chair she has just straightened and pauses. “Still, making sure everyone can get through can hardly be a bad thing.”

She sets down the work notice she is holding. When Sakaguchi says she needn’t oversee everything herself, she nods earnestly. “You’re right. If our colleagues can do something well, we should trust them with it.” A moment later, she adds, “That is something I need to practice, too.”

Artoria sits near the door and gestures for Sakaguchi to choose any seat. “No chair here is reserved for someone of higher rank.” Hearing how solemn she sounds, she softens her tone. “Just sit wherever you’re comfortable.”
Chat with Asuka Shiromiya

Asuka Shiromiya approaches the counter with an empty cup and smiles at Sakaguchi’s greeting. “You don’t have to be so formal here. If everyone keeps calling me Director even in the lounge, I feel as though I ought to sit up perfectly straight.”

Asuka folds away a half-written note. “It always feels as though there’s something left to handle. But if we don’t leave even a little time for breaks, everyone will wear themselves out.” Smiling, she gestures for Sakaguchi to sit. “So let’s talk about something that isn’t in a report.”

Sakaguchi brings up a medical question he is unsure about, and Asuka considers it carefully. “I’d like to check that part further, but I think I know where the key issue lies.” Her smile is a little shy. “Being the director doesn’t mean I can stop learning.”
Chat with Emiko Mido

Emiko Mido casually turns a couple of pages in a magazine, then closes it. “The headline sounds very certain, but the article provides little evidence.” She glances at Sakaguchi and sets it down. “Never mind. We needn’t turn the lounge into a discussion meeting.”

As Sakaguchi approaches, Mido doesn’t look up; she simply pulls the chair beside her out a little. “Sit if you want to. You don’t need to stand there waiting for my permission.” After a while, she adds, “If you keep standing there, I can’t read in peace.”

Mido takes a sip of the drink on the table and offers a brief assessment. “The temperature is right. The taste is ordinary.” Sakaguchi asks whether she grades even her breaks. She answers calmly, “I’m not grading it. I’m stating the facts.”
Chat with Minato Haruka

Minato Haruka looks at the assortment of cups on the rack and smiles. “People’s little habits show even when they’re resting. It’s rather interesting. I often remember how someone likes to put their cup away faster than I remember where I left my own.”

She shifts her chair to make room for Sakaguchi. “You don’t look as though you want to hear a medical report. Come and sit for a bit, then.” Her voice is easy, but she still remembers to ask, “Would you like some water? I can get you some while I’m at it.”

Minato pats the pocket of her white coat, then notices the note she is looking for sitting on the table. “Oh, there it is.” She picks it up with a laugh. “I can never keep track of little things like this. Luckily, the cases that really matter have proper records; they don’t depend on where I stuff my scraps of paper.”
Chat with Kaori Miyama
Kaori Miyama asks whether Sakaguchi is satisfied with several of today’s decisions, then seriously reviews them with him.
The subject turns to time off. Kaori says she does not care, though she has already listed three places she wants to visit.
Kaori remarks that Sakaguchi’s movements were sharper than yesterday, then lowers her eyes to her coffee.
Chat with Sakura

Sakura quietly moves her chair toward a peaceful corner and glances up at Sakaguchi. “I’m not avoiding you. It’s quieter here.” She pauses. “If we’re going to talk about work, let me finish this water first.”

Sakaguchi asks whether Sakura dislikes jokes. She sets down her cup. “I like them. In the right setting.” Seeing that he is still waiting for more, she adds without a change of expression, “You’re not standing beside the operating table now. Go on.”

Sakura watches the lounge clock for a moment, then suddenly says, “Time seems to pass more slowly when it’s quiet.” Just as Sakaguchi is about to answer, she adds, “Don’t worry. I’m not planning to put that in the anesthesia record.”
Chat with Sayaka Nanjo
Sayaka sits opposite him with her coffee. “You may understand this as a break, or as me deliberately arranging a chance encounter.”
She talks about her two years in a school infirmary, where she learned that the same words—‘my stomach hurts’—could conceal ten entirely different problems.
Sakaguchi asks why she appears in so many departments. Sayaka laughs. “Because I do not have one place where I am the best. Put another way, I can help a little almost anywhere.”
Chat with Shiori Fujisaki

Shiori Fujisaki straightens two disheveled magazines into a stack and explains with a smile, “It’s just a habit. Don’t take me for an inspector.” After a moment’s thought, she adds frankly, “Though if it were a contest to see who could arrange them most neatly, I probably wouldn’t want to lose.”

Sakaguchi asks what she would like to talk about now that she has a moment free. Shiori considers it carefully, then smiles. “Let’s talk about something outside the hospital. We can sort patients’ symptoms into categories, but people’s feelings won’t always fit into a tidy table.”

Shiori turns her cup with her fingertips. “Sometimes I think first about how to say something so it won’t be misunderstood.” She looks at Sakaguchi with a slightly mischievous smile. “But if you think I’m being too serious, you’ll have to give me a good reason.”
Chat in the lounge
Don't mind me. I just needed somewhere I could stretch my legs.
The coffee here always smells faintly of disinfectant. ...Probably just my imagination.
The nurses went quiet when they saw me. Must have been talking about something interesting.
I'm not operating today. Fine by me. At least Asuka won't lecture me again.
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_nurs: Chat with Anji Tonegawa

Anji Tonegawa opens a small notebook, her brow furrowing more and more. Sakaguchi asks whether she has found something, and she closes it. “No. I used so many abbreviations in my own notes that even I can’t understand them a little while later. Records need to be readable. I don’t get to make an exception for myself.”

Anji sits down with a drink and stares at the cup for quite a while. “I spent ages choosing what to drink and still picked the most ordinary option. Don’t laugh, Dr. Sakaguchi. I’m not this indecisive when I’m making professional judgments… The choices in the lounge are harder, somehow.”

She opens the book in front of her, then closes it, as though struggling with herself. “I decided to take a break, but my brain is still reviewing my work. This is terribly inefficient.” Sakaguchi says that rest doesn’t need to be assessed. Anji gives a little huff. “I know the theory. Putting it into practice still takes work.”
Chat with Ren Nanase
Ren Nanase asks whether Sakaguchi has eaten properly, then shares a small but reassuring change she noticed in a patient today.
They talk about the ward. Ren speaks gently, but remembers every patient’s details with remarkable clarity.
Ren hands him a cup of warm water and smiles, saying that rest is part of the job too.
Talk with Saeko Hikami
Saeko slips a stack of notes into her private notebook. “Just observations about work. ...No need to read the heading.”
“Everyone is surprisingly close after hours. ...I'm not judging. I've just never seen a hospital like this.”
“Nurse Orikawa told me to relax, then shared a story from the operating room. It had precisely the opposite effect.”
Chat with Hiroko Sugimura

Hiroko Sugimura moves the kettle back to a spot where it is harder to knock over, smiling at Sakaguchi. “The little mishaps most likely to happen in a lounge are often the things everyone assumes won’t go wrong.” She points to an empty seat beside the table. “But this isn’t ward-round time. Sit down and have something to drink first.”

Hiroko sits alone with her cup for a while. When Sakaguchi approaches, she smiles and gestures for him to sit, but speaks first. “For these few minutes, I’m not sorting out anybody else’s problems. If you just want to chat, you’re welcome. If you’ve brought a third handover record, it can wait.”

She hears quiet laughter from a corner of the lounge but doesn’t rush to ask for silence. “Everyone focuses on efficiency when they’re busy. Having to vet every sentence even in here would be exhausting.” Hiroko smiles at Sakaguchi. “As long as they don’t disturb anyone trying to rest, I think it’s lovely.”
Chat with Chizuru Ishigami

Chizuru Ishigami sits near the lounge door. Seeing Sakaguchi standing, she looks up. “Sit. This isn’t a handover meeting.” Just as he takes a seat, she adds, “Nor is it an interrogation room. You don’t need my permission for your second sentence.” Her tone is calm, yet it sounds like a very restrained joke.

People are chatting quietly in the room. Ishigami doesn’t stop them; she simply closes the documents in her hands. “A lounge should have the sound of people in it. As long as they don’t disturb those who want quiet, there’s no need for everyone to stay on edge.” She looks at Sakaguchi. “I don’t run the nursing department by making everyone shut up.”

Ishigami looks at a densely covered note and folds it away. “Doing everything yourself isn’t management. If someone can take over, you should hand the responsibility over clearly.” She pauses, her tone as understated as ever. “Otherwise, all this hospital needs is one very tired head nurse.”
Chat with Rumi Iwasaki
Rumi spreads two duty rosters out and circles an empty slot. “If I can get everyone together that day, drinks are on me. ...Wait, only two of us are free again? Two still count as a get-together!”
Rumi leans back and stretches her feet. “Five more minutes and I have to go back. If you see me chatting at the station again, Doctor Sakaguchi, remember I did finish the records first.”
Rumi takes two snacks from a bag, hesitates, then puts one back. “Shiori said she wanted to pick her own, so I did not choose for her. ...Look at me, resisting the urge to decide for someone else!”
Chat with Megumi Kariya
Megumi is poring over a sheet of paper. “Allowance minus travel and meals... hmm. Ange says I should rest first, but I want to finish the math.”
“Ange keeps such neat nursing notes. I want to learn from her, but she even studies procedures on break. I want a snack!”
Megumi exhales in the chair. “I do not know if I will be a nurse forever. But I am glad I met the patient I helped today.”
Chat with Moe Honjo

Moe Honjo spreads several sticky notes across the table and explains earnestly, “I wanted to write down the little things to remember in the lounge, like washing cups after using them…” She adjusts her glasses, then suddenly laughs. “I suppose that’s something I should already know.”

She sits bolt upright with her cup of water. When Sakaguchi asks why she doesn’t relax, Moe answers quietly, “I keep feeling that if I sit down, I’ll forget what I’m supposed to do next.” Only after looking around does it dawn on her. “Oh, this is where people are supposed to rest.”

Moe studies the steam rising from her cup. “The same cup of water can be too hot for one person and just right for another. Maybe it’s like that when a patient says, ‘It’s all right.’” On this subject, her words suddenly flow easily, and her eyes light up.
Chat with Mika Nakai
Mika Nakai and Sakaguchi review the priorities for the next handoff. Only after the work is settled do they discuss a recent movie.
They talk about teamwork. Mika points out a small unspoken habit Sakaguchi had missed, then naturally asks which night-shift food he disliked most overseas.

Mika pushes the last snack toward Sakaguchi and says everyone worked hard today. When someone suggests a weekend group photo, she smiles and agrees, asking only to stand at the edge in case a call comes in.

The news mentions a cold case unsolved for years. Watching the screen, Mika says, “As long as someone works normally, pays taxes on time, and remembers to greet the neighbors, most people never investigate her twice.” Then she offers Sakaguchi the remote. “Change the channel?”
Chat with Satsuki Orikawa

When Satsuki Orikawa sees Sakaguchi come in, she instinctively adjusts her glasses. “M-Mr. Sakaguchi, are you taking a break, too?” She quickly moves aside, only to notice that there are other empty chairs. Her voice grows quieter. “I just wanted you to be comfortable…”

Looking at a hospital leaflet on the table, she says softly, “It says, ‘Please don’t worry,’ but perhaps patients would rather know exactly what happens next.” As she turns to specific nursing matters, her speech becomes steadier. “Explaining what we’re going to do first makes it easier for people to feel at ease.”

Sakaguchi notices that Satsuki has placed her cup well away from the door. A little embarrassed, she explains, “Fewer people pass by there, so the cup is less likely to get knocked over.” After a brief pause, she adds earnestly, “It’s the same in the ward. Little things affect how safe people feel.”
Chat with Itsumi Sonoda
Itsumi sets her cup down and stretches. “I always say I will rest for just five minutes, then I start chatting. Not today—I still have something I want to finish myself.”
Itsumi flips through a magazine and laughs. “Hiroko always looks dependable, even on a break. ...What? I do not mention her in every conversation!”
Itsumi shows Sakaguchi a blank day-off planner. “I am thinking about what to do on my next day off. Taking care of people is wonderful, but I ought to plan something fun just for myself sometimes.”
Chat with Shiori Yoneda
Shiori sets her cup down and studies the duty roster. “Rumi always used to say which day she was free first. Today I want to check my own schedule before we talk about it.”
Shiori closes her notebook carefully and exhales. “The ward handovers are all checked. I would like to take a little break... not because anyone told me to, but because I want to.”
Shiori looks at an unopened packet of biscuits and smiles. “Rumi used to choose the flavors for me. I picked this one myself today. It was not so hard after all.”
Chat with Miyuki Asakura
Miyuki Asakura lays out handoff forms from two hospitals. Once she learns Hoshimi’s local rules, she quickly summarizes the differences.
Miyuki recounts taking the wrong corridor when she first arrived at Hoshimi, laughing that knowing nursing does not mean knowing every building.
They spend half an hour on her orientation checklist. She crosses off everything she has mastered, leaving only the hospital-specific customs she still needs to confirm.
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_phar: Manami Iimura gathers the scattered tea bags into a box. Noticing Sakaguchi looking over, she smiles gently. “It’s not that I have to tidy everything. It’s just that if things are somewhere easy to see, the next person who comes in for a break won’t have to search for them.”

She slips her work pen into her pocket and lets out a soft breath. “I’m used to checking things over and over in the pharmacy. But here, it’s all right to take a little longer choosing a drink, isn’t it? At least no one will be affected if I pick the wrong tea.”

Sakaguchi mentions how some reminders can offend people. Iimura thinks for a moment. “We can try to speak gently, and apologize if necessary. But when something needs to be pointed out, we can’t pretend we haven’t noticed just to keep everyone happy.”
strings.collections.time_events.lounge_chat_visi: Get Something to Eat with Futaba Sakura
Futaba answers an email while unwrapping curry bread. Sakaguchi glimpses only the words ‘Dr. Maruki’ before she snaps the laptop shut. “Research discussion. No Easter egg.”
She curls into the corner of the sofa with her drink, far more casually than she ever sits in her lab coat. “Successful socialization does not require sitting like a textbook illustration.”

Futaba suddenly asks, “If you believed the wrong cause for years, even though it was wrong, does learning the truth count as healing?” Before he can answer, she bites into her bread. “Never mind. Sample size one. No conclusion possible.”
Take a Break with Maya Ibuki
Beside her healthy lunch, Sakaguchi finds a packet of cat-shaped cookies. Maya adjusts her glasses. “They provide quick sugar during experiments. Their shape... has nothing to do with the research.”
Sakaguchi notices the cat-shaped cushion at her temporary workstation. Maya is silent for two seconds. “It did not come from NERV. It is new.”
Someone says she has been looking increasingly like a certain Dr. Akagi. Maya immediately lowers her head to organize her papers. “N-no, I have not... This is simply practical clothing.”
strings.collections.time_events.office_study_med: Study Case Files and Medical Literature
strings.collections.time_events.office_write_sur: Organize and Write a Surgical Report
strings.collections.time_events.or_chat_doc_take: I'm not planning to operate. Just checking what instruments they brought in today.
This table is a good model. ...Relax. I'm not going to do anything.
Hmm? You again. The cases here have been more interesting than the research papers lately.
strings.collections.time_events.or_chat_nurse_an: While checking the instrument list, Ange asks how Sakaguchi usually gives orders when plans change unexpectedly. After listening, she seriously points out two places where his wording could cause confusion.
The topic moves from operating-room scheduling to the emergency department. Ange complains that whenever she says she will help for only a moment, she always ends up too busy to eat.
Ange asks how preparations for Sakaguchi’s next operation are going. Satisfied with his answer, she nods and insists she is merely checking normally and is absolutely not especially excited.
strings.collections.time_events.or_chat_nurse_ha: As she organizes the count sheet, she describes a small operating-room habit that newcomers often overlook.
strings.collections.time_events.or_chat_nurse_mo: Moe puts on her glasses and checks the room sign repeatedly before entering the surgical area. When she notices Sakaguchi watching, she blushes and explains that she is simply following her anti-getting-lost procedure.
Holding her little notebook, she reviews the surgical hand-scrub steps one by one with such concentration that she nearly starts again from the beginning.
Moe quietly says that she is still unfamiliar with the operating room and asks Sakaguchi to tell her immediately if he sees a problem. Then she nods as forcefully as if accepting a medical order.
strings.collections.time_events.pharmacy_chat_ma: She closes the register and mentions that people have recently been confusing medications with similar packaging.
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_doc: Talk with Narumi Jinguji
Looking into the distance, Narumi says that difficult things seem a little less pressing from higher up.
She asks which patient is weighing most heavily on Sakaguchi today. Together, they slowly put that worry into words.
Narumi does not hurry to discuss work. She simply watches the clouds with Sakaguchi for a while.
Chat with Aqua Mizuki

Looking down at the outside of the hospital, Aqua Mizuki gestures enthusiastically. “Something that looks complicated from below becomes a clear layout when you get a little higher! The body is often like that too. Change your viewing angle—” She abruptly lowers her hands and laughs. “All right, all right. No anatomy lesson today.”

Aqua changes her stance several times before finally nodding in satisfaction. “Same place, slightly different posture, and it feels completely different. Patient positioning works like that too. Details matter.” Seeing Sakaguchi watching, she waves a hand. “I’m just finding a comfortable way to stand. I’m not planning to test anything on you!”

Looking over the city, Aqua suddenly grows thoughtful. “If you get a good idea while you’re resting, does that count as rest or work? I was all ready to switch off, but my brain started a meeting without me.” She sighs, then smiles. “Oh well. At least I don’t have to write the minutes this time!”
Chat with Artoria Pendragon

Artoria listens quietly to the wind. “Up here, I can hear my own breathing.” Sakaguchi asks whether she gets tired, too, and she nods frankly. “Of course. Acknowledging fatigue is how we know when to rest.”

She studies two roads converging below. “People coming from different directions may still end up together.” Then she gives a small shake of her head. “Sorry. I finally come up for some fresh air, and I start seeing team assignments in the scenery again.”

Sakaguchi jokes that at least no one assigns tasks on the rooftop. Artoria looks up at the sky. “That is a good thing.” She turns back, her expression earnest but relaxed. “If there is something you want to say, I will hear you out. We don’t have to rush to a decision here.”
Chat with Asuka Shiromiya

Watching the figures entering and leaving below, Asuka speaks softly. “From here, the hospital seems even bigger than I imagine it when I’m in my office.” She pauses, then smiles. “Not because the building has grown taller. It just makes me think of how many people are here.”

The wind tousles the hair over Asuka’s forehead, and she smooths it back. “Sometimes this is a better place to think than my office. But standing higher doesn’t mean I see everything most clearly.” She turns to Sakaguchi and earnestly asks what he thinks.

She points toward a hospital window visible in the distance. “From outside, it’s just an ordinary room.” Asuka smiles gently. “But the people inside all have their own difficulties. I hope that when they need help, they can actually reach someone.”
Chat with Emiko Mido

Mido stands a little way back from the railing, looking out over the city. “There’s always someone in a hurry downstairs. It’s quiet up here.” She says nothing more until Sakaguchi also looks into the distance, then adds mildly, “Not a bad place.”

The wind ruffles the draft pages in her hands, and Mido holds them firmly down. “Some judgments become clearer with a change of surroundings.” She looks at Sakaguchi, her voice still calm. “But in the end, we must return to the evidence. An elegant idea is no use on its own.”

When Sakaguchi asks whether she wants to be alone, Mido answers frankly, “I only came for a change of perspective.” She glances at him, then turns her gaze back into the distance. “You can stay. You needn’t force yourself to find something to say just to keep me company.”
Chat with Minato Haruka

Minato watches the stream of people outside the hospital. “It’s the little worries patients have that tend to stick with me. Being afraid someone will mispronounce their name, for instance, or not liking other people to answer for them.” She smiles. “The numbers on a calendar, on the other hand, often seem to have it in for me.”

The wind is a little chilly. Minato studies Sakaguchi’s expression. “If you want to talk, I can listen. If you just want to stand here, that’s fine, too.” She smiles lazily. “The nice thing about the rooftop is that no one insists we find something to talk about.”

Minato points to a stretch of road in the distance. “It’s quite easy to get your bearings from here.” Sakaguchi asks whether she gets lost as well, and she waves the idea away with a laugh. “Not on the roads. The time we agreed to meet, though… You’d better write that down clearly for me.”
Talk with Kaori Miyama
Kaori says she only came up for air, yet casually points out one judgment Sakaguchi could improve from today.
For once, she does not hurry him along. She only asks whether he wants to stay until the wind dies down.
Watching the ambulance entrance, Kaori candidly admits that some decisions make her nervous too.
Chat with Sakura

Sakura stands by the wall, letting her mind wander for a while. When Sakaguchi asks if she is thinking about work, she answers calmly. “No. Sometimes I’m simply standing here. It doesn’t need an objective.” After a pause, she adds, “You could try it too. No charge.”

Faint, intermittent sounds drift up from the city. Sakura listens for a while, then says quietly, “Usually, when I hear an alert, I have to decide immediately whether to respond. Not here.” She looks at Sakaguchi. “It turns out that sounds you don’t have to act on can be quite pleasant.”

Sakaguchi says it is hard to tell from her expression whether she is happy. Sakura looks into the distance. “I’m in a good mood.” She waits for his reaction before adding, “I’m not obliged to raise my eyebrows three millimeters to prove it.”
Spend Some Time in the Wind with Sayaka Nanjo
Sayaka leans against a spot one step back from the railing. “Relax, I only came up for air. If I wanted to create a scene where you had to rescue me, I would choose a safer method.”

Looking toward the distant school roof, she speaks of her time as a school health teacher. “Those two years were not a detour. They only made me more certain that I want to be someone who can keep following a problem.”
The wind blows her red hair across her shoulder. Holding down the ends, she tilts her head. “Are you this good at listening on Sundays too, Dr. Sakaguchi?”
Chat with Shiori Fujisaki

Shiori Fujisaki looks at the sky beyond the railing. “This is a good place for a quiet moment.” When Sakaguchi asks whether she dislikes lively company, she smiles and shakes her head. “Not really. It’s just that sometimes, if I don’t rush to answer, I can work out what I truly want to say.”

A breeze passes, and Shiori tucks her hair behind her ear. “When there are several ways to do something, I always want to find the best one.” She tilts her head with a smile. “But hearing other people’s reasons can sometimes be more interesting than rushing to win.”

Looking at the neatly aligned rooftops in the distance, Shiori suddenly laughs. “I’m usually so intent on doing things better that I nearly started comparing the scenery.” She turns to Sakaguchi. “At least up here, I can stop ranking things for a while.”
Chat on the rooftop
Just getting some air. Don't turn the roof into another consultation room.
So much noise downstairs... A few floors make a surprising difference.
Sneaking away from work too? ...Heh. Looks like we finally share an ordinary hobby.
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_nur: Chat with Anji Tonegawa

Anji stands by the railing for a while, pointing to the intersecting paths below. “The routes look so complicated from a distance, but walking them isn’t necessarily confusing. Teamwork is like that too, isn’t it? Knowing the procedures isn’t enough. You have to know one another.” She laughs at herself. “Did I just turn the scenery into another exercise?”

Anji carefully smooths the hair at her temples. “Nobody’s grading my appearance up here, but I still can’t help tidying it. Habit, I suppose.” Noticing Sakaguchi’s faint smile, she adds, “You’re not allowed to put this in my performance review.”

Standing some distance from the railing, Anji looks down. “From here, everyone in the hospital looks like they know where they should be going. But when something happens, everyone has moments when they don’t know what to do, don’t they?” She turns back, her voice earnest. “That’s why I don’t want to be someone who can only recite the right answers.”
Talk with Ren Nanase
Ren says the rooftop is a good place to set down the feelings she had no time to sort out on the ward.
She asks whether Sakaguchi is tired. The simple question finally loosens shoulders that have been tense all morning.
Ren points to the light between the clouds and says the patient discharged today can probably see it too.
Talk with Saeko Hikami
Saeko stands on the rooftop, searching for words. “If something really happened but defies every expectation, how do you describe it accurately?”
“This is a good place to think. As long as nobody suddenly asks what I'm thinking about.”
“I thought I'd understand what kind of hospital Hoshimi is after spending some time here. I'm no longer so sure.”
Chat with Hiroko Sugimura

Hiroko looks into the distance from beside the railing. “You can’t see every ward door from here, but you know there are people behind them who need care.” She turns back with a smile. “A bit of an occupational habit, I suppose. Sometimes it’s nice just to enjoy the view without immediately worrying about someone.”

Hiroko straightens her cuff, in no hurry to go back. “Sometimes younger nurses are so afraid of making mistakes that they try to shoulder every problem themselves. But the whole point of a handover is to make sure someone else can take things on.” She looks at Sakaguchi, her tone still gentle, but entirely firm.

Sakaguchi asks what brought her to the rooftop, and Hiroko smiles. “Because at the nurses’ station, someone is always calling for their senior. It’s quieter here. For a little while, I can just be an ordinary person.” After a moment, she adds, “Of course, if something really is urgent, I’ll go back.”
Chat with Rumi Iwasaki

Rumi leans on the railing and squints into the breeze. “People are constantly coming and going at the station. It is quieter up here. You can relax too, Doctor. No one needs a handover sheet for a break.”
Rumi looks out over the streets. “Our shifts never line up. I tried to get six people together for drinks and ended up with two. ...Turns out, two people can have a great time too.”

Rumi fixes her bangs after a gust of wind. “Shiori said she wanted to choose where to go on our day off. I nearly made the whole plan before remembering to ask her. Her choice was actually pretty good.”
Chat with Megumi Kariya
Megumi looks over the streets from the rooftop. “The hospital looks huge from here. Maybe I will work here someday... if I make it through the internship.”
“Ange says she has wanted to be a nurse for ages. I envy that. My answer is probably... good pay? Is that too practical?”
The wind curls the note in Megumi’s hand. “Ah! That is my weekly expense record! ...Do not laugh. Recordkeeping is a fundamental nursing skill!”
Chat with Moe Honjo

Standing out of the wind, Moe takes off her glasses to wipe them, then quickly puts them back on. “Wow, I really can’t see anything far away without my glasses.” She smiles and points to a tiny fallen leaf by the wall. “But I do notice little things up close like that quite easily.”

A gust catches a small slip of paper in Moe’s hand, and she hurriedly pins it down. “I-it’s just a reminder I wrote about taking breaks, not an important record!” She folds it into her pocket, then adds earnestly, “Still, I shouldn’t let it blow all over the place.”

Moe looks down at the figures coming and going around the hospital, her voice unusually quiet. “Everyone looks so small from here. But each of them has things to do.” She turns to Sakaguchi and smiles. “Thinking that I can help even a little makes me feel energized.”
Talk with Mika Nakai
Standing beside Sakaguchi, Mika talks about each team member’s inconspicuous but important habits.
She says a smooth handoff is like the wind: invisible, but immediately noticeable when it is gone.
Mika slows her speech for once and discusses where to go on their next day off. When Sakaguchi asks where she used to go, she smiles. “Are you asking me out, or conducting a background check?”

The staff entrance below is getting a new access system. Mika casually identifies which elevator still reaches the wards at night, pauses, and adds, “Work enough night shifts and you remember these things.”
Chat with Satsuki Orikawa

When Satsuki Orikawa sees Sakaguchi, she instinctively adjusts her glasses. “Dr. Sakaguchi… It’s much quieter here than in the wards.” She tries to find a suitable topic, then simply looks into the distance with a small smile. “Sometimes it’s nice not to have to explain anything.”

Standing a little back from the railing, Satsuki thinks of the patients she helps transfer. “When patients are wheeled toward the operating area, often all they can see is the ceiling. They don’t know where they are.” Her voice steadies as she speaks about nursing. “So telling her what happens next is more helpful than just repeating, ‘Don’t be afraid.’”

Satsuki takes a small notebook from her pocket, then quickly closes it again. “I came up here for some air, but I’m still thinking about writing down a nursing question that just occurred to me.” She glances at Sakaguchi with an embarrassed smile. “I will take a proper break. At least once I finish this page… Oh. That doesn’t count as resting, does it?”
Chat with Itsumi Sonoda
Itsumi looks down from the railing. “Someone is always calling for me in the ward. Up here I can sort out the noise in my head. ...Not that I dislike a busy place!”
A gust of wind tousles Itsumi’s hair. She brushes it back. “Sometimes one little ‘thank you’ from a patient means more than ten things I could say. I heard one today.”
Itsumi looks at the sky and smiles at Sakaguchi. “Isn’t this a good place to think? I just realized something: sometimes I should stop answering for people and let them finish.”
Chat with Shiori Yoneda
Shiori stands by the railing with a warm drink. “It is quieter here than at the station. There is something about work I want to think through myself before I ask Rumi.”
Shiori looks at the distant clouds and smiles shyly. “I used to think taking a break alone would be boring. But standing here for a little while feels nice too.”

Shiori smooths the windblown hem of her uniform. “Doctor Sakaguchi, there is something I want to report myself today. ...It is not a big deal, but I handled it on my own, so I wanted to tell someone.”
Talk with Miyuki Asakura
Miyuki meant to bring her workflow notes upstairs, but ends up spending half an hour discussing favorite desserts with Sakaguchi.
She points out a train in the distance, then casually confirms tomorrow’s handoff location for cross-department support.
Miyuki says she now recognizes every clinical area. The one route she still gets wrong leads to the staff cafeteria.
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_pha: Looking down at the distant streets, Iimura seems more relaxed than she does in the pharmacy. “People walk so quickly when you watch them from here. Sometimes I’d like to learn to slow down, too. Not to put off work—just to stop treating hurry as the right pace for everything.”

The wind makes her words a little hard to hear. Iimura smiles and raises her voice slightly. “Do I usually speak too quietly? This isn’t the pharmacy; just moving a little closer really won’t do here. Please tell me if you can’t hear me.”

Watching two clouds slowly drift apart, she suddenly says, “Some differences are easier to see from a distance.” When Sakaguchi assumes she is analyzing a case again, Iimura smiles and shakes her head. “This time I really am looking at the clouds.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_chat_vis: Futaba Sakura gestures into the distance. “If the hospital were a map, the rooftop would be a panoramic view you unlock for free. Shame there are no quest markers. You can’t tell who’s slacking off.” She glances at Sakaguchi and grins. “Relax. I’m taking a break too.”

Futaba switches off her phone screen and looks up at the sky. “After staring at data every day, it’s refreshing to find a view without scales or tooltips.” She thinks for a moment, then adds, “But don’t go designing an ‘optimal cloud-watching route’ for me. I refuse to give my breaks a progress bar too.”

Looking at the rows of distant windows, Futaba suddenly grows serious. “Sometimes the hardest thing in research isn’t strange data. It’s everyone deciding too early that something is obvious.” When Sakaguchi puts on his meeting face, she laughs. “Hey, relax. I just thought those windows looked too much alike.”

Maya Ibuki holds a few sheets of paper beneath her palm. When she notices Sakaguchi looking, she gives a slightly awkward smile. “They’re blank, not research records. I left all the important material indoors. Sometimes I just want a different place to organize my thoughts.”

She gazes at the hospital windows and speaks softly. “In research data, a change can look like just a few digits. But behind those windows are real people waiting for their results.” As though worried she has made the conversation too solemn, Maya adds earnestly, “That’s why explaining results has to be about more than the numbers.”

Sakaguchi points to a stretch of reflective glass on a distant building. Maya Ibuki studies it for a few seconds, her eyes lighting up before she speaks. “Change the angle just a little, and what you see changes too.” Then she smiles, a little embarrassed. “Even looking at scenery makes me think about observation conditions.”
strings.collections.time_events.rooftop_pause.la: Spend Some Time in the Wind
strings.collections.time_events.serika_imaging_c: “If you're looking for the report, it's in the system. Printing it won't make the conclusion any more reliable.”
“I don't mind questions from Surgery. I'd prefer you actually look through the images first.”
“The latest postoperative scan shows no new issues. You can finish your surgical notes without worrying about that.”
strings.collections.time_events.station_chat_nur: Saeko reviews a handover sheet, then closes her folder as Sakaguchi approaches. “Today's handover is in order. ...Why are you looking at me?”
“Ms. Sugimura is good at organizing work. She said she'd show me the rest in a few days, so I asked which day.”
“I've seen chaotic days at my previous hospital, too. But the issue here... doesn't seem to be how busy we are.”
Megumi counts the tasks in her folder and smiles. “No missing items in the nursing records today! I wonder whether that earns points on my internship review.”
“My supervisor says nursing takes attention. Remembering the small things patients say must count too, right? That cannot be useful only on exams.”
Megumi clips her pen back into her pocket. “I am calculating living expenses after graduation. It is not all about money, but knowing the salary seems sensible.”
She pushes the handoff sheet aside and talks with Sakaguchi about the ward’s rhythm today.

A photo of an old drug package is tucked into the training material. Mika casually names the color change from before and after it was discontinued. When asked, she only says, “I heard about it at an old job,” and continues checking the next page.

Sakaguchi asks which hospital she worked at before. Stamping a form, she answers, “A few.” Asked why she left, she smiles. “The work environment did not suit me. Is the next question my family history?”
Itsumi tidies the handover log and smiles. “That patient hated feeling like a bother and kept saying she was fine. I am glad she finally told me what was really worrying her.”
Itsumi slips a note into her clipboard. “I like a lively shift, but handovers need to be clear. The next team should not have to guess who I am talking about.”
Itsumi waves to a colleague, then turns to Sakaguchi. “The senior nurses are so quick. But I do more than run errands—I just finished checking that chart myself.”
During a break in the paperwork, she asks whether Sakaguchi has learned his way around the entire hospital yet.
strings.collections.time_events.ward_chat_nurse_: “That patient complained about the preparations, then asked whether she could book the same surgeon next time. ...I'm adjusting.”
Saeko shelves a chart. “The handover was clear, and she's recovering well. Yet I feel I forgot one crucial question.”
“She says she's afraid of surgery. I won't tell her there's nothing to fear. I'm not the one on the table.”
While checking the ward record, Hiroko talks with Sakaguchi about the small changes that are easiest to miss during recovery.
She gathers the scattered forms for a busy junior, then turns and gently asks whether Sakaguchi has eaten properly today.
The subject moves from the ward handoff to Manami Iimura’s latest complaint about medication stock. As Hiroko talks, her smile grows helpless but affectionate.
Megumi closes the ward door gently. “She wants to know what happens after discharge. I did not promise anything; I wrote down her questions.”
“The ward is not quite as frightening as the OR. I like being able to take time to listen to patients here.”
Megumi carries the nursing supplies carefully. “I practiced this many times at school, but with a real patient, I feel I should be even gentler.”
She tells him about a patient on the ward who finally slept soundly. They talk a little longer before the handoff bell rings.
A patient insists that she “doesn’t hurt much.” Mika raises the observation level. “She looked at the door three times when she said ‘really.’ Ask again after her family leaves.”
Itsumi gently closes the ward door. “Her pain is not worse; she just cannot sleep. I talked with her for a bit and will check on her again later.”
Itsumi smiles over the nursing notes. “She asked for the first time when she might go home. Thinking about life after discharge is a good sign, isn’t it?”
Itsumi bends to place the call button within reach. “Ring if you need me. Do not worry about bothering me—that is what I am here for.”
strings.collections.time_events.work_chat_nurse_: Circulating duties
Monitoring records are started. I'll report any trends directly to you.
I've brought the spare supplies and checked their packaging and expiration dates.
The patient reacted just now. I recorded the time and her monitor readings.
Transport and postoperative observation are arranged. Please don't give me an entirely different plan at the last minute.
Nurses’ station work
I checked this shift's medications and handover items. Anything that needs an update is on top.
This record differs from yesterday's. I checked with the staff on duty; it is not a transcription error.
I'm still learning this hospital's habits, but the essentials of handover don't change.
Ms. Sugimura gave me a clear schedule. It's just that... some assignments here are rather unexpected.
Scrub nursing
Instruments and dressings are counted. Please tell me the item and quantity for any additions.
The needle holder is ready. ...Your pace is a little faster than at my previous hospital.
One moment. I need to verify this instrument's size. Replacing the wrong one would take longer.
The count matches. However surprising the operation becomes, this part cannot be vague.
Ward work
I documented her consciousness and vital signs. I'll point out any changes at handover.
She understood the pre-op explanation but still had questions. I let her finish asking them.
I verified the bed, name, and planned procedure one by one. Being busy isn't a reason to skip checks.
Her first question on waking was whether the surgery was over. ...I told her it was, and only then did she loosen her grip on the blanket.
Circulating duties
The monitors and peripheral equipment are checked, Doctor Sakaguchi. I will report any changes right away.
The new sterile supplies are here. I will handle the outside handoff without touching the instrument table.
I have recorded the key time. Call me if you need anything next.
I will double-check the specimen label. No one wants to chase us down after the shift.
I am watching the patient's condition. Do not worry, I am not only watching your hands.
Station duties
I sorted out the morning handover sheets. I clipped the revised ones to the front.
Doctor Sakaguchi, just ask if you need a hand. I can see who is available.
Shiori is checking the ward records, so I will cover the station. We will not leave either side unattended.
I do more than chat, you know. Those records are already sorted by time.
Scrub duties
The instrument table is checked, Doctor Sakaguchi. I am ready for your instructions.
The instruments are within reach. Just call out what you need clearly.
Understood. The instrument is in your hand.
I am keeping count of the gauze and instruments. I am not just here to talk.
This side stays sterile. The circulating nurse can handle communication outside the field.
Ward duties
I have the handover for this patient. I will handle the ward preparation from here.
I have explained what I can. If she has more questions, I will help her ask the doctor directly.
Here are the preparation records. Anything still pending is clearly marked.
I am handling the handover today. Let us not have the old schedule reach the OR before the patient.
Circulating nurse work
Monitoring notes are started. I’ll watch for changes and report anything unusual. (Looking at the monitor is easier than looking at the incision... Breathe. Stay calm.)
I brought the spare supplies. I will verify their specifications before handing them over.
This specimen label needs checking. Could you verify it once more? (Check the name first. Don’t think about what’s inside...)
I logged all the operation milestones here; I won’t skip any. (That smell of blood nearly made my knees buckle... but I can’t leave gaps in the record.)
I checked the postoperative transfer plan and will confirm it again at handover.
Nurses’ station work
I organized the shift notes! I would feel better if my supervisor checked them once more.
I know exactly when my internship allowance gets paid. ...And yes, I remember the handover date too!
I made a list of the questions patients asked, so they will not get lost at handover.
The nurses station is much busier than school. Finishing a task does feel good, though!
Scrub nurse work
I checked the instrument count with the team. Please have my supervisor verify it. (The surgical lights are on... Don’t look toward the incision. Focus on getting the count right.)
Here is the needle holder. ...Yes, this is the one; I checked the label. (Don’t stare at the bloodied gauze. Keep your eyes on the instrument table...)
I will follow the checklist for this step and ask right away if anything is unclear. (My palms are sweating... I can’t keep everyone waiting while I guess.)
The table is getting crowded. I’ll tidy the layout without changing the count record. (Don’t look over there. Just look after this table...)
I do not want to guess the instrument size. Could we confirm it first?
Ward work
I checked the bed number and patient name again. Please have my supervisor confirm the next steps.
She said she was cold. I adjusted her blanket and asked if she needed anything else.
I finished the pre-op record and circled everything still pending.
She speaks quietly. I will move closer so I can hear her properly before writing it down.
Circulating nurse duties
The circulating record is underway, and I am watching the monitors too.
The spare supplies are restocked. Let me know if the sterile team needs anything else.
I checked the specimen and its label. I will send it out through the usual process.
I have logged all the key times, Doctor Sakaguchi. You can stay focused on the operation.
The equipment outside the sterile field is checked. I will confirm the transfer plan again when the operation ends.
Nurses’ station work
The handover papers are organized. I put the copy for the surgical unit right on top.
A patient rang because she could not sleep. I sat and listened for a while, and she seems more at ease now.
I checked Hiroko’s notes. They are clear, which makes things much easier for the next shift.
The next shift is nearly here. I will pass on the little things the patients are worried about, not just the numbers.
Scrub nurse duties
The instrument count is complete, Doctor Sakaguchi. The sterile table is ready.
I placed the sutures and needle holders separately. Let me know when you need them.
Here you are. I have placed the instruments for the next step within easy reach.
I handed the specimen to the circulating nurse for verification. I will stay on the sterile field.
The table is a little crowded. I will reorganize it without disturbing the instrument count.
Ward duties
She finally told me what has been worrying her. I listened first, and now I will check with the team about what we can do.
Here is the preoperative preparation record. I checked off what is done and noted what is still pending.
She does not want to wait alone for too long. I will check who is staying with her next instead of just saying “soon.”
This patient needs the explanation again. That is fine—I will go through it once more before we move on.
Circulating duties
The monitors are checked. I will keep watching the patient's condition.
The peripheral supplies are replenished. Please tell me if more are needed.
The key time is recorded. I will check it again at handover.
The specimen label matches the record.
Doctor Sakaguchi, I will report any changes in the monitoring readings promptly.
Station duties
I have checked the morning handover. There is one revised record I am about to deliver.
Doctor Sakaguchi, this is the updated version. I have marked the old one as superseded.
I can handle this myself. If anything is unclear, I will ask promptly.
Rumi is busy with something else, so I will handle this handover.
Scrub duties
The instrument table is checked. I am ready, Doctor Sakaguchi.
The instrument you requested is within reach.
Understood. I have handed you the instrument.
I will track the instrument and gauze counts in order.
I will maintain sterility here. The circulating nurse can handle outside communication.
Ward duties
I have checked the patient identity and handover record. Here is the preparation status.
She said she was worried, so I let her finish telling me what was on her mind.
One item is still unconfirmed. I have marked it and will not count it as complete.
The ward preparation is complete, Doctor Sakaguchi. Please confirm the next step.

The scrub nurse hands over the scalpel, and Sayaka Nanjo waits for the surgeon's confirmation before the incision.

strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_advice.text: I've read your résumé, Dr. Sakaguchi. But a résumé only says what you have done before. Starting today, we'll see how you judge a situation and how you speak in front of a patient. If you're unsure, ask. You don't need to force yourself to look like a seasoned doctor.
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_composed.text: Good. The pace here can accelerate without warning, though. Keep up when you can, and speak up when you cannot. Saying something in time is also part of a doctor's judgment.
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_first_impression.text: The person assigned to meet Ryuji Sakaguchi is already waiting by the window. She holds a chart against her chest, her white coat immaculate. When she sees him, her gaze first settles on his name badge, and only then does a faint smile appear. It is less a rehearsed welcome than the manner of a senior doctor accustomed to observing before she speaks.
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_honest.text: It's normal to be nervous. The real danger is being too tense to hear anyone else while pretending you know everything. Just stay as you are now.
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_question.choices.1.la: I'll get up to speed as quickly as I can.
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_question.text: Your first day in an unfamiliar hospital—are you nervous?
strings.dialogue.nodes.aoi_welcome.text: Good morning. Dr. Sakaguchi, correct? I'm Narumi Jinguji from General Surgery. I'll show you around today.
strings.dialogue.nodes.arrival.text: April sunlight streams through the glass corridor of Hoshimi Hospital. After completing his training overseas, Ryuji Sakaguchi had not planned to choose his next post immediately. With his record, he had more prominent options.
strings.dialogue.nodes.clinic_handover.text: This is your examination room, Dr. Sakaguchi. The first patient has arrived, and I'll be nearby to assist. When you're ready, we can begin.
strings.dialogue.nodes.clinic_walk.text: Ren Nanase opens the door at the end of the corridor. Charts, a stethoscope, and newly delivered test forms are arranged neatly on the desk. Beyond the door comes the muted conversation of waiting patients. Only now does the reality of a first day about to begin truly settle in.
strings.dialogue.nodes.first_day.text: The scent of disinfectant is faint. A cart rattles past the corner. The new name badge in his white-coat pocket rests against his chest. Today is Ryuji Sakaguchi's first day here.
strings.dialogue.nodes.haru_arrival.text: As she finishes speaking, light but measured footsteps approach from the other end of the corridor. A nurse carrying neatly arranged outpatient files stops before them, nods first to Dr. Jinguji, then turns to Sakaguchi.
strings.dialogue.nodes.haru_first_impression.tex: She keeps her eyes on Sakaguchi as she speaks. Her voice is gentle, but the movement with which she hands him the files is crisp and efficient. Colored tabs line the pages, and even the ward and operating-room locations he has not yet asked about are marked with brief notes.
strings.dialogue.nodes.haru_intro.text: It's nice to meet you. I'm Ren Nanase. I mainly handle surgical nursing and today's coordination. Your outpatient files are ready. If you cannot find someone later, come to the nurses' station first. You can usually find me there.
strings.dialogue.nodes.haru_invite.text: We have a little time before the first patient's appointment. Let's stop by the nurses' station and meet today's team. Then I'll take you to the examination room.
strings.dialogue.nodes.mentor_recommendation.tex:
What finally brought him to Hoshimi Hospital was a recommendation from his medical-school mentor.
“If you still haven't decided where to go, give this place a try.”
strings.dialogue.nodes.one_year_contract.text: Sakaguchi ultimately signed a one-year contract. For now, Hoshimi was simply a place to settle after returning to Japan.
strings.dialogue.nodes.rin_impression.text: Nurse Nakai turns to the next page of her handoff sheet. Her tone is almost stern in its brevity, yet she has already written an extension number beside Sakaguchi's name. She seems like someone who prepares everything one step ahead.
strings.dialogue.nodes.rin_intro.text: Mika Nakai. I mainly handle ward care. I'll verify inpatient preparation, handoff, and postoperative observations with you. When you need help from the ward, say exactly what you need. No need to talk around it.
strings.dialogue.nodes.sayaka_boundary.text:
“Call it a Hoshimi specialty.”
She slides the last page into her folder, her smile carrying the calm of someone who knows exactly what she is saying.
“You can ask me for ordinary assistance or cross-department coverage. If something is beyond me, I'll say so myself. Being able to admit what you cannot do is also part of being a doctor.”
strings.dialogue.nodes.sayaka_generalist.text: “Does that count as introducing your department?”
Soon after they leave the nurses' station, a figure rounds the corner and stops short. Sakaguchi checks his step just in time; their shoulders miss each other by inches. Several health-management forms slip from her arms.
strings.dialogue.nodes.sayaka_intro.text:
“That was close. Are you hurt?”
She crouches to gather the papers, then looks up at the new badge on Sakaguchi's chest.
“Dr. Ryuji Sakaguchi? I'm Sayaka Nanjo. General practice, health management—and whenever another department suddenly needs a doctor, I may get dropped in there too.”
strings.dialogue.nodes.sayaka_tease.text:
“And you've been staring at me because you're trying to remember a new colleague's face, right?”
Before Sakaguchi can answer, she has already stepped aside to clear the corridor.
“Let's record your answer as ‘yes’ for now. Don't be late on your first day, Dr. Sakaguchi.”
strings.dialogue.nodes.station_close.text: For your first day, remembering the three of us is enough. There will be more staff on future shifts, but you have met everyone you will need in the clinic and ward today. Come on—I'll show you your examination room.
strings.dialogue.nodes.station_haru.text: This is the nurses' station. The morning team is small today, so the names should be easy to remember—Senior Nurse Nakai, and Asakura.
strings.dialogue.nodes.station_walk.text: Sakaguchi follows Ren Nanase. She walks half a step ahead at a slower pace, pointing out the medication room, the ward passage, and the doors leading to the surgical area. The ringing phones and tapping keyboards of the nurses' station grow clearer.
strings.dialogue.nodes.yui_impression.text: Nurse Asakura laughs before anyone else can. Her Hoshimi badge is brand new, but the notes in her pocket already sort the hospital's equipment models and handoff sequence into neat categories. Her energy briefly lightens the busy station.
strings.dialogue.nodes.yui_intro.text: I'm Miyuki Asakura, and I'm supporting the clinic today! I've worked in nursing for several years, but this is my first day at Hoshimi, so I'll confirm the hospital's procedures from the beginning. You can leave blood draws, test arrangements, and patient transport to me. Oh—if I ask too many questions, don't take it to mean I can't do the job.
strings.patient_bundles.patient_aerith.encounter: “Oh, I need to take off all my clothes for this examination? …All right. But Doctor, can you first tell me where you'll be examining? I'm still awake, you know.” (Stripping down to nothing at all... Even a joke won't hide my blush now.)

“Oh, we're skipping this examination? …Whew, then I won't have to take off all my clothes. But have you really checked everything you need to?” (At least I don't have to strip off my bra and panties on the spot... though my chart will probably note an incomplete physical exam.)

“…All right, I'll cooperate with the examination. But Doctor, don't just give orders. I'll still ask if there's something I don't understand.” (With the doctor giving the order in such an unmistakable tone, I have no room left to refuse. As I unhook my bra and slide my panties down my thighs, the cool air wraps around my bare breasts and lower body, making my toes curl with shame.) Blushing deeply, Aerith removes her outer clothes piece by piece, bites her lip as she takes off her bra and panties to place them in the tray, and stands stark naked under the exam light while you complete the full physical examination.

“Thank you for explaining first. Mm, I'll cooperate… Though having to take off all my clothes really is a little embarrassing.” (Even though the doctor's tone is gentle, I still have to take off every single piece of clothing. When the last of my underwear leaves my body and I stand completely naked for palpation under the bright lamp, my heart pounds wildly with embarrassment.) Following your gentle guidance, Aerith slowly removes all of her clothes, folds her bra and panties into the tray, and stands bare under the examination light with nowhere to put her hands until the full physical exam is finished.

“…Don't use that tone with me. People have ordered me around like that before. Doctor, I know I need an examination, but I'm not some voiceless test subject.” (Using my medical record and future treatment to pressure me... my fingers are shaking so hard I can barely undo my bra clasp, yet I still have to strip myself completely bare right in front of them.) Biting her lip without further argument, Aerith stiffly removes her outer clothes along with her bra and panties, places them into the tray, and endures the full physical examination stark naked in tense humiliation.

strings.patient_bundles.patient_aerith.patient.r: “No anesthesia? Doctor, are you trying to treat me, or see how long I can stand it? I've seen plenty of that kind of research before.”
“It's really over... Thank goodness. This time I'm not somebody's experimental result, just an ordinary patient, right?”
“All right, I'll stay. But Doctor, remember to use my name this time. I'm Aerith, not a number.”
“Ah! Doctor, it really hurts! Don't just watch my reactions... I can talk! Listen to me...!”
“I know you're not Hojo... It's just that with so many white coats around me, sometimes I remember the past.”
“Doctor...? When you all suddenly go quiet, I remember my days in the laboratory. Could you say something to me...?”
“Wait! That isn't what we agreed on, is it? Doctor, this isn't Hojo's laboratory. You need to explain first.”

“Wait... You're securing my arms, too? I know this is surgery... But hearing 'don't move' still makes me a little frightened.” (Strapping all four limbs down without a drop of anesthesia... I can't even writhe when the blade cuts?!)

“Doctor, do you know what I hated most back then? Being positioned by someone who then just recorded my reactions... So at least talk to me, all right?” (No anesthesia and strapped wide open like this... Can I really survive what's coming...?!)

“W-wait! You're putting it in while I'm completely awake? At least tell me first... Don't just tell me 'don't move'!” (Shoving a catheter straight in without anesthesia... That searing sting nearly made me scream!)
“Ah...! Doctor, I know this is necessary... But it's so uncomfortable... You can hear me talking, can't you?” (It's throbbing raw inside me—I don't even dare twitch my hips a fraction of an inch...!)

“Huh... pumping my belly full of water even though an enema wasn't needed... Your fondness for 'extra steps' is rough on a girl, Doctor...!” (It wasn't even required and yet my belly's pumped full of warm water... You did this on purpose!)

“Calling it extra insurance just to make me pull my pants down in embarrassment for nothing... I can barely hold it in anymore...!” (Humiliated like that for no reason—I can't even bring myself to look the doctor in the eye...)

“Even my ribbon has to come off... All right. But don't just call me 'the patient' afterward. My name's Aerith.” (Even the last lock of hair hiding my face is tucked away—I'm really about to go under the knife...)

“Hiding all my hair... Mm, it feels a little like being at the research facility before. But this time it's just ordinary surgery, right?” (Seeing the gurney waiting right beside the bed, my palms are already slick with cold sweat...)

The surgical team confirms the patient's identity, the procedure, and their respective responsibilities one by one. Aerith listens carefully on the operating table.
“You're arranging the surgery today? …Hehe, don't let my smile fool you. I really am a little nervous.”

“Okay... Hold me steady. I know I had anesthetic, but my body still jerks away on its own...”
“Ah! It hurts like hell! I know I can’t move, but don’t just pin me down without warning...”
“That’s it? At least tell me what happens next! You can’t just tell me to listen.”
“Epidural anesthesia... My head stays awake while my legs stop obeying me? That sounds really uncomfortable...”
“General anesthesia... So I go to sleep without knowing anything? That makes me a little uneasy...”
“Local anesthesia, huh? Fine, I’ll try not to move... But don’t say I didn’t warn you if it really hurts!”
“What?! Surgery without anesthesia? Hey, I’m not made of metal! Are you serious?!”
“Just hold on a little longer? All right, I’ll listen. Tell me how to cooperate and I will.”
“It’s finally over? ...Whew, that’s a relief. Don’t laugh at me; I didn’t expect it to be this hard.”
“Hey... Is it done yet? We’re at the end, so don’t suddenly stop talking...”
“I know! I’ll stay still... But you have to warn me first, too!”
“Hey! I’m still talking! Don’t just keep going like that...”
“Hah... hah... You finally stopped... Give me a moment and I’ll try not to move.”
“Oh, so that’s how it works. Explain it clearly first and of course I’ll cooperate.”
“Huh? I have to stay in the hospital? Can’t we deal with it today? I don’t want to stay here forever.”
“Fine, I’ll stay. But tell me the schedule first. Don’t leave me waiting around.”
“Ngh... Have you already started? I can’t feel it clearly, but knowing you’re really operating is still frightening...”
“Ngh...! I can feel it! You really started cutting... Hey, don’t do the next one without warning!”
“Aaah!! It hurts!! W-wait! No! This isn’t something I can get through just by enduring it!”
“...All right. I’m counting on you. When I wake up, the operation will be over, right?”
“W-wait! I said I’d try to cooperate, not that I could endure any pain!”
“All right, I get it! I’ll cooperate... But you have to explain things properly, too.”

“Hey, wait! That’s not what you said earlier, is it? Doctor, did you make a mistake?!”

"Hiss...it hurts a little. Please slow down, I will try not to move."

strings.patient_bundles.patient_ann.diagnosis_re: She falls silent for a long moment, then touches her lower belly.
“Since you are already opening me up...”
“Could you get rid of a little of the extra fat here while you are at it?”
She goes silent again for two seconds.
“...Never mind. Pretend I said nothing.”
“...You have to cut my breast?”
She looks down at herself.
“You are not going to slice straight through the middle like a watermelon, are you...?”
“...No, at this size it would be more like a peach.”

She covers her face.
“What am I even thinking right now...?”
She is silent for a long time.
“It is not a figure of speech.”
“You really are going to operate on me.”
She looks at the doctor as though only now has she understood what all the previous explanations meant.
Her face slowly turns red.
“So... you will see a place very deep inside me.”
She falls silent for a moment.
“Even my boyfriend could never see that far inside...”

The instant she says it, her whole body freezes.
“...Did I just say something really strange?”
She makes herself sit up straight.
“It is all right.”
“I am not afraid.”
She nods with great conviction.
Three seconds later, she asks, “...Do you really have to saw through my breastbone?”
strings.patient_bundles.patient_ann.encounter.fu: "Wait a minute, why do you have to take off all your clothes for a basic physical examination? Even underwear is not allowed?" (They said it too naturally. The clinic is not a dressing room.)

"That's pretty much it. Just make it clear where you want to check. Don't tell me to take it all off with just one sentence." (The medical record will probably say that I am not cooperative. Let them do it.)

"Okay, you said this is a requirement for a complete physical examination. I will cooperate. If you have seen enough, check it out quickly." (Speak harder, but still freeze when you reach your hands behind your back. No one of them evaded.) She was still unconvinced, but she moved quickly. After taking off all her clothes, she stood at the position you designated and completed the basic physical examination.

"...Okay. Since you said you would come in order, I will cooperate." (You really have to leave nothing behind. No matter how gentle you say it, it is still embarrassing to stand naked in front of them.) She took off her clothes until nothing was left; the doctors and nurses continued to prepare records at the original pace, and you then completed the basic physical examination.
