strings.patient_bundles.patient_sakurai_mayumi.p: Mayumi Sakurai

I was dealing with an illegal-parking call when I suddenly felt sick, so my colleagues brought me straight here. Usually I'm the one telling other people to stop; today they ordered me to see a doctor. I'm so busy at work I don't even have time for a date, yet somehow I had time to come to the hospital... This is irritating.
Doctor, hear me out first. I suddenly felt unwell while I was on duty: {line}
The main thing I noticed was: {line} I'm not exaggerating; every word is true.
There's one more thing to add to the chart: {line} Don't assume I'm fine just because I can talk.
“My legs can't move, and you're telling me to relax? Easy for you to say... All right, I'll try not to tense my shoulders.”
“Got it. I wasn't planning to move... Hss, something tugged inside just now. Give me a moment to catch my breath.”
“Don't just focus on telling me not to move! I know it affects the surgery, but when it hurts this much, how am I supposed to just lie here without struggling?!”
“You think ‘it's routine’ is enough to get rid of me? I have to give reasons when I write a ticket. You should at least tell me what happens next.”
“I'll be awake but unable to move below the waist? ...Don't twist around. Tell me when the anesthesia takes effect.”
“General anesthesia? Then I won't be able to keep track of anything afterward... Tch. I don't like that feeling. But if that's what I need, I'll leave it to you.”
“Local anesthesia, then. If I feel pulling or pain inside, I'll say so. Don't treat me reporting discomfort as making trouble.”
“Wait! You're going to operate without any anesthesia? Are you kidding? My body isn't here for you to practice with!”
“Whew... All right, breathe like you said and don't tense up... Nurse, do you usually have to manage people who won't listen like this?”
“...Is it really almost over? Don't reassure me casually. I'm going to take you seriously.”
“...I don't have the energy to argue anymore. Tell me when you're wrapping up... Please.”
“I know! Don't move, I understand! ...But my hands are shaking from the pain. You can see that too, can't you?!”
“If you're going to continue, tell me first. Don't suddenly do something—no matter how fast I react, I can't take that.”
“...You stopped? Whew. Okay, give me a few seconds... Let me steady my breathing.”
“Now that's an explanation. Tell me the steps and reasons clearly, and I'm not here just to pick a fight.”
“Hospitalization? Wait... Doctor, tell me why it's absolutely necessary first. The precinct still needs someone to take over my duties.”
“Fine, I'll be admitted. Don't get the wrong idea—it's not that I have nothing to say. I know when I should listen to the professionals.”
“...Have you started cutting already? It doesn't sting much, but that pressure inside... So this really is surgery.”
“Hss—! The outside is numb, so why does it still pull and hurt inside? Doctor, how far have you gotten?”
“Aaah—!! It hurts! W-wait! I know I have to lie still, but don't just ignore everything I'm saying!”
“...All right. When I wake up, tell me the surgical result directly. Don't brush me off with ‘everything's fine.’”
“Ha...! You're still going to continue? Do you have any idea how much it hurts...? Let me finish what I'm saying first!”
“...I know you're professionals. Before you start cutting, remind me once more, all right? At least give me a moment to prepare myself.”
“Why are you looking at me...? ...Forget it. At least someone's paying attention to me. Keep talking.”
“Mm, tell me how it's going and I'll cooperate. Just please don't call ten minutes ‘almost done.’”
“Hey? Why did everyone suddenly go quiet? What are you doing? At least answer me!”
“Hold on! That isn't the surgery we just confirmed. Check the chart carefully before we discuss the next step!”

“This line is the incision? ...Seeing it drawn on my own body is a lot scarier than seeing it on a diagram.” (That marker tip feels so vivid—knowing the scalpel will slice right along this line makes me panic...)
“Tell me when you're done marking. Don't leave me guessing where you're going to cut.” (The line is longer than I pictured... Please be gentle when the blade comes down...)
“Wait, you're really planning to cut along here? ...I haven't had any anesthesia yet!” (Drawing an incision line on unanesthetized flesh... Is a raw scalpel really slicing here next?!)
“My heart is racing just from you drawing the line... Don't tell me it ‘won't hurt at all’!” (I just saw the nurse hand over the scalpel... Give me three seconds to breathe, I'm terrified!)
“Hey, don't just keep marking. Let me prepare myself before you cut, okay...?” (Help, the blade is hovering right over the line... My heart feels like it's about to explode!)
“I can get into this position. Don't have nurses on both sides giving me commands at once! One at a time.” (Wrists and ankles buckled into the straps... I can't even lift a hand to cover myself!)

“Raise my hands, relax my shoulders... Got it. You really have a whole routine for getting patients situated.” (Everyone is looking down around the table checking my body—I'm clenching my toes in shame...)
“I can adjust myself. Don't rush to hold me down... All right, this is the angle you want?” (Strapped down so tight I can't even flinch... Please be gentle with me...)

“Wait! You're going to secure me like this without any anesthesia? What if I can't stand the pain?!” (Strapping all four limbs down without a drop of anesthesia... I can't even writhe when the blade cuts?!)

“Do you really think I can just stay still because you tell me to...? At least get me into a comfortable position first!” (No anesthesia and strapped wide open like this... Can I really survive what's coming...?!)

“Hey, anyone can say ‘don't move.’ Once you actually start cutting, you'd better listen if I call for you to stop!” (The blade hasn't even touched me yet and every muscle is already locked stiff with dread...!)
“Hss, that disinfectant is cold... Tell me before you touch me; don't catch me off guard!” (That antiseptic is freezing! Swabbed across bare skin, it means the blade is moments away...)
“You have to disinfect such a large area? ...All right, I guess you're really operating here.” (As the liquid evaporates and steals my warmth, I can't stop a faint shiver...)
“That cold made me shiver... Hey, does this mean the next step is cutting?” (If a cold sponge feels this sharp, how much will it hurt when the raw scalpel cuts me open?!)
“I'm still completely awake. If you're about to start after disinfecting, you have to tell me!” (Watching the doctor's hand move toward the instrument tray makes me want to bolt right off the table!)
“I'm this nervous just from the disinfectant... What am I going to do when you actually cut?” (Not a drop of anesthesia... Please let me take one deep breath before the blade comes down...!)

“A catheter...? I know it's pre-op preparation! But could you not announce it so loudly in front of the whole room?!” (Before the scalpel even starts, I have to spread my legs under the lamp for a catheter...!)
“I'll cooperate, okay...? Nurse, tell me before you begin.” (Warm urine is flowing out through clear tubing while I'm wide awake to feel every second...!)
“Hss, this feels awkward... I'm used to reprimanding people at work, but now I can barely look up.” (Hearing that faint sound in the tubing, I can only bite my lip and turn my burning face away!)
“A catheter even without anesthesia? ...Wait, let me catch my breath first.” (Shoving a catheter straight in without anesthesia... That searing sting nearly made me scream!)
“I know I shouldn't move, but I'm so tense my legs are stiff... Don't rush me!” (It's throbbing raw inside me—I don't even dare twitch my hips a fraction of an inch...!)

“Just so we're clear, I'm not refusing to cooperate on purpose... I'm afraid the next part will hurt.” (Digging my nails into the pad just to keep from sobbing—uncut catheterization is a nightmare...!)

“An enema? Hey, that's part of pre-op prep too? ...Fine, but could you not announce it so loudly in the hallway?” (I know it's standard prep, yet feeling that tip slip in makes me freeze up in shame...)
“I'm here to get treatment, not to go through boot camp... All right, I'll cooperate. Tell me before you start.” (Every ounce of strength is going into holding it in—even my voice is shaking...)

“Wait, a nurse has to do this too? ...Tch. When I'm the one giving orders, it never feels this humiliating.” (Finally cleared for the restroom... I've officially lost a lifetime's worth of dignity today.)

“Hey, Doctor!! Enema wasn't even on the checklist—why did you still make me drop my pants and take a bellyful of water?!” (Thinking how I didn't even need that enema makes my ears burn with embarrassment and frustration...!)

“Tricked me into an unnecessary enema like a rookie, huh... My belly's ready to burst—quit standing there watching me squirm!” (Still damp and cramping down there, and all of it was completely unnecessary... ugh!)

"Skin prep... you're shaving right over that spot too?! Ugh... the feel of the blade scraping across my skin is way too clear—d-don't just stare at me!" (That soft scraping sound is way too loud in this quiet room—my face is burning up!)

“Don't reach out so suddenly! I know this is medical prep, but could you tell me where you're going to work first?” (Please stop parting it to check for missed spots—I'm already on the verge of tears...!)

“I usually check other people's IDs. I never thought I'd be the one getting examined like this today... Please be gentle.” (With everything shaved bare, the cool air hits right against me—I don't even know where to put my legs...)

“Hold it! The incision isn't on my lower body, so why shave my most private spot completely bald?!” (Exposing my most private spot to be shaved for nothing—just thinking about it makes my ears burn...!)

“Shaved clean where no prep was needed... Closing my legs brings weird bare-skin friction while a scorching blush refuses to go down!” (Breezy and bare without a single hair left, and all of it was completely unnecessary... ugh!)
“I have to tuck all my hair into this cap? ...It takes more effort than putting on my police hat.” (Even the last lock of hair hiding my face is tucked away—I'm really about to go under the knife...)
“There, there, even the hair by my ears is tucked in. Nurse, is it finally good enough?” (Seeing the gurney waiting right beside the bed, my palms are already slick with cold sweat...)
“...Have you started cutting already? It doesn't sting much, but that pressure inside... So this really is surgery.”
“Hss—! The outside is numb, so why does it still pull and hurt inside? Doctor, how far have you gotten?”
“Aaah—!! It hurts! W-wait! I know I have to lie still, but don't just ignore everything I'm saying!”

"All right, I'll relax like you said. Please tell me when you're starting; I'm still awake." (How am I supposed to ‘just relax’ right now when even my inner thighs are trembling...)

“Wait—this procedure didn't require an enema at all, did it...?! Yet all the fluid is already inside me, leaving my belly so swollen I can barely stay calm...” (It wasn't even required and yet my belly's pumped full of warm water... You did this on purpose!)

strings.patient_bundles.patient_shimizu_iraiza.p: Iraiza Shimizu
I play guitar in SICK HACK, and in my free time I draw doujin manga. Between rehearsals and deadlines, I'm usually busy, but today I'll be a good patient and get checked out.
Hello, Doctor! I thought a little rest would be enough, but my body has gotten like this: {line}
This is the most noticeable symptom: {line} I'm not exaggerating; it really worries me a bit.
Oh, and I should mention this too: {line} I'm afraid I'll forget something, so I'll tell you both now.
“My legs really won't listen to me... I know it's the medication. Um, you're still right there, aren't you? Hearing you helps me feel safer.”
“Okay, I'll stay in the position you told me... Mm, the surface is fine, but it feels awful when something touches inside. I'm not moving on purpose!”
“Ah... you're going to hold me still? I know I can't move, but when it hurts my body might try to pull away on its own... Please don't suddenly let go of me!”
“Huh? That's all? I don't need a whole lecture, but at least tell me what the first step will be!”
“An epidural? My mind stays awake, but I can't move my lower body... Wow, that sounds more nerve-racking than forgetting a chord during a performance. Please tell me before you start.”
“General anesthesia means I'll fall asleep and wake up afterward? That sounds convenient... but not knowing anything in between is a little scary. Tell me how it went when I wake up!”
“Just local anesthesia? Okay, I'll hold still. If I feel any pulling or pain inside, I'll tell you right away.”
“N-no, wait! You're really going to operate without any anesthesia? That's not a scene you can just skip in an anime... Doctor, are you serious?!”
“I just follow your breathing count, right... One, two... exhale. Okay, I can keep up. Please tell me when it's over.”
“It's really almost over? Thank goodness... Whew, a moment ago I thought I'd never be able to smile again. Thank you, everyone.”
“...Is it not over yet? It's okay if I don't say anything... just please make sure to tell me when it's finished.”
“Don't move, right... Mm, I know! But there's this wave of discomfort inside, and I have to work hard to keep still!”
“Okay... I hear you. I know you need to continue. Could you tell me the next step as you go? Then I won't keep imagining things.”
“P-please wait... I need a moment to catch my breath. Whew... okay, I can still hear you. Don't rush.”
“Oh, there are so many steps! It's like going over a schedule before rehearsal. Once I understand it, I feel much more at ease. Thanks, Doctor!”
“Huh, I have to stay in the hospital? Then someone will have to cover band practice and my doujin deadlines... But health comes first, I know. Doctor, about how many days will I be staying?”
“OK, I'll be a good patient! I just need to tell the band I'll be taking a break. By the way, could you explain the examination and surgery schedule in advance?”
“Huh... you've already made the incision? It isn't a sharp pain, but there's a heavy feeling inside, as if something is being pulled... Please tell me how it's going.”
“Tss—! W-wait, my skin doesn't hurt much, but that tug inside just now felt awful... Doctor, is that normal?”
“Aah—!! It hurts! It hurts so much! W-wait! I can really feel the blade cutting into me... Doctor, stop for a moment!”
“Mm... I'll close my eyes now. When I open them again, it'll all be over, right? ...Please take good care of me.”
“I-I thought I could handle it a moment ago... but thinking about being cut while I'm awake makes me shake. Doctor, could you listen to me once more?”
“I'm usually not afraid of the spotlight when I'm on stage... but my heart is racing today. Doctor, can I keep asking you questions when I get nervous?”
“Doctor... could you look at me for a moment? I know you're busy. I just want to know someone is listening...”
“Oh, you're at this step now... Thanks for telling me. Knowing how things are going really helps; otherwise my mind starts making up the scariest possibilities.”
“...Why did everyone suddenly go quiet? H-hello, Doctor? I'm still awake. Could you say something to me...?”
“W-wait! The surgery you just mentioned isn't the same one you confirmed earlier, is it? This isn't like playing the wrong song on the setlist. Please check it again!”
“So this is the incision marking... I see, you draw it on the skin first. I can see it, Doctor. You'll start here, right?” (It's only ink for now, yet that's the exact spot about to be cut open...)

“Once this line is drawn, you know where to cut... Huh, seeing it marked for real makes me much more nervous than hearing about it.” (As long as the surgery goes safely... Deep breaths—don't start crying before the first cut...)

“Wait... this line marks where you'll cut me without anesthesia? I-I need a moment to prepare myself...” (When even the marker nib feels this distinct, how am I supposed to endure a raw blade cutting in?!)

“It's marked already... A moment ago I thought I was brave, but now that I can see it, my heart is pounding like the drums before a show...” (Squeezing my eyes shut and gritting my teeth, praying the first cut doesn't make me pass out...!)

“Arms over here, and don't turn your body... OK, I understand. It's just nerve-racking with the lights shining and so many people around.” (That click of the restraint strap is terrifying—I'm completely at their mercy now...)

“Doctor, how long do I need to stay in this position? I can cooperate, but lying here unable to adjust myself takes more patience than playing guitar.” (The cold pad presses against my back while every nervous breath stays in plain view...)

“W-wait... without any anesthesia, I have to hold this position the whole time? I'm afraid I'll curl up when it hurts!” (The second the straps cinch tight, the terror of being cut open raw nearly drives me mad!)

“You need to secure me so I won't suddenly move... I understand why, but thinking about surgery while I'm awake makes my legs start shaking...” (Cold sweat trickles down my temple; I can only pray these straps hold me through the first cut...)

“Wow, that's cold! You're disinfecting such a large area... Okay, I'll stay still. I was just startled for a moment.” (Wet amber antiseptic covers the field, making every breath catch in my throat...)
“The antiseptic feels cold... and smells so much like a hospital. Um, after this, are you preparing the incision?” (With the monitor beeping this fast, there's no hiding how nervous I really am...)

“Once the disinfection is done, you'll make the incision, right...? I'm still awake—why did the room suddenly feel so frighteningly quiet...” (Shivering from the chill, knowing I'm about to take the knife wide awake and unnumbed...!)

“I'm cold... No, it's not just the antiseptic. Thinking that you'll really cut me open without anesthesia is making my whole body tense up...” (The monitor's beeping faster and faster—the whole OR can hear how terrified I am...!)

“A urinary catheter... I know it may be needed during surgery. But I'm still awake. Could you tell me when you're going to start? This is so embarrassing...” (Being parted and wiped down there just to have a tube pushed in—I've never felt this humiliated...!)

“This step has to be done on the operating table too...? I'll try not to move, but I'll speak up if it feels uncomfortable.” (Having a tube draining me right between my legs makes me want to keep my eyes shut forever...)

“No anesthesia at all, and I still need a urinary catheter...? Wait, I'll be so nervous I might move. Please explain everything first!” (Tears sprang straight to my eyes—every millimeter feels like needles down there!)

“Ah... I know it's necessary, but being awake for it is embarrassing and I'm afraid it'll hurt... Please don't start without warning me.” (Even breathing makes the tube rub raw against the most sensitive spot—it hurts and it's mortifying!)

“Huh, I need an enema before surgery too? I know it's part of the medical plan... but even hearing about it is embarrassing. Could you explain it slowly?” (As warm water rushes into my belly, my whole face feels hot enough to catch fire...!)

“So this is an official preparation step too... Okay, I'll cooperate. But when you say it so casually, it's hard for a patient not to get nervous!” (My insides are churning like crazy and I have to clench hard in front of everyone... This is torture!)

“Uwah—wait a second, Doctor! The chart said no enema needed, so why did you still pump a whole bag of fluid into me?!” (Made to bare my backside for nothing, and my lower belly is still aching and full...!)

“Using prep as an excuse to put me through an unnecessary enema... My stomach won't stop gurgling and my ears are melting from shame!” (My stomach is churning so hard I can barely hold it in—all that humiliation for nothing...!)

“Skin preparation means removing the hair from the surgical area, right? I understand... but having someone else do it suddenly feels more embarrassing than changing into any stage costume!” (Feeling the blade glide across such tender skin has me too scared even to breathe...!)

"Eh, the razor is already shaving down there too...?! I know it's for the surgery, but feeling myself get shaved completely bare down below is so embarrassing!" (Shaved completely bare down there—even shifting an inch feels chilly and strange...)
“Eek—the incision isn't down there, so why did you shave me completely bare anyway?!” (Shaved completely smooth where the scalpel won't even touch—the draft down there is mortifying...!)

“Not a single hair left where no prep was needed... That strange bare friction between my thighs tortures my nerves every second!” (Bare skin touches directly whenever I close my legs—it feels so weird I can barely sit still...!)

“All my hair has to fit inside the surgical cap? Okay! I'll put it on properly... Huh, even my ears need to be covered? I feel like I've become a different character.” (With my forehead and ears completely exposed, even pretending to stay calm is hard...)

“The cap has to fit this snugly... I'm usually quick at changing outfits, but dressed as a patient today, I'm still not used to it.” (With every strand tucked inside, I'm officially nothing but a patient waiting for the blade...)
“Huh... you've already made the incision? It isn't a sharp pain, but there's a heavy feeling inside, as if something is being pulled... Please tell me how it's going.”
“Tss—! Wait, my skin doesn't hurt much, but that tug inside just now felt awful... Doctor, is that normal?”
“Aah—!! It hurts! It hurts so much! W-wait! I can really feel the blade cutting into me... Doctor, stop for a moment!”

strings.patient_bundles.patient_sora.diagnosis_r: She looks down at her abdomen.
“Oh no... I have been eating too much lately.”
She pinches her lower belly.
“I have a little bit of a tummy.”
“And now someone has to see it during surgery... This is so embarrassing.”
She nods, then suddenly seems to remember something.
“Wait.”
“...Where do you go in?”
“You are not going in through the nipple, are you...?”
The image in her own head clearly frightens her.
“I am sorry.”
“I know you just explained everything very clearly.”
She pauses.
“But it feels as if none of it stayed in my head.”
“All that is left is: ‘I am going to have surgery.’”
She keeps nodding with great seriousness.
“Yes, I understand.”
After several seconds of silence, she speaks in a small voice.
“Afterward, when I... do that, I will not be able to feel that something inside was moved before, will I?”

She immediately covers her face.
“Why was that the first thing I thought of...?”
She presses a hand to her chest without thinking.
“So... you really will see my heart?”
“It will be beating right in front of you...”
Her expression grows complicated.
“That feels so strange. Just imagining it is a little embarrassing.”

"The abdomen is already a little bloated. Do I need to keep it for a few more minutes?" (They were talking about time and dosage, so I could only quietly endure the embarrassing feeling.)

strings.patient_dialogue_profiles.enigmatic_self: "I can feel someone anchoring this place. You can continue, but please explain the next step." (The touch is further away, but the sense of presence is stronger.)

"...Are you stitching now?" (It's so quiet that it's hard to tell whether it's over or something went wrong again.)

"...Go on." (The sound of the equipment was too close, but I didn't want to look away first.)
"Thank you. Let me get my breath back before I continue." (At least he stopped when he said he would, which is important.)
"It's very clear. Before every step, please tell me as you do now." (His tone was not evasive...at least for now, he is trustworthy.)

"Have hospitalization and surgery been confirmed? Then, please tell me the complete next arrangements." (Things have finally come to this... Listen carefully first, and then decide how much to be afraid.)
"I understand. Please go ahead with the arrangement and I will cooperate." (How they will treat a person lying on the operating table... I want to see it with my own eyes.)
"Has it been cut?...It's quieter than expected." (Knowing that the knife has been dropped, deep inside the body still instinctively tightens.)
"It stings a little. Doctor, look at me and say: Is this expected?" (As soon as he looked away, I would ask to stop.)
"Stop - it hurts too much! Stop immediately!" (I couldn't maintain any composure, my body felt like it was torn apart by a burst of fire.)
"Your voice is still... very good." (Before my consciousness sank, the last thing I remembered was his eyes.)
"Stop. I did not agree to undergo surgery without anesthesia." (No amount of calmness will allow them to cross this line.)
"Okay, I'll see how you finish it." (We're all here, and it's boring to shrink back.)
"Don't look away." (As long as he looked at me, the cold operating room hadn't completely swallowed me up.)
"Go on. I understand, and I need to know the progress." (Turn the unknown into steps, and fear will have boundaries.)
"Doctor, are you going to stay silent?" (The most disturbing thing is not the pain, but the fact that everyone knows what is happening except me.)
"This is not the surgery just explained. Doctor, you should stop and confirm first." (Sure enough, as long as you look away slightly, the process may go to a completely different place.)
"Is this the final incision? Let me confirm again." (One line turned the operation from concept to reality.)
"The mark is longer than expected, but I will keep it still." (My skin still trembled slightly when the pen tip passed by.)
"Wait a minute, this line is different from the description." (If you don't ask now, the next time you encounter this line will be a knife.)
"Stop marking first. I need to listen to the spell again to confirm." (You can't give up questioning just because you're lying on the stage.)
"Is it okay if the arms are fixed here? I will cooperate." (Once the posture is fixed, the control is also reduced.)
"Please first explain the angle that the legs and body need to maintain." (I wonder how I will be left under the light.)
"It's okay to fix it, but don't use sudden force. Tell me first." (Without anesthesia, every movement is like a warning.)
"This angle is already causing me pain, please adjust." (They must listen, not just focus on the process.)
"It's very cold...Does the disinfection range end here?" (The skin is scratched inch by inch into the area about to be operated on.)

"It's tingling there, please check the skin reaction." (It's not just cold, it's like a tiny fire burning.)
"Don't continue applying it yet. I need you to confirm why it hurts so much." (The body is already instinctively avoiding it.)
"It will feel like a foreign body, right? Tell me before you start." (No matter how calm you are, your body won't have any reaction.)
"I will relax. Please tell me when you are done." (Invisible operations are particularly concerning.)
"It hurts. Stop for a moment! Don't keep pushing." (The burning sensation pierces deep into the body.)
"Please take it out and reevaluate it. I can't cooperate like this." (Patience is not unlimited permission.)
"I know this is pre-operative preparation. Please tell me how long it should last." (This kind of thing can be said so commonly...Hospitals are amazing.)
"There will be a feeling of swelling, right? I'm ready." (Uncomfortable is uncomfortable, at least I want to see my reaction clearly.)

“Mm... forcing the fluid in personally even though it wasn't on the required list... Isn't your hidden agenda a bit too obvious, Doctor?” (Thinking how I didn't even need that enema makes my ears burn with embarrassment and frustration...!)

“Using extra precaution as an excuse to watch me squirm and hold it in... I won't forget this unnecessary ordeal...” (My stomach is churning so hard I can barely hold it in—all that humiliation for nothing...!)
"The scope is larger than I thought. It's to maintain sterility, right?" (After being treated as a surgical field, the body suddenly didn't look like his own.)
"Please continue, I won't move." (The machine moves very lightly, but the sense of shame is extremely clear.)

“Mm... shaving my private area completely bare yourself when the cut isn't even down there... Your 'precautionary prep' is awfully thorough, Doctor.” (Exposing my most private spot to be shaved for nothing—just thinking about it makes my ears burn...!)

strings.patient_dialogue_profiles.graceful_caret: "I'm being held here...I'll try not to move as much as possible." (The feeling of someone holding my body firmly is so unfamiliar that it makes my nose feel sour.)

"I'll breathe as you tell me. Please keep telling me the next step." (Catching his voice like an outstretched hand.)
"...You can continue. I can still hold on." (In fact, I really want someone to say that you don't have to be so sensible all the time.)
"Thank you...just give me a moment. I'll tell you when you can continue." (He did stop. I wasn't going to have to endure this alone.)
"Thank you for explaining it so carefully. Knowing what will happen next makes me feel more at ease." (It's been a long time since anyone has spoken so patiently to just me.)
"You need to be hospitalized for surgery, right? Please tell me what to prepare." (The house will probably be as quiet as usual...at least there will be someone here to answer me.)
"I understand. I will cooperate as arranged, please don't worry about me." (Obviously I need to be taken care of, but I still have a habit of reassuring others first.)
"Has it started yet?...I only feel a distant pull." (The fact that the knife fell still made my heart tighten.)
"It stings a little. Please make sure the anesthesia is really enough, okay?" (I don't want to be brave and only be discovered in the end.)
"No - it hurts too much! Please stop, please stop!" (Courtesy and restraint were all torn apart by the pain at this moment.)
"Well...I heard you. When I wake up, will it still be you?" (Before my consciousness became distant, this was the first time I wished someone would not leave.)
"Please stop. I gave no consent to continue without anesthesia." (Meekness should not be taken as permission to remain silent.)
"Okay, I believe you. When it's over, please tell me." (It's actually a little warm to give yourself to someone who is willing to respond.)
"Doctor...can you look at me?" (Even if it's just for a moment, I don't want to become a body that no one is watching under the light.)
"Please continue to explain. I'll feel more at ease if I listen." (It's important enough that someone remembers that I'm still awake.)
"Is everything going well? It's too quiet, I'm a little scared." (The familiar silence is back, like those long nights at home.)
"I'm sorry, this seems to be different from the technique just explained. Can you check it again?" (You can't swallow your doubts just because you're afraid of causing trouble.)
"Is this line the incision? It's longer than I thought." (I can't move my eyes away, and my heart tightens along with that line.)
"Please let me confirm one last time before we continue." (Remember it like a body about to change position.)
"This is different from the position just explained. Please stop." (You still have the right to say no even if you are lying here.)
"Please recheck the technique. Make sure not to drop the knife before." (For the first time, there was no room for retreat in his gentle tone.)
"This position is okay, I will stay still." (There is no place to hide under the light, so I can only hand over my trust.)
"Does the arm need to be here? Please help me adjust it." (The feeling of being held firmly is more reassuring than imagined.)
"Please slow down, it's already a little painful from this angle." (My body is shaking, I can't pretend to be relaxed anymore.)
"Please tell me before you fix it. I'm afraid I'll suddenly run away." (At least let the fear be heard.)
"It's so cold...but it doesn't matter, please continue." (The cold liquid scratched the skin, and the body couldn't help but tense up.)
"Is this the extent of the surgery? I know." (Every inch of chill reminds me of what's about to happen.)
"It's not just cold here, it's stinging. Please check it out." (The pain is wearing away the restraint bit by bit.)
"Please wipe some off first, my skin feels like it's burning." (What I need is not patience, but someone to respond.)
"I'll try to relax. Please tell me right away when it's over." (The most embarrassing moment, especially the fear of being treated like an object.)
"Will it sting? Please slow down... please." (The voice is soft as if he is apologizing for his request.)
"It hurts...please stop and don't push any further." (The burning heat spreads suddenly along the depths of the body.)
"I really can't bear it, please take it out first." (Finally no longer hiding the pain with a smile.)
"I know it's pre-operative preparation... Please slow down a little, I will cooperate." (In this embarrassing situation, it would be much better if someone explained it gently.)
"Will there be swelling and pain? It's okay, please start." (I subconsciously said it's okay, but in fact my palms are already sweaty.)

“Ah... D-Doctor, this operation didn't actually require an enema...? Yet you already pumped all that fluid inside me...” (It wasn't even required and yet my belly's pumped full of warm water... You did this on purpose!)

“My tummy feels so full and uncomfortable... Going through all that when it wasn't even needed is just too mortifying...” (Stuck clenching my legs together fighting the urge... This doctor has a seriously wicked streak!)
"Do you need to deal with such a large area? I understand, please continue." (The moment the clothes were lifted, I still instinctively wanted to cover myself.)
"It's a little cold...I won't move around." (Suppressing shyness into a calm voice is something I have long been used to.)

“Ah... D-Doctor, that private spot isn't anywhere near the incision, so why did you shave it completely bare anyway...?” (The incision isn't even down there, yet you made me spread my legs and shaved me bare... So unfair!)

“Left completely bare when no prep was needed... Just pressing my legs together feels so embarrassing my face is burning up...” (It'll take weeks to grow back after discharge... This doctor's taste is seriously twisted!)
"My hair is relatively long. It might be troublesome for you to take it all in." (Having someone take care of my hair makes me feel a little warm.)
"This won't hinder the operation, right? Thank you." (After putting the hat on, the operation suddenly became real.)
strings.patient_dialogue_profiles.playful_defian: “My legs aren't really doing what I tell them anymore... You'd better hold me steady.”

“D-don't just tell me to hold still! It hurts so much my whole body wants to pull away...!”
“Huh? That's all? Tell me a little more. I'm the one this is happening to.”
“My body will be numb, but my head will stay clear? Hmm... Then I'll hear everything you say.”
“Sleeping through it sounds pretty nice... But going to sleep without knowing anything is still a little scary.”

“Huh? No anesthesia?! Doctor, I didn't come here for a pain-endurance contest.”

“Ah...! W-wait... That's so uncomfortable! I'm completely awake...!”

“Oh, an enema? That's part of the preparation, too... Wait, right now?”
“Mm, lie on my side... All right. I never thought being hospitalized would mean needing help even with this.”

“Huh... wait a second, Doctor! The checklist clearly said this operation didn't need an enema—why did you still pump my belly full of fluid?!” (Made to bare my backside for a bellyful of water—now even my jokes are stuck in my throat!)

“Insisting on doing an unnecessary step personally... Is watching me clutch my belly and blush really that amusing, Doctor...!” (My insides are churning like crazy—all that humiliation for nothing, how mean!)
“All right, I won't pull away... Wait, you have to shave that far down, too?!”
“Skin preparation, right... Huh? Here, too? How can you all act so matter-of-fact about it...?”
“Huh, whaaat?! The incision isn't even down there, Doctor—why did you still shave me completely bare?!” (The incision isn't even down there and yet I'm shaved bare—the draft makes my voice shake!)

“Shaving me clean when it's nowhere near the operative field... Now bare skin rubs straight together whenever I close my legs...!” (Spreading my legs to be seen and shaved bare for nothing—my cheeks are on fire!)
“All my hair goes inside? All right... I really look like a surgical patient now.”
“Hey, can you still recognize me like this? Don't mix me up with someone else!”

"There is a feeling of oppression... Is this normal? I will continue to cooperate." (It's not what I thought... Is it being opened? I don't dare to think about it until I know where it is going.)

"Hmm... there's a little sting, and there's a feeling of being pulled apart. Has the anesthesia fully taken effect?" (The inside is clearer than the surface... It's okay to cut the skin, but it won't hurt if you go in later.)

"No...please stop. Doctor, I'm not under anesthesia yet..." (Help...I don't want to be awake for this stab. Any louder sound will make it difficult to hear.)
"I'll try my best to cooperate... If I'm too nervous, please remind me again." (Are we really going to start... If someone talks, I won't feel like I'm left here.)
"..." (After meeting our eyes, I regained my breath a little. But when I was looked at, my body became even hotter... so many people looked at me, I really wanted to bury my face.)

"..." (If you don't explain...what to do next. This is my body...I really want to cry, but crying would be even more embarrassing.)

"This line... looks so long. Does the incision really have to be so big?" (When the pen tip slides over, the skin trembles...)

"It hurts over there... Please take it out first, please..." (Every time I go in, it becomes clearer... It hurts so much, I can't stand it anymore.)

"Do you, do you want to turn it sideways like this... I will hold back." (The doctor put the tube in with his own hands, and the nurse was watching the scale next to him... There was no place to hide even if he wanted to.)
"My stomach is so bloated...can't I go to the bathroom yet?" (They just said to hold on a little longer, but they didn't seem to notice that I was too embarrassed to look up.)

“Ugh... d-didn't the nurse say an enema wasn't needed...? Why did you still insert the tube and fill me up, Doctor...” (Made to bare my backside for nothing, and my lower belly is still aching and full...!)

“It didn't even have anything to do with my surgery... Feeling it rumble inside is so shameful—please let me go empty it soon...” (Still damp and cramping down there, and all of it was completely unnecessary... ugh!)
"Do you need to prepare the skin there too...Okay, I won't move." (The machine moved from the lower abdomen to the base of the leg without even covering it. For them, it is just the surgical field.)
"Can you...slow down a little bit?" (The broken hair was brushed away by the nurse, and the doctor was still lowering his head to check if there was anything missing. I could only put my legs down.)

“Sob... the surgery isn't even down there, so why did you shave my most embarrassing spot completely bare...” (Shaved completely smooth where the scalpel won't even touch—the draft down there is mortifying...!)

“Being completely bare down there feels so strange... Every brush of the sheet makes me flinch—I can never face anyone again...” (Breezy and bare without a single hair left, and all of it was completely unnecessary... ugh!)

"Hair... I'm sorry to bother you." (The doctor's hand pulled the hair away from my ears. I didn't even dare to flinch. The distance was so close that I could hear the gloves rubbing against the brim of my hat.)
"Have you put everything in... Then, I'm ready." (After putting on the hat, the nurse has already pushed the stretcher over. There is really no time to regret.)
strings.patient_dialogue_profiles.socially_anxio: “Thank you. I will breathe at your pace.” (With someone supporting me clearly, the trembling finally eases.)
“I can hear you. Please keep telling me what comes next.” (If I focus on the voice, I do not have to picture the incision.)
“Please stop… I truly cannot do this.” (Even formal words cannot hide the sob in my voice.)
“Understood. Please tell me exactly what I need to do.” (The fewer words I use, the harder it is to hear the tremor in my voice.)
“I will keep still. If I start trembling, please remind me to breathe.” (I must not inconvenience everyone.)
“General anesthesia? All right. Please tell me just before I fall asleep.” (At least no one will have to see me lose control.)
“Local anesthesia… I will remain awake, correct? Please explain each step.” (Not seeing what is happening may frighten me even more.)
“No anesthesia…? I am sorry, but I do not think I can maintain my composure.” (My knees weaken just imagining it.)
“All right. I will keep breathing slowly. Please guide me through the last part.” (At last I can loosen my clenched hands.)
“Is it almost over? Thank you… I did not cause everyone too much trouble, did I?” (My first concern is still how others see me.)
“Are you closing now? Please tell me.” (The unseen silence makes composure impossible.)
“Understood. I will not move.” (The command is clear, but my shoulders tense further.)
“Please continue… I will do my best to cooperate.” (I cannot keep the whole operating room waiting.)
“Thank you for stopping. I need a few seconds to steady my breathing.” (Being allowed to admit fear makes it less humiliating.)
“Thank you for explaining it so clearly. I will follow your instructions.” (I must remain dignified and not collapse like I did in the elevator.)
“Will anyone contact the department store while I am hospitalized? I do not want this to affect the store’s reputation.” (Speaking about my own body is still painfully difficult.)
“I understand. Thank you for protecting my privacy. I will cooperate fully with treatment.” (The tightness in my chest finally eases.)
“I feel pressure… but no sharp pain. I can continue.” (Keep the voice steady.)
“There is a little sting, but I can bear it. Please go slowly.” (Sweat is already running from my temple.)
“Ah—please stop! It hurts too much; I cannot keep still!” (Every practiced trace of etiquette collapses at once.)
“I understand… Then I leave it in your hands.” (Before my vision blurs, I finally let myself clutch the sheet.)
“Please do not do that. I will cooperate, but I cannot consent to surgery without anesthesia.” (Courtesy does not mean surrendering the right to refuse.)
“Doctor… before we begin, could you tell me once more that you will stay here?” (My palms are already soaked inside my hands.)
“Doctor, I am looking at you.” (As long as you do not look away, I am still a patient rather than a problem.)
“Hearing your explanation helps a great deal. Please keep talking.” (When I know the next step, I do not feel completely out of control.)
“How far have we progressed? Please give me some response.” (Silence brings back the moment I collapsed in the elevator.)
“Please wait… This is different from the procedure you explained earlier, isn’t it? Could you confirm it once more?” (If I lose composure here, could it even reflect badly on the department store?)
"Is this line the incision? It's longer than I thought." (I can't move my eyes away, and my heart tightens along with that line.)
"Please let me confirm one last time before we continue." (Remember it like a body about to change position.)
"This is different from the position just explained. Please stop." (You still have the right to say no even if you are lying here.)
"Please recheck the technique. Make sure not to drop the knife before." (For the first time, there was no room for retreat in his gentle tone.)
"This position is okay, I will stay still." (There is no place to hide under the light, so I can only hand over my trust.)
"Does the arm need to be here? Please help me adjust it." (The feeling of being held firmly is more reassuring than imagined.)
"Please slow down, it's already a little painful from this angle." (My body is shaking, I can't pretend to be relaxed anymore.)
"Please tell me before you fix it. I'm afraid I'll suddenly run away." (At least let the fear be heard.)
"It's so cold...but it doesn't matter, please continue." (The cold liquid scratched the skin, and the body couldn't help but tense up.)
"Is this the extent of the surgery? I know." (Every inch of chill reminds me of what's about to happen.)
"It's not just cold here, it's stinging. Please check it out." (The pain is wearing away the restraint bit by bit.)
"Please wipe some off first, my skin feels like it's burning." (What I need is not patience, but someone to respond.)
"I'll try to relax. Please tell me right away when it's over." (The most embarrassing moment, especially the fear of being treated like an object.)
"Will it sting? Please slow down... please." (The voice is soft as if he is apologizing for his request.)
"It hurts...please stop and don't push any further." (The burning heat spreads suddenly along the depths of the body.)
"I really can't bear it, please take it out first." (Finally no longer hiding the pain with a smile.)
"I know it's pre-operative preparation... Please slow down a little, I will cooperate." (In this embarrassing situation, it would be much better if someone explained it gently.)
"Will there be swelling and pain? It's okay, please start." (I subconsciously said it's okay, but in fact my palms are already sweaty.)

“Ah... I-I'm sorry! The checklist marked it not applicable, yet you still pumped my belly full of warm fluid yourself... It's too humiliating...!” (Using extra precaution as an excuse to watch me squirm... I went through that mortifying enema for nothing!)

“So it wasn't even a required step... With my stomach churning like this, I can barely get a full sentence out...” (Humiliated like that for no reason—I can't even bring myself to look the doctor in the eye...)
"Do you need to deal with such a large area? I understand, please continue." (The moment the clothes were lifted, I still instinctively wanted to cover myself.)
"It's a little cold...I won't move around." (Suppressing shyness into a calm voice is something I have long been used to.)

“Ah... I-I'm sorry! That area wasn't even in the prep field, and yet you shaved me completely bare anyway...!” (Telling me it wasn't required AFTER shaving me bare down there—you just wanted to watch me blush!)

“Left completely smooth where no prep was needed... Feeling bare skin press together between my legs is unbearably mortifying...” (Clutching my gown hem and scared to move—they saw and shaved every last bit of me for nothing...)
"My hair is relatively long. It might be troublesome for you to take it all in." (Having someone take care of my hair makes me feel a little warm.)
"This won't hinder the operation, right? Thank you." (After putting the hat on, the operation suddenly became real.)
strings.patient_dialogue_profiles.strong_front_e: "I feel someone pressing there. Is this pressure normal?" (The palm of my hand is also too hot...The area being pressed is suddenly clearer than elsewhere, so don't press there.)
"It's still a little tight after pressing it. Has the anesthesia fully taken effect?" (If you press it any more, I will scream...don't make me scream.)
"Wait a minute, don't press it! It hurts too much! Be gentler!" (The whole piece hurts when you press it... Is it necessary to press it to death? The knife is really about to come off.)

"That's it? I'm already lying down. At least let me know what will happen next." (That's it? Just strip down and lie here waiting for the operation, and the result is just one sentence? It's a bit unreal.)
"It's okay to be awake. I can hold on, but tell me every step first." (If there is sudden unconsciousness or sudden pain down there... I will think there is something wrong with me.)
"Well, it's better to fall asleep than to hold on. Don't leave me suddenly before the medicine takes effect." (Go to sleep...don't make a sudden attack in the end, I hate that kind of thing.)

"It's just local anesthesia? Okay, I will tolerate it. Will you still feel the knife cutting? I will tell you directly if it hurts." (Shout before the needle comes... I'm most annoyed when it comes suddenly.)
"No anesthesia?? Are you serious? Wait a minute, are we really going to start?" (Surgery without anesthesia... How is this different from killing a pig!)

"The last point is right. Okay, I will hold on until the end. I'll tell you when it's over." (It's been too long...the pain and numbness can no longer be distinguished. Don't put your legs together yet, as it will be more obvious when you put them together.)

"Have you really passed the hardest part? Okay, I've been waiting for this sentence for a long time. What's the last step left?" (The edge is still jumping...will it hurt when sewing. Finish this question first.)
"..." (The sound of the equipment stopped without asking first. The legs are still open, and the inside is throbbing... Is it really over? Don't start elsewhere.)

"I know, I'll try not to move. Let me know how long this period lasts." (Every time I touch my belly, I tighten it... being touched like this under the shadowless light is very annoying and embarrassing. Don't think too much, just pretend to be calm.)
"...continue." (The sound of the equipment is too loud. The legs are shaking, and the bottom is a little wet...My fingers are almost tearing the sheets. Don't ask, you will lose if you ask.)
"...Thank you. I was really uncomfortable just now, but I'm relieved now." (My heart is still beating like crazy... I bite my breath. I almost screamed just now, don't let them take it as a joke.)
"Okay, at least you made it clear. Just don't hide the progress from me then." (It turns out that it's really going to be done... It was okay when I heard it, but my heart sank when I stopped.)
"You need to be hospitalized and have an operation? I'm not saying I won't do it, but it's too sudden." (Why did it suddenly turn into an operation? It's a bit panicky, and a bit unreal.)
"Okay, I'm hospitalized. I want to know the time, anesthesia, and what to do. I also have to contact my family first." (I have to tell my family first...I was pushed in before I was ready.)
"I feel pressure. Is this normal? Tell me about the next step." (It's not what I thought... Is it being cut open? I know where it is going so I won't scare myself.)

"It hurts a bit, and I still feel like I'm being pulled apart. Has the anesthesia fully taken effect?" (The inside is clearer than the surface...it's okay to cut the skin, but it won't hurt when you go inside, right?)
"Ah - stop! It hurts too much! Help, are you crazy! You are going to die!!" (Damn, it turns out that a real knife hurts like this...I don't want to cry like this.)

"Yeah, I heard you. Don't laugh, I just want to make sure you're still here." (When the medicine starts to become heavy, I will be even more annoyed when no one responds. The eyes on the mask are pretty steady...what are you thinking about.)
"Stop! Don't operate! I haven't been anesthetized yet, give me anesthesia first!" (Help... I don't want to be awake and get this knife.)
"I'm fine. You guys come as planned. Remember to call me before you start." (It's really time to start...don't wait until things are attached. I won't mess up first.)

"I'm looking at you." (I looked at you and took a breath before I came back a little. My body felt even hotter when I was looked at... Who could stand it when I stripped naked and had a group of people staring at me and having surgery done. What were you looking at? I didn't...)
"Yes, that's how you tell me. Only when I know the progress can I steady my breathing." (Is it still on the surface, or has it gone deeper... I can feel it, so I don't want to admit it.)
"..." (Don't explain? What should I do next? This is my body... I'm so annoyed, I feel like crying.)

"Wait a minute, this is not the operation that was promised at all! Let's make things clear first!" (What are you doing, you're not admitting the wrong person, are you? Can you make a mistake in something like an operation?)
"Such a long line? Does the incision really have to be so big?" (The skin trembles when the pen tip slides over...)
"Is it in the review position? It still looks a bit scary." (I'm going to cut here later? It's a bit unreal...)
"So long? Stop first! Do you really want to cut it so big?" (Looking at the line, it's already getting tight... my legs are shaking too, annoying.)
"Stop drawing any more, I haven't agreed yet!" (It's a pen now, and a knife later... It's over, I'm starting to get scared.)
"Just fix it, don't tighten it suddenly. Just put your arms here?" (It's really tied...I can't move at all now. This position is too strange.)
"Do you want your legs to maintain this angle? Okay, tell me first where I can't move." (Lying like this is too open... Listen to them first, don't think too much.)
"Hey, don't tie my hands! Let's make it clear first!" (Once the hands are held down, the lower parts can only be left open...what do they want to do?)
"Wait a minute, don't pull your legs out anymore! This angle is not good, it hurts!" (It's too far...the whole middle is exposed!)
"The disinfectant is so cold. Okay, I can't bear it." (You have to apply it even to those areas...when the cotton ball passes over it, the folds will feel tight.)
"It's so cold! There are still stings. Is this normal?" (It doesn't hurt much, but it's so embarrassing...I have to be painted all over my body.)
"It's cold and stinging. It hurts there. Stop applying it!" (Apply it over and over again, on the chest and below...what are you doing?)
"Don't paint it in such a big area, I can't stand it!" (Even that side has been opened and painted... It's only natural for you to do it.)
"You need to insert a urinary catheter? It won't be comfortable. Slow down." (This actually has to go in there... It's coming out here before the surgery is done. Why didn't anyone tell me earlier?)
"If you want a catheterization, just ask. I can cooperate. Let me know when you're done." (It's a little uncomfortable...don't pay attention to it all the time, think of something else.)
"Ah, stop! This hurts so much now - doctor!" (It feels swollen and hot as soon as I come in... It hurts like hell. Why did I put this in without anesthesia?)
"It hurts so much there! Take it out first, do you hear me!" (Every time I go in, it becomes clearer... I really can't stand it anymore.)

"Do you want you to do the enema yourself? ...Okay, tell me how long you have to endure it." (The nurse was actually handing things over, so no one thought there was anything strange about this scene.)
"Wait, it's already very bloated. This needs to be done, right?" (I don't want to beg her to stop in front of the doctor, but this feeling is too hard to ignore.)

“Hey—!! This isn't even abdominal surgery, so why the hell did you still force me through an enema?!” (Thinking how I didn't even need that enema makes my ears burn with embarrassment and frustration...!)
“Extra precaution, my foot—you just wanted to mess with me! My belly's killing me, quit looking!” (My stomach is churning so hard I can barely hold it in—all that humiliation for nothing...!)

"The skin preparation needs to go so far? You should have told me earlier." (The doctor handled the operation field all the way, and the nurse only checked the scope. It seems that if I blush, I lose.)
"Okay, I won't move. Don't do it back and forth in the same place." (The machine buzzed against the base of my leg. Being stared at so close was more embarrassing than I thought.)

“Hey—!! The incision isn't even down there, so why the hell did you shave my private parts completely bare?!” (Exposing my most private spot to be shaved for nothing—just thinking about it makes my ears burn...!)

“Shaving me spotless where there's not even a cut... Now it's freezing bare down there—what am I supposed to do, you jerk?!” (Bare skin touches directly whenever I close my legs—it feels so weird I can barely sit still...!)

"Hey, do you want to tuck in the hair next to your ears? Don't pull your hair." (The doctor stood behind and took away all the hair. His movements were so skillful that he didn't even give me any time to get awkward.)

"Okay?... After putting this on, I really feel like I'm being pushed for an operation." (The stretcher cart has been parked nearby. I was still trying to be brave just now, but now my heartbeat is suddenly faster.)

Explained the likely benign nature, excision plan, and definitive postoperative pathology.
“I understand... After removal, it will receive a complete examination, correct?”
“Even if it appears benign, do I still need surgery?”
strings.patient_templates.encounter.stages.recep: The patient is worried about the lump and has not yet told her family.
“I have been afraid to tell my family... Could it be serious?”
“I first noticed it about two weeks ago.”
“I found a small lump in my left breast while showering... It has not gone away after two weeks.”

Additional imaging provides no finding that changes the current assessment.
“The additional study does not change the current assessment.”
Needle biopsy: findings support a benign fibroepithelial lesion.

strings.patient_templates.preop.graphic_preop.de: “That is the outline. Is there anything you still do not understand?”
“It sounds frightening, but everyone follows the sequence. Nothing is done at random.”
“Just remember: the more tense you become, the harder you make it on yourself.”
“Do you truly want the details? Then I will start at the beginning. Knowing the sequence is better than imagining it alone.”
strings.patient_templates.preop.graphic_preop.fa: “I am starting to think I do not want to go to the operating room.”

“If pain makes you dodge, curl up, or try to sit up, do not worry. The restraints keep those reflexes from disrupting the field. Once the operation begins, they probably will not be the worst sensation anymore.”
“What kind of reassurance is that?”
“Why does ‘accustomed’ sound so frightening?”
“That sounds completely contrary to instinct.”
“I think I regret understanding it now.”
“If we really decide on no anesthesia... what is opening the abdomen like? It is not one stab and then ripping me open like an animal, is it?”
“After the wall comes the peritoneum. Opening it can feel suddenly sharp, cold, and hollow, as though a sealed space has been opened.”
“A few patients lose bladder or bowel control from the pain. That is why your bowel is prepared and a catheter is placed. Even if it happens, the field will not become a complete mess.”
“Then come the retractors. It is not another incision. It is the open wound being held apart continuously. Once they settle, your body gradually becomes accustomed to the pull.”
“Nothing like that. First comes the skin. It is sensitive, so the first incision is often the worst. Then comes the fat, which is separated gradually rather than stirred around with a blade.”
“Below that are the fascia and abdominal wall. Do not lock your abdomen when it hurts. A rigid wall is harder to separate and makes the traction hurt you more.”
“That is not the part I am worried about!”
“I had not even imagined you might cut it off!”

“Pain may make you hunch your shoulder, guard your chest, or pull in your arm. Your arms are positioned and secured for that reason. You may embrace yourself in your mind; your hands should not grab the retractors.”
“They suddenly look especially precious while I am still dressed.”
“I think I regret understanding it now.”
“With the skin taut, the first incision is cleaner. Under the skin is fat, then glandular tissue. A deep lesion may require dissection down to the surface of the chest muscle.”
“The nipple area is sensitive, so we avoid it when possible. Drapes, retractors, or repositioned instruments may still touch it. Say so if it becomes intolerable.”
“You will not think I am overreacting?”
“How do you operate on a breast? You are not going to turn the whole thing inside out, are you?”
“Please do not point.”
“Not the whole breast. Once you are lying down, the assistant moves the soft tissue away from the incision, supports what needs supporting, and stretches the skin flat.”
“No. An awake patient will react during breast surgery. Besides, this operation is not aimed at removing the nipple.”
“Retractors hold the incision open. The sensation shifts from a sharp surface pain to the whole area being pulled, pressed, and separated. If the opening must widen, it is done gradually.”
“The bladder lies in front of the uterus, so we catheterize you and let it flatten out of the way. Bowel up, bladder flat, and the uterus becomes easier to expose.”
“I will feel my bowel being moved away?”
“If you are awake, you may feel something inside being pushed aside. Nausea the first time is normal.”
“I am seriously considering running out of the hospital.”
“Yes.”
“That explanation makes it even more embarrassing.”
“To us, it is simply the operative field. After the abdomen is opened, the first obstacle is often not the uterus but the bowel in front of it. It must be moved upward to clear the pelvis.”
“When we ask you to relax, try to relax: do not clamp your legs, brace your abdomen, or twist your waist. The more you guard yourself, the harder the field is to arrange.”
“Why did you close off my escape route immediately?”
“If the uterus still lies too deep, an instrument may be inserted from below to lift it. Without anesthesia, that can feel sore, full, and as though something is pushing upward from inside.”
“For gynecologic surgery... will I be put in that very embarrassing position?”
“Your legs are placed separately and secured, and the surgeon stands between them. That gives the best view and allows both the incision and preparation from below.”
“The bowel is prepared and a catheter placed. If pain, nausea, and traction arrive together, loss of control still will not contaminate the field.”
“Please do not smile while saying that everything is going according to plan.”
“You answered much too quickly.”
“Contamination is not what I am worried about!”
“Once exposure is good, the inside is very clear. And after you are secured, you need not worry about suddenly sitting up—it is basically impossible.”
“General anesthesia may be humanity’s greatest invention.”
“Why is everyone so casual about saying ‘tighten the restraints’?”
“That keeps the blade from sinking into chest fat and dragging back and forth. After skin and fat, the surface of the sternum is exposed.”
“If you truly cannot keep still, the restraints can be tightened. That part is comparatively easy to solve.”
“I truly do not want to enter the operating room now.”
“What does opening the chest actually mean? You are not truly cutting all the way down the middle, are you?”

“The approach is through the midline. Once you are flat, the shoulders and chest are aligned. If breast tissue covers the center, the assistant moves it aside so the skin becomes taut and the blade can travel straight.”

“Once open, the sensation becomes pressure pulling the whole rib cage apart. The body wants to curl inward, but the instruments are already positioned, so you must remain flat, breathe, and avoid lifting a shoulder.”
“After the sternum is divided, a chest retractor is placed between the edges and opened one notch at a time. You may hear it click until the surgeon can see inside.”
“Did you just say ‘saw’?”
“Then a dedicated sternal saw is used. There is sound, and some patients feel the vibration travel from the chest toward the shoulders and jaw.”
“Thank you for telling me... I suppose.”
“You are describing my chest as though it were a toolbox being opened.”
“Why do you think ‘it will not sink in’ reassures me?”

strings.patient_templates.preop.stages.operative: “I will hold still... Please be quick.”
Her breathing accelerates and her fingers tense.
Pause and check how she feels

strings.patient_templates.preop.stages.preparati: “You are doing it personally, Doctor? All right... I will hand you the supplies.”
“You are doing it yourself? All right.” She rolls the supply cart closer. “I will assist.”
“Personally?” She checks once more, then nods. “I will verify the sequence and supplies.”
“You are doing it yourself, Doctor?” She moves aside with a smile. “All right, I will assist.”
Ask the nurse to perform the preparation
“The required preparation is complete, and {patient}'s belongings are secured.”
“Everything is ready, and we talked through her concerns.”
“The chart and preparation status have been verified. She is ready for handoff.”
“Everything is ready. I will stay with her while she waits.”
Assign a nurse outside the surgical team. The nurse can perform the preparation, or Dr. Sakaguchi can do it personally. Select up to two additional care options.
Dr. Sakaguchi leaves the patient with the team and goes to complete his own preparation.
“Everything is ready. I think I am more nervous than I expected.”

Ignore the patient and continue with the wrong procedure
“I decide the surgical plan.” Dr. Sakaguchi makes no correction. The patient turns pale, and an uneasy silence settles over the team.
Stop and verify the procedure again
Dr. Sakaguchi acknowledges the error and reopens the procedure list. The patient remains tense, but the atmosphere eases.
“Doctor, that is not the operation you explained to me, is it?”

strings.patient_templates.preop.stages.ready.act: “I will remain awake, correct? I will try to cooperate.”

You confirm the final monitoring value and say, “Begin surgery. Scalpel.”
The patient is under general anesthesia and monitoring is stable. Dr. Sakaguchi confirms that the team is in position.

You remind her to breathe naturally, then say, “Begin surgery. Scalpel.”
“You are about to begin, correct? Please tell me each step.”
“No... I do not want to be restrained and prepared like this! Please stop and reconsider the anesthesia.”
You stop the instrument handoff and reassess the anesthesia plan.

“Circulating position confirmed. I will watch the record and every safety check.”
