"Your identity must reflect your actual qualifications. You're coming to work, not to play at being a nurse."
"But will anyone really need me running errands around the hospital?"
"You've been a patient. You should remember how busy the nurses were before your operation."
[Mizuho recalls the staff repeatedly checking things and preparing equipment around her before she went onto the operating table.]
"I was so busy being scared that I really didn't have time to notice how much they were doing."
"Once you're on the other side, you'll see."
"I'm glad. But remember, work also means responsibility."
"Don't worry! If I choose to do it, I'll do it properly!"
[Asuka places the temporary employment information before Mizuho but does not immediately ask her to sign.]
"There's one more thing I'd like to remind you of before you decide."
"...What? Didn't I just promise to work seriously?"
"That's one part. The other is getting along with your colleagues."
"Once you work at the hospital, you can't put on the airs of a rich young lady."
"Huh? Director, why are you suddenly saying that?"
"I'm easy to get along with! I had a great time chatting with all the nurses during my stay!"
"I know. You like the staff here, and they took good care of you."
"Because before, you were a patient. Now you're preparing to work alongside them."
"Do you remember what you said when you first heard the surgery quote?"
"You said the cost was about one month's spending money for you."
"The hospital has doctors from comfortable backgrounds, and nurses who live on their wages and carefully plan every expense."
"An amount that means little to you might take a colleague months of hard work to save."
"If you casually say, 'It's only that much,' the person hearing it might not think you're joking."
"But I'm not looking down on them!"
"I really do think the nurses are amazing! Especially on the day of my operation. Everything they did was so practiced."
"It's precisely because you admire them that I'd like you to think about how your words might make them feel."
[Mizuho looks down at the bill in her hands.]
"...So if I think something's cheap, I shouldn't just say it in front of people?"
"At least at work, there's no need to measure other people's lives by your own spending standards."
"You can think that. Not every thought needs to become the shared standard for everyone's conversation."
"Many people haven't been as fortunate as we have."
[Asuka's voice remains calm. Mizuho looks at her and listens carefully.]
"...Director. Are you talking about yourself too?"
"Yes. I need to remember that too."
"Then what if a colleague asks why I came to work at the hospital?"
"The truth? Aren't I supposed to pretend my family is ordinary?"
"When did I ask you to pretend?"
"You have an outstanding medical bill, and you're addressing it through an employment contract with the hospital. That's the truth."
"That's all. You don't need to invent stories if someone asks about your family either. There's simply no need to volunteer your allowance and family assets to every colleague."
"It's... just because something seems easy to me, I shouldn't assume it should be easy for everyone else?"
"I used to be a patient here, and the nurses looked after me. I can't keep acting like, 'I paid, so hurry up and help me.'"
"And right now, I'll be the one who knows the least about doing the job..."
[Mizuho scratches her head, a little embarrassed.]
"But if I accidentally let something slip, don't fire me right away!"
"Learn to listen when someone points it out, and correct yourself."
"...Hehe. I think I can manage that."
[Asuka pushes the contract and job description toward Mizuho.]
"One final confirmation. Do you voluntarily accept three months of temporary nursing support work?"
"You'll need to work regularly, follow ward and operating-room arrangements, and take guidance from qualified personnel."
"Then read it carefully before you sign."
[Mizuho picks up the contract and reads it carefully.]
"I used to think that as long as I could afford it, lots of things could be done the way I liked."
"And this time you've found that isn't entirely true?"
"Something like that. But I chose this operation, so I should take responsibility for the bill too."
"...And working at Hoshimi doesn't seem like such a bad thing."
"It may be busier than you imagine."
"Even better! I've got time right now anyway!"
[Mizuho finishes reading the contract and signs her name.]
"So this time I can finally watch the doctors work without lying on the operating table?"
"...Start with the things you can do."
[Later that day, Mizuho brings her signed employment papers to Chihaya's home. Chihaya is organizing the paperwork they need to finish before going to New York.]
"Mizuho? Didn't you say you were going to Hoshimi to see Director Shiromiya today?"
"I did! And it's pretty much sorted out!"
"Really? Your dad agreed to unfreeze the account?"
"Huh? Then how did you sort it out?"
[Mizuho puts the hospital's temporary employment information on the table.]
"...Temporary nursing support staff at Hoshimi Hospital?"
"That's right! Director Shiromiya says if I work properly for three months, the remaining half of the surgery bill can be handled through employee benefits!"
"...Wait. You mean you're going to work at the hospital?"
"...Mizuho, didn't you say you never wanted to go into an operating room again?"
"I meant I didn't want to lie on the operating table again! This time I'll be the one working beside it!"
"I think it's great. I have the time anyway, and staying home all day is boring."
[Chihaya leafs through the job description, her gaze stopping at the contract period.]
"Did your dad really cut off all the money you normally use?"
"I can't use the spending account. Everything else at home is still there. We didn't suddenly go bankrupt!"
"I know that. But your operation was really expensive."
"I know! I've paid the first half, and the rest will be sorted out when I finish the work."
"...You don't have to worry about this alone."
"What if I lend you the money for now? Then you could pay the rest."
"I can afford it right now. You can pay me back when you have access to your money again."
"The operation was my decision. I want to take care of what I did myself. You don't need to pay this for me."
[Chihaya looks at her and slowly puts the papers back on the table.]
"Besides, don't you think being a nurse at Hoshimi for a few months sounds fun?"
"We'd get to see Dr. Sakaguchi, Dr. Misono, and all those nurses again!"
"Last time I was too busy screaming on the table. Now I can finally see what they actually do all day!"
"You're not really treating nursing work like a dress-up game, are you?"
"Of course not! The director gave me lots of instructions. Work seriously, don't touch things without permission, and listen to the experienced staff."
"...And you actually agreed to all of it?"
[Mizuho pouts, then happily opens the uniform collection instructions.]
"Look! We can wear Hoshimi's white nurse uniform!"
"Don't get caught up thinking only about the clothes."
[Chihaya looks at the three-month work arrangement and falls silent for a while.]
"Wait, you don't owe any surgery fees. Why would you come?"
"You even had your abdomen opened to stay with me. Now that something's happened to you, I can't leave you on your own."
[Mizuho stares at her, mouth open, for quite a while.]
"...You make my operation sound like some great heroic deed."
"Wasn't it? Though I still can't understand why you chose no anesthesia!"
"...Hahaha. That was one of my classic bad decisions."
"But Chihaya, you really don't need to work for my sake. I can handle it alone!"
"I know you can. But wouldn't it be more fun with two of us?"
"We stayed in the hospital together and left together. So let's go to work together too."
"...Oh! You should've just said you wanted to wear a nurse uniform too!"
"Okay, okay. Then let's go ask the director!"
[They gather the papers and return together to Hoshimi Hospital to ask about available work.]
[In the director's office, Asuka listens to Chihaya's request and places another job description in front of her.]
"Ms. Kuramoto, you'd also like to apply for three months of temporary nursing support work?"
"Yes. I'd like to work with Mizuho."
"You don't have the same medical bill problem. You don't need to take on her contractual obligations."
"I know. I want to come of my own accord."
"I told her that too! But she wants to be with me!"
"But if you apply, the job requirements will be the same as Ms. Shite's. Being friends doesn't mean you can pick only the tasks you like."
"Then we'll arrange for your contracts to begin on the same day. Before you start working, someone will guide you through registration and your role orientation."
"Great! We're going to be nurses together!"
[Smiling at their excitement, Asuka hands them the onboarding papers.]
[Before their first day, they complete registration and basic role orientation as arranged.]

[The staff changing area at Hoshimi Hospital. Both have changed into pure white Japanese-style nurse dresses and caps and are straightening their collars and cuffs. Their uniforms have no official nurse name badges.]
[Mizuho turns around and looks at herself in the mirror.]
"But that's the third time you've asked already."
[Chihaya also looks down at her own uniform and gently straightens the skirt.]
"Last month I was still wearing patient clothes, waiting in bed for a nurse to change my dressing."
"Then I wore scrubs and sat in the operating room to keep you company."
"And you really looked like an old hand that time!"
"Now it's different! We're here to help!"
"Yeah... But I'm still a little nervous."
"What's there to fear? We're not here for surgery."
[They look at each other and can't help laughing.]
"Are you both ready? I'm here to take you to the work area."
[They leave the changing area. In her usual nurse uniform, Asakura looks over the two newcomers.]
"They suit you very well. Welcome back, Ms. Shite, Ms. Kuramoto."
"Thank you! But when you call us that, I feel like I'm still a patient."
"Then you'll have to get used to hearing your names without it necessarily meaning you're being called for an examination."
[Asakura gives them the day's support-work assignments.]
"We'll start with ordinary ward preparation and supply handovers. You'll learn alongside qualified nurses."
"Got it! Is there anything we can help with?"
"Of course. First organize these boxes of spare supplies by their markings, then take them to the designated work positions."
[Mizuho picks up a box and is about to walk away when Asakura stops her.]
"Ms. Shite, check the number first. That box belongs to the other group."
"I thought if the boxes looked the same, the contents would be the same!"
"Many things in a hospital look similar. That's why we check carefully."
[Mizuho puts the box back on the table and looks down to check again.]
"...Okay. This is number three, that one's number two..."
"Found it. This is the one we need to deliver."
"Darn it! You're already ahead of me on our first day!"
"There's no need to compete. Just make sure it's correct."
"Also, don't handle medical records, medication, or sterile instruments however you please. If you don't understand something, ask the nurse supervising you immediately."
"For today, start by organizing these light supplies. We'll arrange other tasks once you know your way around the work areas."
"It's finally our turn to prepare things for other people."
"Before, we were always lying in bed waiting for someone to prepare things for us."
"Then this time, please take good care of the next patient too."
[Asakura returns to the nurses' station to arrange other work. Chihaya and Mizuho check the supplies and walk slowly toward the work area.]
[At the other end of the corridor, Serika Misono, in her radiology white coat, has just finished a consultation and is about to pass by.]
[Serika turns and pauses at the sight of them in white nurse uniforms.]
"Long time no see! We're not back as patients this time!"
"Right! We're officially starting work at Hoshimi today! Three months as temporary nursing assistants!"
"We'll get to see you at the hospital again!"
"Ask the nurse guiding you if you have questions. Don't overdo it."
[Serika nods and continues toward radiology. As nine o'clock approaches, the two carry their supplies toward the work area beside the nurses' station.]
[The scene returns to the ward corridor at nine on the morning of the event. Mizuho and Chihaya stand before Sakaguchi in their white nurse uniforms.]
[Mizuho has finished explaining what happened. Sakaguchi is silent for a moment.]
"...So you both signed three-month temporary employment contracts."
"And you chose to join of your own accord too, Ms. Kuramoto?"
"...Now I understand why you're dressed like this."
"Hahaha! Your face just now was so funny!"
"I simply didn't expect two people who were in the ward last month to turn up here for work today."
"Your recovery has been checked, hasn't it? You're able to do this support work normally now?"
"Yes. We've both had our follow-ups as instructed. We're starting with light work today."
"Nurse Asakura specifically reminded me not to rush to carry heavy things!"
"She picked up the wrong supply box earlier."
"I think you'll both get used to things here quickly."
"But remember first: ward preparation and circulating support each have specific duties. Wearing a nurse uniform doesn't mean you can touch surgical instruments whenever you like."
"The director told us! Now I even have to check labels on instrument boxes first!"
"It sounds like Nurse Asakura has already started showing you the ropes."
"Oh, and we ran into Dr. Misono earlier!"
"The moment she heard we'd come back as nurses, she guessed it was Director Shiromiya's idea!"
"Then she let out such a big sigh!"
"Right? Dr. Misono always gets straight to the point."
"Speaking of which, do you think going back into the operating room will feel different now?"
[Chihaya thinks for a moment and adjusts her nurse cap.]
"For my third operation, I walked in myself, but seeing the operating table still made me incredibly nervous."
"Then when I accompanied Mizuho, I sat beside her and watched everyone work. That felt different again."
"Now it's our turn to help prepare other people for the table!"
"Start by doing the ordinary work properly. Follow the experienced nurses when you go into the operating room too."
"...But if someone suddenly says, 'Ms. Kuramoto, please get onto the operating table,' I might still shiver."
"Haha! Then I'll stand beside her and say, 'Don't worry, the nurses are all professionals!'"
"...You said that before your operation too."
"And then I learned it really was scary!"
"I admit it! Scary or not, didn't my operation turn out fine?"
[Mizuho winks at Chihaya, then turns to Sakaguchi.]
"When we run into you at the hospital now, does that make us colleagues?"
"Then I look forward to working with you!"
[Mizuho bows slightly to Sakaguchi, then raises her head with a smile.]
"Me too. I look forward to working with you!"
"Ms. Shite, Ms. Kuramoto! Please bring that batch of supplies we checked over here!"
[They are about to run when Chihaya stops first and looks back at Mizuho.]
[They switch to a brisk walk toward the nurses' station, checking the labels on their supplies again as they go.]
[Sakaguchi stands in the corridor, watching them join the busy nurses' station.]
"Anything really can happen at Hoshimi Hospital."
[Sakaguchi puts away his work records and continues the day's work.]

"Chihaya reminded me again today not to take on everyone else's tasks at once."
"Chihaya reminded me again today not to take on everyone else's tasks at once."
"A little. Other people used to organize my schedule. Now I have to coordinate with everyone."
"Yeah. And working with all these nurses really is fun!"
"Wow, what lovely sunshine! I'd love to go swimming on a day off."
"Wow, what lovely sunshine! I'd love to go swimming on a day off."
"Of course! I'm even thinking of changing swimsuits next time to get different tan lines."
"Don't get so caught up in tanning that you forget to rest."
"You even give reminders about that, Doctor? Hehe, then we'll bring Chihaya next time, and you should come too!"
"I've noticed that when I enter the operating room in a nurse uniform, I'm brave enough to speak loudly to everyone."
"I've noticed that when I enter the operating room in a nurse uniform, I'm brave enough to speak loudly to everyone."
"Different from lying on the table yourself?"
"Completely! Once that surgical lamp shines on me, my courage just stops listening."
"Hehe. After learning the hard way, I should at least admit it."
"Work here is harder than you expected, isn't it?"
"Work here is harder than you expected, isn't it?"
"It is! I never knew the nurses did so many things in a day."
"Of course not! I've met so many people. Even after we go to New York, Chihaya and I will keep talking about these days."
strings.collections.time_events.work_chat_guest_: "Dr. Sakaguchi! What needs doing today? Errands, delivering forms, finding people—I'm ready!"
"I've delivered the handover form! ...Though I'll need someone to teach me the abbreviations again."
"Chihaya says enthusiasm alone won't get you through work at the nurses' station. I know! I am reading the records properly!"
"Someone asked why I came to work at Hoshimi. I told the truth: at first it was to pay my medical bill, but working with everyone turned out to be pretty interesting!"
"Hm? Read the labels before taking supplies? Of course! I never used to realize hospitals had several specifications for even the same kind of item."
"I'm delivering supplies to two floors today. It's a decent workout, and at least it's more interesting than lying in a hospital bed!"
strings.collections.special_event_steps.serika_l: At eleven at night, only the rows of lights at the nurses' station still illuminated the hospital corridor. Returning from his ward rounds, Sakaguchi pushed open the lounge door.
Serika Misono sat by the window, looking at a cup of cold coffee on the table. Only when she heard the door open did she raise her eyes.
“Dr. Misono? You're still here this late?”
“No. I've finished my work in radiology.”
She turned her paper cup halfway around, then stopped.
“At least there are people here. There's nothing wrong with staying a little longer.”
“Using the hospital to pass the time? That doesn't sound like the person you used to be.”
“You didn't seem like someone who would spend an entire afternoon visiting music shops with someone either.”
“…How long are you going to keep bringing that up?”
“Until you can pick out the bass.”
The corners of her mouth moved slightly before she turned back to the window.
“Your coffee's cold. Shall I get you another?”
“Even the doctor on duty is allowed to drink coffee.”
Sakaguchi walked toward the kettle. He had just picked up a paper cup when the pager in his pocket suddenly lit up.
The screen showed only two lines: Emergency admission. Female, severe bleeding, impaired consciousness. Surgery team, attend immediately.
“Heavy bleeding. I need to go down and have a look.”
Sakaguchi had already turned away. Behind him came the soft scrape of a chair sliding back.
“Finishing my work in radiology doesn't mean I can't help now.”
She picked up the pen from her white coat pocket, fastened her coat again, and was already at the door.
“All right. Let's see the patient first.”
They headed for the elevator, one behind the other. The empty paper cup he had just taken out remained beside the kettle in the lounge.
The emergency room doors stood wide open. Two nurses were wheeling a stretcher into the resuscitation bay.
“An adult woman. A passerby found her in an open area outside town. She was already unresponsive when the ambulance arrived. No identification was found.”

The patient lay beneath a thick blanket, her face pale and her hair plastered to her forehead. The dressing at one side of the bed was soaked through with blood, and a nurse was still applying pressure to control the bleeding.
“Seventy-eight over forty-six, heart rate one hundred thirty-two. Two IV lines are in place. The blood request has been sent.”
“Notify the blood bank and prepare to transfuse. Continue fluids and monitor her consciousness. Keep her warm.”
A nurse replaced the patient's blanket with a clean, warm one. The numbers on the monitor remained unstable.
“In grass beside the road. The person who found her said she had no clothes or belongings.”
Serika said nothing. Sakaguchi leaned over to assess the patient's breathing, pupils, and abdominal signs, then examined the injury where temporary bleeding control was already in place.
“There's too much bleeding from below. We need to rule out deep abdominal and pelvic injuries first.”
Serika placed the ultrasound probe against the patient's abdomen. The gray-white image on the screen shifted with the probe.
“There's an abnormal collection of fluid in the pelvis. The tissue contours on the right are unclear too… This may be more than a superficial laceration.”
“All I can say now is that it's highly suspicious. Her circulation won't let us wait for a full workup.”
Sakaguchi gave the nurse instructions for transfusion and continuous monitoring, then reassessed the bleeding at the injury.
“Pressure is only reducing the bleeding temporarily. We have to locate the deep source.”
Serika returned the probe to its holder and was about to report her other findings. Suddenly, she stopped.
She took a step toward the head of the bed, her eyes settling on the patient's profile.
Serika's hand remained suspended in midair. Her face had grown paler.
The patient did not respond. Only the heart-rate numbers on the monitor kept changing.
Serika parted her lips. A moment passed before any sound came out.
“A former colleague. At my previous hospital…”
“She was my scrub nurse when I operated.”
She stared at Nanami, her gaze fixed rigidly in place.
“Doctor, her blood pressure still isn't coming up.”
“She's our patient now. Go and sit down for a moment. I'll take over from here.”
“You don't have to push yourself. You know who she is. It's natural to be shaken.”
Serika lowered her head and clasped her hands tightly together.
She walked to the sink, rinsed her fingers with cold water, and looked up at the mirror. A moment later, she returned to Sakaguchi.
“I know what state I'm in. If you think I'm unfit, I'll step aside.”
“But if you still need an assistant… please let me stay.”
Sakaguchi looked at her. This time, Serika did not look away.
“All right. But I'll judge how you're doing. If necessary, I'll have you step away.”
Sakaguchi turned toward the nursing desk.

“Ange, notify the OR to prepare for an emergency exploratory laparotomy. We need two scrub nurses and two circulating nurses; the circulating nurses will handle monitoring. Dr. Misono and I will go and prepare.”
“Understood. I'll contact the OR, keep watch over the transfusion, and wait for them to collect the patient.”
Serika looked back at Nanami and reached out to tuck the slipped corner of the blanket back over her.

Nanami was transferred onto the operating table. Satsuki Orikawa checked the ECG and blood-pressure equipment at the circulating nurse's monitoring position, while Shiori Yoneda verified the transfusion line nearby. Itsumi Sonoda and Rumi Iwasaki donned sterile gowns and prepared the instrument table.
“Anesthesia preparation and airway protection are complete. Her circulation is very unstable, and the transfusion is continuing. I'll handle monitoring and report any change immediately.”
“Good. You manage her circulation. I'll control the bleeding as quickly as possible.”
After helping confirm the deep injuries and imaging findings before surgery, Serika returned to Sakaguchi's side. She had committed the extent of the damage she had seen to memory.

“The damage is deep. Its shape suggests penetration by a hard foreign object, not an ordinary mucosal tear. It also involves the side of the cervix. We'll have to wait until she wakes to learn what happened.”
“The bleeding won't stop, and there's blood in the abdomen. I'll open her abdomen to find the source.”
“I'll help identify the injuries to the uterus and surrounding structures, and adjust the field as you direct.”
Serika had scrubbed and was waiting outside the sterile area. Shiori Yoneda, the second circulating nurse, helped her into a sterile gown and tied the straps behind her.
She slipped her hands into sterile gloves. Halfway into the first glove, her fingertips paused briefly.
She pulled the glove into place and approached the operating table. Beyond the sterile drapes, Nanami's face was out of sight.
The surgical team verified the patient's temporary identity, emergency indications, planned procedure, blood supply, and everyone's responsibilities, confirming that all was correct.
After making the lower abdominal incision, Sakaguchi entered the abdomen layer by layer. Suction removed the pooled blood, gradually revealing the deep pelvis.
“On the right. The hematoma ends here. Don't pull on that layer yet.”
“I see it. Suction, and raise the field a little.”
Serika adjusted the retractor, avoiding visibly congested tissue. Itsumi Sonoda passed a hemostatic instrument into Sakaguchi's hand.
“Hemostat. Suction is beside your right hand.”
“The tear runs from deep in the vagina to the side of the cervix. The outer part of the lower uterine segment is injured too. An adjacent vascular branch is torn, and blood keeps seeping deeper.”
“So even with external pressure, she's still bleeding inside.”
“The transfusion is continuing. Her blood pressure is barely holding, but we can't wait much longer.”
Sakaguchi clamped the bleeding vascular branch while Serika stabilized the tissue beside it. When suction moved away, they could finally see clearly into the wound.
“The uterine body still has a blood supply. The damage is concentrated in the lower segment and to the side.”
“The cervix and deep vaginal injury need layered repair too. We can't just close the part visible from outside.”
“Yes. The internal wound has to be addressed as well.”
Sakaguchi attempted to treat a deeper bleeding point, but the tissue was extremely fragile. Seeping blood obscured the view they had just gained.
“Continue transfusion. Dr. Misono, help me hold this steady.”
“The additional blood unit has been checked and is being connected. I'll keep recording the transfused volume.”
Serika moved swiftly and precisely. She left the bleeding point Sakaguchi was treating untouched, gently moving aside only the adjacent tissue that obstructed his view.
“This tear is deeper than we thought before surgery.”
“If both sides keep bleeding, repairing the lower uterine segment will get increasingly difficult.”
Sakaguchi glanced at the monitor, then back at the bleeding that had yet to stop.
“If local hemostasis and repair both fail, we'll have to prepare for a hysterectomy. That's the last option to save her life.”
Serika's grip on the retractor tightened slightly.
“Yes. The tissue here isn't all necrotic. We can address the lateral bleeding points separately, and there are still edges we can suture in the lower uterine tear.”
“But the field is very narrow. Further laterally, we also have to avoid the ureter.”
“I know. I'd like to dissect along the intact tissue planes first, identify the ureter and vessels, and then attempt repair.”
Sakaguchi did not reply immediately. He reassessed the tissue color and the extent of the oozing.
“…There's a chance. At least from what we can see now, removal isn't our only option yet.”
“Her life comes first. If we can't control the bleeding, we can't keep taking risks.”
“I understand. If it won't stop, I won't oppose switching to a hysterectomy.”
Serika glanced at the patient's head beyond the drapes. Nanami remained asleep, unable to hear their discussion.
“But she's still alive. Whatever we can preserve… I want to preserve as much as we can for her.”
Sakaguchi examined the intact tissue remaining at both ends of the tear, then looked up at Serika.
“Find a safe plane and the main bleeding points first, then repair the deep tear layer by layer. I can help with this part of the lower uterus.”
“All right. Dr. Misono, let's try your approach. One step at a time. If I think the risk is too high at any point, we stop immediately.”
“Fine forceps, a needle holder, and fine sutures are ready. Just say when you need them.”
Serika switched to finer instruments. Slowing down, she first identified the intact tissue boundary, then gently separated the two closely apposed layers.
“Spare instruments of the same specifications are laid out too, and the gauze has been replenished.”
The instrument was placed in Serika's palm. Her hand did not tremble, and her eyes never left the operative field.
“Here. The vascular branch comes in from this side. It isn't the one we thought earlier.”
“I see it. I'll ligate the bleeding point. Keep the field open.”
Sakaguchi secured the critical bleeding point. When suction moved away again, fresh blood no longer immediately flooded the surgical field.
“The next blood unit is connected. Blood usage and fluid balance are being recorded.”
“She still needs more blood, but her pressure is starting to rise.”
“We can see the deep tear clearly now. Continue the repair.”

Sakaguchi first treated the cervical and deep vaginal injuries. Serika assisted with retraction and identifying the boundaries, then repaired the lower uterine tear with Sakaguchi's confirmation. Itsumi handled the primary fine-instrument exchanges while Rumi assisted with counts and replenishing instruments.
“The next set of sutures is ready. I'm keeping track of the count.”
“One more stitch here. Don't pull too tightly.”
“Right. Let the edges come together naturally.”
Serika tied the knot and released the needle holder. Sakaguchi checked the tension at the repair and assessed the surrounding tissue's blood supply.
“No new active bleeding at present. The blood supply to the uterus and surrounding tissue has been preserved.”
“Her vital signs are more stable now. We can continue monitoring.”
Sakaguchi and Serika checked the pelvis, repaired areas, bladder, and adjacent structures once more, confirming no overlooked bleeding points or obvious associated injuries.
“Starting the final count. I'll verify the needles and instruments.”
“They match the circulating record. Gauze, needles, and instruments all accounted for.”
After closing the incision and completing the instrument count, the operation was finally over. Nanami was taken to a monitored ward for continued observation.
Serika stood still, looking down at the gloves she had just removed. She reached to drop them into the waste bin, but fumbled them on the first try.
Serika leaned against the wall behind her, her knees buckling slightly. Sakaguchi immediately stepped forward to support her.
“No need to apologize. Sit down for a while.”
She did not finish, only shook her head hard.
“Nanami's bleeding has stopped. She still needs monitoring, but she's past the most dangerous part.”
At last, Serika lowered her head. After a long while, she gave an almost inaudible reply.
At daybreak, Serika was still sitting on the bench outside the monitored ward. She held a hot drink from the hospital vending machine without opening it.
Sakaguchi emerged from the ward, carrying the handover notes he had just completed.
“She's stable now, and the anesthetic is gradually wearing off. We need to keep monitoring for bleeding, infection, and other injuries.”
“Preserved. There's no new bleeding at the repair for now. I'll keep following her postoperative examinations.”
Serika's grip on the can loosened a little.
“I should thank you. Without those judgments of yours, the operation would have been harder.”
“Don't say that yet. She hasn't woken up.”
“Right. Once she's fully conscious, we'll explain everything to her.”
Serika lowered her head and finally opened the drink. A little steam rose from the opening.
Serika took out her phone and dialed a familiar number. When the call connected, she did not speak immediately.
“Nanami Horiuchi. She was brought in late last night.”
The other end of the line fell silent for a long while.
“I'll visit her today. Get some rest first. Don't try to bear it all alone.”
After hanging up, Serika glanced at Sakaguchi.
“You don't have to keep standing so straight once the operation's over.”
Serika looked at him, then slowly nodded after a few seconds.
“I've handed everything over to the next shift. Let me take you home.”
“I've handed over now. We both need rest.”
They each changed back into their everyday clothes and left the hospital. Commuters were already on the streets, and a breakfast shop had just raised its shutters.
“It feels as though hardly any time has passed. But it's already morning outside.”
Sakaguchi walked her to her door. Serika found her keys in her bag, then paused.
“Thank you… for walking me home today.”
“Get some sleep first. I'll tell you when Nanami wakes up.”
She opened the door and glanced back before going inside. Sakaguchi was still standing where she had left him.
The door closed softly. Sakaguchi remained outside for a moment before turning to leave.
The following morning, Sakaguchi came to the ward. Before he reached the door, he saw two people standing beside it.
Serika stood very straight, though she held no chart. Miyuki Asakura stood beside her, quietly confirming visiting hours with a nurse.
“Dr. Sakaguchi. The nurse says she's awake and can speak a little.”
“You may. But don't tire her out. Anything else can wait for another day.”
The three entered the room. Nanami rested partly upright against her pillows. Hearing footsteps, she slowly turned her face.
“I'm Sakaguchi. I operated on you in the early hours yesterday. This is Hoshimi Hospital. You're safe now.”
Nanami blinked. Her gaze passed Sakaguchi and settled on Serika's face.
Nanami's eyes immediately reddened. She tried to push herself up, then stopped when it pulled at her wound.
“Don't get up. Your abdominal incision needs time to heal.”
Asakura approached the bed and gently adjusted the pillows so Nanami could rest back comfortably.
“You don't need to finish that now. Look, we're all here.”
“You lost a lot of blood and had severe pelvic injuries. We explored your abdomen, stopped the bleeding, and repaired the damage. Your vital signs are stable now.”
“We didn't perform a hysterectomy. We repaired the damaged areas as well as we could. We'll keep checking how they heal.”
Nanami looked at Sakaguchi, then at Serika. Tears ran down her cheeks.
Nanami closed her eyes and took several slow breaths before speaking again.
The color slowly drained from Serika's face. Asakura said nothing.
“He wouldn't let me leave. Then… he hurt me. I remember begging him to stop before I passed out.”
“When I woke up again… I was here. I don't know where he left me.”
“You don't need to remember the details now. We've treated your injuries, and we'll keep the medical records safe.”
“They're still there. He won't let them go. He forces them to do things they don't want to… Before I got out, none of them had been able to leave.”
Serika rested her hand on the edge of the bed, avoiding Nanami's lines.
“When I left… they were all alive.”
Serika raised her other hand to cover her eyes.
“Miss Nanami, you can decide when to tell this, and to whom. For now, rest and continued treatment matter most.”
“All right. I'll ask the duty supervisor to contact them now. You don't have to recount everything today, but those three may still be in danger. We can't wait.”
“I know the old hospital's address and layout. I can provide them if needed.”
“I'll contact the duty supervisor. Let's get this formally reported first.”
Nanami nodded. Asakura brought the tissues from beside the bed and placed them within her reach.
“We'll step outside for a while, then. If you want to see us, just ask a nurse to call us.”
Nanami watched her for a moment, then finally released the blanket corner she had been gripping.

After leaving the room, Asakura immediately contacted the hospital's duty supervisor and asked them to reach the police. She explained that Nanami had asked to report the crime, and supplied the names of the three other nurses who might still be trapped, along with the old hospital's address.
That afternoon, Serika and Asakura returned to the room. Nanami was awake, watching the light by the window.
“…I've been thinking. There's something I can't keep leaving unsaid.”
“If you're tired, you can tell us next time.”
Nanami turned toward her, tears welling up again.
“Dr. Serika… The things I did back at the hospital…”
“I knew how much you were suffering, but I still took his side. I've owed you an apology all this time.”
“I know. I wouldn't dare ask you to.”
Serika lowered her eyes. A long time passed before she looked up.
“…Back then, there was a lot I didn't dare face either.”
“But that doesn't mean the things you did never happened.”
Nanami reached out. Serika hesitated, then gently took her hand.
“Thank you… for still being willing to save me.”
“You're a patient. At the operating table, I did what I should.”
Her voice remained calm, but she did not immediately let go of Nanami's hand.
“…There's one more thing. I know it's selfish to say this now.”
“Could you go back once? To see your father.”
“That hospital was supposed to be yours. You can operate, and you care for people. It needs someone who can truly make decisions.”
“I'm not asking you to go back and clean up our mess now. It's just… I used to think everything would be different once you returned.”
Asakura took a step forward, stopping where Nanami could see her.
“Nanami. Let's leave it there for now.”
“Serika has heard what you wanted her to hear. But some things don't need an answer today.”
“I'll think about it. For now, put it out of your mind.”
Asakura smoothed Nanami's blanket. Serika slowly released her hand and stood up.
“Press the bell if you need anything. A nurse will come, and I'll visit too.”
Outside the room, Asakura and Serika stopped beside the automatic doors. The glass reflected their figures in white work clothes.
“I didn't do anything. Just helped her stop talking.”
Asakura looked at her. This time, she did not immediately make a joke.
“Back then, too… you were the one who finally got me out.”
“But sometimes I remember the things you did to me at the beginning. I know I'm conflicted.”
“I did things I shouldn't have. Getting you out afterward wasn't meant to make you owe me gratitude.”
“We're both at Hoshimi now. Someday we can talk properly. But we don't have to say everything today.”
Serika looked toward the end of the corridor and remained silent for a long while.
“…All right. Let's leave it here today.”
Asakura gave her a small smile and turned toward the nurses' station. Serika stayed where she was until the ward doors had closed behind her again.
That evening, Sakaguchi finished the last chart and prepared to leave the hospital. Near the exit, he saw Serika standing beneath a light.
Serika pulled her bag strap a little higher on her shoulder, but did not immediately look at him.
“Yes. I have no other plans today.”
“Of course. Where would you like to go?”
At last, she raised her eyes to Sakaguchi.
“I don't really want to be alone today.”
They left the hospital. The nighttime streets were especially quiet, and the lights in the roadside shops were going out one after another.
“Did you talk with Miss Asakura this afternoon?”
“We didn't argue. We didn't hug and say the past was all forgiven either.”
“She said that too. Sometimes you're rather alike.”
After saying it, Serika could not bring herself to smile. She only pulled her coat collar a little closer.
“…After Nanami fell asleep, I kept thinking about what she'd said.”
“I don't know what will happen to those people. And I don't know whether I should go back.”
Serika opened her door and neatly placed her shoes to one side. Sakaguchi followed her inside, gently closing the door behind him.
“Have a seat. I'll get some water.”
She stood in the middle of the living room, as though she had suddenly forgotten what she was about to do.
“…Dr. Misono. Would you like to sit down first?”
Serika sat at one end of the sofa. Sakaguchi placed a glass of water before her and sat at the other end.
“…I thought I wasn't that frightened anymore.”
She stared at the rim of the glass, her breathing growing faster. Tears fell one by one onto the backs of her clenched hands.
“I've already left that hospital and started working again…”
“But whenever I hear his name, I still remember those things.”
At last, Serika looked up. She tried to keep her voice steady, but choked as she began to speak.
“In the operating room, I can still pick up instruments. I can still tell you where to suture and where not to touch.”
“But once the operation is over, I can't even stand steadily.”
She lowered her head, her fingers gripping the hem of her clothes.
“I need to know… that man hasn't destroyed me.”
“You don't need to prove that to anyone tonight.”
“You saved Nanami. You can't save everyone in one night. Being afraid doesn't mean you've done anything wrong.”
Serika's lips trembled slightly. At last, she reached out and caught Sakaguchi's sleeve.
“…Then let me cry for a while.”
Sakaguchi moved closer. Serika stopped forcing herself to sit upright and rested her forehead against his shoulder.
At first, she only sobbed quietly. Then she could no longer hold back the sound. Sakaguchi held her as she cried for a long time.
“…I'm sorry. I've got your clothes wet.”
Serika gave a very soft laugh against his shoulder, then quickly sniffled again.
“…How can you say something like that at a time like this?”
After crying, Serika did not immediately leave his embrace. She lifted her face, her eyes slightly red.
“I can stay. If you want to rest, I'll sit here with you.”
“…Having someone here isn't all I want.”
She moved a little closer and reached out to touch Sakaguchi's face softly.
“I want to be with you. It's what I want.”
It was the first time Sakaguchi had called her directly by her first name in private. Hearing it, Serika paused.
There were still tears in Serika's eyes, but a very small smile slowly appeared.
Sakaguchi kissed her gently. Serika closed her eyes. The hand clutching his sleeve slowly relaxed, then wrapped around him instead.
They drew a little apart. Serika's face was flushed, but she did not avert her eyes.
“…Stay today. Spend the night with me.”
Serika took Sakaguchi's hand and led him toward the bedroom. The door stood half closed, and the bedside light traced their figures drawing closer.
“…Could you dim the light a little more?”
The light softened. Serika kissed Sakaguchi of her own accord, then rested against his shoulder and let out a quiet breath.
Following her words, Sakaguchi gently drew her into his arms. Through her thin everyday clothes, he could clearly feel that Serika's back was still tense.
“…I'm sorry. I was the one who asked you to stay…”
“Didn't I just say it? There's no hurry. It's all right to lean on me and rest for a while first.”
Serika buried her face against his neck, her warm breath brushing his skin. After a moment, her fingers slowly moved to the buttons at her chest.
“…It's all right. I don't want to stop here.”
She undid the first button, but her fingertips stopped at the second, trembling slightly. Sakaguchi reached out and gently covered the back of her hand.
“Let me. If you're uncomfortable, or suddenly feel afraid, tell me to stop at any time.”

Their clothes slipped away one by one and were draped over the chair beside the bed. When the cool air touched her bare skin, Serika instinctively hunched her shoulders. Her arms started to cover her chest, but she held them back.
Sakaguchi lifted the covers around them both, then leaned down and gently rested his palms against her cool shoulders and back.
“Ah… Sakaguchi-kun, your hands… are so warm.”
“Your skin is too cold. Still shaking?”
“…A little. My body seems… unused to being this unguarded against someone…”
“My mind knows it's you… knows I'm safe here… but my heart is still beating far too fast…”
“Serika, don't analyze yourself like a medical chart. You don't need to stay composed now.”
Sakaguchi lowered his head and kissed her lips, swallowing the rest of her words. At the same time, his warm palm slowly traveled up her slender waist and gently cupped her soft breast.
Serika's breathing instantly faltered. Her eyes were tightly closed, her long lashes trembling intensely, and a small, irrepressible moan escaped through her nose.
“Hah… mm… Sakaguchi-kun… Your fingers, they're too close… It feels so strange…”
As Sakaguchi's patient caresses and kisses moved downward, Serika's stiff body gradually softened, giving way to a flush and moisture rising from deep within her skin.
“Serika… Open your eyes. Look at me.”
Panting, Serika slowly opened her moist eyes. Beneath the dim bedside light, Sakaguchi was the only person in her gaze.
“…Sakaguchi-kun. I'm… all right now. Come… I want to feel you completely.”

Sakaguchi parted her legs and slowly lowered himself, entering her little by little. Though her entrance was already wet, there was still unmistakable unfamiliar tightness and resistance deeper within. As he pressed a little farther, the instant that warm, snug embrace enveloped him, Serika threw her head back and gripped the sheets beneath her tightly.
“Does it hurt? I'll stop for now. Breathe slowly.”

Sakaguchi stayed still at the deepest point, not moving immediately, and lowered his head to kiss the fine sweat from her temple. Serika bit her lower lip tightly. Her chest rose and fell sharply several times before she managed to force out a sound.
“No… It doesn't hurt… I just feel… completely filled inside… It's a little hard to breathe…”
“Wait a moment… Let me… get used to it for a few more seconds… mm…”
“…Mm, all right. You can continue, Sakaguchi-kun.”
At first, her legs still tensed instinctively. After a while, they slowly relaxed under Sakaguchi's patient caresses. He tentatively withdrew a little, then slowly eased inside again.
The moment those broken sounds escaped, Serika seemed startled by her own voice. She hurriedly raised a hand to cover her mouth, blushing all the way to her ears.
“You don't have to hold it in, Serika. It's only the two of us here.”
“B-but… Making sounds like that… is so embarrassing… mm, ah…!”

Sakaguchi took the wrist she held over her mouth and gently drew it down, interlacing their fingers beside the pillow. As their rhythm gradually deepened, Serika could no longer hide the tremor in her breathing.
“Ah, hah… Sakaguchi-kun… You're pressing too deep there… mm, ah… It's so embarrassing… but my body keeps drifting somewhere strange…”
“Look at me, Serika. How does it feel now?”
“So hot… Inside and outside… It's all your warmth, Sakaguchi-kun… hah, mm… I'm not afraid at all… Instead, I feel so safe…”

A tear slipped from the moist corner of her eye, but not from sorrow. She drew one hand back of her own accord and wrapped it tightly around Sakaguchi's neck, pressing her burning cheek beside his ear and awkwardly matching his movements.
“Don't let go… Hold me tighter…! Ah, mm… Sakaguchi-kun, Sakaguchi-kun…! I-I can't… I can't think anymore… I'm, I'm coming—! Aah…!”

With one final, tearful tremor, Serika's whole body tensed to its limit in Sakaguchi's arms. Then, as though all her strength had been spent, she sank softly against his chest, leaving only quick, warm breaths in the aftermath.
After an unknown length of time, a faint light returned to the bedroom. Their clothes hung over the chair, and most of the water in the bedside glass was gone.
Beneath the covers, Serika nestled quietly in Sakaguchi's arms. Their intimacy had passed, and her breathing was slowly settling.
“…I think I kept shaking just now.”
“I'd known for so long that I wanted to be close to you… But when it actually happened, I was still terribly nervous.”
Serika looked up at him, at last showing a trace of her familiar exasperation.
She rested her face against Sakaguchi's shoulder again, her voice very quiet.
“And I don't think tonight has solved everything.”
“It's just… being like this now feels safe.”
She reached out and gently rested her hand against the back of his.
Serika closed her eyes. Before long, her fingers relaxed, and she fell quietly asleep in Sakaguchi's arms.
Sakaguchi tucked the covers around her. Distant car lights still moved beyond the window, but the room was already quiet.
Morning light filtered through the curtains into the room. When Sakaguchi woke, the pillow beside him was empty.
From the living room came the soft sound of a cup being set on a table. Sakaguchi walked out and found Serika already dressed, preparing coffee.
“Not long ago. Last night… I slept very well.”
She handed Sakaguchi a cup of coffee and sat at the table with her own.
“…Is that your doctor's occupational habit again?”
“I'm fine. My eyes are a little swollen, that's all.”
She touched the corner of her eye, then lifted her face toward Sakaguchi.
“…Yesterday, you saw me in a dreadful state.”
Serika lowered her head, took a sip of coffee, and paused.
“Nanami asked me to go back and see my father. You heard her too.”
“Not yet. I don't want to make an immediate decision at a time like this.”
“That hospital, my father, and Miyuki… There are so many things I still owe it to myself to say.”
“…But there's one thing I've made up my mind about.”
She set down her coffee and sat a little straighter.
“I won't pretend I haven't seen what Shiozaki has done anymore.”
“Nanami has asked the hospital to contact the police. I'll testify too, and tell them what I know.”
“And… Shiozaki once forced me to poison my father. I didn't actually do it, but I nearly obeyed him then. Miyuki was the one who took me away.”
“…Thank you for being willing to tell me.”
“…I've always been afraid. Afraid I might really become that kind of person one day.”
“But if I run away again, I won't even be able to trust myself afterward.”
Sakaguchi sat across from her, waiting for her to continue.
“For now, I still want to stay at Hoshimi. This place… is somewhere I've chosen for myself now.”
“Then stay. You can decide the next step when you're ready.”
Serika nodded gently. Her gaze left the window and settled on Sakaguchi's face again.
“About last night… I don't want you to think it was only because I was afraid to be alone.”
“I like you. I started liking you some time ago. I just never dared say it.”
Serika lowered her head, her ears turning slightly red. She touched the cup handle with a fingertip, then raised her eyes again.
“…Do you even need my formal confirmation for something like this?”
“I learned it at the hospital. Important things have to be decided by the person concerned.”
“Then may I call you Serika outside the hospital from now on?”
“Didn't you already call me that last night?”
“I didn't get a chance to ask then.”
She held her hand out to Sakaguchi. Once he took it, she did not immediately let go.
“But now that you're my boyfriend… there's one more thing.”
“You still haven't turned in the bass homework you owe me.”
“No need. You can take your time.”
She gave Sakaguchi a small smile and carried their empty cups to the sink. Outside the window, morning had fully arrived.
Sakaguchi helped her pick up the coat beside the table. Together they gathered their things, ready to return to their respective posts at the hospital.

strings.collections.special_event_steps.miyuki_l: After the evening rounds, Asakura clips tomorrow's operating schedule back onto her clipboard and gently caps her pen.
“All right. Ring the bell if you feel unwell tonight. We have a busy morning ahead.”
“Hmm? Is there something else you forgot to ask, Miss Nikaido?”
Yoriko pulls a small notebook from beside her pillow. Its first two pages are crammed with writing, with several question marks drawn in red.
“…Wow. Are you here as a patient, or to conduct an interview?”
“I'm not trying to dig up any secrets! It's just… tomorrow it really will be my turn to have surgery.”
“I know. You read the consent form twice yesterday, and asked me about it six times today.”
“It wasn't six times! …Huh? You even kept count?”
“A good memory is an asset for a nurse.”
“Then I have one last question… No, maybe a few more.”
“From waking up tomorrow morning, to being taken into the operating room, to the doctor actually picking up the knife… what exactly happens to get me ready? Don't skip a single step.”
“Are you sure you want that much detail?”
“Of course. I'm a police officer! The more I know, the more prepared I'll feel.”
“All right. I'll go through it by time. But don't get frightened halfway through and accuse me of scaring you.”
“Don't worry. I'm not that much of a scaredy-cat.”
Asakura pulls up a chair beside the bed and rests the clipboard on her lap. Her expression suggests someone has finally asked about her favorite subject.
“A nurse will wake you at around five thirty tomorrow.”
“Five thirty?! I thought surgery started at nine. Surely I could sleep until seven.”
“Nine is when the incision begins, not when you open your eyes.”
“…Why do you sound so happy explaining that distinction?”
“Because lots of people get it wrong. First we'll check your temperature, blood pressure and pulse, then confirm your wristband, name, procedure, fasting time and allergies.”
“But you already asked all that today!”
“We'll ask again tomorrow. And even more once you reach the surgical area.”
“How worried are you about mistaking me for someone else?”
“Miss Nikaido, when you arrest someone, you can't skip checking their identity just because their face looks familiar, can you?”
“Of course not! …But being asked my name over and over like a suspect still feels strange.”
“Then there's cleaning, skin preparation and putting on your surgical cap. Glasses, jewelry and hair clips are put away, and all your hair goes inside the cap.”
“I can't even wear my glasses? I can't make out your faces without them!”
“Everyone in the operating room wears a cap and mask anyway. You might not recognize us even with your glasses.”
“How is that supposed to be reassuring?!”
“Oh, and your hospital gown and your own clothes all come off. We'll cover you with a blanket afterward. We won't have you going down the corridor like that.”
“…Wait. Did you just say the hospital gown comes off too?”
“Yes. The area needed for surgery has to be cleaned, disinfected and draped. Your own underwear won't be left underneath either.”
“N-not even underwear? That's what I'll be like after I get up tomorrow?”
“We'll keep you covered where you should be. Only the area needed for an examination or preparation will be exposed. It's ordinary preoperative work for us.”
“The more you call it ‘ordinary,’ the more embarrassed I feel…”
“But weren't you the one who said not to skip a single step?”
“Sometime between five and six, we'll have you use the bathroom one last time. After that, you'll need a nurse's help whenever you move. You can't just slip on your slippers and wander out.”
“I'm not a child! …But what if I need the bathroom again later?”
“Tell us. This is a fairly long abdominal operation, so we'll manage urine drainage according to plan. Catheterization comes later.”
“Of course. Were you imagining ‘preoperative preparation’ was something much simpler?”
Yoriko's ears turn red. She starts to close her notebook, hesitates, then opens it again.
“Th-then… will I be awake for that?”
“The current plan is to give you the epidural first, confirm it is working, and then finish that part of the preparation. Tell us whenever you feel anything or are uncomfortable.”
“What is it? Suddenly stopped taking notes?”
“I can remember that part without writing it down!”
“Around six, we'll recheck the IV, your medical records, images and surgical consent form. All the documentation goes to the operating room with you.”
“Of course. Who would the doctor operate on without the patient?”
“I know! I just… wanted to make sure!”
“Then you'll get onto the trolley, with the blanket tucked around you, and a nurse will wheel you over. There'll be another handover at the entrance to the surgical area.”
“I have to lie there while you wheel me all the way? I can't walk?”
“You'll already be prepared for surgery, with lines and coverings to look after. Just lie comfortably and leave the pushing to the nurse.”
“You really intend to keep me lying down from morning until the operation is over…”
“That's how it works. You'll enter the room at seven. The operating table is a little narrower and firmer than this bed.”
“Narrow enough for the doctors to work from both sides. We'll put down padding and position your head, shoulders, arms and legs.”
“That sounds like arranging a piece of… very important evidence.”
“Hehe, you've finally found a police comparison. But evidence doesn't suddenly sneeze by itself. We still have to tell you how to help us.”
“You're a very talkative patient. But when we change your position, it's best to wait for instructions. Several nurses will count ‘one, two, three’ together before moving you.”
“…I don't even get to decide where I lie.”
“Because you'll be undergoing surgical preparation. You can tell us if you're uncomfortable, but you can't roll over and settle yourself into another position.”
“You won't let me fall, will you?”
“There'll be safety straps, padding and supports. They're there to prevent sliding and pressure injuries, not to tie you to a rack like luggage.”
“Don't you think that last comparison made it scarier than saying nothing?”

“Once you're on the table, we'll put ECG electrodes on your chest, a blood-pressure cuff around your arm, a pulse-oximeter probe on your finger, and secure the IV line safely. Someone in the room will keep watching the monitors.”
“So by then I'll have a whole pile of things attached to me?”
“Yes. Everyone is working to keep you safe during surgery.”
“…Miss Asakura, every time you say ‘safe,’ another thing I've never heard of turns up.”
Asakura's eyes curve with her smile, as though Yoriko's discovery has amused her.
“Sometime after seven, Dr. Nanjo will check everything with you, then administer the epidural.”
“That's… the one with a needle in your back and a tube?”
“Yes. You'll need to lie on your side or sit up, then hold that position. The doctor will explain before doing anything.”
“It's my abdomen that needs surgery. Why do I get a needle in my back first…?”

“Because anesthesia blocks sensation carried by the nerves. It doesn't always go directly into the incision site. Afterward, we'll test the area of numbness. Surgery can only start once it's sufficient.”
“So I won't just close my eyes, sleep, and wake up when it's finished?”

“Not according to this plan. Generally, you'll remain awake. Dr. Nanjo will keep monitoring you and adjust the plan if needed. Tell us immediately about any actual sharp pain. If the block is insufficient, we'll address it first, not ask you to endure it.”
“…I'll be awake the whole time, knowing what everyone is doing to me?”
“You'll be aware of quite a lot. Once the drapes are in place, you won't see the work on your abdomen, but you'll hear some sounds.”
“Instrument packs being opened, metal instruments placed on trays, nurses checking things with one another. Someone reporting readings, someone asking about the light, someone checking the suction.”
“S-stop a moment! I feel like I can hear it already!”
Asakura really does stop and watches her quietly. Yoriko covers her ears, then slowly lowers her hands two seconds later.
“I meant pause! Not skip everything that comes afterward!”
“I see. You're the sort who covers her eyes during a horror movie, then peeks through her fingers.”
“This isn't a movie! I'm the one who'll actually be lying there tomorrow!”
“Exactly. That's why I'm explaining it so carefully.”
“You don't… enjoy talking about this a little, do you?”
“I do. Getting the people, instruments, anesthesia, timing and positions all properly organized is one of the interesting parts of an operation.”
“You'll be the center of attention in the whole operating room tomorrow.”
“The center of attention?! Don't make it sound like the star is making her entrance!”
“But it's true. Dr. Sakaguchi, the surgeon; Dr. Nanjo, handling anesthesia; Miss Nakai, handling instruments; and the circulating nurse… everyone will be preparing for your operation.”
“…An entire room of people, all bustling around me?”
“Yes. You can leave it to us with confidence.”
“How do you make the scariest sentence sound like a compliment?!”

“After seven thirty, there'll be catheterization, abdominal disinfection, small adjustments to your position and various other preparations. The nurses will uncover the relevant area as needed, then cover it again.”
“How big an area will you disinfect?”
“Larger than the eventual incision. Your lower abdomen needs thorough disinfection. The solution may feel a little cool, though after anesthesia you might not feel it the way you normally would.”
“…So you'll lift the blanket off me, then look closely at my abdomen while getting things ready.”
“Of course. We have to check the disinfected area, your position, the skin and where the lines are. It's our work.”
“You keep saying ‘work.’ I'll be lying there without any clothes while a whole group gathers around…”
“Because it really is ordinary for us. Nobody is coming in specially to admire how frightened Miss Nikaido looks.”
“Waaah… You say that so naturally, it makes me even more embarrassed!”
“Because I'm the only one who thinks this is a huge deal! You're all just thinking, ‘Right, next item!’”
“Then tomorrow you'll see for yourself just how dependable our ‘next item’ is.”
“…Is that meant to reassure me, or warn me what's coming?”
Asakura deliberately imitates Yoriko's earlier hesitant tone and laughs. Yoriko puffs out her cheeks, but has no reply.

“We'll start placing sterile drapes around eight. The surgical area that needs to be exposed stays in the center opening; everything else is covered. Afterward, you'll hardly be able to see any of the work around your abdomen.”
“So I'll hear you talking, but I won't see what you're doing?”
“Most of the time. Close your eyes if you like, or look at the surgical lights. There's no rule that patients must keep their eyes open to watch the excitement.”
“But if I can't see, I might keep guessing!”
“You can ask. We'll explain the steps we can tell you about.”
“What if my arm feels uncomfortable where it's secured?”
“Tell us it feels uncomfortable. We'll check whether we can adjust it.”
“What if I want to sit up and look?”
“Tell us first. Don't get up by yourself. You may already have lines connected and anesthesia in effect.”
“What if I suddenly decide I don't want the operation?”
“If you want to change your decision, tell the doctor immediately so we can confirm it again. Being frightened and changing your decision aren't the same thing. Don't hide either.”
“…And what if I just see the scalpel and suddenly want to run back to my room?”
“At least tell us first. We can help with your nerves, but we can't guess every escape plan before you say anything.”
“You just guessed a whole bunch of my questions!”
“That's because you're really very easy to read, Miss Nikaido.”
“Around eight thirty, Miss Nakai will count the instruments and gauze again, while the doctors check the images to confirm the locations of the fibroids being treated.”

“Yes. This isn't a matter of removing one little thing and finishing. The surgeon will deal with the fibroids in each location, then carefully repair the uterine wall. It will take longer than an ordinary minor operation.”
“When you say ‘each location,’ I suddenly feel like there's a whole to-do list inside my abdomen.”
“That's a good description. We really do have to check the preoperative images and surgical plan item by item.”
“But I'm a person. Why do you make me sound like a complicated investigation…?”
“You can think of it as us solving a very troublesome case for you. But this time you're the most important witness, so you need to lie quietly.”
“…I never knew being a witness was such hard work.”
“Next, Dr. Nanjo will make a final check of the block, and Dr. Sakaguchi will prepare additional local infiltration at the incision site. Everyone will complete the checks before surgery begins.”
“But I'll already have an epidural! Why inject the incision site too?”

“It's a supplement. Sensation around the incision isn't quite the same as pulling sensations deep inside. Dr. Nanjo will continue assessing you and only let Dr. Sakaguchi start once the anesthesia is sufficient.”
“…Will I hear them all say my name?”

“Yes. Everyone must confirm the patient, procedure, site, anesthetic status and anything needing special attention. You'll notice the whole room suddenly quiet down to listen carefully to each person's response.”
“I'm already imagining what that sounds like…”
“At around nine, the surgeon confirms that preparation is complete, the assistant takes position, and Miss Nakai passes over the first scalpel. Then—”
Yoriko yanks up the blanket so abruptly that her glasses tilt. Asakura really does fall silent, and considerately waits for her to straighten them.
“Didn't you say you wanted to hear everything up to the incision?”
“I do! But you make it sound… far too real!”
“Don't say that with such a happy face!”
“Then I can continue from ‘Miss Nakai passes over the first scalpel.’”
“Hehe. You really are the kind who gets to the scariest part of a horror movie and still can't bear to turn off the television.”
“I keep telling you, this is my operation, not a horror movie!!”
“All right. I won't go any further for now.”
She closes the operating schedule. The room falls quiet, and Yoriko finds herself looking at her notebook again.
“…But is there anything you haven't told me?”
“Huh? Didn't you already tell me to stop?”
“I just want to make sure! The more I hear, the scarier it gets, but if I don't know, my imagination makes it even worse.”
“I see. Usually you're the one finding out about other people, but today other people know more about what's happening to you than you do.”
“Exactly! The whole operating room knows what they're going to do with me next. I'm the only one lying there, unable to do anything…”
“Then let us do the work. Your job is to tell us what's uncomfortable and cooperate when we need you to.”
“So you're in charge of preparation, disinfection, anesthesia and cutting… and I'm in charge of getting cut?”
“You could use the nicer expression: ‘undergoing surgery.’”
“But from the patient's point of view, isn't getting cut exactly my job?”
“From the patient's point of view… yes, I suppose it is.”
Asakura finally laughs aloud. Yoriko laughs with her, though she is still clutching the corner of the blanket tightly.
“Then tomorrow, if I'm really too frightened to say anything… will you tell me which step you're at?”
“Yes. And we'll tell you in advance when we need you to cooperate.”
“Even the anesthesia, catheterization, disinfection and draping?”
“We'll tell you everything we can. If there's something you'd rather not hear, you can ask me to hold off.”
“One more thing. Don't suddenly say ‘All done’ tomorrow.”
“Because every time you say ‘All done,’ it means you're about to do something even scarier!”
“Then I'll be more precise. ‘Epidural complete,’ ‘Disinfection complete,’ ‘Draping complete,’ ‘Final checks complete’…”
“Do all you nurses enjoy explaining the things people fear, step by step?”
“Of course. That's our job. Besides, you're asking so earnestly that I'd feel bad leaving anything out.”
“I'll probably dream about the operating table tonight.”
“Think of it as getting familiar with the surroundings. Get some sleep, Miss Nikaido.”
“…If I get scared again tomorrow, don't complain that I ask too many questions.”
“When have I ever complained? Ask whatever you like. But when we say ‘start’ tomorrow, I won't make the doctor pause until you've finished your notes.”
“I'm not actually going to take notes on the operating table!”
“Right. We'll wake you at five thirty, put you on the table at seven, drape you at eight, and start at nine. We'll remember every step for you.”
Asakura stands and walks to the door, still wearing that professional, deeply satisfied smile.
“…Now I think the scariest part is that you really do remember everything.”
The door closes softly. Yoriko switches off the bedside lamp, her notebook already tucked beside her pillow. A long time later, she feels for it again and opens it to the page marked “nine o'clock.”
Five thirty. When the nurse on duty knocks, Yoriko is already awake. She looks at the notebook beside her pillow and finds she has no desire to open it again.
“…Yesterday I was only listening to her. Today it's really my turn.”
“Good morning, Miss Nikaido. First, let's confirm your name and today's procedure.”

After a series of checks, cleaning and skin preparation, her hospital gown and personal clothes are put away, and a blanket is carefully laid over her. Her surgical cap contains all her hair; her glasses go into the belongings bag too.
“…Everything Miss Asakura said yesterday. Even the order is exactly right.”
Before Yoriko quite realizes it, she is lying on a trolley. One nurse pushes, another watches the lines, and handover confirmations echo along the corridor.
“Wait, wasn't I just in my room?”
“Yes. We're heading to the surgical area now. It's almost seven.”
“…Seven. So there are still two hours to go.”
Seven sharp. The operating-room door opens, and light reflects off the ceiling. Familiar eyes smile at her between a surgical cap and a mask.
“Good morning, Miss Nikaido. How did you sleep?”
“Miss Asakura! I dreamed you kept announcing the time… and now it really is seven!”
“Hehe. Then I'll be looking after you for the next two hours.”
“When you put it like that, it sounds like it's going to take forever again…”
Before she can dwell on it, the nurses are helping her onto the narrow operating table. Someone checks the position of her arms, someone connects the monitors, and someone checks the IV line.
“Ah, it really is narrow… Wait, was that the ECG? What's next?”
“The blood-pressure cuff and oxygen monitor. Someone over there was asking you to say your name just now too.”
“I heard! I'm turning into a machine that automatically answers with my own name!”
“Hehe. By the way, Miss Nikaido, how does it feel lying here?”
“This might sound strange… I'm lying here with nothing on, just a blanket, but…”
The ECG beeps steadily. Every so often the blood-pressure cuff gently tightens around her arm, then slowly releases. Yoriko listens intently.
“Those beeps, and the cuff tightening again and again… It all feels so immediate! Ah, I'm really in an operating room!”
“So you like that feeling. A little different from listening to the radio in a police car, isn't it?”
“Completely different! Usually I'm the one heading to the scene… Today I'm the person at its center. Huh, now that I say it, I'm even getting a little excited!”
Sayaka Nanjo comes to the table, confirms her name and explains the epidural. Asakura stays within earshot, ready to help adjust Yoriko's position.
“Miss Nikaido, I'm Nanjo, handling your anesthesia today. Turn onto your side with me, and curve your back a little… Yes, very good. Tell me if you're uncomfortable.”
“Ugh… Just hearing about this last night scared me. But now everyone's talking to me, I hardly have time to imagine things.”
“Then follow Dr. Nanjo's instructions and breathe slowly. We'll tell you clearly whenever we need your help.”

Seven forty. The epidural is complete. Nanjo checks the area of the block while the circulating nurse continues watching the monitors. Then come catheterization, positioning and rearranging the coverings; someone explains each action, and someone is always moving on to the next task.
“Just hearing you describe this part yesterday made my face burn… and today it's already finished?”
“Miss Asakura, something just occurred to me. Taking off all your clothes and going somewhere full of people you barely know… it's a bit like your first trip to a hot spring.”
“Hehe, a hot spring? Well, you did wash first, move somewhere else, and everyone around you treats it as perfectly natural.”
“Exactly! Just now I even thought that since everyone seems so used to it, maybe I don't need to feel so embarrassed.”
Yoriko instinctively tries to turn a little. The safety strap, arm supports and connected monitoring lines immediately remind her where she is lying.
“…Until I got tied up and couldn't move! W-wait, what hot spring ties its guests to lounge chairs?!”
“It's safety support to prevent slipping, not tying you up. Though… I doubt a hot spring has quite so many staff all attending to just you.”
“That makes perfect sense… so why doesn't it reassure me at all?!”
“You've been doing very well. Is anything uncomfortable now?”
“I'm a little cold, and… without my glasses, everyone's face is blurry.”
“All right, I'll adjust the warming. You may not see our faces clearly, but you can still recognize our voices, can't you?”
“I can! Especially one particular nurse who always sounds so happy describing frightening things!”
“Oh? Somehow that sounds like a compliment.”

After eight. The sound of instrument packs opening, Mika Nakai checking instrument and gauze counts, and doctors discussing images and the scope of surgery follows one after another. Yoriko looks left, only for someone on her right to call to her.
“What are they counting over there? …Ah, all right, I'll keep this hand still. Huh, are you adjusting the light now?”
“We're checking the instruments and gauze. Every count has to be exact. You can leave this part to me, Miss Nikaido.”
“You're the ones doing all the work! But it feels like someone comes over to see me every few moments…”
“Weren't you afraid of being surrounded by everyone last night?”
“I was… But it's strange. I thought I'd lie here nervous for two hours. It doesn't seem that long now.”
“We haven't skipped a single thing you were so frightened of last night. It's just that whenever you almost have time to be scared, someone else comes to see you.”
“Yesterday it sounded like a long, terrifying movie… Today it feels more like everyone's filming the same scene, and I'm the only one who hasn't learned her lines.”
“You already know your lines. Your name, your procedure, and telling us if something feels uncomfortable. We'll prompt you for the rest when the time comes.”
“Pfft… Put that way, I suppose you're right.”
Eight fifty. The sterile drapes are in place, and a blue screen blocks Yoriko's view of her abdomen. Sakaguchi, fully dressed for surgery, comes to the table.
“Good morning, Miss Nikaido. We've rechecked the anesthesia. Are you uncomfortable anywhere?”
“No obvious pain… Doctor, I didn't expect to see you so soon.”
“Soon? You've been in the operating room for almost two hours.”
“What?! Really? …It feels like someone's been talking to me the whole time, and it's gone by in a blink!”
Sakaguchi looks at Yoriko, then at Asakura, who is checking her monitors and coverings. Asakura's eyes curve in a smile, but she offers no explanation.
“Miss Nikaido, after all we talked about last night, do you still have any questions?”
“I do! Like whether they've already got the scalpel ready over there, and…”
Asakura leans down slightly and lowers her voice, as though sharing a secret just between them.
“Are you nervous, or thinking about something else… or a little of both?”
“Hehe. When we got to this part last night, you pulled the blanket right up to your chin.”

Sakaguchi catches half the exchange and seems about to ask what they discussed last night. But Asakura has already straightened up, professionally checking the identity, procedure, anesthesia and instrument readiness with the team.
“The block and monitoring are confirmed. Miss Nikaido, I'll be here throughout. Tell me immediately if you actually feel pain.”
As planned, Sakaguchi adds local infiltration around the incision site. The team completes the final time-out checks, their clear responses sounding through the operating room.
“Preparation is complete. Miss Nikaido, we're going to begin now.”
Yoriko instinctively looks at the clock. Nine sharp. Mika Nakai passes the first scalpel to Sakaguchi. Behind the blue screen, the medical team is in position.
“W-wait! Are you really making the incision now?!”
