The door to the surgical department's women's changing room closed softly. Miyuki Asakura hung her white nurse's uniform in a locker and placed a set of light green scrubs on the bench.
“Phew… They’re actually letting me assist with such a long operation today. This will go on my internship evaluation too, right?”
“You’ve assisted with long cases like this before, haven’t you? I memorized the procedure yesterday, but I still feel unsure.”
“Wonderful! Then I’ll make sure to learn everything I can from you today!”
“Hehe. Remember that. Say it again when you see the instrument table.”
“Because then I'll ask you to concentrate on your own work first.”
Asakura put away her watch and accessories, deftly arranging her belongings in the locker. The younger nurse held a pair of scrub trousers, still studying the ties at the waist.
“Oh, these trousers tie shut. I thought they'd have a zipper like our ward uniforms.”
“You've come from the ward. It's normal to find things unfamiliar on your first day.”
Asakura put her personal clothes, including her underwear, into the locker, changed straight into the scrub trousers and top, then smoothed her sleeves.
“Um... Do we have to change everything underneath too?”
“That's how we've always dressed for operations in our surgical department.”
“I thought I could just put the scrubs on over my own underwear...”
“Understandable. Nobody on the ward specifically teaches you how to change for the operating room.”
“Then... why? Does everyone dress like that?”
“At least here, we try not to wear our own undergarments during long operations. It's a nuisance if they get wet.”
“That too. Irrigation fluid, blood... If you're unlucky, even your scrubs won't keep it all out.”
“B-blood can get on our underwear?! That wasn’t in the internship handbook!”
The younger nurse instinctively glanced down at her clothes. Watching her suddenly stiffen, Asakura's lips curled slightly upward.
“Hehe, what's so strange? We're performing surgery, not playing house.”
“I know it's surgery! But I thought... well...”
“You thought all the blood would stay obediently inside the patient and disappear once we were done?”
“Are you… trying to scare the intern on purpose!”
Asakura blinked, her smile so sweet it left little room for complaint.
“If those cute pink panties of yours get a female patient's blood on them, won't that be awkward when you get home?”
“H-how did you even see the color?!”
“I happened to catch a glimpse when you took off your ward uniform just now. I'm only worrying about them.”
“Ooh… You really are making fun of me…”
“I'm not. Think about it. Hospital clothes are easy to get washed. Ruining underwear you like isn't worth it.”
“…All right, I’ll change now. I don’t want to slip up over something like this today.”
“Don't worry. Most of the time, proper protection keeps everything fine. It's just best to consider what might happen during a long operation before going in.”
“Why didn't you say the reassuring part first...?”
“Your expression was so amusing that I got a little carried away.”
The younger nurse put her undergarments in the locker and dressed properly in her scrub trousers and top. She took a few steps, stopped, and discreetly tugged at the fabric of her trousers.
“What is it? Found something else this time?”
“The trousers... They rub a little when I walk, directly against my skin.”
“The top too. Without a bra, the fabric against my chest feels so rough...”
“I thought I was just terrible at adapting… Does it really not bother you at all?”
“The first time I wore this fabric, I thought it was stiff too.”
“Of course. I'm not made out of scrub fabric.”
“I thought once you got used to it, you wouldn't even notice those things anymore.”
“You forget when you're busy. Especially when the doctor suddenly holds out a hand for an instrument. Who has time to think about their trousers chafing then?”
“But this batch really is a bit stiff. Let me see.”
Asakura pinched her own sleeve and compared its fabric with the younger nurse's top, then checked inside the collar.
“Mm, these must be from the new delivery. Older ones that have been washed are actually softer.”
“So it's not just me being strange?”
“Of course not. Uncomfortable clothes are uncomfortable. Putting up with them won't make them softer.”
“There are some spare sets that have softened in the wash in the next locker. I'll get you one. It should be your size.”
“Why wouldn't you, if you can? You'll be standing for hours today. You're not here for an endurance contest.”
Asakura took a folded set of scrubs from the spare locker and handed it over, then folded the stiff new set and put it aside to be checked.
“I'll mention it to the director later. At least we can get more comfortable fabric next time.”
“Can you… really bring something like this straight to the director?”
“If we have to wear something uncomfortable all day, of course I do. Patients aren't the only people we need to look after.”
“...And you were being so mean just a moment ago.”
“Are you really going to pretend you don't know?!”

The younger nurse finally laughed. They each picked up a surgical cap and put it on. Asakura straightened the collar of the spare scrub top for her, then checked the cap's rim, which was not quite tucked into place yet.
“Come to think of it, didn’t you say you were still settling in at Hoshimi too?”
“But you even know which batch of scrubs has bad fabric. And when you mentioned long operations, you sounded like you'd done lots of them.”
“I said I was inexperienced at Hoshimi, not that I learned to be a nurse today.”
“And tuck that side of your cap in properly. Keep your ears and the ends of your hair inside.”

Asakura put on her mask and opened the door to the surgical corridor. The younger nurse hurried after her. Her face was still nervous, but her steps were much steadier than when she had entered the changing room.
“If I get so nervous I start fumbling… will that go on my internship evaluation?”
“First, watch what I'm doing. Ask if you don't understand. Say so if you're unsure. That's much more useful than pretending to be calm.”
“Good. Then let's go see whether we really are playing house today.”
“Why are you bringing that up again!”
Their voices gradually faded down the surgical corridor.
The door to the surgical department's women's changing room closed softly. Miyuki Asakura hung her white nurse's uniform in a locker and placed a set of light green scrubs on the bench.
“Phew—finally my turn on a long case! I’ve heard about them so often on the ward, but it feels different when it’s your turn.”
“Do you often assist with operations this long? I’d like to see how an experienced nurse paces herself.”
“Then I’ll be watching closely and stealing your tricks today!”
“Hehe. Remember that. Say it again when you see the instrument table.”
“Because then I'll ask you to concentrate on your own work first.”
Asakura put away her watch and accessories, deftly arranging her belongings in the locker. The younger nurse held a pair of scrub trousers, still studying the ties at the waist.
“The ties on these scrub trousers are different from the ones I usually wear. I’ll be standing so long today, I’d better tie them securely.”
“Yes. You’ll be standing for a long time. Get your clothes comfortable now, before you’re too busy to think about it.”
Asakura put her personal clothes, including her underwear, into the locker, changed straight into the scrub trousers and top, then smoothed her sleeves.
“Um... Do we have to change everything underneath too?”
“That's how we've always dressed for operations in our surgical department.”
“I thought I could just put the scrubs on over my own underwear...”
“You don’t necessarily run into this on short cases. Today’s a long one, so it’s best to think ahead for your own clothes.”
“Then... why? Does everyone dress like that?”
“At least here, we try not to wear our own undergarments during long operations. It's a nuisance if they get wet.”
“That too. Irrigation fluid, blood... If you're unlucky, even your scrubs won't keep it all out.”
“Wait, even our own underwear can get blood on it?! Don’t make it sound like an everyday occurrence!”
The younger nurse instinctively glanced down at her clothes. Watching her suddenly stiffen, Asakura's lips curled slightly upward.
“Hehe, what's so strange? We're performing surgery, not playing house.”
“I know it's surgery! But I thought... well...”
“You thought all the blood would stay obediently inside the patient and disappear once we were done?”
“You’re definitely picking out all the scariest parts to tell me!”
Asakura blinked, her smile so sweet it left little room for complaint.
“If those cute pink panties of yours get a female patient's blood on them, won't that be awkward when you get home?”
“H-how did you even see the color?!”
“I happened to catch a glimpse when you took off your ward uniform just now. I'm only worrying about them.”
“You just want to see me embarrass myself, don’t you?”
“I'm not. Think about it. Hospital clothes are easy to get washed. Ruining underwear you like isn't worth it.”
“Fine, I’ll change! I’m not sacrificing my favorite underwear.”

Asakura put on her mask and opened the door to the surgical corridor. The younger nurse hurried after her. Her face was still nervous, but her steps were much steadier than when she had entered the changing room.
“If I really do get nervous at the table, you’ll give me a reminder, won’t you?”

“Good. Then let's go see whether we really are playing house today.”
Their voices gradually faded down the surgical corridor.
The plaza is much busier on Sunday than on weekdays. Sakaguchi turns his phone over on the bench and looks up once more at the people passing by.
He and Miyuki Asakura agreed to meet at two in the afternoon. Now the minute hand on the plaza clock has leisurely completed another lap.
Sakaguchi calls again. The phone rings for a long time before someone finally answers.
“Yes, it’s me. Are you all right?”
Rustling comes through the phone, followed by the dull thud of something falling onto the floor.
“Is today Sunday?! Were we supposed to meet at two?!”
The other end falls silent for two seconds, then hurried footsteps follow.
“I’m sorry! I’m so sorry! I’ll be right there!”
“Don’t rush. Were you on duty last night?”
“Then how did you sleep until now?”
“It’s that drama I watched yesterday! The last episode ended on such an outrageous cliffhanger. How could I possibly stop there!”
“Until sunrise. Then I thought I’d sleep for a little while… The next thing I knew, your call woke me.”
“Don’t laugh! I’ll be there in twenty… no, thirty minutes!”
“Take your time. Just make sure you put your shoes on properly.”
The call ends. Sakaguchi looks at the dark screen, then up at the three-o’clock afternoon sky.
“…Asakura notices even a handover five minutes early at the hospital, and yet…”
Forty minutes later, Asakura jogs over from the far side of the plaza. She is in light casual clothes with a small bag over her shoulder, her hair still showing the curves of a hurried styling.
She presses her palms together, smiling sweetly and obediently. Before Sakaguchi can speak, Asakura raises her phone.
“I promise, I really did set an alarm.”
“Then why did you only wake up at three?”
“I’d like to know too. My phone says I turned it off, but I don’t remember doing it at all.”
“You remember the hospital rota so clearly, but not turning off your own alarm?”
“That’s different. Patients are waiting at the hospital. Of course I can’t be careless.”
“On a day off… nobody needs surgery just because I stay in bed a little longer.”
“Someone waited for you for over an hour today.”
“Ooh… I admit that was my fault. What would it take for you to forgive me, Dr. Sakaguchi?”
“Let’s at least get something to eat first. I’m getting hungry.”
“All right! My treat today. You can have anything you like!”
“Well… except the kind of fancy restaurant you have to book three months ahead.”
“I haven’t even had breakfast yet. Have mercy on me first.”
She gently tugs Sakaguchi’s sleeve and heads toward the shopping street. Her embarrassment doesn’t last long; there is already a spring in her step again.
They enter a small restaurant still serving afternoon tea. Their window seat overlooks the pedestrians outside, and patterned paper menus lie on the table.
“Huh… They’ve stopped serving the lunch set.”
“I know. But I haven’t had lunch today.”
“So your lunchtime is nothing like the hospital’s.”
“It’s a rare day off. The clock ought to work around me.”
“I’ve never heard you say that at the hospital.”
“How could I? If a patient is due at seven, it means seven. If an instrument is missing, can I say I’ll look for it after I’ve had my sleep?”
“So the moment you finish work, you become a completely different person?”
“Not a different person. This person finally gets to be lazy.”
Asakura orders a hot sandwich, then studies the dessert section intently.
“Didn’t you say you needed a meal? Why are you still looking at cake?”
“The meal is for now. The cake is for afterward. Surely a doctor understands the order?”
“I thought you might have some special diet plan.”
“I do. Step one: feed the me who’s been hungry for half a day.”
“Make sure the handsome doctor who waited an hour for me enjoys his meal too.”
“Can’t I? I’m very good at reassuring patients.”
“If you’d like, I could take care of you until you feel better.”
“Something about that doesn’t sound quite right.”
“Hehe. Let’s eat first, then. No more hospital talk.”
The hot sandwich arrives. Asakura closes her eyes in satisfaction at the first bite, all her clever remarks momentarily defeated by food.
“Mm! Try some. This sauce is delicious.”
“You were late, but now you sound like you’re showing me your favorite places.”
“Of course. Being late means I have to make the rest of our time even more worthwhile.”
After they eat, sunlight slants across the table. Asakura taps her dessert glass with a small spoon and finally stops rushing to speak.
“When I watch you work, you really don’t seem like a newcomer.”
“This again? Didn’t I tell you last time that I’m only new to Hoshimi?”
“I mean, you seem to know all about handovers, operating-room routines, and exactly where newcomers will make mistakes.”
“Well… I’ve done all those things before.”
“Just how much were you responsible for?”
“Routine nursing, scheduling, training new staff… Later I was even the leader of the second nursing team.”
“Officially. I led a whole team on shift, and before leaving I had to make sure everyone had handed everything over properly.”
“Then why have you kept calling yourself an inexperienced new nurse since coming to Hoshimi?”
“Because I really am unfamiliar with the people and systems here. The way my old hospital scheduled things doesn’t mean Hoshimi does the same.”
“If you think that means I’m going to become meek and obedient, you’re wrong.”
“When I was promoted, everyone said it was a good thing. I could manage more people, and my words carried more weight.”
“At first, I was happy too. Who doesn’t like having their work recognized?”
“Then I found that everyone wanted me on their side.”
“What should have been arranging nursing care for patients turned into guessing which superior might be upset first.”
“You didn’t like that kind of work?”
“I don’t mind managing things. Who should help when someone is overwhelmed; how to teach a newcomer until she understands—I like all that.”
“But smiling to appease people, finding out who’s fighting with whom, cleaning up messes for the higher-ups that have nothing to do with nursing… No, thank you.”
“Did you say that outright back then too?”
“Yes. Though whenever I did, someone would say I was immature.”
“You don’t look as though that would bother you now.”
“It does. But one day I suddenly thought: why should those people get to decide whether I’m happy every day?”
Asakura scoops up a small spoonful of dessert, as though discussing something she has already thought through thoroughly.
“I want to care for patients and teach newcomers. Those things interest me, so I’ll keep doing them.”
“I don’t want to take sides all day, or have dinner with people I dislike every evening after work. So I won’t be that kind of team leader anymore.”
“So coming to Hoshimi was your own choice?”
“Of course. You didn’t think I came here for retraining because I couldn’t do anything right at my old hospital, did you?”
“Good. Otherwise I might have to check your handover sheet again tomorrow.”
“Hey, weren’t we avoiding work talk today?”
“Oh, right. I nearly brought the hospital into our date again.”
“But you really do seem happy now.”
“I am. I can work hard, sleep in, watch dramas, and dress up to go out for good food.”
“I’m only twenty-three. Surely there’s more to look forward to than shifts and rotas?”
“Fair enough. What else would you like to do?”
“So much. Go to the seaside, see a new film, sleep until I wake up naturally…”
“You already managed the last one today.”
“And find a man I like the look of to take me on a date now and then.”
“Rather than flatter those awful, powerful doctors, I’d much rather tease a handsome doctor I actually like.”
“…You wouldn’t happen to mean me, would you?”
She doesn’t rush to say anything else, merely sets her spoon back on the saucer and smiles at Sakaguchi.
“It took me so long to get a whole day with you. Of course I have to make it interesting.”
“Didn’t you only remember this date at three?”
“…You’re awful. Can we retire that joke now?”
“Who just said she wanted to make today interesting?”
“Hmm… So Dr. Sakaguchi can talk back after all.”
Asakura smiles and reaches for the bill. Before Sakaguchi can say anything more, she is already on her way to the till.
“Come on. The afternoon isn’t over yet.”
Leaving the restaurant, they follow the shopping street to the river. A breeze blows along the waterside path, where the Sunday crowds are much thinner than in the shops.
“You said you like teaching newcomers. But sometimes you’re quite strict with them.”
“Am I? I thought I’d been exceptionally gentle here at Hoshimi.”
“Sometimes you even seem a little pleased to see someone nervous.”
“Being nervous isn’t always bad. Newcomers ask me serious questions because they know how much they don’t understand.”
“Patients too. Some are scared, but still desperately want to hear what will happen next.”
“…Do you mean that policewoman from before?”
“You said we wouldn’t talk about the hospital today.”
“This is a personal interest, not a discussion about the rota. Two different things.”
“Shall I tell you something even more dangerous?”
Asakura turns to face Sakaguchi and takes two steps backward. As if about to offer a serious professional opinion, she suddenly lowers her voice.
“I’ve always thought surgery is actually like an enormous SM play session.”
“Think about it. Outside, people can walk, sit, and make their own decisions. Once they enter the operating room, so much has to be left to the doctors and nurses.”
“Where they lie, where their hands and feet go, when they can move… It’s their own body, but we set the pace for everything that follows.”
“I know. But don’t you think that mixture of fear, embarrassment, and having to trust someone else… is rather intriguing?”
“I’ve never heard a nurse describe her work that way before.”
“Hehe. That just means the others hide it better.”
“You don’t actually treat patients as playthings, do you?”
“Of course I do my job properly at work. I wouldn’t deliberately disrupt an operation just because I found something amusing.”
“But observing a patient’s reactions is part of a nurse’s skill. Terrified, yet unable to stop asking what comes next—sometimes they’re very easy to read.”
“So you just smile and wait for them to keep asking?”
“If they want to know, I can hardly rush to force the answers on them.”
“…No wonder you were so pleased that day.”
“Still, not every patient feels that way.”
“In all the operations I’ve assisted with, quite a few young women have been both frightened and curious, always wondering what we’ll do next.”
“It doesn’t seem quite as obvious with older patients.”
“I am a nurse, after all. Working out what a patient is actually worried about is part of the job.”
She smiles and turns forward again, casually brushing the windblown hair away from her cheek.
“Come to think of it… for some reason, almost all the patients at our hospital are young women.”
“Dr. Sakaguchi, don’t you think that’s a little strange?”
“I wouldn’t know how to answer that even if you asked me.”
Asakura walks on as though nothing happened, leaving Sakaguchi standing there wondering what exactly he has just been asked.
The light gradually softens. They sit on a bench beside the river. Someone cycles past in the distance, and the bell soon fades into the breeze.
“I can understand now why you don’t want to deal with factions and positions anymore.”
“You’re clearly better at managing people than many others. But from what you’ve said, you seem to know exactly what you don’t want.”
“It took me some time to work that out.”
“You and Serika used to work at the same hospital, didn’t you?”
“You came to Hoshimi together. Did something happen?”
Asakura gazes at the river, slowly gathering up the strap of the small bag beside her. She doesn’t answer right away.
“…Sorry. I shouldn’t have asked so suddenly.”
“You don’t need to apologize. I know you’re curious.”
“There are just some things I don’t want to talk about yet.”
She turns back, still smiling, but this time she isn’t teasing him.
“If you want to get to know me… could you start with who I am now?”
“If you don’t want to talk, I won’t ask.”
The distant river reflects the sunset. Asakura looks away for a moment, then turns back to Sakaguchi as though something has occurred to her.
“There is one thing I’d like to ask you, though.”
“When you can, would you help Serika a little more?”
“Sometimes she struggles to say what she wants to say. You’ve probably noticed that working with her.”
“I can’t tell you those things for her. But if one day she wants to tell you herself… would you hear her out?”
She exhales softly, as though she has finally entrusted him with a small concern that has been on her mind.
“All right—! That’s enough serious talk for today!”
“It’s a rare chance to go on a date. I don’t want the whole thing to feel like a nursing meeting.”
“What would you like to do next?”
“Hmm… First, let’s see if that dessert shop is still open.”
“That was afternoon tea. It’s almost dinnertime now.”
“Your sense of time really does follow its own rules.”
“At the hospital, my time belongs to the patients and everyone else. I want to keep the rest of today for myself.”
“Why else would I have rushed over today? Just to eat a sandwich on my own?”
“You make it sound as if you weren’t late.”
“Oh, Sakaguchi-kun. Could we stop bringing that up for the rest of today?”
Her “Sakaguchi-kun” comes lightly and naturally. As Sakaguchi turns, Asakura is already standing, holding out her hand.
“…All right. I’ll let you off today.”
“Hehe. You really are a good doctor.”
“What does being a doctor have to do with it?”
“You waited for me, listened to me, and will even join me for a second round of dessert. Very high marks.”
Sakaguchi takes her outstretched hand, and they walk along the path toward the shopping street as the streetlights come on.
“Oh, and I’ll definitely be on time for our next date.”
“What time will you set your alarm?”
“…Why don’t you call to wake me up?”
“It’s different. Today I didn’t hear your good morning until three.”
“Next time… I’d like to hear it earlier.”
She smiles, but doesn’t let go of his hand. Warm lights come on in the shop windows ahead.
strings.ui.miyuki.lv3.serika_unmet: Meet Serika Misono before continuing this date. Your Sunday activity has not been used.
strings.collections.character_events.serika_firs: Sakaguchi enters the imaging room. Serika stands before the viewing screen, with several examination images in front of her. Compared with her usual self, she seems unusually quiet.
“Serika? What’s wrong? You don’t look quite yourself.”
Serika turns abruptly, her cheeks bright red and a little defiant moisture still at the corners of her eyes.
She strides up and gives Sakaguchi two thumps on the chest with her fists. They aren’t hard; it is as if she has finally found someone to vent to after holding it in for a long time.
“Do you know how embarrassing surgical preparation is?! Those nurses who normally work alongside me... They were the ones who had to prepare me...!”
“And... having you operate on me yourself... W-was so embarrassing too!!”
“...So that’s what’s been on your mind all this time.”
“Don’t answer me so calmly! I-I was... It was all for you!!”
“I know. Even the preparation that day had you so nervous. ...I couldn’t stop worrying about you either.”
“...Of course you had to stay calm. You were the surgeon... I know that.”
“But that day I couldn’t do anything. I could only lie there... Even though I understood every step, when it was actually my turn, I was still that frightened. ...It’s so frustrating.”
As if suddenly remembering something else, she turns back to the viewing screen and picks up one of her follow-up images.

“Look... I knew I would recover quickly, but I’ve looked at this follow-up image over and over, and I can’t find a single trace of the operation! In the image, it’s as though nothing ever happened... But I remember so clearly lying on the operating table that day, having you operate on me with your own hands... Aah, the more I think about it, the stranger it feels, and the more embarrassing it gets!!”
Serika puts the image back on the desk and covers her flushed face with both hands, refusing to look at Sakaguchi for quite a while.
“You know better than anyone how recovery at Hoshimi works, don’t you?”
“Of course I do! ...Knowing it as a doctor is one thing. Actually being the person lying on the table... is something else entirely.”
She slowly lowers the hands covering her face. This time, the earlier anger is gone; instead, she looks a little bashful.
“...But actually, I rather liked having you operate on me.”
“Those two things don’t contradict each other!”
Having said that, she cannot help laughing a little herself. Then she steps closer and gently leans into Sakaguchi’s arms.
“...I’m not saying the preparation wasn’t embarrassing, or that I wasn’t scared when you operated. ...I was really scared.”
“But... that day you kept taking your work seriously. I knew that everything I had entrusted to you was truly being taken care of.”
“Being with you is so strange... My feelings are all tangled up. I feel uneasy, and frightened... yet I also feel so safe.”
“To think those two feelings can exist at the same time... It’s so strange...”
“...Ryuji. Wherever I go in the future, I hope you’ll stay with me... always stay with me...”
“...Yes. I’ll be there for you. Whenever anything worries you, tell me, all right? You don’t have to bear it alone.”
Serika nods softly in his arms. After a while, she raises her face and puts on a little of her usual cool expression again.
“...And one more thing. Don’t tell anyone what happened here today.”
“You mean those two thumps you gave me?”
Sakaguchi smiles and nods. Serika rests her forehead against his chest again. The camera lingers on the image on the viewing screen, now completely normal, then fades out.
strings.collections.character_events.serika_lv5_: Only the light above the workstation is on in the imaging room. Serika sits before the viewing monitor, checking a report line by line.
She checks the last line and presses Save before noticing Sakaguchi standing by the door.
“Sakaguchi-kun. Give me a moment. I'm almost done.”
“No rush. I was just passing by and wondered whether you'd finished.”
“You don't often hear ‘no rush’ in the imaging room.”
Serika sends off the report, takes off her glasses, and sets them at the corner of the desk. An opened document envelope lies beside them.
“Did you have something else to do today?”
“I went to see the police this morning.”
“Yes. I told them everything I knew. There is still a lot to verify, so I may have to go again.”
“If they need me to testify in court, I'll go.”
She smooths the edge of the envelope, as though organizing a complicated imaging report.
“It was actually calmer than I'd expected. Whatever they asked, I tried to answer as accurately as I could.”
“Only after saying some things aloud did I realize how many times I'd already repeated them in my head.”
“Nanami is still recovering slowly. She messaged me today, too. She said several of the others had safely left the old hospital.”
“Aya, Yayoi, Eri… Where they want to work next should be for them to decide.”
“I'd be happy if they wanted to come to Hoshimi. But I don't want ‘for their own good’ to turn into making their decisions for them again.”
She puts the envelope away, and her phone screen lights up. Serika glances at the call history but takes a long time to lock the screen.
“…Yes. He called once this morning, but I didn't answer. Today, I want to call him back myself.”
“But right now, I don't quite want to walk over there alone.”
“I'll walk with you to the courtyard. When you want to talk alone, I'll step away.”
“I'll wait nearby. There's no rush to talk.”
“I'll walk with you to the courtyard. When you want to talk alone, I'll step away.”
“…All right. You always know when to stand a little closer.”
“I'll wait nearby. There's no rush to talk.”
“I haven't even said anything yet… and you've already left me a way out.”
Serika changes out of her white coat, picks up her handbag, and leaves the imaging room with Sakaguchi.
“After the call, I'm meeting Miyuki for coffee.”
“Sounds like a busy day for you, then.”
“…I planned it myself. Just thinking about that feels a little unbelievable.”
In the courtyard at dusk, tree shadows cover half a bench. Serika stops beside it, holding her phone.
She looks down at the number on the screen, her thumb hovering over the call button.
“…A moment ago, I thought I was ready.”
“Sakaguchi-kun, would you wait over there for a moment?”
“Of course. I'll be by the covered walkway.”
After Sakaguchi walks away, Serika sits down and finds her father's number again. She takes a deep breath and calls.
“It's me. I saw your call this morning.”
“You finally called. I thought… Never mind. How have you been feeling lately?”
“I'm well. I'm still working at Hoshimi. I spent today reading scans as usual.”
“I heard you went to help with the investigation.”
“Yes. I'll keep going. I don't intend to hide what I know anymore.”
“…I've been thinking back over what happened at the hospital, too.”
“Back then, I was so focused on whether the hospital was running properly that I never really asked how you were getting through each day.”
“Father. I didn't call today to place all the blame on you.”
“There's something… I have to tell you myself.”
Her other hand slowly clenches the fabric of her skirt. She holds the phone to her ear, but for a while, no sound comes.
“Shiozaki tried to force me to hurt you. He even… wanted me to poison your medicine.”
“I didn't do it. In the end, Miyuki got me out of there.”
“But for a time, I came so close that I couldn't even be certain I wouldn't do what he told me.”
“I didn't want someone else's statement to be the first place you heard about this.”
There is a long silence on the other end. Serika does not hurry him; she simply waits with her eyes lowered.
“I don't know what to say right now. I had no idea you'd been pushed that far.”
“I didn't call to ask you to forgive me right away, either.”
“I want to hear you out first. This time, at least let me listen properly.”
“I'll deal with the hospital myself, too. You don't have to tell me on the phone today whether you'll come back to take over.”
“I haven't decided yet. For now, I want to stay at Hoshimi.”
“All right. Then make a good life for yourself there for now.”
“When you have time, come home for a meal. Just a meal at home, not a meeting.”
Serika lifts her head. The sunlight has already moved off the other end of the bench.
“…All right. I'll call you when I can find the time.”
“…And thank you for being willing to call.”
The call ends. Serika rests the phone on her lap and sits quietly for a while before wiping a little moisture from the corner of her eye with a finger.
Sakaguchi returns from the covered walkway and stops a step away from her.
“Yes. …We were finally able to really talk.”
“But I think there's one more person I need to talk things through with today.”
“Yes. I want to see her on my own tonight. I'll come find you afterward.”
Serika stands and gives Sakaguchi a small nod. After a few steps, her stride is much steadier than when she arrived.
Miyuki Asakura is already seated by the café window. Two drinks sit on the table, and she is studying a small plate of sweets.
“Not at all. I made a point of coming early today. Don't I deserve some praise?”
“You actually got here before me today?”
“That's why I said I deserve praise. Sit down. I haven't touched the dessert yet.”
Serika sits across from her and takes the menu she offers. A glance at the drinks on the table brings a hint of surprise to her face.
“Of course. We worked together for so long. I'm not about to forget a little thing like that.”
They pick up their cups. Asakura tries a bite of dessert first, while Serika merely runs a fingertip around the rim of her cup.
“Did you go to see the police today?”
“Yes. I've told them everything I could.”
“That must have been hard. If it's my turn later, I'll go, too.”
“Nanami told me Aya and the others have all left the old hospital.”
“I heard, too. Let them get some proper rest first. They don't need to decide about work right now.”
“I used to think that if I could just bring everyone back, we could start all over again.”
“The people you bring back might not want to start over, you know.”
“…Yes. So I thought I'd ask each of them what they wanted first.”
Asakura nods and puts down her fork. Serika sets her cup back on its saucer and looks directly at her.
“Miyuki. I called my father today, too.”
“Really? Haven't you been too afraid to call him?”
“I was still very afraid. But this time… we actually talked like a father and daughter for a while.”
“And I finally felt that I could talk to you properly about the past.”
Asakura's smile slowly fades. She puts down the fork in her hand and sits up straight.
“When we were at that hospital, you pressured me on Shiozaki's orders, too.”
“You knew I was afraid. For a while, whenever I saw you coming toward me, I'd wonder whether something else was about to happen.”
“Yes. You had every reason to hate me.”
“I was afraid back then, too. I wanted to protect myself. But that doesn't make what I did disappear. I'm sorry, Serika.”
Serika does not answer at once. She looks at the pedestrians passing outside the window, then turns back after a while.
“But in the end, you were also the one who took me away.”
“I still remember that day. You called out to me, took my hand, and told me I didn't have to listen to him anymore.”
“At the time, I just… couldn't bear to watch him drag you down any further.”
“I know. So I've also kept feeling that I owed you for the rest of my life.”
“Serika, you don't have to pretend the things I did never happened just because you're grateful to me.”
“And I didn't take you away so you'd owe me a favor.”
“…It took me a long time to understand that both things could be true.”
“You hurt me, and I really am grateful to you.”
“That's right. Here we are, safe and sound, drinking coffee together.”
“…I'm just happy we can sit together like this.”
Asakura reaches out and gently lays her hand over Serika's on the table. Serika does not pull away.
“Miyuki. If one day I really decide to return to the old hospital… would you come with me and be the head nurse?”
“Oh my, are you already poaching Hoshimi's staff?”
“I'm only asking. You've always understood how to care for a whole team better than I do.”
“Hold on. You haven't decided yourself yet. There's no need to arrange my job for me.”
“I have it so easy at Hoshimi right now. The pay is decent, my colleagues are interesting, and no one's insisting I become someone important.”
“…You're right. I shouldn't make your decision for you just because I'd miss you.”
“When you've really made up your mind, come and ask me properly. I'll give it serious thought, too.”
“All right. I'll wait for your answer.”
“And I haven't agreed to be head nurse, you know. If you really want me back, you'd better offer a higher salary.”
“…I'll make a note of your price.”
“Right now? You really haven't changed a bit.”
Serika finally smiles. She picks up her coffee, which has cooled a little, and slowly finishes it with Asakura.
When they leave the café, they walk side by side to the intersection. Asakura waves and heads toward the hospital, while Serika takes another street to her own rendezvous.
Night has fallen. Standing beside a streetlamp outside the hospital, Sakaguchi sees Serika come around the corner.
“…I had coffee with Miyuki and said a lot of things I'd never dared to say before.”
“A little. But it's easier than keeping all those words hidden.”
She slips her arm through Sakaguchi's. They walk slowly along the pavement, passing a row of small shops with their shutters already down.
“My father asked me to come home for a meal when I have time.”
“He specifically said he wasn't asking me back for a meeting. …I nearly laughed on the phone.”
“Then he knows what you're worried about.”
“Perhaps he didn't before. Today, at least, he was willing to hear me out.”
Serika holds his arm a little tighter but keeps walking.
“It was the same with Miyuki. We finally talked about how we hurt each other at the old hospital.”
“I used to think that because she'd saved me, I shouldn't resent her anymore.”
“She said I could remember both things. …I think she's right.”
“So where does that leave you two?”
“Still friends. Perhaps better able to be friends than before.”
“I even asked whether she'd come back with me someday as head nurse.”
“No. First she quoted me a very high price.”
“And she was right. I don't even know whether I want to go back. What gives me the right to plan someone else's future first?”
“Sakaguchi-kun. Do you think I'm still too indecisive?”
“If you want to stay now, then stay without worrying. If you change your mind later, we can talk again.”
“I want to know what you want to do. I don't want to decide for you.”
“If you want to stay now, then stay without worrying. If you change your mind later, we can talk again.”
“…So I can be heard this sincerely even without rushing to make a promise.”
“I want to know what you want to do. I don't want to decide for you.”
“…From someone else, that might sound cold. From you, it makes me feel safe.”
“For now, I want to stay at Hoshimi. Work in diagnostic imaging, and assist in surgery when I'm needed.”
“Perhaps one day I'll want to go back and see whether the old hospital can really start over. Perhaps I won't.”
“But at least I don't have to give anyone an answer tonight.”
“And… if that day really comes, I'd like to hear what you think first.”
“When you want to talk, I'll listen.”
Serika stops, turns to face Sakaguchi, and looks up at him for a moment.
“What is it? We're lovers, aren't we? May I not call you that?”
“Of course you can. It's just the first time I've heard you say it, so I was a little surprised.”
Serika freezes for a moment, then turns her face away. Under the streetlamp, the tips of her ears turn faintly red.
They walk on a little farther. Serika suddenly lifts her head, as though recalling an important piece of work.
“By the way. That thing you've been doing… where hospital staff volunteer to take part in surgical practice as patients.”
“You mean the hospital's surgical practice program?”
“Yes. I used to think it was absurd.”
“I still think it's… a little absurd.”
She lets out a small laugh at her own words, then looks seriously at Sakaguchi.
“But if you'd like, I could take part in the future, too.”
“I know. I used to stand on the other side of the operating table.”
“I know what needs to be prepared and explained beforehand. But that doesn't mean I won't be afraid at all when I'm actually lying there.”
“…I want to try trusting my own choice, and trusting you.”
“When the time comes, I'll follow the full patient process and carefully explain and confirm everything with you.”
“When you really want to arrange that day, we'll talk it through properly. There's no rush now.”
“When the time comes, I'll follow the full patient process and carefully explain and confirm everything with you.”
“Good. Don't skip what needs explaining just because I understand it.”
“When you really want to arrange that day, we'll talk it through properly. There's no rush now.”
“…You're getting better at knowing whose decision it should be.”
“But let me make this clear first. I'm volunteering. It's not to atone for anything, or to prove to anyone that I still deserve to be a doctor.”
“What operation, when to have it, and how to prepare—we'll discuss those when I actually apply someday.”
“And—if I'm a nervous wreck when the time comes, you're not allowed to laugh.”
“I'll take you seriously, just as I would any other patient.”
“But if I can barely get my words out then, don't tease me with ‘Doesn't Dr. Misono know all about this?’”
Serika looks at Sakaguchi, and the trace of feigned sternness finally leaves her face. She leans gently against his shoulder.
“It's strange. I used to think that shouldering everything myself was the only right thing to do.”
“Now, just walking beside you like this makes me feel… I can leave tomorrow's worries for tomorrow.”
She lifts her hand and interlaces her fingers with Sakaguchi's. Neither is in a hurry as they continue along the lamplit street.
“Walk with me a little longer tonight.”
strings.collections.surgery_team_dialogue_profil: “Scrub nurse? I do not normally work in the operating room... I will follow the checklist, but please tell me clearly which instruments you need, Dr. Sakaguchi.”
“Me, at the instrument table? A-all right. I will review the names beforehand. Please tell me immediately if I pick up the wrong one.”
“Understood, I will handle the instruments. I do not have much operating-room experience, though, so I may not anticipate the next step like a dedicated scrub nurse.”
“Circulating nurse... I will keep a close eye on the records and supplies, but please go over the operating-room procedures with me again.”
“All right, I will circulate. If I fall behind, please call my name directly. I am worried I might miss an instruction.”
“I can try circulating, though it is not a role I am familiar with. I will check the monitoring and records one item at a time.”

strings.collections.character_events.miyuki_lv4_: After finishing our daytime shift at the hospital, Asakura lured me out with a claim that there was an "off-site training facility" she absolutely wanted Dr. Sakaguchi to inspect with her—leaving me standing inside a themed private suite decorated to look just like a clinic examination room.

A dark-green leather flat examination bed, and in the corner, a replica motorized gynecological chair complete with curved leg rests. Everything down to the kidney dish and disinfectant jars on the stainless-steel trolley is in place—except instead of the sharp chlorine smell of a hospital, a faint woody incense lingers in the air.
"Sorry to keep you waiting, Dr. Sakaguchi. Look—doesn't this place's nurse uniform fit me even better than I imagined?"

The curtain of the changing partition is drawn back. Asakura has changed into a pink one-piece nurse dress cut closer at the waist than Hoshimi Hospital's standard issue, with a noticeably shorter hem. A silver dual-head stethoscope hangs around her neck as she stands beside the steel trolley, unhurriedly peeling open a pack of sterile latex exam gloves.
"Wearing a nurse uniform at the hospital every day isn't enough for you, so the moment we clock out, you drag me to a medical-themed roleplay club... You really do love hospitals, don't you?"
"At the hospital, it's called work. Coming here after hours is what you call a personal hobby."
Her lips curve into an easy smile. With light, silent steps, she circles around to my side, her fingers casually resting on the suite's doorknob—
*Click.* She turns the thumb-lock, and above the doorframe, a replica crimson sign reading "EXAM IN PROGRESS - DO NOT DISTURB" flickers on.
"Counting our ward shifts over the past few days, you've already taken me—the 'new nurse'—along to personally perform quite a few pre-op preparations in the wards, haven't you, Dr. Sakaguchi?"

"Every time I stood by the curtain assisting you, watching you put on your gloves with such a serious face, asking young female patients to lift their gowns, and saying in that gentle, irresistible voice, 'This will be a little cold, so please spread your legs a bit wider for me'... I always thought how amazing you were."
"That's standard clinical pre-op assessment and sterile verification procedure. Stop summarizing it in such a weird way."
"I've been learning from you very seriously, Doctor. Still, if I only watch and never practice, how will I ever know if my technique actually passes the test?"
She pinches the cuff of a latex glove and gives it a tug. With a crisp *snap*, the thin milky-white latex wraps snugly around her five fingers.

"So for today's 'special off-site practice'—first, I'd like to ask Dr. Sakaguchi to lie down on this flat exam bed so I can give you a pre-op physical exam. And once I'm done... it'll be my turn to sit on that gynecological exam chair over there. How does that sound?"
"First things first—since we're doing roleplay in a place like this, we need to set the rules and boundaries clearly."
"The moment you snapped those gloves on, I had a feeling this wouldn't be a simple physical exam."
"Hehe, leave it to the thorough Dr. Sakaguchi to insist on pre-op informed consent even when playing a game."
"When dealing with someone like you who's an expert at setting traps with a smile, I'd be crazy not to clarify the boundaries first."
"Oh my, usually you're the one who's best at coaxing patients to relax in the treatment room, Doctor. Why are you suddenly so on guard now that it's your turn to lie down?"
"Because I know all too well how much mischief you hide behind that gentle smile. Before anything else, let's be clear about how far we're going today."

"Alright. Since this is a private exam room just for the two of us, the rules are naturally yours to set, Dr. Sakaguchi. Whether it's instruments that are off-limits or a safeword to make me stop, I'll follow your lead completely."

"First, those replica metal instruments and catheters on the trolley are strictly for show—no genuinely invasive actions. Second, if either of us actually feels uncomfortable or calls a stop, we stop immediately."
"Understood. No invasive procedures that could actually hurt, and the moment Ryuji seriously says 'stop,' I promise I won't touch you for even a second longer."
Smiling, she holds up two latex-gloved fingers—half playful conspirator, half reassuringly measured. Then her tone shifts, dropping a little lower:

"In return, though—as long as we're still within the safe boundaries we just agreed on, even if Mr. Patient stubbornly says 'wait a second' halfway through, a responsible nurse won't let you off the hook so easily, okay?"

Before I can take even half a step back, Asakura closes the distance with a smile. Pressing her latex-gloved hand against my chest with deceptively deft leverage, a light push is all it takes to back me up against the edge of the white-sheeted examination bed.

My back rests against the cool dark-green leather mattress. Asakura stands by the bedside, the indoor gooseneck light slanting across her shoulders and throwing the tailored silhouette of her nurse dress into sharp relief.
"First is chest auscultation and abdominal palpation. Mr. Sakaguchi, please unbutton your jacket and shirt... Or would you prefer the nurse to undo your buttons one by one with her own hands?"
"Too slow. I'll have to deduct points for that."
My hand has barely reached my collar when Asakura's latex-gloved fingertips slip between my fingers, pressing my wrist back down onto the bedsheet at my side.

Her movements are startlingly practiced—without even looking down closely, her fingertips work as crisply as if tying sutures at the operating table, flicking open my row of shirt buttons in seconds and sweeping the front wide open to both sides.
"...With unbuttoning speed like that, do you really expect me to believe you were just an ordinary ward nurse before coming to Hoshimi?"
"Who knows? Maybe I've just spent so much time watching how you dress at work, Doctor, that I've memorized even which button is a little tight."

The room air brushes against my bare chest and abdomen. Asakura lifts the silver dual-head stethoscope hanging around her neck, deliberately skipping the usual step of warming it in her palm for a patient, and presses the icy metal chestpiece straight against the apical impulse over my left chest.

"Ah, sorry, sorry—I forgot to warm the stethoscope up for you, Mr. Sakaguchi. When you tell the girls 'This will be a little cold, please bear with it,' they probably make the exact same face you just did, don't they?"

As the cold metal disc rests firmly against my chest, she leans forward slightly, the front of her nurse uniform nearly brushing my arm with her posture. The rubber tubing of the stethoscope dangles across my chest, swaying gently with each breath.

"Thump, thump, thump... Your heart rate is up by nearly twenty beats compared to when we walked in, Mr. Sakaguchi. We already promised not to use any real instruments, so why are you still this nervous?"
"When you're leaning in so close your collar is practically against my face, any normal man's heart rate would speed up."
"Is that so? Then I'll have to make a careful differential diagnosis—whether it's tension from lying on the exam table, or some other unruly reaction."

She removes the stethoscope and sets it on the tray, then slowly lays her latex-gloved right palm over my upper abdomen. The slight, clingy friction unique to thin latex mingles with the heat of her fingertips as she presses and glides inch by inch down from just below my xiphoid process.
"Your abdominal wall is a little tense. Take a deep breath for me—inhale... That's right, now exhale slowly."

The instant I exhale and my abdominal muscles relax, her fingertips suddenly draw together. Using the pads of her index and middle fingers, she traces slowly and steadily straight down my linea alba, from above my navel all the way toward my pubic symphysis.
The trajectory is so surgical in its precision that it sends an instant shiver across my scalp—it is the exact marking line for a standard lower midline laparotomy.
"Say, Dr. Sakaguchi... Every time I hand you a scalpel in the operating room, I find myself wondering."

"If the person lying under the shadowless lamp were you instead, Dr. Sakaguchi... with your stomach completely exposed just like this, while I drew a black marker line right down here and pretended to incise the skin and fascia inch by inch—what kind of expression would you show me?"
"Hey, Miyuki... That kind of hypothetical is way too dangerous for a surgeon to hear."

"You call it dangerous, yet when my fingers traced that 'incision line' down to the bottom just now, the muscles in your lower belly clearly clenched tight. And besides... didn't you just call me 'Miyuki' directly?"

Leaving me no room to cover it up, her fingers glide along the edge of my lower abdomen down to the waistband of my trousers. The metal belt buckle gives a soft clink at her touch, and my zipper is drawn halfway down, exposing the edge of my briefs and the taut lines of my groin on either side.

"Strictly speaking, the skin prep inspection area for a lower abdominal surgery has to be checked all the way down to the pubis and bilateral inguinal regions. Even though I promised not to do any actual catheterization... checking through your clothes for abnormal local engorgement is completely within the rules, right?"

With her other hand, she picks up the round-tipped surgical marker from the tray. Using the cool, rounded plastic end of the cap, she presses lightly through the briefs already warmed by my body heat, right against the outline straining beneath, slowly tracing a circle from base to tip.
"...! You're being way too thorough with this inspection..."

"Oh my... Pressing up this hard while a female nurse is examining you—isn't Mr. Patient being a little too naughty? Still... my first-half experience playing the nurse is more than satisfied right here."
Catch her wrist holding the marker: "If the first half is over, then it's your turn to go sit on that gynecological exam chair over there."
Pull her by the waist and sit up: "Since you say the patient isn't behaving, why don't you get on the gynecological chair and demonstrate what an obedient patient looks like?"
"Kya...! Even though you're still half-lying on the bed with your shirt undone, the look in your eyes when you grabbed my wrist turned right back into the attending surgeon's..."
"You're the one who said it when we walked in—once you finished examining me, it'd be your turn over there."
"Mmn...! Wait, if you pull my waist like that, I'm going to lose my balance...!"
"No backing out now, Nurse Asakura. You had plenty of fun with your exam just now—now it's your turn to get on that gynecological chair."

With the soft clatter of the marker rolling onto the tray, I rise from the flat exam bed. Asakura, who had been dictating the pace so effortlessly until a moment ago, doesn't pull back; following the tug on her wrist, she walks deeper into the suite, lifts the hem of her nurse dress, and seats herself on the replica motorized gynecological exam chair.
"Hehe... Now it really is my turn. But Dr. Sakaguchi, since this is a proper gynecological exam chair... shouldn't the doctor personally set my positioning for me?"
"Being hurried along by someone who sleeps until three on a Sunday afternoon before telling me 'good morning' doesn't carry much weight."

"Mmn... Are you planning to hold that oversleeping incident over my head forever, Ryuji? I'm always on my best behavior assisting you in the wards, and now that I'm already sitting on the exam chair, don't just bring up old scores..."

She leans back against the reclined backrest of the gynecological chair, the heat rising all the way to the tips of her ears impossible to hide. Standing directly in front of the chair, I cradle her white-stockinged ankles in both hands, slowly lifting her legs one by one and settling them securely into the curved padded stirrups on either side.

As the standard lithotomy position takes shape with her legs spread and supported in the stirrups, the hem of her pink nurse dress slides naturally down to the base of her thighs, leaving the outline of her lavender lace panties completely unshielded under the light.
"Mmn... I've helped set the leg rests for other girls so many times in gynecology and the OR, but having Ryuji spread my own legs and place them up here by hand... even my toes are curling up..."

Her breathing is noticeably quicker now, yet she still raises her latex-gloved hands and—*pop, pop, pop*—unfastens the three snap buttons at the chest of her nurse dress right in front of me. The crisp pink collar parts to either side, revealing her chest cupped in a lavender lace demi-bra beneath her collarbones, rising and falling with each breath.
"Go ahead, Dr. Sakaguchi. Since I'm already sitting on this exam chair... whether it's a full-body palpation or a much deeper examination today, I'm leaving it all to you."
"You're the one who climbed up here. Until you say 'stop,' you're going to stay still and cooperate no matter how awkward the posture gets."
"Yes... Please do as you like, my attending doctor."
Leaning in between the parted stirrups, I pin her wrists beside the headrest with one hand, lower my head, and press my lips directly onto hers.

The instant our lips meet, a muffled hum slips from Asakura's nose. With her legs held apart in the stirrups, she has nowhere to brace herself, tilting her chin up to meet me as her tongue slips eagerly against mine amidst quick, feverish breaths.

Amidst the deep kiss, my free hand slips inside the open front of her nurse dress, cupping the fullness cradled in lace. With a light flick of my fingers, I push the demi-bra upward, and the resilient flesh springs into my palm along with a pale pink tip already stiffening to the touch.
"Ah... haah, nnh...! Ryuji's hand... is so much hotter than the stethoscope just now..."

"Patient Asakura, the skin temperature from the upper outer quadrant of your right breast to the areola is noticeably elevated, and your nipple is already this firm... Is this supposed to be a normal clinical sign too?"

"Nnh... Now who's being mean... You're the one circling and kneading right there with your thumb... With my legs held open on the exam chair so I can't even close them, anyone would react being 'palpated' like this by the person they love... Ah, don't graze the tip with your fingernail like that...!"

I dip my head to take one peak into my mouth, my tongue swirling around the areola, while my right hand glides down across her taut stomach—following the exact midline laparotomy path she had traced on me earlier—all the way to the edge of the seat cushion, pressing through the lace panties already damp and hot against the cleft laid wide open by the lithotomy position.
"Kyaa...! W-Wait a second... Ryuji, with my legs up on the rests I can't pull back at all... touching me straight down there before even doing sterile prep... mmn!"
"Who was it that teased me for not behaving a minute ago? Yet the moment you sit on the gynecological chair yourself, haven't you already soaked your panties under your skirt?"

"That's because... usually I'm the one standing beside the table watching others get flustered, so having Ryuji put my legs up in the stirrups and pin my wrists overhead... With even my most private place laid bare to you, my body can't slow down at all... Haah...!"

The back of her neck arches against the headrest, her long hair spilling across the white pad. Pushing the soaked gusset of her panties aside, I slide my fingers half an inch along the slick folds, immediately met by a tight clench from within.

At the same time, her wrists—now freed from my grip—loop around my shoulders, and her hand still clad in the sterile latex glove reaches down between us, wrapping around my aching, fever-hot shaft through the smooth, cool film of latex.

"Haah... Holding you here while wearing an exam glove, Ryuji... I can feel every single pulse beating so clearly... Since I'm already positioned on the exam chair and this ready for you, won't my attending doctor begin the deepest examination right away...?"

Her legs resting in the stirrups tremble slightly as she parts them even wider. Guiding my tip to her slick, parted entrance with her gloved fingertips, she tilts her flushed cheek back, welcoming me as I stand before the exam chair and sink inside her inch by inch.

"Mmn... aah...! I-It's in... so deep... Being filled up bit by bit from the front by Ryuji while kept in a gynecological exam position... it feels like you're pressing all the way against my very deepest spot...!"

Her slick, tight walls envelop me without a single gap. Her half-open white nurse dress spreads across the backrest of the exam chair while her white-stockinged calves resting in the stirrups sway with every movement, her gloved knuckles gripping the edge of the seat cushion pulling taut.

Bracing the base of her thighs inside the leg rests, I drive into her in steady, deep strokes. Asakura wraps both arms tightly around my neck, pressing her hot cheek against my ear, letting out unguarded, breathless whimpers every time we meet at the deepest point.

"Nnh, mmn... Ryuji... a little deeper... Ah, right there... It feels like even the most sensitive place deep inside me is being pressed over and over... My mind's going completely blank... it feels so good...!"
"Yes...! Don't stop, Ryuji... Whether it's on this exam chair today, or from now on... I'm leaving everything in your hands alone... Together... aah...!"

After several consecutive, deep thrusts straight to her core, the insteps of Asakura's feet resting in the stirrups arch tautly, her five latex-gloved fingers clutching my back as a long, shuddering contraction tightens around me, carrying both of us into the lingering heat of complete release.

Moments later, only the sound of our gradually steadying breaths remains in the suite. I reach out first to lift Asakura's weak legs down from the stirrups and help her sit up. She nestles in my arms to catch her breath for a long while before reaching for wet tissues to wipe both of us clean, then peels off the crumpled latex gloves and tosses them into the bin.
"Phew... So when I actually sit on the gynecological exam chair and get worked over like that by you, Ryuji, it's the kind of feeling that makes even my fingertips tingle."
She glances around the elaborately furnished themed suite, lightly tapping the armrest of the replica exam chair beneath her as her lips curve into a playful smile tinged with professional critique:

"Still, come to think of it, the instruments and exam table in a shop like this aren't quite realistic enough compared to a real hospital... Then again, on a date, sometimes being *too* realistic wouldn't be any fun either."
"You're complaining it's not realistic enough after going that far? And who was it on that exam chair just now being ten times more honest than she ever is at the hospital?"

Asakura lets out a soft laugh. Reaching out, she carefully buttons my shirt back up one button at a time and smooths down my collar before unhurriedly fastening the snap buttons across the chest of her own nurse uniform, looking up at me with unmistakable warmth.
"That's because it's you, Ryuji. Whether it's teasing you like usual, or lying back obediently at your mercy like just now, you're the only one I'd ever let do those things to me."
"Then when we're back on shift at the hospital tomorrow, whose boyfriend is it that'll be having you assist him in the treatment room?"
"...Hehe, whose else could you be? Though if you dare call yourself that at the nurses' station during work hours, a responsible nurse will have to deduct points from you, Mr. Boyfriend."

Her eyes crinkle into a smile as she leans in to press a light kiss to the corner of my lips, then rests her head quietly against my shoulder for a moment. As if the lingering warmth reminded her of something that genuinely fascinates her, she looks up and speaks softly:

"Say, Ryuji... While I was lying on the exam chair just now, something suddenly crossed my mind. In the future, if there's ever a real **unanesthetized surgery** at the hospital—the kind of special operation where the patient stays wide awake from start to finish—please be sure to include me on the team, okay?"
"A real unanesthetized surgery? Operations like that are extremely demanding on both instrument handling and keeping the patient calm at the table. Why the sudden interest?"

"Precisely because the patient is entrusting her body to the operating surgeon while wide awake, that kind of tension needs an experienced nurse beside her holding her hand and steadying her emotions. Speaking of patients—a young policewoman I know named **Chie Sagamiono** happens to be planning to visit our outpatient clinic at Hoshimi Hospital soon for a minor health issue."
Changing back into her everyday clothes, Asakura picks up her handbag, walks over to the suite door to turn the lock, and looks back at me with a meaningful smile.

"That girl always puts on such a tough front at the police station, so if a formal examination shows she actually needs surgery and has to lie down on the operating table, wouldn't that be fascinating? Whether it's our work at the hospital or our next date together... I'll be looking forward to all of it, Ryuji."
Today I’ll Be Doing the Exam
