strings.collections.character_events.ev_doc_take: Nine o'clock in the morning, Operating Room 2. Since Tae Takemi was officially cleared to join our surgical roster, this is a routine awake laparotomy with me as lead surgeon and her assisting across the table.

Beneath the shadowless lamp, the young female patient on the table has been given no general anesthesia. As my scalpel steadily incises the right anterior rectus sheath and peritoneum, the warm, living structures inside her abdominal cavity come into view.
"D-Dr. Sakaguchi, the retractors and warm saline laparotomy pads are ready..."
"No need to pack the gauze in so quickly, Sakaguchi. Just look at this girl's mesenteric vascular arcades—without anesthetic hypotension dulling them, they're pulsing like a work of art."

Across the table, Takemi's eyes gleam above her mask. Gripping the abdominal wall retractor with her sterile-gloved hands, she sinks her wrists outward with practiced ease—widening an incision that was originally standard length by a full margin.

"Mmph...! W-Wait a second, Doctor... My stomach is being pulled so tight to both sides... I-I held still when you cut me open just now, but spreading it this wide makes my insides feel so strange...!"
"Takemi, the exposure is already plenty wide for me to work. You don't need to crank the retractor to the maximum."
"It's a rare opportunity. Hey, little scrub nurse holding the tray over there—Honjo, was it? Lean in a bit closer."

Moe inches forward half a step timidly. Using atraumatic tissue forceps, Takemi gently lifts the patient's faintly moving with peristalsis terminal ileum and mesenteric root, pointing them out as if giving a demonstration in a university lecture hall:

"All you ever see in nursing textbooks are lifeless illustrations, right? Look closely right here—while the patient is awake, the moment my forceps lightly graze the serosa, the bowel contracts and pulls away on its own, and you can watch every tiny vasa recta beating one pulse after another."
"Whoa... It's really moving on its own...! So this is what living internal organs actually look like... It's so much clearer than the diagrams in our textbook..."
"Uu...! Um, Doctors, Nurse... Please don't discuss the quality of the teaching material right in front of the teaching material herself while rummaging around inside my belly...!"
"Alright, Professor Takemi's live anatomy lecture is adjourned. Moe, hand me the curved hemostat; Takemi, hold the retractor steady for me so we can address the lesion."
"Tch, how strict. Still, your incision is remarkably clean, without a single drop of wasted bleeding—assisting a lead surgeon like you isn't half bad."

By the time the operation wraps up smoothly and the patient is wheeled back to the ward for observation, it is just past eleven. Following the stairs down to the Underground Research Lab on the lowest level of the hospital, I push open the door to find Tae Takemi lounging in her swivel chair with her long legs crossed, sipping an iced coffee.
"Yo, Lead Surgeon. What brings you down here—delivering a lecture on behalf of that little Director Shiromiya, or settling the score with me for widening the retractor at the table?"

"If I wanted to lecture you, I would've done it at the scrub sink. Though after Moe blurted out that your explanation was clearer than a textbook, the girls at the nurses' station have fresh material for their hospital ghost stories about you."
"Ghost stories? Let me guess—are they whispering again that 'that woman named Takemi in the basement is actually a madwoman whose ultimate hobby is performing vivisections on living people'?"
"Then I'll ask the woman herself—is your ultimate hobby really vivisection?"
"Watching the patient's awake reactions at the table earlier, you looked even more thrilled than I was as lead surgeon."
"Haha, aside from that girl Shiromiya, you're the first person in this hospital with the nerve to ask me that to my face."
"After standing across the table from you through a whole operation, pretending not to notice would be harder."
"Look who's talking, Dr. Sakaguchi. A man who cuts that steadily without a drop of anesthesia has no business calling me a freak."
"I do it for clinical training and special indications. Meanwhile, the nurses are whispering that your ultimate hobby is 'vivisection.'"
"Laypeople have given the word 'vivisection' such an ugly ring. As if the mere mention of dissecting a living body means you have to torture the subject to death on the table."
Setting down her coffee cup, she leans forward slightly, her dark-painted lips curving into a matter-of-fact smile:
"Back when I was in middle school, we had a frog dissection lab in biology class. The whole class was making a huge fuss, snipping their frogs' bellies into a mangled mess."
"I found it baffling—if our goal was simply to observe the beating heart, the expanding lungs, and the course of the intestines in a living state, why did everyone assume the frog had to die?"

"I opened the abdominal cavity while avoiding every major vessel, observed every single beating organ inside from top to bottom, and finished my anatomical drawings; then I used the finest suture needle and thread I'd brought from home to close it back up layer by layer, and flipped it back over on the wax tray."
"It kicked its hind legs and hopped right off the lab table on its own."
She delivers the line with utter calm, as though recounting nothing more remarkable than a home-economics sewing assignment.
"...Your biology teacher's face must have been a sight to behold."

"The teacher nearly dropped his lesson plan. And doesn't the exact same logic apply here at Hoshimi Hospital? Since our medical safeguards guarantee that no matter how wide we open an incision or how thoroughly we examine the organs inside, the patient will heal without a scratch once sutured back up—what's wrong with taking a closer look while she's wide awake and her organs are pulsing right in front of us?"
"So Director Shiromiya banned you from routine lead surgery because you wanted to treat patients like that middle-school frog?"

"I only opened that last case a little deeper than usual—who knew the hydraulic bracket on the old operating table in OR 3 was so flimsy it would jam halfway through? That girl Shiromiya made a mountain out of a molehill, claiming if I kept cutting I'd dismantle the patient and the table together."
Leaning lazily back against her chair, she looks me up and down with the amused glint of someone who has found a kindred spirit:

"Still, standing across from you as first assistant is surprisingly pleasant. At least when I widened the retractor earlier, your hands didn't waver a millimeter—in fact, your eyes looked even more focused than mine."
"As long as it doesn't get in the way of the actual procedure, I don't mind letting you slip in a two-minute anatomy lesson for the rookies."

"The only downside is that ordinary patients are still too squeamish. Even without anesthesia, the second you pull the retractor two centimeters wider or reach inside to turn over a loop of bowel, they start hollering in pain and ruin the quiet."
Resting her index finger lightly against her chin, Takemi lets out a wistful sigh as if making a casual wish:

"If only a **patient who naturally feels no pain at all** would walk into our clinic one day. No anesthesia needed, and no screaming when we open her up... If a case like that ever shows up, I'll go straight to Shiromiya for a special-approval lead surgery permit, draft you as my first assistant, and inspect a living abdominal cavity from top to bottom to my heart's content."

"What are the odds of that? If someone actually had congenital insensitivity to pain, she wouldn't even notice when she fell ill—by the time she walked into a hospital, who knows how badly her insides would have festered."

"Wouldn't that make it even more fascinating? We'd get to admire healthy living anatomy *and* clean up a complex mess in one go. ...Alright, it's hampir twelve noon—go grab your lunch, partner. And if you have any more unanesthetized cases this afternoon, be sure to call me."
Who Said Vivisection Has to Be Fatal?
Who Said Vivisection Has to Be Fatal?
Who Said Vivisection Has to Be Fatal?

Nine o'clock in the morning. Barely after clocking in for the day, a phone call from Tae Takemi summons me to the Director's Office. Behind her desk, young Director Asuka Shiromiya holds a referral chart, eyeing Takemi across from her with high alert.

"I'm confirming this one last time, Dr. Takemi. This twenty-year-old university student, Ms. Fujino Asagami, had repeated perforations from chronic appendicitis masked by long-term insensitivity to pain, forming an extensive inflammatory mass in her right lower quadrant involving the ileocecal region, greater omentum, and right adnexa—and that is the *only* reason I'm granting special approval for you to lead the surgery with Dr. Sakaguchi as First Assistant."

"I know, I'm the one who screened her chart from outpatient yesterday. Sakaguchi's blade work is rock-solid now; with him across the table holding retractors and managing hemostasis, what could you possibly be worried about?"
"The person I'm worried about is you! Listen carefully—First, perform the surgery normally."
"Second, no pulling junior nurses over for impromptu live anatomy lectures at the operating table."
"Asakura is assigned as scrub nurse today; she knows the anatomy as well as I do, so there's nothing to teach her."
"And third—**you are strictly forbidden from taking advantage of the patient's lack of pain to widen the surgical field and rummage around healthy organs!**"
"Why did you suddenly go silent?! Answer me! Dr. Sakaguchi, besides serving as First Assistant at the table today, your job is to keep a close eye on her hands for me!"
"Rest assured, Director. I'll make sure the operation is completed safely along standard anatomical planes."
Leaving the Director's Office, Takemi and I head to Examination Room 1. Seated beside the exam table is a young woman with waist-length jet-black hair and a poised, gentle demeanor—Fujino Asagami.
"Good morning, Dr. Takemi, Dr. Sakaguchi. I am deeply grateful to have two specialists scrubbing in together for my sake today."

She inclines her head with a graceful smile, every gesture carrying the refined upbringing of an old-family heiress—giving zero hint that deep inside her right lower abdomen lies a suppurating, adherent mass severe enough to send an ordinary person into shock from pain.

"Save the formalities, Ms. Asagami. We'll do one final pre-op abdominal palpation to confirm the margins—lie down on the exam table, unfasten your skirt waistband, and pull your sweater up above your chest."
Obediently lying flat on the examination table, Asagami rolls the hem of her knit sweater upward with slender fingers, baring a flat, toned waist and abdomen without an ounce of excess flesh.

"Put on a pair of gloves and feel this for yourself, Sakaguchi. With a right lower quadrant inflammatory mass of this size, an ordinary girl would scream and arch off the bed the instant your fingertips touched her skin."
Snapping on exam gloves, I step up to the bedside, lay my palm gently over the cool skin of Asagami's right lower abdomen, and press all four fingers slowly and firmly deep into her abdominal cavity.

Through the supple muscle layer of her abdominal wall, the pads of my fingers clearly meet a hard, unyielding mass tightly adherent to the surrounding bowel loops and pelvic wall. Yet the young woman lying beneath my hand doesn't even furrow her brow—only a faint blush creeps up the tips of her ears at the sensation of a man's hand pressing deep into her lower belly.

"Mmn... Your hand is stronger than I imagined, Dr. Sakaguchi... I can feel your fingers sinking all the way into the deepest part of my stomach, pressing against that hard lump... It's just that I truly don't feel any pain at all."

"Precisely because your sensory pathways have been blocked for years, repeated bouts of appendicitis and perforation were registered by your body as mere mild bloating—allowing the inflammation to weld your ileocecal region, greater omentum, and the area around your right ovary and fallopian tube into a single mass."

"Moreover, based on the imaging review I did with Dr. Misono in Radiology, the dense scar tissue deep in your right lower quadrant is directly compressing the retroperitoneal nerve plexus—in other words, a large part of your current insensitivity to pain is actually being locked in place by this chronic lesion itself."
"I see... No wonder I barely felt anything even when I sprained my ankle these past two years. Then regarding the method for this afternoon's surgery..."

"Just as we explained earlier, operating under general anesthesia would mask the critical threshold response of your nerve function; and since you feel no pain right now anyway, we'll perform an **unanesthetized laparotomy with zero anesthesia**. Do you have the nerve to sign?"

"Since I don't feel pain to begin with, skipping anesthesia should be gentler on my body, shouldn't it? Only... I heard that once you sign Hoshimi Hospital's surgical consent form, you cannot cancel halfway through once you're on the operating table, even if you get scared?"
"That's right. Once you sign and enter the pre-op workflow, the operation will not stop until we've resected the lesion cleanly and sutured your abdomen back up."
"I understand. Since I won't cry or make a fuss from pain anyway, I place myself in your hands, Dr. Takemi, Dr. Sakaguchi."

Twelve-thirty p.m. After Miyuki Asakura completes full skin prep, bowel cleansing, and indwelling urinary catheterization for Asagami in the ward, the stark-naked black-haired girl is wheeled into the operating room and positioned flat on the table directly beneath the shadowless lamp.

"Both arm restraints are secured, the Foley catheter is draining smoothly, and povidone-iodine prep across the abdomen and perineum is complete. From undressing and catheterization in the ward up till now, Ms. Asagami's heart rate has barely ticked up—such a sweet, obedient patient it almost makes my heart ache."
"Because... even though I can't feel pain, lying here completely undressed while wide awake, with a tube between my legs and three medical staff looking down at me... is still deeply embarrassing..."
"Blushing proves your tactile and emotional responses are in great shape. Come on, Asakura, hand me a #20 scalpel; Sakaguchi, have dry gauze ready to brace both sides of the incision."

Once the sterile fenestrated drape is laid, Takemi doesn't hesitate for a split second, bringing the sharp blade steadily down just right of the midline across Asagami's flat, snow-white abdomen. Skin and pale-yellow subcutaneous fat part cleanly, and the bright red beads of blood that well up are immediately blotted away by my gauze.

Next comes the electrocautery dividing the anterior rectus sheath, blunt separation of the deep-red rectus abdominis muscle belly, and lifting the translucent peritoneum to snip it open—the entire abdominal entry is executed with surgical perfection. Astonishingly, apart from a faint flutter of her eyelashes as the blade parted her skin, Asagami's breathing on the table remains completely steady.

"Mmn... Just now I felt a cool blade gliding across my stomach, followed by the sensation of it parting to both sides... So this is what it feels like to have one's abdomen cut open? It really... doesn't hurt a bit."

Above her surgical mask, Tae Takemi's eyes light up with startling intensity. Setting a Balfour self-retaining abdominal retractor into the wound, she ratchets the metal blades wide open with several clicks, laying Asagami's abdominal cavity generously bare beneath the shadowless lamp—then suddenly pauses her hands and looks down with a purring smile at the wide-awake girl:
"Say, Ms. Asagami. As you can see, your belly is now wide open, and you genuinely don't feel an ounce of pain."
"Yes... Is something the matter, Dr. Takemi?"

"Since we've already opened you up and an opportunity like this comes once in a blue moon... before we resect that inflamed, adherent mess in your lower right side, how about we take a thorough, detailed look through all the other healthy organs inside your belly from top to bottom?"
"Hey, Takemi, did you already forget Item Three from Director Shiromiya this morning?"
"Hehe, I knew there was no way Dr. Takemi could resist going straight to business when presented with a patient this obedient who doesn't cry out in pain."
Yet lying on the operating table, Fujino Asagami blinks her clear dark eyes and asks a question in dead earnest that freezes all three of us in our tracks:
"Excuse me... if you inspect the rest of my insides along the way, will the surgery fee remain the same?"
"Pfft... Haha! Exactly the same—not a single yen extra. Consider it a complimentary full-course internal organ checkup courtesy of your lead surgeon."
"If the fee is the same and I don't feel any pain anyway... then please do as you both see fit. Feel free to inspect as thoroughly as you like."
"...With the patient herself giving her blessing that readily, I can hardly stop you on the Director's behalf."
"Let's be clear first: atraumatic manual inspection only, and don't drag out the operative time."
"Hear that, Asakura? Even our First Assistant voted in favor. Bring over the warm sterile saline so we can wet our gloves first."
"I just know that unless you get this out of your system first, you won't focus on dissecting the actual lesion."
"Relax, don't you know my touch by now? I'll be ten times gentler than I was with that middle-school frog."
"Don't bring up your middle-school frog in front of the patient—Ms. Asagami will take you seriously."

With Asagami's express permission secured, Takemi drops all restraint. Dipping both gloved hands in warm saline, she reaches straight into the depths of Asagami's wide-open abdominal cavity—starting from the greater curvature of the stomach and transverse colon in the upper abdomen, lifting and turning over the rosy, living organs rising and falling with her breath inch by inch.
"Mmph...! Haah... W-Wait a moment, Dr. Takemi..."

"N-No, it isn't pain... It truly doesn't hurt at all... Only, when your hands reach deep inside my stomach and lift my intestines up... there's an indescribable sinking, tugging sensation inside... as if my organs are about to be lifted right out of me... Nnh, haah..."

Insensitivity to pain blocks sharp nociception, but leaves deep visceral proprioception and vagal traction reflexes intact. As Takemi's slick latex-gloved fingers run loop by loop along the small bowel mesentery toward the pelvis, fine beads of sweat break out across Asagami's pale forehead, her breathing growing rapid and shallow.

"Don't just stand there watching, Sakaguchi—put your hands in and help me cradle these loops of jejunum and ileum gently toward the upper left. Look at her left ovary and fallopian tube down here in the pelvis—completely untouched by the inflammation on the right, and such a lovely color."

Following Takemi's lead, I slide both sterile-gloved hands into Asagami's warm, slick abdominal cavity, gently cradling her soft, peristaltic loops of small intestine in my palms to sweep them aside—while Takemi's fingers glide down along the uterine fundus to the left adnexa, lightly rolling the healthy ovary and fimbriae between her fingertips.
"Kyaa...! Mmn, nnh...! Dr. Sakaguchi... Dr. Takemi... Having four hands moving around inside my belly at the same time... f-feels way too strange...!"
"Bear with it a moment, Ms. Asagami. Right now my palms are supporting your small intestine while Dr. Takemi verifies your healthy left uterine adnexa."

"Haah... I-I know you're examining me... Yet even though it doesn't hurt, why does having Dr. Sakaguchi's palms cradling my intestines while Dr. Takemi touches the deepest part of my lower belly... make my insides feel so heavy and achy that even my toes are going weak... Uu, it feels so weird... Every inch inside my stomach is being touched..."

"Hehe, your face is flushed as red as if you had a fever, Ms. Asagami. Even without pain, having the most private depths of a girl's belly felt over inch by inch by the lead surgeon and assistant carries a shame even stronger than pain."
"Mmn... P-Please don't say it out loud, Nurse Asakura... I can even feel my intestines squirming against your palms inside my head... Are you not finished inspecting yet...?"
"Alright, I've had my fill of admiring the healthy parts—truly a gorgeous specimen of a body. —Time to get down to business. Sakaguchi, shift the retractors toward the right iliac fossa."
Having satisfied her curiosity, Takemi's eyes turn hawk-sharp in an instant. Every trace of her languid playfulness vanishes, replaced by top-tier surgical dominance on par with Emiko Mido herself.

Deep within Asagami's right lower quadrant, thick pus-filled cavities and granulation scars formed by years of silently perforating chronic appendicitis have encased the lower cecum, part of the greater omentum, and the ampulla of the right fallopian tube into a rock-hard inflammatory mass, with dense fibrous bands at its base pressing directly against the retroperitoneal nerve plexus.

"The right fallopian tube and ovary are only encased by inflammatory fibrous adhesions—the parenchyma itself isn't necrotic. With meticulous dissection, we can preserve her right adnexa completely and only resect the necrotic appendiceal base, the inflamed ileocecal tissue, and the involved omentum."

"Right in line with my thinking. I have no taste for lopping off a young girl's useful parts unnecessarily. Asakura, switch to fine dissecting forceps and bipolar cautery; Sakaguchi, hold traction on the right ovarian ligament for me and don't let it budge a millimeter."

Under the shadowless lamp, only the crisp slap of instruments and the soft sizzle of bipolar cautery remain. Takemi's blade moves with breathtaking speed and precision, navigating effortlessly through vascularized adhesion bands until Asagami's intact right ovary and fallopian tube are freed completely unscathed from the outer wall of the mass.
"Mmn... The tugging deep in the right side of my stomach is getting heavier... Like a stone is being peeled off my flesh bit by bit... Haah, it still doesn't hurt, so please continue..."
"We're right at the deepest scar root compressing the nerve plexus. Sakaguchi, clamp the ileocecal mesenteric vessels and prepare to ligate and divide—"

The moment I secure the double ligatures, Takemi's Metzenbaum scissors reach deep into the retroperitoneum, aligning squarely with the dense inflammatory root strangling the sensory nerve pathway, and snip cleanly all the way through—
*Snip.* The dark-red inflammatory mass that had tormented and locked away Fujino Asagami's bodily sensations for years is completely excised, dropping into the kidney dish in Asakura's hands.
And in the exact same split second that the lesion separates from the retroperitoneal nerve plexus—

Asagami's brow, which had only been lightly knitted from traction, freezes abruptly as her pupils contract to pinpricks. The next instant, nociceptive signals dammed up for years surge like a bursting levee straight from her wide-open, oozing right lower abdominal cavity into her cerebral cortex!

A piercing, pitch-shattered scream rips through the operating room! The poised heiress who had lain calmly while we turned her organs over in our hands a moment ago arches violently off the table, her wrists yanking the leather restraints with loud snaps as fat tears burst from her eyes!
"IT HURTS!! IT HURTS SO MUCH—!! My stomach—why does my stomach suddenly feel like it's being burned with fire and sliced with knives?!! Uwaaaahhh—!!"

"Her heart rate just spiked to 130! Asakura, hold her shoulders down so her thrashing doesn't eviscerate the bowel loops through the incision! Excising that retroperitoneal mass just released the compression block on her nerve plexus—her sense of pain woke up right on the table!"

"Dr. Takemi!! Dr. Sakaguchi!! I don't want to do this without anesthesia anymore!! It hurts—my belly is really cut wide open and it hurts so much!! Give me anesthesia... I'm begging you, please put me under general anesthesia right now!! Uwaaaahhh—!!"

Faced with Asagami sobbing and screaming for anesthesia on the table, Tae Takemi doesn't show a trace of panic; instead, she straightens her back unhurriedly, her eyes crinkling into a smile above her mask:
"Congratulations, Ms. Asagami. It looks like the operation is a resounding success—not only did we clean out the rotten mass, we cured your insensitivity to pain along the way."

"Uwaaaahhh I don't want congratulations right now!! It hurts to death... Even taking a single breath makes my insides cramp in agony!! Anesthesia... I'll pay extra right now if I have to, just please give me anesthesia and put me to sleep!!"
"Asking for anesthesia now? Too late for that, Ms. Asagami."

"The hardest resection steps are already finished. All that's left is irrigating the abdominal cavity clean with warm saline, checking for bleeders, and suturing your belly closed layer by layer. Even if we paged Chief Sakura to come intubate you for general anesthesia right now, by the time the drugs kicked in, Sakaguchi and I would already have tied off the final skin suture."
"H-How could that be...?! Doesn't that mean I have to lie here wide awake enduring the pain of having my insides washed out and my stomach sewed up stitch by stitch until the very end?!"
Brace the edge of her abdominal wall to steady the incision: "We can't add general anesthesia now, but I'll work with Dr. Takemi to close your abdomen as quickly and smoothly as possible."
Say to Takemi: "Stop teasing her—she just got her sense of pain back with a full laparotomy wide open. Let's irrigate with warm saline right away."
"Uu... Dr. Sakaguchi... Even when your hand presses beside the incision, the sting of your glove brushing against the raw flesh is so vivid... Please hurry...!"
"Hear that, Lead Surgeon? The young lady is rushing us—though we can't cut corners on debridement and irrigation; we have to wash her out nice and thoroughly so she doesn't get a post-op infection."
"Feeling sorry for her already? Witnessing a painless patient regain her sense of pain right under your blade is a once-in-a-lifetime clinical moment."
"A miracle for the surgeons, maybe, but pure torture for Ms. Asagami on the table. Asakura, hand me the warm saline and suction."

The next forty minutes become the young heiress's first true baptism of pain in her twenty years of life. As copious warm saline pours into her open abdominopelvic cavity to thoroughly irrigate the raw bed where the mass was dissected free, Asagami bites down hard on her lower lip, tears streaming endlessly down her temples into the edge of her surgical cap.

"Mmn—!! Haah, ah... Th-The water is washing right over the raw wound inside my belly... It stings so much... Even when the suction tube draws the bloody water out, my insides are throbbing and cramping... uuu..."

"Good girl, hang in there just a little longer, Ms. Asagami. You didn't make a peep when we turned your whole belly inside out earlier, so being able to cry out in pain this loudly means your body is completely back to normal."

Once irrigation is complete and we verify that her right adnexa and bowel loops are returned to their proper anatomical positions, Takemi and I begin closing the abdomen stitch by stitch, layer by layer. Every time the curved needle draws suture thread through the sensitive peritoneum, approximates the rectus sheath, and cinches a knot tight, Asagami's body tenses from the sharp piercing and pulling pain, letting out tearful gasps.
"Ah...! Ow, that stitch pulled so tight... My stomach is being sewed shut one stitch at a time... Uu, I'm never believing 'skipping anesthesia is fine' ever again...!"
"Final subcuticular stitch—cut the thread. There, the wound edges are approximated beautifully. It won't even leave a scar."

Five o'clock in the evening, post-operative observation ward. Thanks to Hoshimi Hospital's recovery guarantee, Fujino Asagami—who underwent a major laparotomy just hours ago—is already changed into a fresh hospital gown and propped up against the headboard, only a faint flush from her earlier crying bout lingering on her cheeks.

When Takemi and I push open the door for our final end-of-shift rounds, Asagami is looking down and gingerly prodding her right lower abdomen through the thin gauze dressing with her fingertip—immediately sucking in a sharp *hiss* of breath.
"Stop poking at your incision—it was just sutured closed, so of course it still hurts."

"I am so sorry, Dr. Sakaguchi, Dr. Takemi... Screaming and crying so ungracefully on the operating table at the end, and begging you relentlessly for anesthesia... I made a complete spectacle of myself in front of you both."
"No need to apologize. If you hadn't made a sound right after I freed the compression on your retroperitoneal nerve plexus with your belly still wide open, that would've meant my surgery failed."
Lowering her eyelashes, Asagami rests both hands gently over her lower abdomen. Crystal tears well up at the corners of her eyes once more, yet her lips curve into a smile of unmistakable warmth:
"Truthfully... after returning to the ward and calming down, feeling this steady, throbbing ache beneath my fingers feels almost miraculous to me."

"Before today, no matter how badly my insides were festering, it felt like I was living behind a pane of frosted glass, unable to feel a thing. On the operating table earlier it hurt terribly, and the two of you inspected every inch inside my stomach... yet being able to feel pain like an ordinary girl, and having Dr. Sakaguchi scold me gently not to poke my incision, makes me feel from the bottom of my heart that I am truly alive."

"Your right ovary and fallopian tube were preserved completely intact, and the inflammatory mass is gone for good. Get a good night's sleep tonight, and you'll be free to walk around normally tomorrow."
"Yes. Thank you both from the bottom of my heart."

By the time we step out of the ward, six-o'clock twilight has settled outside the windows. Hands tucked into the pockets of her white coat, Tae Takemi strolls unhurriedly beside me down the corridor leading to the basement stairs.
"Phew... Now that was a fulfilling full day's work. We got to inspect a living abdominopelvic cavity in peace during the first half, and heard such a lively scream in the second."

"It's a good thing Ms. Asagami is good-natured. Any other patient who found out you threw in a 'complimentary full-abdominal manual inspection' while she couldn't feel pain would march straight into the Director's Office to report you before discharge."
"If she reports me, the First Assistant who had both hands inside her belly cradling her small intestine for me is an accomplice—there's no escaping for you either."
Stopping at the top of the basement stairs, she turns to look at me, a rare glint of genuine approval shining in her usually languid, teasing eyes:

"Seriously though, Sakaguchi... when her pain suddenly came back and she started thrashing on the table, an ordinary assistant would have lost his head—yet you braced the incision to protect her bowel loops with one hand while matching my pace through irrigation and closure without missing a beat."

"In all my time at Hoshimi Hospital, you're the first man I've met who can keep up with my rhythm this comfortably. ...Come on, after a full day on our feet, come down to my lab for a drink—consider it a treat from your lead surgeon."

strings.collections.cameo_patients.guest_ayako.n: An adult manga artist and illustrator visiting from outside the hospital. She is not a romance option or surgery team member. strings.collections.cameo_patients.guest_chisato: An adult alternate-universe character and the patient in the first advanced referral teaching case, undergoing open-chest artificial heart system replacement. She is not a romance option or hospital staff member.
A friend who visits Chihaya the day after her second surgery, age 18. She appears only in the story and does not join the hospital staff or unlock romance or patient flows.
strings.collections.cameo_patients.guest_yoriko_: An adult woman, age 24. She retains her original long dark brown hair, reddish-brown eyes, round glasses, and earnest but easily flustered manner. In this event she removes her glasses and tucks her hair under a surgical cap before entering the OR suite. After physically resisting at the doorway, she still tries to keep her composure, bolstering herself with police-like phrases such as “insurance” and “line of defense.”
strings.collections.cameo_patients.guest_yurika_: An adult woman, age 22. She retains her original long dark blue-violet hair, large blue-green eyes, and lively, expressive, carefree, teasing personality. Exaggerated but clear eyebrows, mouth shapes, and head movements convey her emotions; she becomes noticeably subdued only in real pain, fear, or recognition of an accident’s gravity. She has received long-term internal-medicine care for recurrent gastroduodenal disease. She is the patient in Origawa Satsuki’s Lv3 same-name mistaken-identity surgery event; her ward, preoperative stretcher, anesthesia induction, recovery-room, and scrub-clad observer art is completed and integrated into the Lv3 event.
strings.collections.cameo_patients.patient_ayako: The adult woman actually scheduled for surgery. Her silver-violet hair, face shape, and surgical patient clothing resemble Katagiri Ayako’s, but her eyes are narrower and gray-green, and her nose bridge and jaw differ. Staff unfamiliar with either woman struggle to distinguish them during a hurried handoff. Agitated before surgery, she flees the OR and runs past Ayako, triggering the mistaken-identity chain. Her name and long-term profile remain to be decided in a later event design.
strings.collections.cameo_patients.patient_chiha: Appears as a female patient in Hiroko’s introduction event. Her first successful surgery is established backstory; the second is a separate three-day narrative event, outside the Surgery Runner, and does not unlock staff or romance status.

strings.collections.micro_events.haru_micro_afte: After surgery, she checks on the team and patient first, usually leaving her own feelings until last.

strings.collections.micro_events.haru_micro_miss: As an OR nurse, she knows the team’s rhythm and reads pressure from silence and shifts in movement.

strings.collections.micro_events.yui_micro_hando: She uses mnemonics of her own to ease tension and is willing to let the player into her little world.
strings.collections.micro_events.yui_micro_if_i_: As the relationship deepens, she uses a hypothetical question to learn how the player sees her when she is vulnerable.
strings.collections.micro_events.yui_micro_last_: Curious by nature, she hides her hopes for the future in lighthearted questions.
strings.collections.micro_events.yui_micro_long_: She knows formal procedure names but checks Hoshimi’s shorthand so she will not bring her old workplace’s terms into handoffs.
strings.collections.micro_events.yui_micro_no_wo: Although she loves learning, she begins to realize their relationship need not always revolve around teaching.

strings.collections.micro_events.yui_micro_red_k: Her powers of observation are growing, and remembering small details about a patient makes her happy.
strings.collections.micro_events.yui_micro_stead: Her technical skills are steady; she cares about fitting Hoshimi’s team rhythm and welcomes specific feedback.

She strictly checks identity, indication, consent, and anatomical risk. Her strengths include benign gynecologic disease, hysteroscopy and laparoscopy, vaginal procedures, pelvic-floor repair, and positioning and exposure.

Young, beautiful, and exceptionally approachable, she makes newcomers wonder whether she is truly the department head. Five minutes into work, everyone understands the astonishing depth of her gynecologic knowledge.

Sakaguchi first sees the absurd sight of her trapped in an examination chair, then gradually discovers her nearly pure love of gynecologic medicine. Their relationship develops through shared surgery, mutual teasing, and professional trust.

Usually direct, lively, and quick-tongued; her eyes light up at gynecologic medicine. With an anxious patient, she slows down and explains purpose, process, the option to stop at any time, and the next step.
Exceptional at gynecologic diagnosis, pelvic anatomy, and procedures
Reliable and clear when a patient truly needs help
Quickly spots gynecologic risks and anatomical abnormalities
Never lets her comic side interfere with medical judgment
When real clinical risk emerges, she instantly stops joking, shortens her speech, and sets clear priorities. When her own life goes wrong, she tries to preserve her dignity through deadpan formality.
strings.collections.staff.doc_aqua.dialogue_styl: Expressive and quick to react; speaks faster and loses some social filter when excited by medicine. With patients, a reminder is enough for her to switch immediately to the clear, reliable, consent-conscious tone of a department head.

Before surgery she requires a primary plan, a fallback after failure, and clear roles. During surgery she respects the lead surgeon’s final judgment while actively taking over team coordination and outside interruptions.
A 28-year-old deputy head of surgery and candidate for director. She establishes authority through rigor, fairness, and team assignment, rather than leaning on age or seniority.

Initially she sees Sakaguchi as an excellent surgeon whose leadership needs assessment. After sharing responsibility for complex operations, she gradually lets him carry some of the burden and learns not to define all their time together by work.
Highly formal and direct, with little sarcasm. She lets others finish before concluding with “I understand” or “Here is the decision.”
Openly acknowledges colleagues’ strengths in particular techniques
Brings highly skilled team members together
Under greater pressure she becomes briefer and more focused on priorities and responsibility. She steadies the team first, then processes her own unease alone.
strings.collections.staff.doc_artoria.dialogue_s: Formal and direct, with little sarcasm; hears everyone out before making a clear final decision. Under greater pressure, her sentences grow shorter.

She knows sterile procedure, teamwork, and hospital management, and excels as an assistant. When leading surgery independently, she openly acknowledges her experience gap and reviews her work seriously.

Once her identity is public, she is Hoshimi Hospital’s young incumbent director and a surgeon just beginning to carry independent lead-surgeon responsibility. She is approachable and eager to learn, building authority without airs.

Sakaguchi first mistakes her for a young OR colleague at the scrub sink, then learns she is the director. Their relationship grows through shared surgery and mutual appraisal of hospital ideals toward entrusting the hospital’s future to each other.

She often uses gentle questions and light jokes to close the distance. On patient safety, staffing, and management decisions she will say, “I understand your view. But the decision on this matter is made.”
Excellent foundations in medical theory and OR procedures
Mature as an assistant and team communicator
Clear administrative judgment and willingness to own decisions
Values real training opportunities for young women in healthcare
Even as pressure rises, she remains soft-spoken and courteous, but her sentences shorten. Once she has decided, she calmly repeats her conclusion without yielding.
strings.collections.staff.doc_asuka.dialogue_sty: Soft-spoken and polite with a hint of youthful warmth; precise and perceptive in medical discussions. She slows down and restates boundaries clearly when making a formal decision.

She prioritizes the surgical department’s efficiency and operative quality, demands complete information before surgery, gives precise instructions during it, and directly pursues process failures afterward. She respects colleagues who are truly competent and willing to take responsibility.

A senior physician in the surgical department and a strong candidate for its next director. Exceptionally capable and demanding, she makes no secret of her ambition for the position and professional achievement.

At first she treats Sakaguchi Ryuji as a young doctor to be evaluated; shared complex operations and departmental pressure build respect. In her romance route she moves from restraint and testing to unusually resolute, candid, and lasting commitment.

Short sentences, little inflection, few exclamations. She often asks, “What is your conclusion?”, “Continue,” or “Show me your judgment.” Even in private affection she is not saccharine, but states promises directly and acts on them.
Exceptional surgical technique and judgment in the moment
Makes clear decisions quickly under pressure
Willing to take responsibility for high-risk decisions
Offers sustained practical support to people she respects
The greater the pressure, the cooler and more forceful she becomes, tightening control and explaining less. She admits uncertainty only when alone or with those she trusts most.
strings.collections.staff.doc_emiko.dialogue_sty: Concise and calm, often ending a conversation with a conclusion or request. She rarely praises people outright; when emotionally moved, she instead shows unusually frank and lasting concern.

Before surgery she emphasizes communication and past details; during surgery she calmly completes open procedures with precision; afterward she remembers the recovery issue that matters most to the patient.
A mature, kind, slightly easygoing general surgeon with a relaxed manner who readily finds a comfortable distance with patients and colleagues.

Sakaguchi first sees the contrast between her chaotic scheduling and reliable surgery. Through building dependable processes together, owning mistakes, and daily companionship, they form a mature, easygoing intimacy.
Low-pressure and natural, with occasional gentle teasing. She slows down to explain things to patients, then becomes concise, clear, and steady at the operating table.

At a clinical risk, she immediately stops joking, speaks more briefly, and acts by priority. When her personal schedule goes awry, she first calculates seriously and sometimes explains an absurd result with a straight face.
strings.collections.staff.doc_minato.dialogue_st: Relaxed and natural, with slightly mature humor; remembers individual patients and their worries. Once surgery begins, her speech becomes concise and her judgment steady.

strings.collections.staff.doc_sayaka.characteriz: Her attraction to men does not mean she dislikes women. Her sensuality, jokes, and initiative are adult choices. She excels in general care and health management, can serve as a regular assistant and fill cross-department gaps, and explicitly yields work beyond her qualifications to someone better suited.

An approachable, popular young doctor with a slightly older-sister air. She openly likes men and fits naturally among her female colleagues. She is proactive and enjoys flirtation, but never crosses someone else’s boundaries or lets it displace patient care.

They exchange numbers and establish mutual interest on their first date, then build an understanding back at the hospital: they can flirt and still do their jobs well. Her route is light, proactive, and low on artificial barriers, without relying on tragedy or a healing narrative.

Cute, mature-sounding short sentences and natural speech, occasionally using “Huh?”, “Oh?”, “Come on,” or “Sure” to draw closer. She knows when she is flirting but cannot always land it smoothly. When Sakaguchi truly catches her off guard, she pauses, glares, looks away, or laughs first.
Broad clinical foundation and quick to fill gaps across departments and roles
Skilled at easing tension and building cooperation
Knows what she can do and states clearly what she cannot
Under rising pressure she jokes less, shortens sentences, and proactively confirms boundaries. She never uses flirtation or levity to conceal patient risk.
strings.collections.staff.doc_sayaka.dialogue_st: Seventy percent relaxed and natural adult woman, twenty percent knowingly flirtatious little devil, ten percent unexpectedly endearing when a direct approach briefly makes her pause, look away, or laugh at herself. She speaks in short, colloquial sentences and does not win every exchange with a polished comeback. With patients or medical risk, she immediately becomes brief, steady, and practical.
