strings.collections.character_events.manami_lv2_: In the evening lobby, Manami is waiting around for Hiroko to get off work.

At six-thirty in the evening, the outpatient windows in Hoshimi Hospital's first-floor lobby had long since pulled down their shutters, leaving only the duty lamp at the end of the corridor glowing with soft white light.
Having wrapped up his charting for the day and changed into casual clothes, Ryuji Sakaguchi walked from the elevator bank toward the first-floor exit.
Passing the public waiting area around the corner of the lobby, he paused slightly.

A familiar figure was sitting on the bench by the window. Manami Iimura from the pharmacy department had already shed her white coat for a bright, well-fitted cream knit top and a light apricot skirt. Holding her phone in both hands, she swung her legs idly over the edge of the bench while humming a tuneless little melody.
“Manami? It's already this late—you haven't headed home yet?”
At the sound of his voice, Manami looked up sharply, her spaced-out expression instantly breaking into a radiant smile.
“Oh, it's Ryuji! Did you just get off work too?”
Ever since that chaotic “sneezing” incident in the pharmacy department, the two of them had dropped stiff formalities whenever they ran into each other off duty.
Ryuji glanced at the small shoulder bag slung over her arm:
“Dressed like that, you don't look like you're waiting for a night-shift handover. Waiting for someone?”
Manami waggled her phone screen at him and let out a long sigh, her shoulders slumping dramatically.
“Don't even get me started! I'm waiting for Hiroko so we can go out for dinner together.”
Ryuji glanced at the clock on the wall:
“It's already six-thirty. What time did you two agree to meet?”
Manami held up a single finger with a tragic expression:

“Five-thirty! The second the pharmacy shift ended, I clocked out on the dot and rushed down here, and I haven't seen hide nor hair of her—Ryuji, I've been sitting on this bench staring toward the corridor for a whole hour!”
“A whole hour? Didn't you go over to the operating rooms to look for her?”
Resting her chin in her hand, Manami puffed out her cheeks helplessly:

“I texted her twenty minutes ago, and she said she was handing over to the night-shift nurses and would be right down. You know how Hiroko is—the moment operating room work is involved, she's so thorough she'd practically count tomorrow's sutures three times over for everyone else. If I barged into the surgical wing to rush her, she'd only blame herself and get even more flustered.”
“For someone complaining this loudly, you still sat here patiently waiting for her for a full hour.”
Manami blinked and lifted her chin matter-of-factly:
“Well, of course! How could I ditch my best friend and go enjoy good food and drinks after work all by myself? Still, if I wait any longer, my stomach really is going to stage a rebellion—”
Before she could finish, hurried footsteps suddenly echoed from the corridor leading to the surgical locker rooms.
Changed into a gentle light-blue cardigan and long skirt, Hiroko Sugimura came jogging into the lobby carrying her commuter bag, her bangs slightly tousled from running.
“M-Manami! I'm so sorry to keep you waiting...!”

Stopping in front of the bench, she braced her hands on her knees to catch her breath, only to look up and realize Ryuji Sakaguchi was standing right there too; a flush of embarrassment crossed her face:
“Ah... Dr. Sakaguchi is here too? G-Good evening!”
“Good evening, Hiroko. No rush—catch your breath first.”
Manami stood up from the bench, put her hands on her hips, and deliberately circled halfway around Hiroko in mock interrogation:
“Miss Hiroko Sugimura, please take a look at what time it is! Five minutes later, and you would have found a starved corpse named Manami Iimura right here in the hospital lobby!”
Flushing bright red, Hiroko pressed her palms together and apologized repeatedly:

“I'm really sorry, Manami! Clearing the final operation this afternoon ran a bit later than expected, and while I was handing over the special instrument packs and supply inventory to the night shift, there were two items I didn't feel right leaving half-explained, so one thing led to another and the handover took way too long...”
Seeing her best friend looking both flustered and dead serious, Manami burst out laughing and reached out naturally to tuck a stray lock of hair behind Hiroko's ear.

“All right, all right, I'm just teasing you! As if I don't know what a worrywart you are. Still, as punishment for being an hour late, you have to help me eat two extra plates of yakitori in the first round tonight!”
Hiroko let out a breath of relief, her eyes curving into a soft smile:
“Okay, I'll follow your lead on everything tonight.”
Manami nodded in satisfaction, then turned toward Ryuji beside them, her eyes suddenly sparkling with an idea:
“Oh, right, Ryuji! You were about to head back and grab dinner by yourself too, weren't you?”
“I haven't eaten yet—I was just going to grab something quick on the street.”
Manami clapped her hands together enthusiastically:
“You can't just settle for something random! Since we bumped into each other right here in the lobby, why don't you come eat with the two of us? With more people, we can order way more dishes!”
Hiroko smiled at Ryuji as well:
“She's right—if you don't have other plans tonight, Dr. Sakaguchi, why not join us for a lively meal?”
Looking at the two of them extending such a warm invitation, Ryuji smiled and nodded:
“Then I'll gladly take you up on that. Hope I'm not intruding.”
“Awesome! Let's go, let's go—next stop, the shopping district izakaya!”
Side by side, the three of them pushed open the hospital's front doors and stepped out into the evening breeze as the city lights came on.
When they slid open the wooden lattice door of the first yakitori izakaya, the savory aroma of fat sizzling over charcoal and the lively clamor of the crowd washed over them at once.

Before they had even flipped past the second page of the menu, Manami—starving after her hour-long wait—rattled off a long list of dishes in one breath. Before long, sizzling green-onion chicken skewers, salt-grilled chicken skin, mentaiko tamagoyaki, and three frosty mugs of draft beer topped with creamy foam filled the wooden table.
“Here! To getting off work smoothly today—cheers!”
As the ice-cold draft beer went down, Manami squinted in bliss and let out a long sigh, then picked up a green-onion chicken skewer and pressed it into Hiroko's hand.
“Eat up, eat up, Hiroko. You were on your feet in the OR for so long today, you probably didn't even get a chance for an afternoon snack, right?”
Hiroko took the skewer with a slightly sheepish smile:
“I really was busy with the instrument trays all afternoon... Mm, the yakitori here is as tender as ever. It's delicious.”

Watching Hiroko—who was always so poised, thorough, and focused on taking care of everyone else in the operating room—finally shed her daytime tension and take relaxed little bites of her skewer brought a quiet smile to Ryuji's face.
Squeezing lemon juice over the plates, Manami launched into chatter:

“You two have no idea—this afternoon at the pharmacy window, I almost burst out laughing. Dr. Mizuki sent over an internal requisition slip with handwriting zigzagging like an ECG trace. Hiroko, guess what it turned out to be after I spent ages deciphering it?”
“Pep-up vitamin gummies for her department! She actually scribbled her snack shopping memo on the back of a prescription pad!”
Hiroko couldn't help covering her mouth with a laugh:

“Dr. Mizuki is always whirlwind-busy in the corridors too. Though Manami, didn't you complain to me last week that you mistook your newly bought lipstick for your name seal and stuffed it into your white coat pocket?”
“Hey! Didn't we agree to keep that a secret?! Ryuji is sitting right here listening!”

Trading stories back and forth, the two of them jumped from hospital anecdotes to trying out lipstick shades together at the department store the previous week, the mood light and effortlessly familiar. Ryuji chimed in occasionally, but mostly held his mug and listened quietly as the two best friends teased each other.
Before they knew it, the bamboo holder on the table was packed full of empty skewers, and the plates had been wiped clean.
Manami patted her stomach and glanced around at the increasingly rowdy diners, her eyes lighting up:

“All right, my stomach finally has a good base! Still, this place is full of uncles playing loud drinking games, so it's getting way too noisy—I know a newly opened Japanese bistro in the alley up ahead that serves amazing fruit wines. Let's head to the next spot and keep drinking!”
“We're changing venues for a second round?”
Her cheeks faintly flushed, Hiroko smiled with a hint of anticipation:
“It's rare to see Manami in such high spirits... Dr. Sakaguchi, shall we keep her company and try their fruit wine?”
Cutting through two lively shopping-district alleys, the three of them stepped into a tasteful Japanese fruit-wine bistro for their second stop.
The lighting here was much softer than in the yakitori shop, and a delicate scent of citrus and plum wine drifted through the air.
The moment they sat down, without even glancing at the drink menu, Manami waved a server over like a seasoned regular:

“Could we get a rich plum wine on the rocks and a lightly sweet white-peach oolong sour—make sure the peach one has light ice, please! Plus an order of grilled cheese mochi and fried chicken cartilage. Ryuji, order whatever you'd like to drink!”
After ordering a glass of sake, Ryuji looked at Manami with genuine admiration:
“You didn't even have to ask about the light ice or the side dishes. You two must come out together all the time.”
Cradling her warm hand towel, Hiroko smiled gently:

“Manami and I have known each other for a very long time. Whenever I go out to eat with her, I don't even have to use my brain—she always takes care of ordering everything I want to eat but feel too shy to ask for.”
Manami bobbed her head proudly and leaned over to wrap an arm around Hiroko's shoulders:
“That's because you're always busy taking care of the doctors, the patients, and the younger nurses at the hospital, Hiroko! If nobody spoiled you after work, that would be way too unfair!”
Her cheeks warming, Hiroko reached out and lightly pinched Manami's fingers:

“Listen to you—one mug of beer and you're already this sweet-talked. Who was it last time that drank too much plum wine and insisted on dragging me to stand in front of a street claw machine for half an hour?”
Manami immediately clapped a hand over Hiroko's mouth:
“Uwah! Bringing up embarrassing history is strictly forbidden! Ryuji, you didn't hear a thing just now, right?”
“Heard every word. So Miss Iimura from Pharmacy is secretly a claw-machine pro.”
“You two really do look much more relaxed when you're together than at the hospital.”
Ryuji raised his sake glass with a laugh:
“Heard every word. So Miss Iimura from Pharmacy is secretly a claw-machine pro.”

“I'm no pro at all! I tried over a dozen times without catching a single thing, and in the end Hiroko couldn't bear to watch anymore—she put in one coin and won that little bear for me on her first try!”
Hiroko let out a soft laugh:
“You two really do look much more relaxed when you're together than at the hospital.”
Hiroko took a gentle sip of her white-peach sour, her eyes softening:
“That's true. My nerves are always wound so tight in the operating room, but whenever I come out to eat and bicker with Manami, I feel like I come right back to life.”
Manami swirled her glass with a grin:
“Then from now on I'll camp outside the operating room doors to ambush you after work every week!”
As the ice cubes slowly melted in their glasses, the second round of fruit wine and bar snacks disappeared amid laughter and chatter.
A pleasant buzz had melted away most of Hiroko's usual prim reserve, making even her laughter ring clearer than usual.
Glancing out the window at the lively night-market lights, Manami stood up in high spirits:

“It's only nine-thirty! Since we all got together tonight, we have to drink to our hearts' content! Come on, come on—there's a fantastic oden izakaya right around the corner. Let's go have a bowl of hot broth to wrap up the night!”
Ryuji didn't know whether to laugh or cry:
Though her cheeks were already rosy, Hiroko picked up her bag with a smile and followed along:
“Once Manami enters her bar-hopping mode, she never stops until she's hit all three spots. Dr. Sakaguchi, will you join us for one last round?”
The third stop was a traditional oden izakaya with fabric noren curtains and only a handful of wooden tables.

Inside the bubbling partitioned copper pot, daikon radish, konjac noodles, and chikuwa fish cakes soaked full of dashi broth gave off an inviting savory aroma. Ordering a flask of warm sake, Manami and Hiroko sat side by side on one side of the square table, while Ryuji sat across from them.
After three stops in a row and several rounds of warm sake, whatever polite distance had remained between them had vanished without a trace.
Propping her rosy cheek on one hand, Manami poked gently at the daikon radish in her bowl with her chopsticks and suddenly let out a wistful sigh.
“Sigh... Come to think of it, ever since I started working at Hoshimi Hospital, my luck with men seems to have gotten terribly bad.”
“Luck with men? Back when we first met, I thought I heard someone mention you were seeing somebody?”
Manami waved a hand briskly, her tone frank and breezy without a trace of awkwardness or heartache:
“Oh, you mean my ex-boyfriend? We broke up ages ago! No need to bring up ancient history—right now I'm a hundred percent happily single!”
She took a sip from her warm sake cup and pouted in mock complaint:

“I figured once I was single again, with my charm, I'd run into a romantic encounter in no time. Instead, I spend every day either staring at medicine bottles in the pharmacy or hanging out with Hiroko after work—without a single reliable man in sight.”
With that, Manami turned her head and playfully bumped her shoulder against Hiroko beside her:
“Right, right? Just look at our Hiroko—she's so gorgeous and so gentle and considerate, yet she's wide open and single right now too!”
Hiroko's hand paused on her teacup; thinking seriously along those lines for a moment, she suddenly spoke up:
“Still, now that you mention it, Manami... the Director, Dr. Miyama, Dr. Mido—they all seem to be single too!”
Manami's eyes flew wide open, and she slapped a palm down on the table:
“Right?! Isn't that super weird?! Our hospital has so many gorgeous doctors and nurses—how are every single one of them single?!”
“And it's not just the doctors—the nursing department seems to be the same way...”

“Exactly! Every last one of them is a knockout who'd turn heads walking down the street, so how come the moment they enter Hoshimi Hospital, they all end up members of the singles club? It defies all logic!”
The more the two women talked about it, the more baffling they found it, leaning their heads together and murmuring for quite a while.
All of a sudden, the table beside the oden pot fell quiet.

As if struck by the exact same thought at the exact same instant, Manami and Hiroko stopped talking in unison, turned their heads together, and fixed two pairs of gleaming eyes straight on Ryuji sitting across from them.
Pinned between two meaningful stares, Ryuji felt a layer of cold sweat break out across his back as he held his sake cup.
“...Hold on. Why are the two of you suddenly looking at me like that?”
Folding her arms, Manami narrowed her eyes mischievously and sized Ryuji up from head to toe:
“We were just thinking—across the entire hospital, aren't you the only eligible male doctor with great credentials who spends every day surrounded by beautiful women, Ryuji?”
“You can't possibly blame me for the female colleagues at the hospital being single.”
Grinning, Manami leaned forward over the edge of the table and pointed at Hiroko beside her:
“Why not! Look, a wonderful girl like Hiroko happens to be unattached right now, and you partner with her in the OR every day, Ryuji—don't tell me it's never crossed your mind?”
Put on the spot, Hiroko blushed slightly, but she didn't back down—nudging Manami lightly with her elbow, she shot right back:

“Sure I'm single, but I'm speaking up on behalf of the flower of our operating room! Come clean, Dr. Sakaguchi—are you so focused on studying your scalpel that you treat all the beauties around you like thin air?”
Seeing Ryuji looking thoroughly outmatched, Hiroko couldn't help curving her eyes into a smile and joining Manami in teasing him:
“She has a point. You're always so sharp and observant at the operating table, Dr. Sakaguchi—how come you suddenly turn so dense the moment work ends?”
“Hear that?! Even Hiroko, who always takes your side, is roasting you now!”
As the two single women played off each other without missing a beat, the table filled with cheerful laughter.
Folding her arms, Manami narrowed her eyes mischievously at Ryuji and slung an arm around Hiroko beside her:

“We were just thinking—across the entire hospital, you're the only male doctor wandering around surrounded by beautiful women every day, Ryuji! Even our gentle, gorgeous Hiroko is still unattached right now—does our star surgeon really have no appreciation for a beauty right in front of him?”
Hearing Manami declare with such certainty that she was “still unattached right now,” Hiroko stiffened almost imperceptibly beside her.

Remembering the intimate nights the two of them had already shared in private, Hiroko's fair cheeks flushed crimson from the tips of her ears all the way down her neck, her gaze turning shy and flustered in an instant.
Pressing her lips together, she unconsciously raised her lashes and stole a quiet glance at Ryuji across the table.
Ryuji happened to look her way at that exact moment, and their gazes—tinged with guilty conscience and quiet sweetness—collided midair.
Yet in that very second, Manami, sitting pressed right up against Hiroko, sensed something was off.
Manami's half-teasing smile froze at once. Her eyes went wide as she looked from the beet-red Hiroko to the subtly composed Ryuji, and she suddenly let out a dramatic yelp:
“Eh? Ehhh?! What's with that look on your face?!”
Startled, Hiroko grew even more flustered, quickly raising both hands to cover her burning cheeks as she stammered:
“W-What look?! I-I wasn't making any face!”
Manami leaned right into Hiroko's space, her nose nearly touching Hiroko's as she stared at her in deep suspicion:

“Something's fishy! Totally fishy! Whenever I teased you about being single before, you'd always fire right back at me—why did you suddenly blush like this today? And you just snuck a peek at Ryuji, didn't you?!”
Her eyes darting everywhere, Hiroko fumbled for the glass of ice water on the table and pressed it against her cheek:
“I-I didn't sneak a peek at anyone! It's just because we went to three places in a row tonight, and that warm sake just now had such a strong kick—I'm only red from drinking too much!”
Manami narrowed her eyes, clearly not buying that excuse for a second as her suspicious gaze swept back and forth between Hiroko and Ryuji:
“Really just from drinking too much? Why do I get the feeling the vibe between you two tonight is a little sneaky...”

Seeing Manami's sharp radar about to lock onto the truth, Ryuji seized the chance, calmly picking up a piece of tender, broth-soaked daikon radish and placing it into Manami's bowl to change the subject:

“Manami, weren't you saying just now that you wanted to eat this shop's signature daikon? Leave it in the pot any longer and it'll melt away. Besides, speaking of alcohol kicking in, wasn't it you who drank two glasses of rich plum wine at the second place?”
Catching on immediately, Hiroko hurried to pick up the warm sake flask and chimed in along with Ryuji's lead:
“T-That's right! Your own face is super red too, Manami—hurry and eat some hot radish to line your stomach, or you'll wake up with another headache tomorrow morning!”
With the two of them piling her bowl full of oden from both sides, most of Manami's attention was indeed drawn away by the savory aroma.
Manami picked up the daikon radish, took a big bite, and mumbled around a mouthful:
“Mm... the daikon really soaked up the broth! Wait, don't think you two can brush me off with food... I haven't caught any proof yet, but something definitely feels fishy...”
Watching Manami finally let the subject slide, Ryuji and Hiroko exchanged a quiet glance across the curling steam and breathed a simultaneous sigh of relief in their hearts.
Once they finished the oden in their bowls, the mood at the table returned to lively laughter and conversation.
Cradling her cup of hot tea, Hiroko composed herself, curved her eyes into a warm smile at Ryuji across the table, and said:
“You'll have to work hard, Dr. Sakaguchi.”
Beside her, Manami immediately jumped right in, clapping Hiroko on the shoulder and declaring loudly:
“Yeah, yeah! Hiroko is wide open right now!”
Her cheeks warming slightly, Hiroko shot her a playful look and retorted:
As she said the words “wide open,” Manami deliberately drew out her tone, her teasing gaze sweeping between Hiroko's and Ryuji's faces once more:
“...I didn't get that wrong, did I, Hiroko?”
Feeling the tips of her ears burn, Hiroko quickly sat up straight and retorted loudly to cover her guilty conscience:
Without changing expression, Ryuji raised his teacup for a sip and played dumb as he casually remarked:
“How did we circle all the way back to this topic again?”
Manami snickered, raised her sake cup, and pointed it squarely at Ryuji:
“Anyway, you've got to work hard, Dr. Sakaguchi!”
Exasperated, Ryuji spread his hands helplessly:
Manami and Hiroko exchanged a look and, giving him no chance to press further, called out together at the top of their voices:

Their crisp, ringing duet echoed through the small oden shop, and the moment the words left their mouths, the two girls couldn't hold back anymore—leaning on each other's shoulders as they burst into peals of laughter.
Watching the two of them laughing together, Ryuji could only shake his head in fond resignation and drain the last of the warm sake in his cup.
At ten-thirty at night, the three of them finally stepped out of the third izakaya.

The cool night breeze brushed away the linger of alcohol and the warmth of the oden. Most of the shops along both sides of the street had already closed for the night, leaving only the orange streetlights stretching their three shadows long across the pavement.
Manami stretched her arms high overhead in satisfaction and turned to face Ryuji:
“Phew—I'm so full tonight, and the drinks were super fun! Thanks for accompanying the two of us to all three places today, Ryuji.”
Hiroko gave a warm little bow with a smile as well:
“I had a wonderful time tonight, Dr. Sakaguchi. Please take care on your way home.”
“You two as well—remember to message each other once you get home.”
Beaming, Manami linked her arm through Hiroko's and waved at Ryuji:
“Don't worry! Hiroko and I are taking the same train line back. See you back at the hospital, Ryuji—and don't forget what we told you just now!”
Watching the two girls chatting and laughing arm in arm as they walked toward the station, Ryuji let a faint smile touch his lips and turned to head home.

“Hospitalization? Hey, I wasn't planning on staying here that long!... How many days? There's still work waiting for me back at Earth House.”
“Fine, I'll stay. You do a proper job treating me, and I'll cooperate.... Just don't call my whole crew over for something like this.”
“Hey! That's not the procedure you explained earlier, is it?! Are you messing with my body? Double-check the chart first!”
“Oh, so that's how those steps fit together. Got it, we'll do it your way—just tell me ahead of time if anything changes.”
“Just 'standard procedure' and that's it? Hey, at least tell me what you're about to do to me next!”
“...The nurse said she'd keep watching over me the whole time. Fine, I'll trust you guys once. Don't make me regret it.”
“General anesthesia? So I won't know a thing until I wake up... Tsk. The moment I open my eyes, you'd better tell me the result yourselves.”
“Epidural... My head stays wide awake while the lower half of my body won't listen to me? Hey, that sounds way worse than sitting in a cockpit.”
“Local anesthesia, huh. I'll cooperate as best I can, but if it still hurts inside, I'm definitely speaking up!”
“Huh?! No anesthesia at all? I pilot mobile suits—I'm not a mobile suit myself! Are you people serious?!”
“...Hey, don't make me feel like I'm just being left behind here.... All right, I'm leaving the rest to you.”
“It hurts! Hey, did you hear me?! I'm not picking a fight—I really can't take this anymore! Stop for a second!”
“Don't just pin me down out of nowhere!... I know I might jerk around, but who could lie dead still with no anesthesia at all?!”
“Hold me steady if you have to, I never said I wouldn't cooperate... Agh, it's pulling so hard inside—can you go a little slower?”
“My body's so numb you even have to position me yourselves... Fine, I'm counting on you. Just don't let go all of a sudden.”
“Hey, hold on!... Stop bringing that blade any closer! A minute ago I could still yell at you, and now—now I can barely even catch my breath...!”
“...You already cut? There's no sharp pain like I imagined, but feeling you touch me inside... it's really happening to my own body.”
“Ghh—! The outside feels numb, so why does it tug so terribly inside?! Doctor, I can still feel it right there!”
“Aaaah—!! It hurts like hell! Stop! I-I really can't take it... Please stop for a second!”
“You stopped?... Phew. Don't rush me—let me catch my breath for a second. I still want to cooperate properly.”
“I get it, I won't move!... But when it hurts that much, my body flinches on its own!”
“...Go ahead. Just please say something before the next step so you don't startle me all over again.”
“Yeah, keep talking—how far along are we? Knowing the progress keeps my head from jumping to the worst.”
“Hey, what are you staring at me for... Forget it, don't look away. Just for a little while, okay?”
“Why'd everyone suddenly go quiet? Hey! I'm still wide awake here—at least answer me!”
“Really almost wrapping up?... Phew, good. Keep going then—I can hang on a little longer.”
“Breathe in... breathe out... Got it. I'm following your lead, so don't laugh if I'm clumsy right now.”
“...I'll quit making noise for now. Just finish up properly... Thanks.”

"An enema too...?! I know it's pre-op bowel prep, but lifting my hospital gown and lying on my side with my bottom bare... P-please draw the curtain shut first!" (Having my pants pulled down on the bed for a tube... I want to bury my face in the pillow!)

"Nngh... the nozzle is inside my rear... The warm solution keeps flowing into my belly, and my lower stomach is swelling fuller and fuller... I-I'll try my best to clench tight!" (Please stop timing me right beside the bed—if you keep watching, I won't last another minute...!)

"My belly feels so full and crampy, I'm almost at my limit...! Do I really have to hold it for several more minutes before using the toilet...?!" (If I let anything slip right here on the bed, I might as well pass out on the spot...!)

“Uwah—hey, jerk Doctor! This surgery didn't even need an enema, so why'd you still pump my belly full of water?!” (It wasn't even required and yet my belly's pumped full of warm water... You did this on purpose!)

“Safer my foot, you just wanted to mess with me... My stomach's cramping like crazy—quit standing there watching!” (Humiliated like that for no reason—I can't even bring myself to look the doctor in the eye...)

"Skin prep... you have to shave all the hair below my lower abdomen clean too?! I understand it's for sterile disinfection, but exposing that place to be shaved is way too embarrassing..." (Having to spread my legs so they can shave right down there... I'm curling my toes in mortification!)

"Nngh... the warm lather is on, and I can feel every stroke of the razor scraping across my skin so clearly... P-please go slowly!" (Bare skin brushing directly against the sheet feels so cold and sensitive it makes my heart race...)

"I'm not pulling away... It's just that when your fingers press down there to hold the skin taut, my body trembles on its own... Please finish shaving quickly." (With everything shaved bare, the cool air hits right against me—I don't even know where to put my legs...)

“Eek—hold it! The cut isn't down there at all, so why'd you shave my most embarrassing spot completely bald too?!” (The incision isn't even down there, yet you made me spread my legs and shaved me bare... So unfair!)

“Shaved bare nowhere near the surgery... Closing my legs feels weirdly bare and mortifying—where am I supposed to put my face?!” (Clutching my gown hem and scared to move—they saw and shaved every last bit of me for nothing...)
"Tuck all my hair inside the sterile cap... Okay, is it on properly like this?" (Putting on this surgical cap makes my heart jump straight into my throat...)

"Even the stray locks by my ears are tucked in... Putting on this cap really turns me into nothing more than a patient about to go under the knife." (Next stop is the operating table... Deep breaths—don't lose your nerve now!)

"My wrists have to be buckled into restraint straps and my legs spread and secured in holders...?! I know it's required for surgical positioning, but strapped to the table like this, I can't even cover myself!" (The surgical lamp is blinding, and knowing I'll be cut open in this pose makes my heart pound...)

"The cold OR air is blowing right against my bare thighs and skin... Being placed in such an open posture in front of all these staff members has my whole face burning..." (Wide awake yet unable to budge a limb—my palms won't stop sweating...)
"Wait a moment—warn me before you tighten the wrist straps and leg stirrups! I won't move around..." (Strapped down so tight I can't even flinch... Please be gentle with me...)

"With zero anesthesia at all, you're strapping my wrists and legs tightly to the operating table...?! If it hurts unbearably when you cut into me, I won't even be able to flinch!" (Bound wide awake waiting for the raw scalpel... My teeth are already chattering in terror!)

"The feel of the restraint straps biting into my wrists is terrifying... Just thinking about taking the scalpel alive in this completely exposed posture has my legs shaking uncontrollably..." (Pinned fast to the table by my wrists and ankles—even the thought of bolting is gone...)

"P-please make sure the straps are secure... I'm not trying to break free, I'm just terrified my body will thrash on instinct when the real blade slices into me...!" (The blade hasn't even touched me yet and every muscle is already locked stiff with dread...!)

"You're inserting a urinary catheter while I'm wide awake...?! Doesn't that mean spreading my legs apart so you can push a tube into my most private spot... This is way too mortifying!" (Feeling that tube slide inch by inch into my urethra is terrifyingly vivid and uncomfortable...)

"Ah...! The freezing antiseptic swab just touched right there... As the thin tube slides into my urethra, it stings and aches so strangely—my body can't possibly 'relax' like you're asking...!" (How am I supposed to ‘just relax’ right now when even my inner thighs are trembling...)

"Nngh, haah... Is it all the way inside my bladder now? With the balloon inflated, there's a constant swollen urge inside as if I'm leaking..." (Hearing that faint sound in the tubing, I can only bite my lip and turn my burning face away!)

"Without any anesthesia at all, you're pushing the catheter straight in...?! Nngh—ah...! That sharp sting just now felt like my insides were being forced open...!" (Raw, unanesthetized mucosa forced open inch by inch—the burning ache and urge to pee are brutal!)

"My legs are spread wide in the cold air with a tube sticking out of my bladder... Thinking about the un-anesthetized scalpel coming next has my whole body trembling...!" (The scalpel hasn't even touched me and this catheter already has me drenched in cold sweat...!)

"Is the catheter taped to my inner thigh now...? Just having a tube put in already hurts and humiliates me this much—what am I going to do when the real blade comes down..." (Digging my nails into the pad just to keep from sobbing—uncut catheterization is a nightmare...!)

"Sss—it's freezing! The swab soaked in antiseptic is wiping directly across my bare skin, circling outward from the incision center... The chill goes straight to my bones." (Goosebumps rise the instant the cold sponge wipes past, and my heart is beating faster and faster...)

"The disinfection area is even wider than I imagined... With my chest, belly, and private area glistening wet under the shadowless lamp while everyone looks down, I feel as helpless as a specimen awaiting dissection." (Glistening wet under the surgical lamp, all I can do is wait for the drapes and the knife...)

"Wait! The freezing antiseptic has coated the whole surgical field... Does that mean with no anesthesia at all, the very next step is slicing straight into my bare skin with a scalpel?!" (Every swipe feels like tracing a path for the raw blade—my unnumbed skin is already trembling!)

"Just the antiseptic swab brushing across my skin has me shivering uncontrollably... Picturing the searing agony of a real blade slicing through my flesh makes it impossible to catch my breath!" (Please don't cut without warning me first—I'm not ready for raw steel on bare flesh...!)

"I can feel the tip of the marker gliding across my bare skin so clearly... That purple line is the exact spot where you're about to cut my body open, isn't it?" (Seeing that dark incision line drawn across my own skin sends cold sweat down my back...)
"Seeing that line drawn across my body makes it sink in that I'm really about to be opened up by a scalpel..." (My fingers clutch the table pad tight—only one step left before the actual incision...)

"Without a single drop of anesthesia... you're going to cut my flesh open alive right along the line you just drew on me?! ...I can't bear to look down!" (That marker trail feels like a sentence on bare skin—every muscle in my body just locked stiff!)

"D-don't hand over the scalpel so fast! Looking at that marker line on my bare skin has my teeth chattering out of control...!" (My teeth won't stop chattering—facing cold steel without anesthesia strips away all bravado...!)

"Doctor, please promise me... Right before the tip of the blade touches that marker line, warn me out loud first—please don't slice into me without warning...!" (Help, the blade is hovering right over the line... My heart feels like it's about to explode!)
