My name's Chuatury Panlunch—just call me Chuchu. Everyone back at Earth House gets the job done even with old gear. I get into arguments easily, sure, but when I'm sick and seeing a doctor, I know what matters.
Outpatient Examination of Chuatury Panlunch (Chuchu)

"Huh?! I have to strip completely naked for a basic physical? Not even my bra and panties can stay on?! ...I didn't say I wouldn't cooperate, but at least tell me where you're looking first!" (I've never backed down from a fight, but stripping bare in front of them makes my whole face burn!)

"I don't have to strip naked after all? ...Phew, why didn't you say so sooner! Still, if there's really something seriously wrong, don't you dare skip a check just because I raised my voice!" (At least I kept my underwear on, though seeing the nurse jot a note on my chart makes me wonder if they're marking me down as uncooperative...)

"F-fine, alright! Since it's a strict hospital rule, I'll strip! Just get the exam over with quickly once you've looked enough, and don't stare longer than necessary!" (The doctor looks dead serious—if I argue back any more, it'll look like I'm chickening out. Still, pulling off my own bra and panties makes my face burn like it's on fire!) Gritting her teeth, she strips off her coveralls, school uniform, and underwear piece by piece into the tray, leaving her bare, toned body completely exposed to the cool clinic air; craning her flushed neck beneath the examination lamp, she clenches her fists and toughs it out through your full visual and palpation exam.

"...If you'd explained it nicely like that from the start, I wouldn't have snapped at you. Fine, I'll take them off as you say..." (Even when explained politely, the result is still stripping down to nothing. As my panties slide down past my ankles, I wish I had a cockpit to crawl into and hide...) Turning her blazing red cheeks away, she slowly removes her coveralls, school uniform, and underwear, standing stark naked before you and the nurse while muttering under her breath to keep her nerve through the entire physical exam.

"Y-you're holding my treatment over my head?! Everyone at Earth House is waiting for me to come back, so I can't just walk out... I'll strip! I'll strip stark naked right now!" (What a dirty move, threatening to cancel my care! But I can't gamble with my own body and storm out, so I just have to swallow my pride...) With reddened eyes and trembling fingers, she angrily yanks off her coveralls, school uniform, and underwear and tosses them into the tray, standing stark naked under the lamp as she shivers with mortification through the complete physical exam.
Preoperative Preparation of Chuatury Panlunch (Chuchu)
“Doctor, what's the exact order we're doing things in today? It's not that I'm scared of trouble... I just need to be able to explain it clearly if the folks at Earth House ask.”
“I want it spelled out clearly! Once I'm on the table, positioned, and disinfected, right up to when you actually cut... how does everything go step by step? I don't want to just lie there guessing!”

At first, Chuchu tries to stay composed and listen carefully to every pre-op explanation. Yet as she hears about stripping in the ward for an enema and intimate shaving, lying bare on the cold operating table with her limbs strapped down, having her legs parted under the glaring lights for a urinary catheter, and finally having her flesh sliced open by a scalpel, her breathing noticeably falters. Those clinical steps that sounded so routine on paper are about to happen inch by inch to her unshielded body; she clutches the blanket tightly, unable to hide the shame and fear rising in her eyes.
Dr. Sakaguchi will serve as the lead surgeon for Chuatury Panlunch's operation. Select the assistant surgeon, scrub nurse, and circulating nurse to form the surgical team.

Chuatury Panlunch waits in her ward room for pre-op preparation. Assign a ward nurse (or have Dr. Sakaguchi perform the prep personally) to complete the required bowel and skin preparations and up to two optional comfort measures.
“All the prep's done already?... That was fast. Hey, can you give me another second? I haven't gotten my heartbeat to slow down yet.”
With ward preparations complete, you and the surgical team head to the locker room to change into sterile scrubs, complete your surgical scrub at the sink, and step into the operating room.
“Why are these lights so bright... And hey, stop standing around staring at me!... I know, I'm lying still already.”

Before the operation begins, the team gathers around the operating table to verify Chuatury Panlunch's identity, surgical site, planned procedure, and roles. Lying on the cold table amidst the clinking of instruments, Chuchu's voice tightens slightly as she confirms her name.
Review the diagnosis and pre-op assessment for Chuatury Panlunch's current case, and confirm the surgical procedure to perform.
“Hold on! That's not the surgery you told me about earlier, is it?! Check it again first—I'm not here to try my luck!”
Chuatury Panlunch has completed ward preparation and is waiting on the operating table. Confirm the anesthesia method and conditions to begin the operation.
“Okay, I won't move around... Hey, Nurse, you'll keep watching over me the whole time, right?... Then I'm counting on you.”

As the anesthetic takes hold through the mask and IV line, Chuatury Panlunch's eyelids slowly close, and she sinks into the deep, unconscious sleep of general anesthesia. With vitals steady on the monitor, Dr. Sakaguchi signals the team to begin.
“My lower body really is so numb it won't listen to me at all... Tsk. Tell me before you start doing anything—I'm still wide awake!”
“The local anesthesia's kicked in, right? Okay, I'll try my best not to move. If I still feel anything, I'll speak up right away.”
“Hey! We're really starting like this without any anesthesia?!... I know we decided earlier, but seeing the instruments right now is making my heart race!”
Dr. Sakaguchi extends a gloved hand with a brief command, and the scrub nurse places the first gleaming scalpel firmly into his palm.
The assistant surgeon places both hands on either side of the planned incision with sterile gauze, maintaining steady skin tension as she awaits Dr. Sakaguchi's cut.
The shadowless lamp focuses squarely on the center of the exposed surgical field. The sharp tip of the scalpel hovers millimeters above the purple marker line on Chuatury Panlunch's bare skin.

Deep under general anesthesia, Chuatury Panlunch feels nothing as the blade parts her skin. Dr. Sakaguchi and the team work in seamless coordination, dissecting tissue layer by layer and completing the core procedure while the monitor ticks steadily.

The instant the scalpel slices into her flesh, the awake Chuatury Panlunch jolts violently against her restraints, her breathing and physical distress spiking at once. Dr. Sakaguchi must decide how to respond.

Instruments continue separating and retracting deeper within the incision. Wide awake, Chuatury Panlunch endures the visceral dread, tugging, and pain of having her body opened, breathing rapidly as she awaits Dr. Sakaguchi's next response.

The most intense phase of the operation is over, and the team moves into hemostasis and suturing. Looking at the exhausted, sweat-drenched Chuatury Panlunch, how will Dr. Sakaguchi bring this intraoperative exchange to a close?
With the incision fully exposed, the surgical team advances into the key anatomical steps of the procedure.
The core lesion has been addressed and hemostasis across the operative field is secure. You are ready to close and suture the incision.

As the final suture is tied and covered with a sterile dressing, the scrub and circulating nurses complete the instrument and sponge counts, bringing Chuatury Panlunch's operation to a successful close.
“...You already cut? There's no sharp pain like I imagined, but feeling you touch me inside... it's really happening to my own body.”
“Ghh—! The outside feels numb, so why does it tug so terribly inside?! Doctor, I can still feel it right there!”
“Aaaah—!! It hurts like hell! Stop! I-I really can't take it... Please stop for a second!”
strings.collections.character_events.ren_lv1_nig: The ward corridor was quiet at night.
The lights of the nurses' station reflected on the floor, and an occasional monitor beep sounded in the distance.
Ryuji Sakaguchi had just finished a round of the wards and returned to the nurses' station.
Ren Nanase sat at the desk organizing the night-shift handover notes. An open sandwich box rested beside her, with half a sandwich still inside.
“Ah, Dr. Sakaguchi. I finally caught you.”
“You make it sound as if I've done something wrong.”
“Not at all. But I've been looking for you for quite a while.”
She glanced at the night-shift roster on the desk and suddenly smiled.
“Come to think of it, when you first arrived at Hoshimi, the director assigned me to be your partner.”
“Of course I remember. Why bring that up all of a sudden?”
Ren stood and gave Sakaguchi a small, earnest bow.
“Since we happen to be on the night shift together, let me say it properly—I'm in your care tonight, Dr. Sakaguchi!”
“Why so formal all of a sudden?”
Ren straightened and immediately added one more thing.
“But while I have the chance, there is one thing I should make clear first.”
“What do you need to make clear?”
“Being your assigned partner nurse is only a work arrangement. I'm not your personal secretary.”
Then I may really need you to remind the doctor to eat on time.
Don't worry. I always take care of my own personal affairs.
“Then I may really need you to remind the doctor to eat on time.”
Ren blinked, looked at the half sandwich left in the box on the desk, and could not help laughing.
“...Doctor, is that your indirect way of reminding me that even I haven't had time to finish dinner?”
“Honestly, teasing me like that... You made me nervous for nothing.”
“Don't worry. I always take care of my own personal affairs.”
Ren let out a quiet breath and smiled with relief.
“That's good. Someone once asked whether being an assigned partner meant I could also find his glasses and organize his desk... It seems Dr. Sakaguchi needs no one to worry about things like that.”
“This is a hospital. Nurses have more important professional responsibilities.”
“Hearing the lead surgeon say that himself is very reassuring.”
Ren pushed the sandwich box aside and drew a chart from the folder.
“All right, down to business. I was looking for you because I have a record that I want the lead surgeon to verify personally.”
Ren opened the chart and slid it between them.
“Bed 34, scheduled for a local excision of a breast mass tomorrow morning.”
“Bed 34... Thirty-four years old. A solitary nodule was found on screening ultrasound, and the biopsy favors a benign fibroadenoma. I reviewed her imaging and operative plan this afternoon.”
She laid several records side by side on the desk.
“The examination report and the surgery booking say right side. So does the consent form the patient signed.”
Ren pulled out a nursing record left during the evening handover.
“But this preoperative nursing record from the evening handover says ‘left’ in the field for the planned operation and preoperative preparation site.”
Sakaguchi looked at the place she indicated.
It was exactly as she said.
“That's possible. But when the records disagree, I don't want to dismiss it as a clerical error without verifying it.”
“I have. She said she remembered it being the right side, but after seeing this note, she wasn't sure anymore.”
“She said, ‘It's fine. Whatever the doctors and nurses decide is all right.’”
“But I don't think she really is.”

“When I went to check her evening preparations and take her temperature, she folded the handover note and tucked it under her pillow. After I turned away, she quietly took it out and read it again several times.”

“She was clearly worried that we might have it wrong, but she did not dare ask directly, probably because she was afraid of troubling a doctor this late. She only mentioned it quietly after I asked whether something was worrying her.”
Sakaguchi stood and retrieved the patient's original imaging report, initial consultation record, and operative plan, checking each in turn.
The lesion's location in the right upper outer quadrant and the operative plan were both unambiguous.
Ren looked up in mild surprise.
“Didn't you say she still seemed worried?”
“That's true... but I thought you would say we should leave the formal explanation until tomorrow morning's preoperative verification.”
“Of course we will verify it again tomorrow according to the preoperative protocol. But since we found the discrepancy tonight, we should resolve it face-to-face tonight.”
“Besides, the patient needs to be able to sleep.”
“Yes! That's what I thought too. I'll bring the verification documents and lead the way.”
The lights in the ward had already been dimmed.
The adult woman in Bed 34 by the window was still awake.
Hearing footsteps, she hurriedly sat up a little.
“Oh... Doctor, nurse. I'm sorry to make you come here so late.”
“It's all right. Nurse Nanase told me you still had some questions about tomorrow's operation.”
The patient glanced at Ren beside the bed and lowered her head awkwardly.
“No, it isn't anything important... Maybe I simply read it wrong. The doctors are busy enough during the day. You didn't have to come all this way just for me...”
“The handover note really does say left side. That's why we're checking it again.”
“But… I remember it being the right side.”
Sakaguchi sat beside the bed and showed her the verified operative plan and initial consultation record.
“Yes. We just rechecked the original imaging, clinical records, and surgical consent form. The lesion is clearly on the right, and tomorrow's operation is planned for the right side.”
The patient looked at the word ‘right’ in the record and visibly relaxed:
“Then why does that paper say left?”

“There is an error in the nursing handover record. We are verifying and correcting it according to procedure, and we will notify the relevant staff. Before tomorrow's operation, the entire surgical team will confirm your identity, the operation, and the surgical site with you again.”
“I see... I thought I had remembered it wrong.”
“But the doctors are so busy, and I don't understand these things. I thought... perhaps it was just written differently in medical terms.”
“Left and right can't be different ways of writing the same thing.”
The patient was startled for a moment, then smiled a little.
“Since we're here, you can ask about anything else you don't understand or that is troubling you.”
The patient hesitated, her fingers tightening slightly.
“Then... after tomorrow's operation, will the scar be very noticeable? I don't usually wear clothes that show my shoulders, but the thought of having a scar still upsets me.”
Ren glanced quietly at Sakaguchi, stepped back half a pace, and poured the patient a cup of warm water, placing it by the bed.
Sakaguchi explained the anticipated extent of resection, the incision plan, and the possible postoperative changes.

“On the current imaging, the mass is about one and a half centimeters and appears benign. If tomorrow's operative findings match the preoperative assessment, we plan to place the incision along the edge of the areola or a natural skin crease and close it with fine absorbable sutures, minimizing the cosmetic impact as much as possible.”

“The exact extent of treatment and final conclusion will, of course, depend on the operative findings and subsequent pathology, and healing varies from person to person. But while completing the operation safely, we will do everything we can to keep the mark as small as possible.”
The patient asked several more questions, and Sakaguchi answered each one.
Ren neither spoke for the patient nor hurried her. Only when the patient momentarily forgot a question did Ren gently remind her:
“When you changed clothes earlier, you also said you wanted to ask when you could resume normal activity and bathe after the operation.”
Sakaguchi and Ren carefully explained the precautions for early postoperative activity and keeping the wound protected from water.
By the time they finished talking, it was nearly midnight.
At last, the patient relaxed completely.
“I'm sorry I took so much of your time.”
“It wasn't a waste of time. You're the one having surgery tomorrow. It's only right that you understand these things.”
“If you hadn't asked me, I probably would have kept it to myself.”
“…You'll make me blush if you say that.”
This time, she finally gave a natural smile as she spoke.
The two returned to the nurses' station.

While preserving the traceability of the original entry, Ren followed procedure to record the verified correction, signature, date, and time in full, then prepared the correction and handover notice for the relevant staff.
Sakaguchi stood beside her and confirmed that all relevant medical records were now consistent.
“Yes. I'll remind them again in person at tomorrow morning's handover.”
“You didn't see one discrepancy and make a guess, and you didn't stop checking just because the patient said she was fine.”
Ren looked at the chart and spoke quietly.
“That's because... it clearly mattered to her.”
“I know doctors have a lot to do every day. A single error in a record can look like a very small thing.”
“But it may not be small to the patient, especially when she is having surgery tomorrow.”
She let out a quiet breath.
“Actually, before I called you over, I was worried I might be disturbing you.”
“If something needs the surgeon's confirmation, you should call the surgeon.”
“So what? If you have to consider whether the doctor might be offended before raising a problem, what is the point of a nurse questioning the lead surgeon?”
Ren fell silent for a moment.
Then, as if trying to hide something, she suddenly straightened her back.
“Then I'm really going to be strict with you from now on!”
“If you forget to write your notes, I'll remind you.”
“If the preoperative preparations haven't been checked, I'll keep asking.”
“If the lead surgeon tries to rest after an operation without clearly completing the postoperative medical handover—”
Then please go and bring the doctor back.
I'm lucky to have a partner who dares to point out the surgeon's mistakes.
Ren blinked, then could not help laughing.
“What lead surgeon asks a nurse to drag him back?”
“I'm lucky to have a partner who dares to point out the surgeon's mistakes.”
Ren blushed slightly and looked away in embarrassment.
“...When you suddenly praise someone that seriously, you leave her with no idea what to say.”
Ren gathered the records she had organized.
“You're a little different from what I imagined.”
“You didn't just correct the handover note and call the matter closed.”
“Didn't you say she was still anxious?”
“…Yes. She kept saying she was fine, but she almost wore that paper out from looking at it.”
“In the end, she asked about the scar and life after surgery.”
“Yes. Those were the things she really wanted to ask but couldn't bring herself to say.”
“You noticed first. I only listened to the rest of what she had to say with you.”
Ren watched him for a moment, then said softly:
“Well then, Dr. Sakaguchi. Since we worked well together tonight, I have a request too.”
“Please don't give me every odd job on the night shift just because I'm usually agreeable.”
Ren finally sat down again and opened the sandwich box that had been waiting so long.
Sakaguchi poured two cups of warm barley tea and placed one by her hand.
“I ate half of it this afternoon and meant to finish the rest tonight. But I've been busy until now.”
She picked up the sandwich but did not eat immediately, glancing instead at the night beyond the window.
“Dr. Sakaguchi, what do you think of the night shift here?”
“If every ward stays quiet and no one rings the call bell, I wouldn't mind sitting here and resting for a while.”
“Ha ha, how practical. But... I really do like the night shift here now.”

“Because the nights here are peaceful. The corridors are quiet, and all I need to do is walk calmly through each ward, listen to the patients breathing, and see whether a blanket has fallen from someone's bed.”
She took a small bite of her sandwich.

“So my greatest wish now is for every night shift to be safe and uneventful—so boring that I can finish my sandwich in peace. Then morning comes, everyone changes clothes and goes home as usual, and we buy ice cream at the convenience store on the corner...”
A rapid ward call alarm suddenly sounded from the nurses' station panel.
The sandwich Ren had just raised to her mouth stopped in midair.
The nurses' station was silent for two seconds.
“Bed 27—the postoperative observation patient who had an open cholecystectomy this afternoon.”
Ren looked at the sandwich in her hand, with only one small bite taken from it, sighed softly, and resignedly put it back in the box and closed the lid.
“I take it back. Wishing for an uneventful night in a hospital really is the greatest luxury.”
“It looks like your late-night snack will have to wait.”
Ren stood, straightened her nurse's uniform, and turned to Sakaguchi with a brilliant smile.
“This is the night-shift ward, after all!”
Sakaguchi pushed open the nurses' station gate.
One after the other, they hurried into the corridor.
strings.collections.character_events.narumi_lv1_: Afternoon sunlight streamed into the surgical office.
Ryuji Sakaguchi was reviewing the day's operating schedule. His name appeared in the lead surgeon field for the next open ovarian cystectomy, while Narumi Jinguji was listed as first assistant.
The office door opened, and Narumi Jinguji entered carrying two cups of hot tea.
“It looks as though you've already seen the afternoon schedule.”
Sakaguchi accepted the cup she offered him.
“Yes. You'll be my first assistant for this afternoon's operation?”
“No. I simply remember that you followed this patient from her initial consultation through her admission assessment, so I assumed you would lead the operation.”
She set the other cup in front of herself without rushing to drink it.
“Still, the director showed me your résumé a few days ago—your experience at several overseas hospitals, and those rather impressive surgical records.”
She drew out the words, a faint smile on her face.
“Whenever a résumé looks a little too impressive, I become curious. I want to see for myself whether the doctor standing at the operating table is truly as reliable as he appears on paper.”
If a senior colleague is testing me personally, I'll have to show you what I can really do.
It sounds as though today's first assistant is stricter than the operation itself.
“If a senior colleague is evaluating me personally, then naturally I'll have to show you what I can really do.”
Narumi raised an eyebrow slightly and smiled.
“A very composed answer. But I only arrived at Hoshimi a little before you and was assigned to help you learn our procedures. I would hardly call myself your senior.”
“Anyone who can keep watch over a lead surgeon at the operating table deserves respect.”
“Flattery won't earn you any extra points once we're in the operating room.”
“It sounds as though today's first assistant is stricter than the operation itself.”
Narumi blinked, then gave a quiet laugh.
“My, I've been nothing but gentle. How did I suddenly become a strict examiner?”
“Gentle people are often at their strictest when they say they want to see for themselves.”
Narumi picked up the chart and tapped it lightly against the desk.
“Don't take it too seriously. I've checked your surgical credentials and the patient's arrangements. This is a normal assignment, not a test using a patient as the exam question.”
“But since we have a chance to operate together, I do want to take a good look.”
“In that case, I'd like to learn from a Hoshimi senior as well.”
“What happens here if the lead surgeon ignores the first assistant's opinion?”
“Oh? That depends on how capable he is.”
“Though there's one way your overseas experience won't give you much of an advantage here.”
“The nurses at Hoshimi don't care how many awards you won overseas. If you ask for an instrument vaguely or fail to explain a step clearly, they'll make you clarify it all the same.”
“I prefer a team that's willing to correct the lead surgeon.”
She didn't continue the joke. Instead, she turned the chart to the page of examination results.
Narumi spread the patient's pelvic examination and imaging records across the desk.
“The patient is thirty-two. She has a right ovarian cyst, and her symptoms have persisted for some time. Imaging suggests it's benign, but its size and position led us to recommend surgery.”
“The plan is to remove the cyst through an open approach while preserving as much normal ovarian tissue as possible.”
“Yes. That matters a great deal to her.”
“She asked me several times whether, if conditions allow, we can remove only the cyst and leave the ovary.”
“I told her that's our goal, but I can't make an absolute promise before we see the actual situation.”
“After I told her that, she asked again.”
Sakaguchi noticed a separate handwritten note beside the consultation record:
“So you made a separate note of it.”
“The surgical record tells us what we plan to do. Sometimes the patient's words tell us why we need to do it carefully.”
“You're not remembering it for my sake.”
Narumi walked to the desk and pulled out a neatly bound set of research materials and clinical summary notes.
Sakaguchi leafed through the first few pages of anatomical-layer notes and follow-up analyses before his eyes settled on the author credited on a paper filed at the back.
“This clinical review of detailed female pelvic anatomy and tissue preservation is very solid... ‘Ryuji Hirasaka’?”
Narumi's movement stopped for an instant.
“I read his research on female pelvic anatomy and operative field management while I was overseas. The level of detail is genuinely impressive.”
She closed the materials and set them back at one side of the desk.
At some point, the smile had faded from her face.
Sakaguchi had been about to say something else, but Narumi had already reopened the patient's imaging records.
Sakaguchi returned his attention to the images:
“Look here. The planes on the images may not match what we find during surgery exactly. If the base is adherent to the surrounding tissue, we'll need to establish a clear operative field first.”
“If the boundary isn't clear at first, there is no reason to force the dissection from the outside. Identify the surrounding tissue first, then adjust the traction.”
Her usual lightness returned to her voice.
“At least you sound like more than a doctor with a pretty résumé when we discuss a case.”
Sakaguchi glanced at the research materials set aside on the desk.
He had the vague impression that the earlier subject had displeased Narumi. Perhaps she simply had reservations about that researcher's views; there was no need to press her now.
Narumi had administered anesthesia according to the preoperative plan, and all other preparations were complete.
Under the surgical lamps, the team performed its final checks.
“Patient identity, procedure, site, and consent form all match.”
With her surgical cap and mask on, all that remained visible of her usually gentle face were her focused eyes.
“The instrument table here may differ from what you're used to. If you need anything, just say so. There's no need to accommodate me.”
“I have something to say as well.”
“If there's anything I miss, please point it out directly.”
But after the layers were opened and the target tissue exposed, the actual findings proved slightly more complex than the preoperative images suggested.
“The adhesions here are more pronounced than expected.”
“I see them. Don't pull outward too firmly yet; we don't want to rupture the cyst wall.”
She skillfully placed moist gauze and changed the retractor's angle of traction.
The operative field, which had been somewhat cramped, became much clearer.
“That's a good angle. Hold it there.”
The instrument nurse passed them an instrument.
The two began to work together with increasing ease.

Narumi did not stand by like an examiner merely watching Sakaguchi work. When assistance was needed, she provided precise traction and suction; when the tissue planes were unclear, she voiced her opinion without hesitation.
As the dissection continued along the capsule boundary, oozing increased at the junction with the base.
“Wait. There's still a very thin layer of tissue here.”

“This plane lies directly against the normal ovarian tissue. If we continue dissecting from this side and add hemostasis, we could easily injure the part we need to preserve. Wouldn't continuing through the loose plane on the other side make it easier to preserve the normal tissue?”
Sakaguchi carefully confirmed the anatomical plane she indicated.
“You're right. Continuing from that side will reduce traction and injury to the normal tissue. We'll follow your suggestion.”
With steady hands, she changed the direction of traction and brought the clear capsular plane on the opposite side into the center of the operative field.
A moment later, the dissection resumed. Along the adjusted approach, the cyst was soon removed intact, with the normal ovarian tissue well preserved.
“A lead surgeon who gets distracted at a time like this loses points.”
Her eyes curved slightly in a smile.
With the cyst removed, the team carefully inspected the operative site and confirmed hemostasis.
“We've preserved a good amount of normal ovarian tissue.”
Before the operation ended, the team again confirmed the procedure performed, the specimen, and the instrument count.
After completing the postoperative record, Sakaguchi returned to the surgical office.
The two cups of tea from the afternoon were on the desk.
Sakaguchi picked up his own cup.
“I thought a doctor back from overseas might be more particular about taking breaks.”
“Working abroad was no different. When things get busy, there's no time to think about breaks.”
“I checked on the patient again just now. She's recovering well from anesthesia. We still have to wait for the pathology results, but the operation met its planned objective.”
Narumi lifted her teacup, then set it down again.
“I think I understand a little better now why the director was so eager to bring you to Hoshimi.”
“Your hands are steady, and your judgment in the moment is good.”
“But I think what's rarer is that you listen seriously to other people even when you're the lead surgeon.”
“Why wouldn't I listen to an experienced first assistant?”
“…Some doctors don't see it that way.”
But the seriousness lasted only a moment.
“Then I'll be a little more honest too.”
“Before we went into the operating room today, I had planned to test you more during the preoperative discussion and on the technical details—to put you through your paces a little.”
“In the end, I couldn't find an opportunity.”
“After all, working with a doctor who truly knows what he's doing is much more interesting than proving my own assessment right.”
Then I'll give Dr. Jinguji an evaluation too—you are an excellent first assistant, but you must also be a formidable lead surgeon.
Now that I've passed the first assessment, how about you operate next time and let me match your rhythm?
“Then I'll give Dr. Jinguji an evaluation too—you are an excellent first assistant, but you must also be a formidable lead surgeon.”
“That is more accurate than you might imagine. Next time we have the opportunity, let's switch places and see whether you can match my surgical rhythm.”
“Now that I've passed the first assessment, how about you operate next time and let me match your surgical rhythm?”
“Just what I had in mind. You can be my first assistant, and I'll see whether you can keep up with my rhythm. I can be a very demanding lead surgeon.”
Narumi stood and gathered the materials from the desk.
She reached the doorway, then suddenly looked back.
“…I thought you would have said that when I first arrived.”
“Back then, I'd only seen your résumé.”
“Today I finally met the person himself.”
Sakaguchi looked at the cup of tea on the desk, now completely cold.
He realized he was already looking forward to operating with her again.
It wasn't because someone had acknowledged his credentials.
It was because there were colleagues here who truly deserved his respect.
strings.collections.character_events.narumi_lv4_: An adult pursuit—and genuine affection—after the white coat comes off.
A soft night rain pattered beyond the wooden lattice window, while warm yellow paper lanterns cast a gentle glow over the table in the izakaya's half-private booth.
The aromas of grilled chicken skewers and salt-roasted ginkgo nuts mingled with the warmth of sake, slowly spreading between the narrow wooden tables.

Narumi Jinguji was not wearing the plain glasses she occasionally used for reading papers at the hospital, nor her immaculate white coat. A fitted, deep burgundy knit dress traced her mature figure. Resting her cheek on one hand, she regarded him through lightly tipsy eyes with a languor rarely seen in the clinic.
"Here, Chief Surgeon Sakaguchi. This one is on me."
She lifted the sake flask and unhurriedly filled Ryuji Sakaguchi's shallow cup, her fingertip seeming to brush the back of his hand by accident.
"Why so formal all of a sudden? I thought tonight was just an ordinary dinner out."
Narumi took a small sip, leaving a faint sheen on the rim of the porcelain cup.
"I've called you 'Dr. Sakaguchi' all week at the hospital. On the rare Sunday night when I don't have to read charts or listen to Aqua go on about her data model, of course I deserve a proper treat."
The corners of her eyes lifted as she appraised him with an enigmatic smile.
"Or have you grown so used to seeing me in scrubs, Dr. Sakaguchi, that you don't recognize me in a different outfit?"
"I was only thinking that, dressed like this, you're even harder to look away from than you are in the surgical office."
Narumi laughed and leaned slightly forward, the neckline of her dress forming an elegant curve.
"Such a sweet talker. It seems your overseas training taught more than how to hold a scalpel."

They chatted over several small dishes, moving from the latest troublesome family in the outpatient clinic to the laptop Aqua had nearly ruined with sandwich mayonnaise. The mood was relaxed and familiar.
After several rounds of drinks, Ryuji recalled a name he had seen on the day's roster and asked casually.
"Come to think of it, Nurse Nanase wasn't scheduled today either, was she? I assumed the two of you often went out together when you had weekends off."
The smile on Narumi's face abruptly faded.
She set down her cup, narrowed her beautiful eyes, and deliberately glared at him with feigned displeasure in her voice.
"Talking about another woman while you're on a date with one?"
At the sight of him suddenly at a loss for words, Narumi could no longer contain the mischief in her eyes. She burst into laughter and lightly tapped the table with one fingertip.
"I'm teasing. It was only a joke. Look how nervous you got."
She picked up her cup again, rubbing the warm porcelain with her thumb as genuine warmth and concern gradually entered her expression.

"Ren went shopping with some of the younger nurses today. That girl... She may always look gentle and obedient, but you saw her at the negotiating table. When it is truly time to decide, she has a mind of her own more than anyone."
"When she told that person, 'It was my own decision,' she really was admirable."
Narumi sighed softly, her eyes holding the concern of an older sister and a longtime partner.
"Yes. She stopped being a little girl who needed me to decide for her a long time ago. Even knowing that she can make her own decisions, after all these years I still can't help worrying about her."
Then Narumi raised her eyes and looked directly into Ryuji's.

"So, Dr. Sakaguchi, let me make one thing clear in advance. If you truly decide to pursue Ren someday, that is between the two of you. But if you ever treat her poorly or make her shed so much as half a tear, I will not let you off."
"So, Dr. Sakaguchi, let me tell you this to your face. Ren has chosen you, and that is her decision. But if you ever treat her poorly or make her shed so much as half a tear, I will not let you off."
Her tone was as calm as if she were discussing the weather, yet left no doubt that she meant every word.
(Tighten your grip on the cup, slightly flustered.) "...I really was only asking how she was doing."
(Meet her gaze with a wry smile.) "After seeing Dr. Jinguji negotiate in the director's office, I would never dare ignore that warning."
Ryuji instinctively tightened his grip on the cup.
"...I really was only asking how she was doing."
Narumi studied him for two seconds before the seriousness in her eyes instantly gave way to a teasing smile. Covering her mouth with one hand, she laughed until her shoulders trembled.
"Why do you get nervous the moment I tease you? How cute."
Ryuji met her gaze and smiled helplessly.
"After seeing Dr. Jinguji negotiate in the director's office, I would never dare ignore that warning."
Narumi saw the way he had tensed for an instant and smiled, her eyes curving with amusement.
"Your face turned so serious just now, yet you're still pretending otherwise. Why do you get nervous the moment I tease you? How cute."
Narumi drained the last of her sake, a faint flush coloring both cheeks.
She set down her cup and gently brushed Ryuji's calf with her toes beneath the small table, fixing him with a direct gaze.
"All right, enough about other people. How are you planning to keep me company for the rest of tonight, Dr. Sakaguchi?"
The rain had stopped by the time they left the izakaya. A damp evening breeze swept through the neon-lit intersection, carrying the coolness of night.
They walked side by side to the crossroads. As Ryuji stopped to ask which way led to her apartment, Narumi reached out and naturally linked her arm through his.
The softness of her chest pressed against the crook of his arm through the thin knit fabric, bringing with it the scent of roses and faint sake.
Narumi looked toward a quietly lit boutique hotel not far away, a smile curling at her lips.
"Dr. Sakaguchi, I don't particularly feel like going back to my lonely room tonight."
She turned toward him, her lightly tipsy yet lucid eyes studying him from close range, and lowered her voice.
"Will you come sit with me over there?"
Ryuji looked at her lips, now only inches away.
Narumi laughed softly. Her fingers slid down his forearm until they intertwined with his.
"Two small flasks of sake aren't enough to get me drunk. I know exactly what I'm doing, Ryuji Sakaguchi. What about you? Do you dare come with me?"
Ryuji asked no more questions. He clasped her warm fingers and led her through the hotel entrance.
The soft click of the door closing and locking sounded unusually clear in the quiet entryway.
Before Ryuji could reach for the room's main light, Narumi turned beneath the single dim wall lamp and raised both arms around his neck.
Warm, soft lips carrying the lingering taste of sake met his.
Her kiss was practiced and composed. Her tongue deftly parted his lips, and a barely audible hum escaped with her breath.
"Mm... I've wanted to do this ever since I watched you drinking at the izakaya..."

Ryuji wrapped an arm around her waist and drew her against the edge of the bed, trying to deepen the kiss. But as their breaths mingled, Narumi turned her head aside, placed her slender fingers against his chest, and pushed him back onto the broad mattress.
Narumi looked down at him, her eyes dancing with a teasing smile.
"Don't rush, Dr. Sakaguchi. I always follow your directions when you're operating. Shouldn't it be my turn to take charge tonight?"
She slowly reached for the hem of her deep burgundy knit dress and drew it upward, inch by inch, along the curves of her waist and hips.
In the dim light, pale, full skin and black lace lingerie came into view. Unabashed beneath Ryuji's heated gaze, she removed the last restraint, parted her long legs, and straddled his waist.
Ryuji's breathing deepened as both hands settled at the warm roots of her thighs.

Narumi leaned down, her long hair falling on either side of his chest. One hand pressed his shoulder while the other reached naturally toward the heat between them, her fingertips guiding him as she whispered against his ear.
"Your heart is racing... Don't move. Let me..."
As her hips slowly descended, enveloping heat and tightness swallowed them both at once.
Narumi arched her slender neck, an uncontrollable, trembling sigh spilling from deep in her throat.
"Mmm... ahh... You're... deeper than I imagined..."
Though her fingertips trembled at the overwhelming fullness of their first moment together, she kept firm control of the rhythm from above.

Bracing both hands against Ryuji's broad chest, she used the supple strength of her hips to lead every alternating rise, descent, and grinding stroke. At first she could still look down with an amused smile, tracing his throat and lips with her fingertips. But when the hands at her hips tightened and he began thrusting up to meet her, Narumi's effortless composure gradually dissolved into genuine abandon and a deep flush.
"Ah... mm, wait... Ryuji, there... too deep...!"
Ryuji supported her sweat-dampened lower back.
"Didn't we agree that you would be in charge tonight?"

Narumi bit her moist lower lip, the corners of her eyes reddening. Rather than retreat, she leaned down, wrapped herself tightly around his neck, pressed her heated chest to his, and moved her hips with even greater boldness and urgency.
"Ahh... I never said... you could take over... Mmm... Look at me, Ryuji... You're only allowed to look at me...!"

Quickened breaths, the wet sound of skin meeting skin, and low moans intertwined beneath the light until they reached the peak together in a final, taut shudder. Only then did she collapse bonelessly into his arms, burying her burning cheek against his neck while her ragged breathing slowly settled.
The night deepened, leaving only a dim warm light beside the bed.
A thin blanket half covered their intertwined bodies. Narumi lay languidly on her side beside Ryuji, one pale leg carelessly draped over his while her finger traced idle circles across his chest.
Ryuji held her smooth shoulder and looked down at her relaxed, contented expression.
Sensing his gaze, Narumi opened her eyes and curved her lips in an understanding smile.
"Let me guess what you're thinking. You wonder whether I bought you drinks and brought you to a hotel tonight only because you helped me with the Hirasaka matter, don't you?"
"After everything we went through together, it is hard not to read more into it."
Narumi gave a soft, amused hum, propped herself up on one elbow, and met his eyes with an earnest, candid expression.

"Then you underestimate me, Dr. Sakaguchi. If I only wanted to repay you for helping at the negotiating table, I could take a few troublesome surgeries off your hands or add your name to a new research project. I, Narumi Jinguji, have kept accounts my entire life. I can still tell the difference between a debt of gratitude and a set of bedsheets."
She lowered her head and lightly kissed Ryuji's lips, pure delight spreading through her eyes.
"So don't think of this as repayment. I simply like you."
Ryuji stared for a moment, then clasped the hand resting on his chest.
Narumi nestled back into his arms, found the most comfortable position, and closed her eyes. Her voice was languid but certain.
"It is that simple. I wanted you, and I wanted to hold you, so I did. What, is Chief Surgeon Sakaguchi dissatisfied with that reason?"
Ryuji laughed and tightened his arms around her.
Monday morning at Hoshimi Hospital was as busy and orderly as ever.

When Ryuji returned to the surgical office after morning handover, Narumi was already at her desk in plain glasses, intently reviewing the preoperative assessment for the afternoon's abdominal-wall hernia repair.

Every button of her white coat was fastened with impeccable precision, and her long hair was neatly tied back. Even the faint mark still lingering on her neck from the previous night was completely hidden beneath her collar.
Ryuji walked over to her desk.
Narumi looked up, met his eyes calmly and naturally, and offered a standard professional smile.
"Good morning, Dr. Sakaguchi. Perfect timing. The repeat coagulation panel for the patient in bed three just came back. Take a look."
There were no lingering, suggestive looks, no shyness after becoming intimate, and no special treatment.
She picked up her red-and-blue pencil and crisply indicated two details on the lab report and preoperative plan.

"The patient stopped anticoagulants two hours later than planned last night. The current INR is barely within the safe range, but your preoperative plan lists only conventional gelatin sponge as backup for bleeding in the preperitoneal space. To be safe, I suggest having the scrub nurse prepare an additional bipolar cautery set and absorbable hemostatic gauze."
Ryuji looked down and checked the figures.
"You're right. I overlooked that. Add what you suggested."
Narumi nodded, closed the chart after signing her review, and handed it back to him.
"Everything else is fine. I'm going to make rounds on the ward. I'll see you in the operating room this afternoon."
Watching her leave the office with the chart held in her arms, composed and capable, Ryuji remained where he was with a subtle sense of confusion.

She was clearly neither angry nor deliberately distancing herself from him. Yet compared with the woman who had whispered, 'I simply like you,' beside his ear in a hotel bed the night before, Dr. Jinguji was being almost excessively professional.
It was not until half past noon, after lunch, that Ryuji encountered Narumi again around a corridor corner.
She carried two warm cans of black coffee. Seeing no one nearby, she slipped one into his hand and murmured.
"The breeze is pleasant up there. If you have a moment, come have coffee with me on the roof."
Afternoon sunlight covered the open hospital roof. A breeze stirred the chain-link fence, carrying the distant noise of the city.
Narumi leaned against the rooftop railing, opened her can, and took a small sip of warm coffee.
Hearing the rooftop door open behind her, she turned. At last, her eyes held the same teasing intimacy as the night before.
"What is it, Chief Surgeon Sakaguchi? You've spent the whole morning secretly watching my expression. Are you wondering if last night was only a pleasant dream?"
"I wouldn't call it a dream. I just didn't expect Dr. Jinguji to switch roles faster than a scalpel the moment she put on her white coat."
"You were so merciless when you picked apart my preoperative plan this morning that I wondered whether my performance last night had been unsatisfactory."
Ryuji stepped beside her and leaned against the railing.
"I wouldn't call it a dream. I just didn't expect Dr. Jinguji to switch roles faster than a scalpel the moment she put on her white coat."
Narumi laughed and shot him a sidelong glance.
"If I looked at you in the surgical office the way I did last night, every nurse in the hospital would know about us before half a day had passed."
Ryuji stepped beside her and leaned against the railing.
"You were so merciless when you picked apart my preoperative plan this morning that I wondered whether my performance last night had been unsatisfactory."
Narumi burst into laughter and lowered her voice for a teasing retort.
"Don't worry. If I were grading last night, you would already have a perfect score. As for criticizing you this morning, you really did omit the hemostasis contingency from your plan."
Once their laughter subsided, Narumi turned away, holding the warm coffee can in both hands as she looked down at the hospital's bright, immaculate courtyard.
The breeze lifted a few loose strands along her cheek. Her voice became calm and serious.
"Ryuji, I wasn't trying to put on airs in the office this morning. But as long as I am at work and still wearing this white coat, I want to devote myself to being a good doctor."
She paused, sincere warmth entering her eyes.

"I know better than anyone how badly my reputation and circumstances had deteriorated when Ren and I left our previous hospital. Asuka knew perfectly well that I had a difficult past, yet she hired us in spite of all the criticism and gave me a clean desk and operating table here at Hoshimi... I don't want to betray that trust."
Ryuji listened in silence and nodded gently.
"I understand. During working hours, we are colleagues and partners first."
Narumi turned toward him, a soft curve appearing at her lips.
"Yes. And isn't our private affection more interesting when we save it for outside working hours?"
She took half a step closer to Ryuji.
The distance between them closed until they could hear each other's breathing. Narumi raised her face slightly, watched him in silence, and spoke softly.

"And you don't need to feel burdened by anything that happened last night. There truly isn't anything I want from you. Just spend time with me when you can. If I genuinely wanted something from you, it would not be this relaxed and easy."
She delivered the final sentence slowly and softly. It sounded playful and suggestive, yet underneath lay a quiet edge and a trace of danger.
Ryuji looked at her smiling face, now inches from his own, and answered without flinching.
"Then I should be grateful that, for now, Dr. Jinguji only wants me to drink coffee with her."
Narumi narrowed her eyes in satisfaction and lightly tapped the lapel of his white coat with one slender finger.

"Good that you understand. Lunch break is almost over. I'll see you at the operating table this afternoon. And if your attention wanders during the procedure, I still won't spare your pride, Dr. Sakaguchi."
Leaving him with that playful warning, she tossed the empty can into the recycling bin by the door, opened the rooftop door, and disappeared down the stairs with her usual composed stride.

strings.collections.character_events.hiroko_lv2_: Off Work on Time for Once
After the last surgery of the afternoon wraps up smoothly, Hiroko stands outside the nurses' station studying a shopping street food map in dead earnest.
Off Work on Time for Once
At 4:10 PM, the main shadowless lamp in Operating Room 2 had already been switched off, leaving only the soft overhead lighting.

The last scheduled surgery of the day had just concluded smoothly, and the patient had been escorted to the recovery room. Standing beside the instrument table, Hiroko Sugimura briskly finished counting the final set of hemostats and suture needles, then pushed the verified sign-off sheet toward the charting desk.

Ryuji Sakaguchi peeled off his sterile gloves, tossed them into the medical waste bin, and walked up to the charting desk to pick up a pen. Before he could even speak, Hiroko had already flipped another folder open to the exact page and placed it steadily beside his hand.

"Here is the postoperative order confirmation sheet, and this is the special instrument preparation checklist for tomorrow morning's two surgeries—I've already highlighted the key items according to your usual preferences."
Sakaguchi's fingers paused as he took the folder, and he couldn't help looking up at her.
"How do you always know what I'm about to ask before I even say a word?"
Hiroko's eyes curved into a gentle, slightly proud smile.
"Hehe. Work alongside you for this long, Doctor, and I'm bound to pick up a little experience."
As Sakaguchi signed the postoperative record, he asked casually:
"Am I really that easy to read?"
Hiroko tilted her head slightly, tapping her chin lightly with a fingertip:
Sakaguchi stopped his pen and looked at her:
Hiroko let out a soft giggle, her eyes curving into lovely crescents:
Just then, the outer intercom of the operating room chimed once, and a ward nurse poked her head in through the doorway to report:

"Excuse me, Dr. Sakaguchi, Nurse Sugimura. The inpatient ward just called to ask—since this afternoon's operations finished early, the family of the inguinal hernia repair patient in Bed 42, originally scheduled for the second slot tomorrow morning, is wondering if we could move the surgery up to this evening instead?"

Sakaguchi glanced at the wall clock. It was just past four-ten, and for patients who had already completed admission procedures, hospital policy did allow surgeries to be scheduled into the evening or even late at night depending on actual circumstances.
Sakaguchi pulled up Bed 42's electronic chart and looked it over:

"Bed 42 is already admitted, and all of the preoperative lab work came back this afternoon. As long as we confirm fasting status and anesthesia readiness with the ward, adding an uncomplicated indirect inguinal hernia repair to tonight's schedule is medically feasible..."
He turned his head, habitually consulting his partner beside him:
"Hiroko, what do you think from the OR scheduling side?"
The relaxed smile on Hiroko's face faded slightly as her gaze swept earnestly across the scheduling board and instrument turnover log before she spoke in a clear, structured tone:

"From the standpoint of medical readiness and operating time, it is certainly something we could consider. However, Dr. Sakaguchi, we already performed three consecutive surgeries this afternoon, and all of the standard surgical instrument sets from that batch were just sent down for central washing and sterilization; on top of that, one of the night-shift nurses is on scheduled rotation tonight, leaving the on-duty night nursing staff very short-handed."
She reached out a finger and tapped lightly on the instrument turnover and handover column at the bottom of the schedule board:

"This patient has no signs of incarceration or emergency indications. If we add the case now and it runs past the five o'clock shift handover, not only would we have to open tonight's sole emergency backup instrument set and backup operating room, the night nursing team would also be stretched thin between instrument turnover and postoperative monitoring—if a true emergency surgery comes in overnight, the OR's backup resources would be put in a very tight spot."
Hiroko met his gaze, her voice remaining gentle yet firm:

"Since Bed 42 is a standard elective procedure, I believe keeping the original schedule and performing it tomorrow morning—once the day-shift staff and standard instrument sets are all in place—is the safer choice for both the patient and the operating room team."
After a brief moment of thought, Sakaguchi closed the schedule clipboard without hesitation and nodded:
"You're right. Even if adding the case tonight is medically feasible, we can't tie up the night shift's staffing and emergency backup resources just to move an elective surgery forward."
Turning toward the ward nurse at the door, he gave a decisive instruction:

"Please let the patient in Bed 42 and their family know that in order to ensure the best possible operating room preparation and postoperative care, the surgery will remain on its original schedule and proceed on time tomorrow morning. I'll stop by the ward shortly to explain to them in person."
Once the ward nurse had left, Hiroko let out a quiet breath of relief and looked up at Sakaguchi:

"I'm sorry, Doctor. Speaking up against your suggestion right in front of the ward nurse just now might have come across a bit too blunt... Still, hearing that you were willing to reconsider the schedule really was a relief."

"What are you apologizing for? You kept a check on night-shift turnover and our emergency reserves for me—I should be thanking you. If the OR nurses simply went along with whatever the lead surgeon said, that would be the real problem."
A bright spark of joy flickered in Hiroko's eyes as the corners of her lips lifted softly:
"Thank you for listening to my input, Doctor. I'll go finish confirming the final handover log, then—to think we'll actually get to clock out on time at five today."
After stopping by the ward to briefly explain the situation to the family in Bed 42, Ryuji Sakaguchi returned to the locker room and changed into his casual clothes.

The clock hands had just reached ten past five. Free for once from staying late to write charts or cover a night shift, Sakaguchi walked lightly out of the staff corridor, ready to leave the hospital.
As he passed the hallway outside the surgical nurses' station, his footsteps suddenly came to a halt.

There stood Hiroko Sugimura, already changed into a soft beige-apricot knit cardigan over a light plaid skirt—yet instead of heading toward the main entrance, she was standing alone beside the side counter of the nurses' station. With her head lowered and both hands holding an open tri-fold brochure, her delicate brows were slightly knitted, her gaze as intensely focused as if she were studying a baffling clinical case.
"Hiroko? Still haven't headed out yet—was there something in the handover log that didn't match up?"
Startled, Hiroko jerked her head up:
Seeing Sakaguchi looking with concern at the leaflet in her hands, a faint blush crept across Hiroko's fair cheeks, and she sheepishly turned the full-color brochure around.
Printed across the brochure wasn't a medical chart at all—it was packed from edge to edge with photos of dorayaki, omurice, and seasonal limited-edition parfaits.
"I-it's not work! I finished the entire handover ten minutes ago... I was just seriously trying to figure out which shop in the shopping district to go eat at tonight."
Staring at the colorful shopping street food map, Sakaguchi was momentarily at a loss for words:
"...With how serious your expression was just now, I thought something had gone wrong with the instrument sets for one of tomorrow's surgeries."
Hiroko burst into a soft laugh, hugging the brochure to her chest as she gave a playful wink and teased:

"Hehe, in your eyes, Dr. Sakaguchi, do you think my head is still filled with nothing but hemostats and sterile gauze even after I take off my nurse's uniform? It's rare enough that we get to clock out on time at five—what to have for dinner is a matter of top priority."
"Fair enough. Did your research turn up a conclusion, then?"
Hiroko pointed to a shop in the corner of the brochure illustrated with a warm yellow lantern, a hint of eager anticipation brightening her eyes:

"There's actually a little place in the shopping district that serves Japanese-style Western dishes and freshly baked sweets. I've heard colleagues mention it several times and have been wanting to try it, but I usually get off work too late to make it in time."
Speaking up to here, she raised her eyes toward Sakaguchi and extended a natural invitation:
"Since you also happened to finish on time today, Dr. Sakaguchi, if you don't have other plans for the evening... would you like to go try it together?"

"Mhm. Back in the operating room just now, didn't you say you wanted to thank me for helping keep check on the schedule? Besides, their dinner set for two lets you pick two extra side dishes—it'd be such a waste to go eat there all by myself."
"When Nurse Sugimura puts it like that, how could I refuse? Let's go—I'm getting hungry myself."
Hiroko's eyes lit up as she happily picked up her handbag:
"Wonderful! Let's head over right away—if we go now, we definitely won't have to wait in line!"

Rows of warm streetlamps had come on along the evening shopping arcade, and the steady stream of commuters, housewives shopping for dinner, and students heading home from school made the street feel lively and welcoming.

The little bistro Hiroko led him to was tucked around a corner midway down the arcade, its wooden tables and chairs wiped spotless and gleaming, the air rich with the buttery aroma of beef stew and sweet baked red beans.
Brought to their table were a steaming hamburger steak set meal and golden, fluffy thick-rolled tamagoyaki, alongside a chestnut matcha parfait Hiroko had specially ordered on the side.

Pressing her hands together with a cheerful "Thank you for the meal," Hiroko picked up a small piece of the thick-rolled egg with her chopsticks, popped it into her mouth, and narrowed her eyes in pure satisfaction:
"Mmm... the balance between the dashi stock and the sweetness is just right! No wonder everyone recommends this place—coming here today was definitely the right call."
Using the serving chopsticks, she placed a piece of tamagoyaki onto Sakaguchi's small plate and urged him with a smile:
"Try some too, Dr. Sakaguchi! It's so much more tender than the kind the hospital cafeteria serves on Wednesdays."
"It really is good. I had no idea you knew the little shops in the shopping arcade this well."
Resting her cheek lightly on her hand, Hiroko smiled:

"Work keeps me busy on most days, sure, but whenever I walk past the arcade I secretly jot down promising-looking shops in my phone's notes. You, on the other hand, Dr. Sakaguchi—when we looked at the menu just now, you decided on the hamburger steak set in under ten seconds. You order dinner just as briskly as you call for instruments at the operating table."
"I'm used to eating alone, so I just pick whatever catches my eye first without thinking too much about it."
Hiroko shot him a teasing glance:
"I knew it. When you're home by yourself, Doctor, don't tell me you just make do with instant curry or convenience store bento every night?"
"You caught me. Getting to tag along with a food expert for an upgrade once in a while really isn't bad at all."
"You seem a lot more talkative tonight than you usually are at the hospital."
"You caught me. Getting to tag along with a food expert for an upgrade once in a while really isn't bad at all."
Scooping up a spoonful of her matcha parfait, Hiroko curved her eyes smugly:
"Hehe, then the next time we both manage to get off work on time, I'll generously take you through every single shop on my list one by one, Dr. Sakaguchi."
Sakaguchi looked at her bright, smiling face:
"You seem a lot more talkative tonight than you usually are at the hospital."
Hiroko's hand paused over her ice cream before she gave a playful wink:

"Because at the hospital, I'm Nurse Sugimura who has to help keep everything in check for everyone. Now that we've clocked out for the day, I don't need to keep up my nurse's poise at the dinner table."

Over the steaming dinner, the two chatted about their favorite flavors, movies they had seen recently, and how they liked to spend their days off. She would wrinkle her nose ever so slightly when biting into a tangy pickle, and laugh right out loud whenever something funny came up.
When they went to pay the bill, the shopkeeper handed over three slips of paper printed with red lettering, beaming from ear to ear:

"Thank you very much! The shopping arcade is holding a pre-weekend Fukubiki lottery right now—your bill qualifies for three draws! The lottery booth is just fifty meters to the right outside the door, so go try your luck!"
As Hiroko took the three lottery tickets, her eyes lit up at once.
In the small plaza at the center of the shopping arcade stood a lottery booth festooned with red-and-white bunting flags, an octagonal wooden rotary lottery drum resting on the counter.
Perched on the very top shelf of the prize rack was a plump white cat mascot cushion—the emblem of the shopping arcade—waving its paw endearingly at passersby.
Stopping in front of the booth, Hiroko's gaze was immediately captured by the white cat cushion.
"Wow... Dr. Sakaguchi, look at that kitty cushion up on top—it's so fluffy and adorable!"
Sakaguchi handed all three tickets over to her:
"All three tickets are right here. Go give it a spin—maybe you'll hit the grand prize on the first try."
Happily taking the tickets and handing them to the booth attendant, Hiroko took a deep breath, rolled up the sleeve of her knit cardigan, and gripped the handle:
"Then I won't hold back! Watch this—"
The wooden drum rumbled around a full turn, and with a crisp clack, a pure white wooden ball dropped out.
The booth attendant rang a small brass bell:
"Congratulations! Consolation prize—one pack of pocket tissues!"
Hiroko blinked in surprise as she took the tissues:
Flexing her fingers with a touch of stubbornness, she took hold of the handle again:
"I spun it too fast just now—I'll turn it more slowly this time!"
Another unmistakable white ball rolled into the tray.
Beaming, the attendant handed over a second pack of tissues:
Staring at the two neat packs of pocket tissues in her hand, Hiroko fell silent for two seconds as her gaze gradually turned dead serious.
Fixing her eyes on the octagonal wooden drum, her delicate brows arched slightly as she analyzed it in earnest:

"That's strange... On the second turn just now, I distinctly heard the clink of a colored ball with a slightly different center of gravity inside. As long as I control the reverse angle properly, I can definitely shake a colored ball out on the next spin!"
Watching from beside her, Sakaguchi could barely hold back a laugh:
"Hiroko, all the balls inside a lottery drum like that weigh the exact same—there's no angle trick to it. If this last ticket doesn't hit either, we should probably wrap it up."
Hiroko turned her head, puffing her cheeks out slightly:

"No way! Third time's the charm, and I've already got a feel for the handle! Besides, buying two boxes of throat lozenges at the general store next door comes with one bonus ticket—if this spin misses, I'm going over to trade for one more try!"
Sakaguchi didn't know whether to laugh or cry:
"How does someone who's normally so scientific in the operating room get this competitive with a wooden box at a lottery booth?"
"Work is work, and lotteries are all about momentum! Just watch closely, Doctor!"
Holding her breath, she gripped the handle with total concentration, turned it half a circle at an unhurried pace, and gave a gentle flick backward—
A bright yellow wooden ball rolled down the chute.
The booth attendant rang the brass handbell vigorously:
"Ding-ding-ding! Congratulations to the young lady—Fourth Prize: one shopping arcade white cat mascot mini keychain!"
Even though it wasn't the large cushion on the top shelf, Hiroko's eyes lit up and she let out a delighted cheer as soon as she received the tiny metal keychain shaped like the beckoning white cat:
"Awesome! See, Dr. Sakaguchi? I told you a colored ball would come out once I got the feel for it!"
She held the little keychain up in front of Sakaguchi and gave it a proud shake, her eyes curving like crescent moons.
Looking from the thumb-sized keychain in her hand to the identical merchandise clearly price-tagged in the general store window next door, Sakaguchi couldn't help speaking honestly:

"Winning it is impressive, sure... though Hiroko, the exact same keychain in that shop window looks like it costs three hundred yen. Buying one outright might've been cheaper than buying extra items for lottery tickets."
The triumphant smile on Hiroko's face froze on the spot.
Lowering the keychain, she puffed her cheeks and glared at Sakaguchi, unable to keep from complaining:
"Meanie! You really have no sense of romance, Doctor!"
Sakaguchi blinked, then chuckled and raised his hands in surrender:
"My mistake—I spoke out of turn. A trophy won with your own hands definitely means a lot more than buying one off the shelf."
Giving a soft humph, Hiroko carefully clipped the white cat keychain onto the zipper of her commuter bag, then pressed one of the two tissue packs she had drawn into Sakaguchi's hand:
"This pack is for you, as a souvenir for keeping me company at the lottery booth. And no complaining that it's cheap!"
Smiling, Sakaguchi tucked the tissues into his jacket pocket:
"Don't worry, I'll keep it with me."
Leaving the lively shopping arcade behind, the two chatted as they strolled along the quiet walkway until, before they knew it, they had reached the street corner in front of the train station.
The night breeze rustled through the leaves of the street trees, carrying a pleasant, refreshing coolness.
At the steps leading up to the station platform, Hiroko stopped and turned to face Sakaguchi, the soft halo of the streetlamp falling across her smiling eyes.
"Thank you for walking me all the way here tonight, Doctor. It's been such a long time since I got to eat out and browse the shops so carefree after work—I really had a wonderful time today."
"Same here. Thanks to you leading the way, not only did I get to eat at an authentic local spot, I also got to witness Nurse Sugimura's prowess at the lottery wheel firsthand."
With a faint blush on her cheeks, Hiroko lightly fingered the white cat keychain on her bag and looked up at him with a smile:

"Come to think of it, I discovered something new today too—when we only worked together in the operating room and the wards, I always thought of you as someone who was calm and serious no matter the occasion, Dr. Sakaguchi. I didn't expect that hanging out after work, you're actually quite an interesting person."
"'Quite an interesting person'? What's that supposed to mean?"
Watching him press for an answer, the corners of Hiroko's lips curved into a playful arc as she teased him on purpose:
Hiroko tilted her head with a beaming smile:
The two stood looking at each other beneath the streetlamp for a quiet moment as the evening breeze drifted across the intersection.
Taking a gentle breath, Hiroko spoke up on her own:

"There are still quite a few shops on that food map we looked at earlier that I haven't tried yet. If we ever manage to clock out on time like today again... let's go out for another walk together, Dr. Sakaguchi."
Sakaguchi nodded with a warm smile:
Stepping up two stairs toward the platform, Hiroko suddenly seemed to remember something; turning back around, she gave a playful wink and teased him with a hint of mischief:
"Though next time, there might not be such a good opportunity, you know?"
Seeing the slightly stunned look on Sakaguchi's face, Hiroko finally couldn't help covering her lips with a soft laugh and giving him a gentle wave:
Leaving behind that light-hearted farewell, she turned around, the hem of her skirt swaying gently with her buoyant steps as she blended into the bright lights of the station.
Watch Hiroko head into the station
