strings.collections.character_events.hiroko_lv3_: Walking past the corridor after an on-time shift, you run into Hiroko carrying a light-green paper bag with a thermos and a gardening picture book.
At ten to five in the afternoon, the surgical department corridor is quiet and orderly.

Hiroko Sugimura stands beside the counter in the instrument prep room, neatly arranging sterile suture boxes by size for tomorrow's first operation. Hearing footsteps at the door, she turns and deftly hands the annotated handover board to Ryuji Sakaguchi as he walks in.

"Dr. Sakaguchi, the recovery room handover records for both of this afternoon's post-op patients have been double-checked. Also, the patient for tomorrow morning's first surgery has fairly sensitive skin, so I put an extra roll of hypoallergenic non-woven tape in the supply basket—we can switch to that directly when securing the post-op dressing tomorrow."
Ryuji Sakaguchi glances over the handover board and nods:
"Thinking ahead even to the tape for the post-op dressing—thorough as always."
Hiroko Sugimura gives a faint smile:
"During rounds last time, I noticed the skin around her wrist IV site was slightly red. Preparing it in advance is much less trouble than looking for it on the spot."
Ryuji Sakaguchi signs his name and sets the clipboard back in place:
"There are no add-on cases today either, so we finally get to wrap up on time again."
"Yes. I'll head to the locker room to change, then. Thank you for your hard work today, Doctor."
Ten minutes later, Ryuji Sakaguchi walks out of the staff corridor in his street clothes and runs into Hiroko Sugimura again near the side of the main lobby.

Hiroko has changed into a gentle light-beige knit top and a long deep-blue skirt. Besides her usual commuter bag, she is carrying a light-green paper bag, with a thermos and a neatly bound gardening picture book peeking out from the top.
She glances down at her wristwatch, walking slightly faster than usual as if timing a train or bus.
Ryuji Sakaguchi steps up and greets her casually:
"Hiroko, meeting up with a friend tonight?"
Hiroko Sugimura pauses and turns toward him:
Her fingers tighten slightly around the handles of the light-green paper bag, her gaze resting on Ryuji's face for two seconds as if hesitating over how to answer.
Noticing her subtle expression, Ryuji Sakaguchi adds gently:
"If you're in a hurry, don't mind me—go right ahead."
Hiroko Sugimura shakes her head, that brief hesitation quickly giving way to a warm, earnest look. She raises her eyes to Ryuji and speaks up on her own:
"I'm not in that much of a rush. It's just... Dr. Sakaguchi, if you're heading straight to the station right now, would you mind walking part of the way with me?"
Slightly surprised, Ryuji Sakaguchi smiles and nods:
"Sure. I don't have anything urgent on my end anyway."
Hiroko Sugimura lets out a soft breath, the corners of her lips curving into a faint smile:
"Thank you, Doctor. Shall we go, then?"
The evening sun stretches the shadows of the roadside trees long across the pavement as the after-work crowd slowly disperses along the sidewalk.
Walking side by side past the fork in the shopping district, the two of them do not turn toward their usual train station, instead taking a quiet walkway leading toward the neighboring ward.
Ryuji Sakaguchi glances at the paper bag in her hand:
"Is that a gardening book in the bag? Sounds like the friend you're visiting today is pretty fond of flowers."
Hiroko Sugimura looks down at the book in her hand, her fingers lightly brushing the edge of the paper bag, her voice natural yet tinged with a shy softness:
"I'm not going to see a friend... I'm going to visit my mother. She's staying at a hospital over this way."
Ryuji Sakaguchi blinks slightly, slowing his pace by half a beat:
Hiroko Sugimura nods, her tone calm and candid:
"Yes. She's been staying at the municipal general hospital two bus stops ahead for quite a while now."

Stopping before a red pedestrian light at the crosswalk, the evening breeze lifts the stray locks by Hiroko's ear. Watching the signal blinking across the street, she continues in a peaceful, conversational voice:

"When I was very young, my father passed away from an illness. For as long as I can remember, it was just my mother at home—going out to work while looking after my schoolwork and three meals a day, raising me all on her own."
Ryuji Sakaguchi stands quietly beside her without interrupting.

"Watching how hard she worked back then, I always thought that once I graduated from nursing school and became a full-fledged nurse, it would be my turn to take good care of her. Yet not long after I finally put on my nurse's uniform, my mother collapsed from a chronic condition and needed long-term inpatient care and observation."
The light turns green, and the two cross the street to the bus stop ahead.
"Do you often come over like this after work to keep her company?"

"Yes. Whenever my shift schedule allows and it doesn't interfere with my work at Hoshimi, I come by two or three times a week to check on her, bring fresh daily necessities, or bring a picture book she likes, like today."
She looks down at the thermos in her hand, a faintly self-deprecating yet tender smile touching her lips:

"Even though I'm a nurse myself and completely used to caring for patients at the hospital every day, sometimes after a full day of surgeries, when I'm hurrying over here right after work, I still can't help worrying whether her spirits are good today... and every once in a while, it does feel a little tiring."
At that, she quickly lifts her head again, her eyes clear and composed:

"Still, the doctors and nurses over there take wonderful care of her, and her condition has been very stable. At Hoshimi Hospital, aside from Manami—who has known me for a long time—I haven't mentioned this to any of our other colleagues."
"Waiting until we walked all the way here to tell me—does that mean I passed Nurse Sugimura's inspection?"
"Balancing both sides on your own for this long really hasn't been easy."
Ryuji Sakaguchi looks at her and smiles lightly:
"Waiting until we walked all the way here to tell me—does that mean I passed Nurse Sugimura's inspection?"
Hiroko Sugimura blinks, the slight stiffness from speaking of family matters melting away as she lets out a soft laugh:
"Hehe, that's because Dr. Sakaguchi is always so dependable. As we were walking together, I just felt it would be alright to tell you."
Ryuji Sakaguchi speaks gently and earnestly:
"Balancing both sides on your own for this long really hasn't been easy."
Hiroko Sugimura gently shakes her head, her gaze soft yet steady:
"Because she's my mother. Seeing her safe and sound actually makes me feel more grounded at work."

The bus pulls smoothly into the stop. Without prying into her mother's specific diagnosis or offering as a physician to review her chart or step into her care, Ryuji Sakaguchi simply boards the bus to the neighboring hospital beside her.
At ten past six in the evening, the inpatient lobby of the municipal general hospital glows with warm light, filled mostly with visiting family members carrying meal boxes and fruit baskets.
Reaching the public waiting area in front of the elevators, Ryuji Sakaguchi stops and gestures toward a bench:
"I'll wait for you right here in the lounge area. Take your time catching up with your mother—no need to rush down."
Hiroko Sugimura pauses, looking at him apologetically:
"Leaving you sitting down here waiting for me, Doctor... isn't that too impolite?"
"I didn't come here today as a doctor on rounds. That's time for you and your mother—reading a magazine out here suits me just fine. Go on."
Hearing those words, a unmistakable warmth crosses Hiroko's eyes. Without standing on ceremony any further, she gives a gentle nod:
"...Yes. Thank you, Dr. Sakaguchi. I'll just head up for a visit and be right back down."
After sitting on the bench in the public waiting area for about half an hour, the elevator doors chime and slide open once more.

Hiroko Sugimura steps out carrying the now half-empty paper bag. Compared to the slightly preoccupied look she wore when arriving, her brow is noticeably lighter, and even her footsteps carry a brisk ease.
Ryuji Sakaguchi stands up from the bench:
"Back down already? How is your mother feeling today?"
Walking up to him, Hiroko Sugimura cannot help curving her eyes in a bright smile:

"She's in great spirits! The moment she got that gardening book, she couldn't stop flipping through it—she even pointed at the hydrangeas inside and said she wants to plant two pots on the balcony once she's discharged."
She pauses and lets out a fond, helpless sigh, her eyes brimming with unmistakable warmth:

"And then after barely two sentences, she started patting the back of my hand and fretting again, asking whether I'd eaten dinner yet or if I'd just grabbed a piece of bread to save time... Even though I'm a full-fledged operating room nurse now, in her eyes it's like I'll always be a little girl who needs reminding to eat on time."
"In a mother's eyes, a daughter is still a child no matter how old she gets. Though you really haven't had dinner yet tonight, have you?"
Hiroko Sugimura touches her cheek a little sheepishly:
"Mom shared half of the tangerine she was saving with me up in the ward, so I'm not too hungry right now. Let's step outside for some fresh air first, Doctor."
By the time they step out of the inpatient building, night has fully fallen. Row after row of softly lit ward windows glow quietly against the dark sky in the distance.
Walking along the path outside the hospital for a few minutes, they stop beside a wooden bench in a small pocket park and sit down side by side.
After a quiet moment, Hiroko Sugimura folds the empty paper bag neatly on her lap, turns to look back at the brightly lit inpatient building behind them, and speaks softly:

"Dr. Sakaguchi, you must have been wondering earlier—since having a parent in the hospital is such a normal thing, why haven't I ever mentioned it to anyone despite working at Hoshimi Hospital for so long?"
Ryuji Sakaguchi looks at her profile:
"Everyone has their own reasons for not bringing family matters into the workplace."
Hiroko Sugimura nods gently, her gaze earnest and clear:

"Everyone at Hoshimi Hospital is wonderful—the director, the doctors, and all the nurses in the department are so considerate. But precisely because everyone is so kind... I know very well that once people find out I have a hospitalized mother at home with no one else around, every time a heavy major operation is scheduled or someone is needed to cover a night shift, everyone will hesitate and think, 'Nurse Sugimura has a sick family member to care for, so let's not assign it to her.'"
Her fingers tighten on her lap, her voice quiet yet unmistakably firm:

"I truly love Hoshimi Hospital's operating room, and I cherish my place standing beside the operating table working with the team. When the doctors entrust an important operation to me, I want it to be because they trust 'Hiroko Sugimura's professional skill'—not because the first thing they see is someone with difficulties at home who needs special consideration."
She turns her face toward Ryuji Sakaguchi, the glow of the streetlamp reflected in her eyes:

"If the day ever comes when my mother genuinely needs me to take leave or adjust my shifts, I'll apply to the hospital openly through the proper channels. Until then, I don't want everyone tiptoeing around me and arranging a way out before I've even said a word."
Having said all that in one breath, Hiroko suddenly realizes how much she has poured out; the tips of her fair ears flush slightly as she lowers her head in mild embarrassment:
"...I'm sorry, Dr. Sakaguchi. Did I suddenly talk way too much about things unrelated to work?"
Looking at her faintly reddened ears, Ryuji Sakaguchi speaks with gentle sincerity:
"There's nothing to apologize for. Thank you for being willing to tell me all this, Hiroko."
Hiroko Sugimura raises her eyes to look at him.

"I understand how you feel completely. Rest assured, when we return to Hoshimi's operating room tomorrow, you're still Nurse Sugimura, my most trusted partner. Whether you ever tell anyone else about tonight—and when—is entirely up to you. Even if you need a schedule adjustment someday, we'll handle it through standard hospital procedures; I won't take it upon myself to give you special treatment."
Hearing his answer, the slight tension in Hiroko's shoulders eases away.
She lets out a long, soft breath, her eyes curving into crescents again as she reminds him in a half-playful, half-serious tone:
"Hearing you say that puts my mind completely at ease. Though Doctor, if you start being extra polite to me in the operating room tomorrow because of this, you'll really put me in a bind."
"Don't worry—when it's time to call for instruments tomorrow, I won't slow down by half a beat just because you treated me to the evening breeze tonight."
Hiroko Sugimura lets out a soft giggle:
Rising from the bench, the two chat about light, everyday things along the brightly lit street until they reach the corner in front of the train station.
The sound of an evening train pulling in drifts faintly down from the elevated platform above.
Hiroko Sugimura stops before the station entrance and turns to face Ryuji Sakaguchi, her hands folded over the small bag in front of her.
"Thank you so much for walking all the way over here with me tonight, Dr. Sakaguchi."
"I didn't help with a single thing today—I just tagged along for a walk."
Hiroko Sugimura gently shakes her head, her gaze warm and heartfelt as she looks at him:

"No, that alone was more than enough. Truthfully, when I called out to you after work today, it wasn't because I wanted you to do anything for me... I just looked at your face and suddenly felt that if it was Dr. Sakaguchi, it would be okay to tell you."
The night breeze brushes softly across her bangs; she pauses for a heartbeat, her voice softening:
"Something I've been carrying quietly on my own all this time—having someone willing to just listen to me talk it through like tonight really makes my heart feel so much lighter."
Across the soft halo of the streetlamps, the two share a quiet look as the evening breeze drifts past the peaceful corner.
"Whenever you need company for a walk again, just call me anytime. Get some rest tonight—see you in the operating room tomorrow."
A bright, cheerful smile blossoms across Hiroko Sugimura's face as she nods firmly:
"Yes! Please be careful on your way home too, Doctor. See you tomorrow, Dr. Sakaguchi!"
Giving Ryuji a wave, she turns and walks with a light step up the stairs toward the platform.
Watch Hiroko walk up the stairs to the station platform
strings.collections.character_events.hiroko_summ: On a warm summer evening without night duty, Hiroko invites you to the annual riverside fireworks festival in a morning-glory yukata.

The midsummer evening air carries a warm river breeze; rows of red-and-white lanterns already hang across the festival grounds in the distance, accompanied by the lively sound of taiko drums and flutes.

Several days ago, Hiroko Sugimura carefully picked out an evening off when neither of them had night duty and took the initiative to invite Ryuji Sakaguchi to the annual riverside summer fireworks festival.
Arriving at the agreed-upon street-corner clock tower a few minutes early, Ryuji Sakaguchi is looking around when the crisp clatter of wooden geta against flagstones suddenly sounds behind him.
"Dr. Sakaguchi, have I kept you waiting long?"
Ryuji Sakaguchi turns around, and his gaze freezes on the spot.

Standing in the afterglow of sunset, Hiroko Sugimura is wearing neither her crisp white nurse's uniform nor her usual knit casual clothes. Instead, she is dressed in a soft navy summer yukata patterned with pale pink morning glories, a pale-yellow heko obi accentuating her slender waist; her hair, normally worn smoothly down, is swept up into a neat yet graceful updo that reveals the fair, slender line of her nape and collarbone.
Meeting Ryuji's momentarily stunned gaze, Hiroko's fingers tighten slightly around her woven bamboo pouch, a trace of quiet anticipation in her eyes.
After barely two seconds, however, she gracefully lifts the sleeve of her yukata, spins half a turn in front of him, and tilts her head with a teasing smile:
"Why are you staring at me without saying a word... Don't tell me you thought I only ever wear a nurse's uniform even after work, Dr. Sakaguchi?"
Coming back to his senses, Ryuji Sakaguchi smiles candidly:

"Seeing you in a yukata with your hair pinned up is such a striking contrast from how you usually look at the hospital that I got completely transfixed for a moment. You look beautiful—it really suits you."
At such a straightforward compliment, a faint blush rises to Hiroko's cheeks, though she lifts her chin with feigned composure and gives a playful wink:
"Hehe, since Dr. Sakaguchi praised me so sincerely, starting my preparations two hours early today was well worth it. Come on—if we wait any longer, the stalls inside will have huge lines!"
As the sky deepens into a rich ultramarine, hundreds of paper lanterns along both sides of the approach light up all at once, illuminating the riverside night market as bright as day.
Weaving through the bustling crowd in summer yukata, Hiroko looks over the festival stalls lining the path with lively enthusiasm.

"Look over there! Ramune soda chilled in wooden tubs, plus freshly grilled salted ayu and shaved ice—if you don't take a sip of ice-cold ramune before watching summer fireworks, it feels like half the ritual is missing!"

Ryuji Sakaguchi follows her lead with a smile. The stall owner hands over two glass bottles of ramune beaded with condensation, cheerfully tossing in a bamboo festival fan printed with a fireworks motif.
Taking the bottles, Ryuji presses the glass marble down into the neck of Hiroko's bottle for her.
With a crisp pop, cool bubbles fizz up inside. Hiroko happily takes the bamboo fan and soda bottle, sips a mouthful, and narrows her eyes in satisfaction:
"Mmm—so refreshing! When you have time off in the summer, do you usually come visit lively night markets like this?"
Ryuji Sakaguchi takes a sip of his ramune:

"Mostly I've been busy with work or reading over papers, and even when I passed by occasionally, I never felt much like squeezing into a crowd on my own. I didn't expect you to love the lively atmosphere of a festival this much, though."
Hiroko Sugimura swirls the blue glass bottle in her hand, laughing as if it were the most natural thing in the world:
"Work is always so busy every day, so being able to stroll through a summer festival in the night breeze and snack along with everyone makes my whole body feel lighter."
She lightly taps the back of Ryuji's hand with her new bamboo fan, adding teasingly:
"You, on the other hand, still look so serious even while holding a bottle of ramune in front of a takoyaki stall—relax a little more!"
"Super obvious! Still, don't worry—with me leading the way tonight, I guarantee you'll experience a proper summer night festival."
"Then I'll leave the rest of our stall tour entirely in Guide Sugimura's hands."
"Leading the way is fine, but since you're wearing geta today, there's no rush—take your time."
Raising the bottle of ramune in his hand, Ryuji Sakaguchi plays along with her joke:
"Then I'll leave the rest of our stall tour entirely in Guide Sugimura's hands."
Hiroko Sugimura's eyes light up; tapping her chin lightly with the handle of her bamboo fan, she nods with mock solemnity:

"Hehe, that's the spirit! Then let's start with that takoyaki stall up ahead with the longest line—and on our way back after the fireworks, we have to try the candied apples in crisp sugar glaze too!"
Glancing down at the wooden geta on her feet, Ryuji Sakaguchi slows his pace by half a step and reminds her gently:
"Leading the way is fine, but since you're wearing geta today, there's no rush—take your time."
Hiroko Sugimura blinks, looking down at her wooden geta with their pale-pink straps as a soft warmth touches her cheeks. Slowing her pace a little to walk closer beside Ryuji, she laughs softly:
"...Here I was trying to lead you all around the festival, and somehow you're the one looking out for me again. Alright, let's take our time walking over, then."
Trading light banter, the two continue down the lantern-lit approach.

As seven-thirty approaches, an announcement over the speakers signals that the fireworks display is about to begin. All at once, the crowds scattered across the stalls surge toward the stone steps of the riverbank viewing area.
In the blink of an eye, the surrounding crowd grows dense, passersby brushing past and narrowing the space between them.
In her wooden geta, Hiroko Sugimura sways slightly amid the stream of people, looking up toward the crowded embankment slope ahead.
As the crowd ahead thickens, Hiroko cannot walk very quickly in her geta.

Seeing that a group of oncoming festivalgoers is about to separate them, Hiroko Sugimura hesitates for half a second before reaching out and lightly catching the cuff of Ryuji Sakaguchi's shirt with her fingertips.
Feeling the gentle tug at his sleeve, Ryuji Sakaguchi immediately slows down, turning to step half a pace closer to shield her from the pressing crowd.
Looking down at her fingers pinching his cuff, her fair ears flushing faintly in the lantern light, Hiroko Sugimura explains in a small, slightly self-conscious voice:

"U-um... there are so many people heading up the embankment steps, and I can't walk fast in geta today. If we get separated in the crowd, we won't even be able to hear our phones ring once the fireworks start, and that would be a real hassle..."
Looking down at her faintly flushed cheek, Ryuji Sakaguchi does not call out her excuse.
After a brief pause, he lowers his arm slightly and very naturally closes his hand around hers where it rests at his cuff.
His warm fingers gently fold over her cool fingertips. Hiroko Sugimura's shoulders give a tiny tremor as she raises her eyes to him, her breath skipping half a beat amid the surrounding clamor.
Yet she does not pull her fingers back; after a fleeting moment of shyness, she gently squeezes his hand back and curves her eyes with a quiet, playful remark:
"...Since Dr. Sakaguchi took my hand first, if I still get lost later, it'll be entirely the primary surgeon's responsibility."
Ryuji Sakaguchi smiles, holding her hand securely:
Making their way up the lively stone steps, the two finally find an open spot with a clear view near the top of the grassy embankment slope.
Below them lies the wide, shimmering surface of the river; across the water, the floodlights at the launch site have gone dark, and the surrounding crowd falls into a hushed anticipation.
The first great golden shell trails a long whistle straight up into the night sky and bursts open directly overhead.

A dazzling shower of gold and crimson instantly lights up the ink-blue summer sky, followed in quick succession by second and third chrysanthemum and weeping-willow shells, their layered brilliance flickering across the river and the upturned faces of the crowd.
Waves of cheers and admiration rise all around them.
Ryuji Sakaguchi turns his head to look at Hiroko Sugimura beside him.

The blossoms of fire filling the sky reflect in Hiroko's clear eyes, tinting her fair profile a warm orange-gold. The river breeze stirs a lock of hair at her temple, and the wide sleeve of her yukata sways gently in the night wind, brushing against Ryuji's arm.
Tilting her head back slightly, she gazes up at the radiant night sky in pure, quiet absorption.
In the pause as a giant brocade crown shell slowly dissolves into falling stardust, Hiroko lets out a soft breath, her voice remarkably gentle and unadorned amid the distant rumble and river wind:
"...I'm really glad we could come this year."
Watching her profile illuminated by the fireworks, Ryuji Sakaguchi replies softly:
"Yeah. Being able to stand here and watch them with you like this is really nice."
Hearing Ryuji's reply, Hiroko turns her head slightly, her eyes meeting his for a heartbeat in the flickering light of the fireworks.

Both of them are clearly aware of how much closer they are standing than usual. Without an extra word, Hiroko simply gives the fingers still intertwined with his a gentle squeeze, curves her lips in a slightly shy smile, and looks back up at the night sky.
When the final grand finale barrage fades from the night sky, long applause echoes along the riverbank, and the spectators begin chatting and laughing as they slowly file back toward the station.
Walking along the return path atop the embankment, Hiroko—who had been so quietly absorbed beneath the fireworks—quickly regains her usual bright, spirited energy.
Fanning herself lightly with the bamboo fan in her hand, she turns toward Ryuji with a touch of pride:

"How was it, Dr. Sakaguchi? That blue-violet hydrangea firework third from the end was super pretty, wasn't it? I told you that embankment slope I picked had the best view—we could even see the reflections on the water across the river crystal clear!"
"You really picked the perfect spot—nothing less from Guide Sugimura after doing all her homework."
Hiroko Sugimura giggles, tilting her head to size him up teasingly:
"Though when that very first firework went off earlier, you were staring at the night sky so intently that you didn't even hear me call your name once."
Ryuji Sakaguchi gives a helpless smile:
"I was busy watching the fireworks... and watching the person standing next to me."
Hiroko Sugimura's cheeks warm slightly; she raises the bamboo fan to lightly cover the lower half of her face, though the corners of her eyes curve like crescent moons:

"...You really know how to say things like that out of nowhere tonight, Doctor. Alright, the station entrance is right ahead—thank you for coming to see the fireworks with me today, Doctor. I had a wonderful time. Please be careful on your way home, and see you at the hospital!"
Giving Ryuji a gentle wave, she lifts the hem of her yukata slightly and walks up the station steps with the light clatter of her geta.
Watch Hiroko walk up the station steps in her yukata

"Leading the way is fine, but since you're wearing geta today, there's no rush—take your time."
Hiroko Sugimura blinks, looking down at her wooden geta with their pale-pink straps as a soft warmth touches her cheeks. Slowing her pace a little to walk closer beside Ryuji, she laughs softly:
"...Here I was trying to lead you all around the festival, and somehow you're the one looking out for me again. Alright, let's take our time walking over, then."
Trading light banter, the two continue down the lantern-lit approach.

As seven-thirty approaches, an announcement over the speakers signals that the fireworks display is about to begin. All at once, the crowds scattered across the stalls surge toward the stone steps of the riverbank viewing area.
In the blink of an eye, the surrounding crowd grows dense, passersby brushing past and narrowing the space between them.
In her wooden geta, Hiroko Sugimura sways slightly amid the stream of people, looking up toward the crowded embankment slope ahead.
As the crowd ahead thickens, Hiroko slows her pace in her wooden geta.
Before Ryuji Sakaguchi even reaches out to steady her, Hiroko Sugimura naturally slips her hand into his palm, twining her fingers snugly with his.
Steadying her steps in the geta against his arm, she leans close to his side, looks up into the warm glow of the lanterns, and gives a playful wink:
"Hehe, with a crowd this big, if I don't hold onto my boyfriend tightly, what would I do if we got squeezed apart?"
Closing his hand firmly around her soft fingers, Ryuji Sakaguchi chuckles:
"Seeing how enthusiastically you were leading the way just now, I thought you were too busy to hold hands."
Hiroko Sugimura leans lightly against his arm, giving him a playfully reproachful glance:

"You're the one who wasn't taking the initiative in the crowd, Ryuji, and now you're turning it around on me. I'm wearing geta today—if you don't hold onto me steadily, I'll make you carry me on your back when my feet get tired later."
Ryuji Sakaguchi laughs, drawing her a little closer to his side:
"Then I'd better hold on tight. The embankment slope is right ahead—take the steps slowly."
With a sweet curve of her lips, Hiroko Sugimura leans comfortably beside him as the two walk through the bustling crowd with fingers intertwined.
Making their way up the lively stone steps, the two finally find an open spot with a clear view near the top of the grassy embankment slope.
Below them lies the wide, shimmering surface of the river; across the water, the floodlights at the launch site have gone dark, and the surrounding crowd falls into a hushed anticipation.
The first great golden shell trails a long whistle straight up into the night sky and bursts open directly overhead.

A dazzling shower of gold and crimson instantly lights up the ink-blue summer sky, followed in quick succession by second and third chrysanthemum and weeping-willow shells, their layered brilliance flickering across the river and the upturned faces of the crowd.
Waves of cheers and admiration rise all around them.
Ryuji Sakaguchi turns his head to look at Hiroko Sugimura beside him.

The blossoms of fire filling the sky reflect in Hiroko's clear eyes, tinting her fair profile a warm orange-gold. The river breeze stirs a lock of hair at her temple, and the wide sleeve of her yukata sways gently in the night wind, brushing against Ryuji's arm.
Tilting her head back slightly, she gazes up at the radiant night sky in pure, quiet absorption.
In the pause as a giant brocade crown shell slowly dissolves into falling stardust, Hiroko lets out a soft breath, her voice remarkably gentle and unadorned amid the distant rumble and river wind:
"...I'm really glad we could come this year."
Watching her profile illuminated by the fireworks, Ryuji Sakaguchi replies softly:
"Yeah. Being able to stand here and watch them with you like this is really nice."
Hearing Ryuji's reply, Hiroko's eyes curve softly, and she rests her cheek unhesitatingly against his shoulder.
With her soft updo brushing his shoulder, she watches another multicolored chrysanthemum shell rise into the night sky and murmurs softly:
"Let's come watch them together again whenever we get the chance, Ryuji."
Ryuji Sakaguchi gives her hand a gentle squeeze and answers warmly:
"Yeah. Anytime you want to see them, we'll come together again."
When the final grand finale barrage fades from the night sky, long applause echoes along the riverbank, and the spectators begin chatting and laughing as they slowly file back toward the station.
Walking along the return path atop the embankment, Hiroko—who had been so quietly absorbed beneath the fireworks—quickly regains her usual bright, spirited energy.
Fanning herself lightly with the bamboo fan in her hand, she turns toward Ryuji with a touch of pride:

"How was it, Ryuji? That blue-violet hydrangea firework third from the end was super pretty, wasn't it? I told you that embankment slope I picked had the best view—we could even see the reflections on the water across the river crystal clear!"
"You really picked the perfect spot—nothing less from Guide Sugimura after doing all her homework."
Hiroko Sugimura giggles, tilting her head to size him up teasingly:
"Though when that very first firework went off earlier, you were staring at the night sky so intently that you didn't even hear me call your name once."
Ryuji Sakaguchi gives a helpless smile:
"I was busy watching the fireworks... and watching the person standing next to me."
The tips of Hiroko Sugimura's ears flush faintly, yet she openly swings their still-joined hands and teases him using her workplace form of address:
"Who knew our 'Dr. Sakaguchi' could talk so smoothly in private—you get full marks for tonight. Come on, Ryuji, let's take the train back together before the station entrance gets completely packed!"
In the warm summer night breeze, the two walk hand in hand, chatting and laughing as they merge into the warm lights of the station.
Walk hand in hand with Hiroko into the warm lights of the station
strings.collections.character_events.narumi_ren_: A saleswoman carrying an instrument catalogue seems to know far too much.
A brief downpour had just passed outside.

A young woman in her mid-twenties folded her umbrella and approached Hoshimi Hospital's reception desk in high heels. Her short hair was neatly styled, and she wore a fitted navy business suit with a medical-device company visitor badge pinned to her chest.
“Good afternoon. Do you have an appointment?”
“Mika Shimotsuki, two thirty. I contacted your purchasing office. I'm here to deliver our catalogue of new surgical instruments.”
The receptionist looked down to check the register.
“Ah, yes. Please wait a moment while I contact the surgeon assigned to meet you.”
Mika maintained a polished professional smile, but her gaze drifted past the desk toward the clinical corridor as if by chance.

“I heard your hospital recently recruited Dr. Sakaguchi from overseas, an exceptionally versatile surgeon, and that your surgical volume has grown sharply. Once our company heard, we hurried over with our newest instrument catalogue.”
“Dr. Sakaguchi certainly has been busy lately. It's lucky your company sent a woman. Our hospital has an unusual custom and normally doesn't let male sales representatives into the clinical area.”
“A colleague mentioned that before I came, so I was assigned to this account.”
Her reply was perfectly natural, though she continued watching the staff moving through the corridor as she spoke.
At the far end of the hall, Narumi Jinguji walked past carrying a chart.
The moment Mika saw Narumi's face and name badge, her gaze paused almost imperceptibly. She quickly looked away and lowered her head to straighten the folder in her hands.
Narumi did not break stride. With an unchanged expression, she turned into the surgical nurses' station.
Ren Nanase was checking the afternoon supply sheet. Seeing Narumi enter, she looked up softly.
“Has the saleswoman who just registered at reception ever done business with our hospital?”
Ren glanced at the internal routing form:

“No. The register says this is her first visit. She used Dr. Sakaguchi's arrival and the expansion of surgery as an opportunity to bring a catalogue of new gynecologic and pelvic surgical instruments.”
Narumi's fingers paused lightly at the edge of the chart.
“Her first visit… Yet when we passed in the corridor, her first reaction to seeing me wasn't how someone looks at a complete stranger.”
“…Could she simply have recognized your name?”
“Perhaps I'm overthinking it. One look alone proves nothing.”
She closed the chart, her voice calm and cautious.

“But to be safe, don't alert Dr. Sakaguchi yet. OR Three has no cases this afternoon, and its equipment was just inspected. When you collect her from reception, don't introduce yourself. Tell her you're taking her to verify tray specifications in the surgical area, then bring her straight to the pre-op room beside OR Three.”
Ren looked at Narumi and immediately understood her intent.
“Understood. I'll put away my name badge and bring her over now.”
Mika spread her branded product catalogue across the table one page at a time, explaining it in a crisp, efficient cadence.

“These pelvic retractors and atraumatic dissectors use an improved curvature that maintains excellent exposure in a narrow, deep field. The jaws are specially blunted to minimize compression injury to the ovarian cortex and surrounding vessels.”
Narumi calmly studied the specification page:
“You know the specifications and indications by heart. You clearly are an experienced specialist in gynecologic surgical instruments, Ms. Shimotsuki.”
Mika smiled with a trace of pride:
“I handle priority departments at several major hospitals. Without knowing the business, I would never get through a chief surgeon's door.”
“But the catalogue doesn't appear to include long-term clinical follow-up data for this set.”
“That data is still being compiled. I can have the company send it to your purchasing email later.”
As she put away the presentation charts, she changed the subject with studied casualness:
“While researching before my visit, Dr. Jinguji's name seemed familiar. Before Hoshimi, did you work at another very large general hospital?”
“My medical résumé has always been public. It is no secret.”
“That hospital's research platform is famous in the field. Why did you suddenly leave it for a small hospital like this?”
Narumi did not answer immediately. She simply watched Mika steer the conversation toward personnel changes.
Still arranging her folder, Mika added as if it meant nothing:

“I also heard a young nurse left that hospital at about the same time. Nurse Nanase, who brought me here from reception, moved so confidently. She must be an old partner who followed you here then, correct?”
A knock sounded at that exact moment.
Ren entered carrying a tray and casually pulled shut the door from the preparation room to the outer corridor.
She set down the cup but did not turn to leave. Instead she remained by the door, her calm gaze fixed on Mika's face.

Having heard the final sentence outside, Ren understood everything. When collecting Mika, she had deliberately worn an unbadged work coat, never spoken her name, and discussed nothing beyond instrument specifications. Yet this woman had called her “Nurse Nanase” and even knew that she and Narumi came from the same former hospital.
Narumi lifted the teacup without drinking and spoke in an even tone:
“Perfect timing, Nurse Nanase. Ms. Shimotsuki was just taking an interest in our former careers.”
“Just a salesperson's professional habit. I was making conversation.”
Ren remained by the door. Her voice was gentle, but every word was clear:

“If this were a salesperson's professional habit, on the way from the first floor to surgery you would have asked about our tray dimensions and sterilization procedures. But since entering, you have watched the duty roster on the corridor wall, not the instrument cabinets.”
Narumi set down her cup and looked directly into Mika's eyes:

“I have a question as well, Ms. Shimotsuki. Reception never introduced the nursing staff. When Nurse Nanase collected you, she wore no badge and never gave her name. How did you know her surname was Nanase without any introduction?”
Mika's eyes flickered, and she forced a smile:
“I… asked colleagues about your staffing before I came…”

“Hoshimi publishes only attending physicians' profiles. Nursing schedules and employment histories are never public. Even our own colleagues rarely know she once worked at the same hospital as I did.”
Narumi reached out and closed the elegant catalogue on the table, taking in the familiar custom exhibition brooch at Mika's collar as well.
“That concludes the instrument presentation. Now let us discuss something outside the catalogue.”
The air in the preparation room abruptly turned cold.
Caught in her mistake, Mika snatched up her briefcase and sprang to her feet.
“If Dr. Jinguji isn't interested in our products, there must be some misunderstanding. I won't take any more of your time. Goodbye.”
Ren stood quietly before the door without yielding a step.
“Ms. Shimotsuki, please answer Dr. Jinguji first.”
“What are you doing? You have no right to detain me!”
“You're right. So tell us honestly who sent you with a list to confirm that the two of us were at Hoshimi, and I will stop wasting your time.”
The five syllables fell into the silent room, almost soundless.
Mika's pupils contracted violently. Her forced composure shattered, and even the fingers holding her briefcase trembled.
Ren slowly lowered her eyes by the door.
“Move! Don't think hiding in a place like this means you can pretend nothing happened—!”
She spun toward the door and lunged for the handle.
A brief struggle cut her off.
Ren swiftly turned and caught Mika's wrist. At the same instant, Narumi produced a prepared syringe and decisively injected her upper arm.
Mika's eyes widened in terror. Pain flashed through her arm; she tried to scream, but her voice rapidly lost its strength.
Narumi caught her as she slid down the door.
Before she could finish the last word, she lost consciousness completely.
Ren looked down at Mika, then raised her eyes to Narumi.
“Dr. Jinguji, are we really going through with this?”
Narumi looked at her, voice calm and controlled.
“If we stop now, Hirasaka will send a third person tomorrow. Only if she becomes too frightened to involve herself again can we buy time.”
Her customary gentle smile had vanished entirely.
When Mika awoke, the first thing she saw was the preparation room's stark white ceiling.
She lay on a transport bed. Her jacket, skirt, and heels were gone; she now wore a thin patient gown, and a pre-op cap completely contained her hair.
ECG and blood-pressure monitors were connected beside her wrist.
Ren stood beside the bed in green scrubs, checking the instrument readings.
Mika tried to sit up with a violent struggle, but the restraint at the side of the bed held her down.
“What are you trying to do?! Let me go! I'm calling the police!”
Printed clearly at the top of the page were the words:
The signature field also bore a signature almost identical to her own handwriting.
She admitted it so calmly that Mika momentarily forgot what insult should come next.
“I will ask again. What did Ryuji Hirasaka send you here to do?”
Mika bit down hard on her lip:
“Then we will have to talk somewhere else.”
At the far end of the inner passage, the doors to OR Three slowly opened.
The transport bed stopped beside the operating table in OR Three.
Narumi and Ren were the only other people in the room.
Under the glaring surgical lights, Mika saw the narrow operating table and finally understood that the earlier consent form was more than a simple threat.
“No… no! I'm not sick! I don't need any operation!”
Ren stood by the table wearing only green scrubs, cap, and surgical mask. Her voice remained soft, but offered no reassurance.

Narumi and Ren moved Mika onto the operating table and fastened the restraints around both wrists and legs. Mika stared in terror at the neatly arranged metal instruments and heard the faint sounds of cloth, metal, and packaging as Ren opened the preparation set.
Again and again, Mika cried that she had never signed the consent form.
Yet Ren's preoperative preparations did not stop.

Ren silently and expertly completed abdominal hair preparation, urinary catheterization, and povidone-iodine antisepsis in sequence. Once the green sterile fenestrated drapes covered and secured her entire body, only the planned abdominal field remained exposed beneath the surgical lights.
In real surgery, each step served a medical purpose. Here, they were being used to create a hopeless illusion.
Tears slid beneath the edge of Mika's cap as she cried out to Ren beside the table:
“Please… don't cut me! I told you I'm not a patient! Nurse Nanase, you don't look like this kind of person… Make her stop!”
Narumi had changed into a complete sterile gown and gloves and now walked slowly to the surgeon's position.
A surgical mask covered the lower half of her face. Her exposed eyes were almost emotionlessly calm.
“You are not a patient. I know that better than anyone.”
“Because from the moment you entered, you treated this place as someone else's territory.”
She extended a hand toward Ren across the table.
A scalpel was placed in her sterile-gloved palm.
The metal made no unusual sound, yet the immobilized Mika seemed to hear something terrifying.
Narumi did not raise the blade. Instead she gently rested the cold back of the scalpel against the still-unbroken skin of the abdominal field.
Mika broke completely, a scream bursting from her throat:
“Hirasaka! Dr. Hirasaka! It was all his idea!”
Mika shouted through tears and mucus:

“He heard you might be at Hoshimi and told me to confirm it while delivering an instrument catalogue! He wants your current names, jobs, addresses, and exactly how much you've told Director Jogu about the past!”

“Because I sell gynecologic instruments for him! He controls all my contracts with the major hospitals. I owe him favors, and I had a private relationship with him… I took his money, but he also warned that if I refused this errand, he would have every partner hospital blacklist me!”
“Yes! I thought I only had to confirm who was here and ask a few questions! I never meant to hurt you!”
Ren remained by the instrument table, one hand resting lightly over the breast pocket of her scrubs. The miniature recorder concealed inside was running.
Haltingly, Mika disclosed the contact method, payment, and agreed reporting deadline. She spoke so quickly that several times she had to stop and gasp for breath.
Narumi neither lifted nor withdrew the scalpel, as though waiting for a report to reach its final page.
At last, Ren raised her head.
“Dr. Jinguji. She has told us everything.”
Narumi looked at Ren, then drew back her hand and returned the scalpel to the instrument table.
“No one is going to cut you.”
For a moment, Mika could not speak.
After a long while, she finally asked in a trembling, tearful voice:
“From the beginning… this was an act?”
“I never intended to make an incision.”
“How could I possibly know that while I was lying on the table?!”
This time Narumi gave no answer. She and Ren simply began releasing the restraints and removing the drapes and catheter.
Ryuji Sakaguchi had come to the supply room at the end of the surgical wing to verify an inventory record for surgical sutures.
Passing the inner corridor outside OR Three, he saw its indicator light illuminated despite no case being scheduled there that afternoon.
Through the heavy door, he faintly heard a man's name from within.
Sakaguchi stopped. He had recently seen that name on the title page of an old paper in Narumi's office.
Then came a woman's uncontrolled sobbing.

Frowning, Sakaguchi approached the blind angle beside the observation window and looked inside. The operating table was draped. Narumi, in a sterile gown, returned an unstained scalpel to the instrument table and said coldly, “No one is going to cut you… I never intended to make an incision.” Beside her, Ren wore only green scrubs and moved to remove the woman's drapes.
Sakaguchi slowly released his hand from beside the door handle.

The scene clearly exceeded the bounds of normal medical practice. Yet after seeing Narumi put down the scalpel and hearing her explicitly say she would not cut, Sakaguchi did not storm inside to condemn them. He knew something extraordinarily difficult must have driven the normally rule-bound Narumi and Ren to such misconduct inside the hospital.
Footsteps sounded from the other end of the corridor. A duty nurse approached carrying a tray and looked curiously toward the lit OR Three:
“Dr. Sakaguchi? Is there an emergency operation in OR Three this evening?”
Without showing any reaction, Sakaguchi shifted to block the door and spoke calmly:
“There is no operation. I asked Dr. Jinguji and Nurse Nanase to help check the placement of several instruments. They turned on the light and are nearly finished cleaning up.”
“I see. Then I'll get back to work up front.”
After sending her away, Sakaguchi took one final look at the two women cleaning the instruments. Without interrupting, he quietly turned and left the corridor.
Inside, Ren had just removed her mask. Through the observation window she caught sight of the departing white coat and froze slightly:
“Dr. Jinguji… I think that was Dr. Sakaguchi outside.”
Narumi looked at the empty corridor beyond the window, her expression sharpening:
“…First take her to observation. Once we finish dealing with today's situation, we will confess everything to the director.”
In the private observation room, Mika had changed back into her own clothes.

A regular outpatient nurse who had not participated in the afternoon's events had followed standard procedure to measure her blood pressure and heart rate. Only after confirming stable vital signs and no obvious acute abnormality did the nurse leave.
Narumi and Ren now stood at the doorway without approaching her again.
“I will keep the recording secure. I won't give it to Hirasaka.”
Mika looked up, her face darkening further:
“The forged consent form has been destroyed. You may call the police or complain to the director about what happened today. We will not deny it.”
Mika gripped her phone until her knuckles turned white:
“And then what? You hand over the recording of my confession?”
“We cannot decide the consequences for you.”
The phone in Mika's bag vibrated. A message appeared, demanding a progress report.
Mika stared at the screen, her voice rough:

“What am I supposed to say when he asks whether I found you? If I say yes, he'll ask why I stayed in the hospital so long. If I tell him about the operating room, he'll only suspect that I've confessed everything about him.”
She slowly raised her head and looked at the two women by the door:
“You know better than I do what he does to people who betray him, don't you?”

Mika typed rapidly, revised the message several times, and finally pressed send: “Made contact with Hoshimi Hospital as agreed. Found no evidence that either target works here. Recommend no further manpower.”
She held up the successful-send screen for Narumi to see and spoke coldly:
“I told him you aren't here. Not because I trust you. I just… don't want to destroy myself.”
“I won't ask you to thank us.”
Ren placed Mika's briefcase beside the table:
“A car is waiting at the hospital entrance. The driver only knows he is collecting a departing visitor. Whether you take it is your choice.”
Mika picked up the bag and reached the door, then abruptly stopped:
“A doctor and a nurse at Hoshimi Hospital.”
Mika stared at her for a long time, then gave a cold laugh:
“…Today, I don't want to believe that at all.”
With that, she left the hospital without looking back.
After seeing Mika off, Narumi and Ren did not return to the lounge. They went directly to knock on the director's office door.
The recorder lay on the desk beside the written incident reports they had prepared voluntarily.

After hearing the account and confirming that an independent clinician had verified Mika's stable vital signs before departure, Asuka Jogu exhaled softly and regarded them both with a grave expression.
“Neither of you concealed this from me. You came here to confess immediately after seeing her off. I will remember that.”
“Using the spare operating room to frighten a visitor was my decision. I will accept every internal penalty. Please do not implicate the hospital or Ren.”
“Director, I chose to help Dr. Jinguji. If there is punishment, include me too.”
Asuka shook her head. Her tone was not harsh, but the boundary she set was unmistakable:

“I took you into Hoshimi despite the pressure because I wanted you to escape that old environment and practice openly as a doctor and nurse. Even if neither of you ever intended to cut her, using this hospital's operating room as an instrument of intimidation crossed an absolute line. I will seal this record in our internal file, but nothing like it may ever happen again in a Hoshimi operating room. Understood?”
“I understand, Director. There will never be a second time.”
Asuka's expression softened, and one finger lightly touched the final paragraph of their statement:
“But you said Dr. Sakaguchi passed OR Three this evening, heard the disturbance, and deliberately sent away a duty nurse who approached?”
“Yes. He didn't come inside to accuse us, but he must have heard Hirasaka's name.”

“And when Mika Shimotsuki registered this afternoon, she used Dr. Sakaguchi's recent arrival as her excuse. If Hirasaka doesn't fully believe her false report and sends someone else to test us, they may target Dr. Sakaguchi next…”
Asuka considered this, then looked up to ask their opinion:

“Dr. Sakaguchi covered for you at the door, and he is now your most frequent surgical partner. Keeping him in the dark only leaves him vulnerable. Tomorrow morning I will speak with him for ten minutes. Without revealing private details about your former hospital, I will warn him that Hirasaka sent someone to investigate. Do you agree?”
Narumi and Ren exchanged a look and nodded together.
“If it is Dr. Sakaguchi, I agree.”
Early the next morning, Ryuji Sakaguchi came to the director's office as requested.
Asuka pushed a cup of warm tea toward him:
“Good morning, Dr. Sakaguchi. I called you before clinic begins. This will take only ten minutes.”
“Good morning, Director. This is about OR Three yesterday evening, isn't it?”

“Nothing gets past you. After Narumi and Ren saw off that saleswoman, Mika Shimotsuki, they came straight to me last night to confess and accept punishment. They made a point of telling me that you helped by sending away the nurse outside.”
“I saw they were already finishing. There was no need for anyone else to stumble onto the scene.”
“When you saw a doctor and nurse you trust clearly violating the rules in a spare operating room, did you never consider going straight inside to stop them?”
I saw Dr. Jinguji put the scalpel down herself and heard her say she would not cut. Once I knew no one would be harmed, barging in would only have made the situation more chaotic.
In clinical work, they follow the rules more strictly than anyone. Rather than storm in to accuse them, I wanted to know what trouble had driven them that far.
“I saw Dr. Jinguji put the scalpel down herself and heard her say she would not cut. Once I knew no one would be harmed, barging in would only have made the situation more chaotic.”

Although what they did in the operating room yesterday did cross a line, you saw Narumi put the knife away, heard her say she had never intended to cut the patient open, and even steered passersby away for them. They must be very grateful to you.
“In clinical work, they follow the rules more strictly than anyone. Rather than storm in to accuse them, I wanted to know what trouble had driven them that far.”
Asuka's expression tightened, and she shook her head seriously:

“Still, Narumi did not lose her head in a panic yesterday. She knew exactly what she was doing and deliberately chose that method after careful consideration. I can understand their circumstances, but Hoshimi Hospital can never become a tool she uses against old enemies.”
Asuka let the smile fade and earnestly explained the situation to Sakaguchi:

“After obtaining Narumi and Ren's consent, I called you here today to formally bring you into the loop. Both of them once worked at a hospital under Ryuji Hirasaka's control, but later broke with him completely. Narumi in particular has a very complicated history with Hirasaka. I think what happened should be for her to tell you herself. When they left and Hirasaka suppressed them throughout the medical field, I was the one who brought them to Hoshimi.”
“So Mika Shimotsuki was an investigator Hirasaka sent to find them.”

“Yes. To protect herself, Mika sent Hirasaka a false report saying she found no evidence they worked here, but a man like him may not believe it easily. She also deliberately used your name at reception yesterday. If Hirasaka tries a more discreet probe next, he may approach your surgical clinic directly.”
“Understood. If I notice anything unusual in clinic or among referrals, I will report it immediately.”

“There is one more thing. When they left this office last night, both were deeply uneasy. They feared that after seeing yesterday's scene, you would consider them dangerous and refuse to work with them again.”
I don't approve of yesterday's method, but the Dr. Jinguji and Nurse Nanase I know are more than what I saw in that operating room.
They have admitted their mistake to the director, so that page is finished. The next time trouble comes from outside, we will face it together.
“I don't approve of yesterday's method, but the Dr. Jinguji and Nurse Nanase I know are more than what I saw in that operating room.”
“That sounds exactly like you. Hearing you say it puts my mind completely at ease.”
“They have admitted their mistake to the director, so that page is finished. The next time trouble comes from outside, we will face it together.”
“With those words, the weight on both their hearts can finally lift.”
The wall clock completed exactly ten minutes and pointed to eight fifty.
“There. Exactly ten minutes. I needn't relay the message for you. Those two have probably been waiting in the corridor to read your expression this whole time.”
Sakaguchi said goodbye, opened the office door, and stepped outside.
In the sunlight at the corridor corner, Narumi and Ren had indeed stopped on their way to the clinic and ward.
At the sound of the door, they turned together. The normally composed Narumi's fingers tightened slightly, while Ren watched him with open unease.
“D-Dr. Sakaguchi… Is the director finished talking to you?”
Sakaguchi looked at their tense expressions and lifted his clipboard as naturally as he did before daily rounds.
“We're finished. Clinic begins in ten minutes. Dr. Jinguji, have you checked the pre-op assessment for this afternoon's operation?”
Narumi froze for a moment. The guarded tension in her eyes quietly melted away, and her usual warm, intelligent smile returned to her lips.
“It is checked. We can operate at any time.”
“Nurse Nanase, what about this morning's ward handoff?”
Ren's eyes lit up. She nodded vigorously, smiling brightly:
“Everything is confirmed! We can start whenever you're ready, Dr. Sakaguchi!”
strings.patient_bundles.patient_yoshizawa_miho.p: Miho Yoshizawa
“Hospitalization... is it? I will follow your arrangements. Only... could you tell me roughly how long I will need to stay? I need to put things in order at the house first.”
“Understood, I will stay. I will explain things to the painter myself... please don't trouble yourself over me.”
“I'm sorry, I would like to confirm something... The operation explained earlier seems to have a different name from the one mentioned just now. Did I mishear?”
“Thank you for explaining it so clearly. As long as I know what will happen next, I don't have to keep guessing.”
“Yes... I will cooperate. Um, forgive me for asking one more thing, but is the next step an examination, or is the surgery about to begin?”
“Doctor, I will try my best to stay composed... If I cannot answer right away, could you please ask me once more?”
“General anesthesia... Once I fall asleep, I won't know anything at all, will I? If someone could tell me it is over when I wake up, I would feel much more at ease.”
“Epidural anesthesia... I will stay awake while part of my body cannot move, is that right?... Understood, I will try my best not to panic.”
“With local anesthesia, I will still be able to speak, won't I? If it feels uncomfortable inside... I will do my best to tell you instead of holding it in silently.”
“Without anesthesia...? I'm sorry, I thought I should agree to what is asked of me... but having surgery directly like that truly frightens me.”
“...Thank you. I will close my eyes now. I leave everything else in your hands...”
“Ugh... it hurts...! Please wait... I'm not trying to be uncooperative, I truly, truly cannot keep enduring this...!”
“I'm sorry, I can't stop trembling... Please don't grab hold of me all of a sudden. If you tell me first, I will do my best to follow.”
“I know I need to hold this posture... it's just that the pulling sensation a moment ago made me flinch without meaning to. Please give me a little time.”
“...So I really cannot move on my own. If you need to adjust my position, could you tell me beforehand? It's a little frightening when I cannot see.”

“Dr. Sakaguchi... am I really having surgery today? I have already put matters at the house in order. Could you please tell me once more how everything will be arranged from here?”

“Um... may I ask in a little more detail? Once I am on the operating table later, from positioning and disinfection to the actual incision, which step comes first...? I'm afraid I won't dare to speak up then.”

strings.collections.character_events.narumi_ren_: A second referral brings a real patient to Hoshimi—and forces Narumi and Ren to settle their past for good.
The pelvic imaging report on the desk lay open to its third page.
