Two toothed curved clamps landed left and right with pinpoint accuracy. Clamp, divide, double suture-ligate—Aqua's knot-tying was almost a blur yet rock-solid on every throw, safely mobilizing both healthy ovaries and distal tubes and tucking them gently outside the pelvic sidewall.
Next, the operation reached its first major hurdle of the day—the dense band of adhesions fusing the posterior uterine wall to the anterior rectum.
Pausing her instruments, Aqua Mizuki raised her eyes to Ryuji Sakaguchi across the table:

"Now we dissect the rectal adhesions in the right posterior pouch of Douglas. Sakaguchi, steady the retractor with your left hand and reach your right hand into the channel under the sterile drapes to grip the uterine manipulator handle—following the safe boundary you mapped before incision, elevate two centimeters cephalad and add fifteen degrees of ventral anteversion to put the posterior adhesion band on full stretch!"

Sliding his right hand into the channel beneath the sterile drapes, he closed his gloved fingers once more around the cool stainless-steel handle protruding from between Serena's legs, applying steady wrist pressure to elevate along the pelvic axis while angling the handle slightly downward to antevert the uterus.
From behind the anesthesia screen at the head of the table came Serena's involuntary, trembling groan.

Although the epidural completely blocked the cutting pain of the laparotomy, with her abdominal cavity wide open she could still feel with startling clarity as Ryuji Sakaguchi gripped the iron rod outside her vagina and levered her deep internal uterus high once again! The taut, visceral pulling sensation made her fingers clench the armboards white, and between mortification and tension she forced her voice past her teeth from behind the screen:
"Haa... Dr. Sakaguchi... even with my stomach cut open you still have to shove that iron rod upward...?! Chief Mizuki, how much longer are the two of you going to rummage around inside me..."

Without even lifting her eyelids, Aqua Mizuki rested the tips of her long Metzenbaum dissecting scissors steadily against the fibrous adhesion band stretched taut as a bowstring, her voice calm yet carrying unquestionable authority:

"Don't talk, and don't hold your breath, Serena. Right now the tips of my scissors are two millimeters from your anterior rectal wall—Sakaguchi lifting from below is what keeps your rectum safely out of harm's way. Slow your breathing and stay still; we'll be through in thirty seconds."
No teasing, no banter—only the absolute certainty of a surgeon holding life and death in her hands.
Behind the drape screen, Serena's breath caught. Swallowing the sharp complaint on the tip of her tongue, she pressed her lips shut obediently for the first time, not daring to breathe out of turn.

Under the shadowless lamp, aided by the rock-steady tension of Sakaguchi's manipulator beneath the drapes, Aqua's wrist glided effortlessly as she sharply lysed layer after layer of dense scar tissue. In barely half a minute, the anterior rectal wall that had been fused behind the large isthmic fibroid fell cleanly away without a single nick to a serosal vessel.

Incising the vesicouterine peritoneal fold, Aqua Mizuki let her gaze rest on the large right isthmic fibroid bulging laterally into the broad ligament, paused slightly, and looked up to quiz Sakaguchi:

"The adhesions are freed, and next are the deep uterine vessels. Sakaguchi, let's test the real skill you've built over your first ten gynecological cases—this right isthmic fibroid bulges laterally and distorts the normal parametrial space. I'm about to place clamps across the right uterine vessels: how should your uterine manipulator coordinate with me, and what is the single most critical structure we must avoid injuring before clamping?"
"Use the metal colpotomy cup rim to push the bladder well down first, identify the right ureter 'water under the bridge,' then slide the clamp flush against the cervix."
"Elevate cephalad and pull toward the left with the manipulator under the drape to expose the right parametrium, confirm the right ureter's course, then clamp flush against the corpus."
Keeping his eyes focused on the deep operative field, Ryuji Sakaguchi answered steadily:

"The most critical structure to protect is the right ureter passing beneath the uterine artery close to the parametrium. I'll push the metal colpotomy cup firmly from below as a landmark while assisting you in mobilizing the bladder flap and ureteric knee well downward; once we verify the 'water under the bridge' course of the ureter, we slide the clamp flush against the lateral uterine isthmus."
Aqua Mizuki's eyes lit up as she praised him behind her mask:
"Full marks! You even remembered to mobilize the bladder downward to drop the ureteric knee away when a fibroid crowds the space—your gynecology foundation is even more solid than I imagined!"
Holding the sub-drape manipulator handle steady, Ryuji Sakaguchi answered clearly:

"The most critical structure to protect is the right ureter displaced by the bulging fibroid. Now that the right posterior adhesions are lysed, I'll elevate cephalad and deviate toward the left with the manipulator to open up the right parametrial space; then we palpate and confirm the actual course of the right ureter together before clamping flush against the uterine wall."
Aqua Mizuki's eyes curved in genuine admiration:

"Beautiful! Using manipulator tension to open the parametrial space first and verifying the ureter's course by hand before placing a clamp—never rushing blindly, you've completely grasped the essence of deep pelvic surgery!"

As Ryuji Sakaguchi applied steady force beneath the sterile drapes—driving the metal uterine manipulator deep cephalad and drawing it contralaterally—the uterine isthmus once recessed at the bottom of the pelvic funnel was lifted cleanly into shallow view.

Following the rigid circular ridge tented up by the metal colpotomy cup, Aqua Mizuki used a peanut sponge to gently dissect the bladder off the anterior cervix, palpated the right parametrium between her left thumb and index finger to confirm the ureter's course and safety margin, and slid two heavy Heaney clamps flush down the lateral cervical wall!
Clamp, divide, and doubly suture-ligate the bilateral uterine vessels; then serially clamp and divide the bilateral cardinal and uterosacral ligaments.
Now, the entire enlarged, fibroid-ridden uterus remained attached to her body only along the circular vaginal fornix at the very bottom.
Aqua Mizuki took a deep breath:
"Final step, Sakaguchi—push the manipulator under the drapes as high cephalad as it goes so that metal colpotomy cup stretches the entire ring of the vaginal fornix taut!"
Ryuji Sakaguchi lifted firmly upward with his right hand.

Behind the anesthesia screen, Serena tensed from head to toe, feeling the cold metal cup pressing against the deepest part of her vagina to the absolute limit; inside the pelvic field, the circular ridge raised by the cup rim stood out as sharply as a drawn ruler line.

With her scalpel, Aqua Mizuki incised the anterior vaginal fornix precisely along the upper rim of the metal colpotomy cup, exposing the gleaming silver lip of the cup beneath, then switched to curved Mayo scissors to circumscribe the entire vaginal wall flush against the metal rim!
As the last strand of posterior fornix tissue parted, Aqua secured the anterior and posterior margins of the vaginal cuff with long curved clamps to prevent retraction and gave a crisp command:

"The uterus is completely freed! Sakaguchi, release the traction under the drapes and gently withdraw the uterine manipulator out through the lower channel while I lift the specimen from the abdomen!"

Following her order, Ryuji Sakaguchi smoothly withdrew the stainless-steel uterine manipulator caudad and handed it off to the non-sterile basin below; in that same second, Aqua Mizuki lifted the heavy, fibroid-studded uterus and cervix intact out of the abdominal incision with both hands and placed it gently into the stainless-steel specimen kidney dish.

At the exact moment the cold metal shaft that had transfixed her insides slid out of her body and the heavy lesion that had caused her months of agony and bleeding was lifted away from her pelvis, Serena felt a sudden, eerie hollowness deep within her lower abdomen.

There was none of the agonizing pain she had dreaded, nor any dramatic complication. Staring blankly at the white ceiling above and hearing the soft thud against the metal specimen dish, she found herself completely speechless.

Without relaxing her focus for an instant, Aqua Mizuki swabbed the vaginal cuff lumen thoroughly with povidone-iodine, closed the cuff in a tight continuous running suture with synthetic absorbable thread, and anchored the cuff angles to the cardinal and uterosacral ligament stumps to support the pelvic floor—before irrigating the pelvis repeatedly with warm saline to confirm normal peristalsis of both ureters and rosy perfusion of both preserved ovaries.
Moe Honjo and the scrub nurse called out the final count together:
"Chief Mizuki, Dr. Sakaguchi—sponges, needles, and instruments counted twice, all numbers correct! Total intraoperative blood loss... is only eighty-five milliliters!"
Nodding in satisfaction, Aqua Mizuki stepped half a pace back and looked across at Ryuji Sakaguchi, her eyes above her mask brimming with pure surgical pride:

"Blood loss under a hundred milliliters, zero collateral injury from the adhesions. All yours, Mr. First Assistant—show me how you finish the layer-by-layer closure of the peritoneum and abdominal wall!"
Taking the needle holder and suture, Ryuji Sakaguchi met Aqua's trusting gaze and nodded steadily:
At 9:30 the next morning, holding the gross specimen sectioning note and rapid pathology verification slip, Aqua Mizuki led Ryuji Sakaguchi through the door of the private room for Bed 7.

In bed, Serena had changed back into a clean light-colored patient gown, her long dark hair brushed smooth once more. Though her face still looked slightly pale after major abdominal surgery, the relentless, twisting cramping deep in her lower belly that had tormented her for the past half-year had vanished without a trace.

Walking to the bedside, Aqua Mizuki professionally lifted the corner of the blanket to inspect the abdominal binder and incision dressing—confirming it was dry and clean—listened for bowel sounds with her stethoscope, and checked the clear, normal urine output in the bedside drainage bag before straightening up with a bright smile:

"Temperature normal, bowel sounds are back, and your urine is crystal clear! Pathology matched this Chief's preoperative diagnosis to the letter—diffuse adenomyosis plus four leiomyomas, clean margins, and both preserved ovaries are in great shape. From now on, you'll never have to suffer agonizing monthly pain or dizzy spells from anemia again!"
Leaning against her pillow, Serena stared with a complicated expression at the beaming Aqua Mizuki, then glanced over at the calm Ryuji Sakaguchi beside her.

Having listened wide awake to every step of the operation in OR 2 yesterday, she knew better than anyone how masterfully this seemingly scatterbrained chief handled a scalpel; yet whenever she remembered how her surgery had been ambushed forward—forcing her to climb naked onto the operating table right in front of Ryuji Sakaguchi and have her legs strapped high while the two of them took turns levering a metal uterine manipulator inside her as a live teaching aid—her fiercely competitive pride burned hot.
After three seconds of silence, Serena gave a soft huff, lifted her chin slightly, and resumed her discerning, aristocratic poise:

"...Very well. Seeing that the cramping in my abdomen really is gone this morning and the incision is sutured neatly enough, I won't nitpick your surgical technique itself—I'll consider the two of you barely passing."
With that, her eyes shifted and her lips curved into a sweet smile laced with thorns, attempting to reclaim the upper hand between a formal complaint and a bargain:

"However, Chief Mizuki—moving next Friday's surgery up to first thing the next morning was bad enough, and before the incision you even had a young male doctor stand in that position and rock a freezing iron rod inside my body for half an hour while you lectured... If I were to ask Director Jogu to come up here later to file a complaint against the Chief of Gynecology for 'excessive teaching demonstration'—and while I'm at it, ask to waive this week's private-room surcharge and replace that bland rice gruel at lunch with Darjeeling tea and caramel pudding—that would be perfectly reasonable, wouldn't it?"

Beside the bed, Ryuji Sakaguchi suppressed a wry smile—even lying in bed the morning after a total hysterectomy, Ms. Serena's calculating, give-no-quarter nature hadn't changed one bit; she was definitely not the type to turn into a docile lamb after going under the knife.
Yet faced with that velvet-gloved leverage, Aqua Mizuki showed zero guilt; instead, her eyes lit right up and she clapped her hands in excitement:

"Huh?! You're going to call Asuka over in person just to praise how well our uterine manipulator teaching demonstration went yesterday?! That's wonderful! Make sure you mention to the Director how steady Sakaguchi's hands were as first assistant when he reached under the sterile drapes and elevated your uterus two centimeters with the manipulator! I was just wondering how to brag to the Director about my star pupil!"
The graceful smile on Serena's face froze solid, the corner of her eye twitching:
Completely unfazed, Aqua Mizuki flipped open the order sheet, signed her name with a flourish, and waved her hand firmly:

"As for black tea and caramel pudding, don't even think about it! Your bowels just started moving, so you're strictly limited to warm clear rice gruel—this Chief wrote it in black and white on your order sheet, and I won't change it even if Asuka begs me in person! Let the nurse help you stand by the bed for five minutes this afternoon to prevent adhesions. Come on, Sakaguchi, let's go!"

Serena's chest heaved sharply as all three of her prepared bargaining gambits punched straight into steel wrapped in cotton. Watching Aqua already turn toward the door, an unwillingly bested Serena gritted her teeth, glared at Ryuji Sakaguchi, and lowered her voice for one last barbed parting shot:

"...Dr. Sakaguchi, if I were you, I'd stay far away from this Chief who doesn't understand human speech. I'm keeping score of everything that happened on that operating table yesterday—once I'm discharged and back on my feet... we'll see about this."
Ryuji Sakaguchi offered a polite, unruffled bow:

"Seeing you deliver threats in such high spirits today puts my mind completely at ease as your first assistant, Ms. Serena. Please remember to finish your rice gruel at noon, and I wish you a speedy recovery."
Meeting Serena's speechless, lip-biting glare, Ryuji Sakaguchi calmly pulled the ward door shut.
Stepping out of Room 7, the hospital corridor was bathed in bright morning sunlight.
Having already forgotten Serena's threats completely, Aqua Mizuki turned around with her hands on her hips and patted Ryuji Sakaguchi's arm with beaming pride:

"How about that, Sakaguchi! From pre-incision uterine manipulator positioning to sub-drape elevation and exposure, all the way to dividing the uterine vessels and circumscribing the vaginal fornix—you've got all the essentials of an Open Total Abdominal Hysterectomy down pat now, right?"
Looking at the bright-eyed Chief of Gynecology before him, Ryuji Sakaguchi nodded with genuine respect:

"I've committed all of it to memory. Watching you dissect those rectal adhesions within a two-millimeter margin and safeguard the ureters on the table yesterday was truly eye-opening—your gynecological surgical skill is undeniably top-tier, Chief Mizuki."
Praised so earnestly by Sakaguchi, Aqua Mizuki practically glowed with pride, tossing her long blue hair as her voice rang out across the corridor again:

"Hehe, now you know just how amazing this Chief is! Starting today, you're officially cleared to scrub in as primary surgeon for Open Total Abdominal Hysterectomies at Hoshimi! And this is only the first step of your advanced gynecology training—once you log a few more gynecological cases, I'll find another chance to give you a live demonstration of even more impressive deep instrument maneuvers! Oh, look, here comes Moe—"
Rounding the corridor corner with a stack of temperature charts in her arms, Moe Honjo abruptly heard the words 'live demonstration' leap out of Aqua Mizuki's mouth.

The terrifying image of that gleaming stainless-steel uterine manipulator tenting up the patient's belly in OR 2 yesterday flashed instantly through her mind, making the eighteen-year-old nurse shudder and turn pale on the spot:
"Waaah—!! Ch-Chief Mizuki, Head Nurse Ishigami just asked me to go check the sterile gauze inventory on the first floor—I have to run!!"
With a gust-like patter of footsteps, Moe Honjo bolted away without looking back.
Her hand still raised in greeting, Aqua Mizuki froze and blinked her wide eyes in bafflement:
"...Weird, I'm not even holding any gynecological instruments today—why did she run away?"
Looking down the gynecology corridor that had once again emptied in record time, Ryuji Sakaguchi offered a deadpan summary:
"In the nurses' eyes, Chief Mizuki, simply having you stand in the hallway probably counts as a restricted-grade gynecological instrument."
"Hey—!! What kind of way is that to talk to your mentor, Sakaguchi!!"
strings.collections.special_events.miyama_01_saf: Miyama admits a young band vocalist clutching her stomach on the way to rehearsal. A sharp safety-pin shadow on her X-ray sends the afternoon straight into the operating room.
strings.collections.special_event_steps.miyama_0: At 3:40 p.m., Ryuji Sakaguchi was just passing down the corridor when Kaori Miyama called him into the examination room.

Sitting on the edge of the exam table was a twenty-two-year-old woman. Her striking bright-red hair was tied into a lively side tail, and even though one hand was pressed over her lower abdomen, the moment she saw Sakaguchi walk in she sat straight up and flashed a social smile so sunny it practically came with its own sparkle filter.
"Oh, another doctor! Good afternoon—I'm Ikuyo Kita! Sorry for suddenly rushing into the ER in the middle of the day and causing trouble for both of you!"
Sakaguchi blinked slightly and gave a polite nod:
"Hello, I'm Ryuji Sakaguchi from Surgery. Is your stomach giving you a lot of trouble?"
Pressing her belly with one hand while waving her lit smartphone with the other, Kita spoke in a tone as breezy as if she were chatting about weekend plans:

"Honestly, it's nothing that dramatic! Maybe it's because I was rushing to revise lyrics at noon, drank an iced Americano on an empty stomach, and ate way too fast, so my stomach's been cramping on and off ever since. My band has ensemble rehearsal in Shimokitazawa at seven tonight, so I figured I'd swing by the hospital for some fast-acting painkillers and head over at a hundred percent—hss..."
Before she could finish, a sharp cramp hit; her practiced smile froze for half a second at the corner of her mouth before stubbornly curving right back up.
Standing in front of the X-ray lightbox, Kaori Miyama wasn't thrown off by her cheerful tone in the slightest, her brows slightly knit as she gave a concise briefing:

"Admitted twenty minutes ago. Subjective complaint of intermittent lower abdominal pain without a fixed location, no external trauma on inspection, and initial palpation showed no classic localized tenderness at McBurney's point. Just to be safe, I sent her for an upright plain abdominal film first."
As she spoke, Miyama raised her hand and snapped on the lightbox switch.

Right in the center of the stark black-and-white abdominal X-ray—superimposed directly over the lower abdominal pelvic projection—lay an unmistakably sharp, elongated metallic shadow, down to the coiled spring at one end and the closed clasp at the tip.
Sakaguchi leaned in for a closer look:
Kita craned her neck curiously for a peek, and her eyes instantly flew wide:
Miyama turned around, fixing Kita with a sharp gaze:
"Ms. Kita, give us the whole truth. When did you swallow something like this?"
Kita waved both hands furiously, shaking her head like a rattle-drum:

"No way, Dr. Miyama!! I'm twenty-two years old, not a three-year-old toddler—how could I possibly swallow a safety pin?! Even if I wolfed down my convenience-store rice ball at lunch, biting into an iron pin would definitely have cracked my teeth, right?!"
Pointing at the film, she tried her best to put on a polite yet aggrieved smile to smooth things over:
"Um... could Radiology have accidentally mixed up someone else's film just now? Or maybe a pin happened to stick to the camera lens or something?"
Miyama glanced at the name, age, and timestamp printed in the corner of the film, briskly ruling out any wishful thinking:
"Name: Ikuyo Kita, age twenty-two, taken at 15:32. Metal hardware on her outer garments was cleared per protocol before the exposure—there's no chance the film was mixed up."
"That's so weird... All I had today was an iced Americano and one rice ball—I swear I never put a safety pin anywhere near my mouth!"
Staring at the metallic shadow sitting dead center over her lower abdomen, Miyama's expression turned completely grave.

"Whether you swallowed it by accident or forgot how it happened, two objective facts remain: first, the plain abdominal film captured a sharp metallic foreign body projected over your lower abdomen; second, you are sitting in the ER right now with acute abdominal pain of unknown origin. If that pin is lodged in a bowel loop and the clasp springs open to cause a gastrointestinal perforation, there is zero room for slow observation."
Without a trace of hesitation, she turned straight toward Sakaguchi:

"Dr. Sakaguchi, we need to prep this case immediately as an acute abdomen with a suspected foreign body. You have more open laparotomy experience than I do—you take primary surgeon, and I'll scrub in as your first assistant."
Hearing the words "primary surgeon," the radiant smile on Kita's face at the edge of the exam table finally cracked.
"W-Wait a second! Doctors, when you say 'prep this case'... don't tell me you mean cutting me open?!"
Signing the emergency transfer slip, Miyama answered calmly:
"Based on the current imaging and symptoms, we have to prepare for surgery."
Sakaguchi took the chart, scanned her vital signs and initial bloodwork screen, and made the call steadily:
"Agreed. Notify the OR to set up an emergency table immediately."
Kita sprang straight up from the edge of the exam table:
"Eeeh?! Today?! I still have band rehearsal for our new song at the livehouse at seven tonight, and we have a joint gig next week!"
Miyama raised her eyes to look at her, her tone completely free of intimidation yet calm enough to make a person's hair stand on end:
Emergency prep at Hoshimi Hospital moved like clockwork.

In less than twenty minutes, having signed the emergency surgical consent form and had a barcoded wristband snapped around her wrist, Kita had already hurriedly shed her outer clothes for an emergency transport gown in the airlock, had every strand of her bright red hair neatly tucked into a blue elastic surgical cap by circulating nurse Rumi Iwasaki, and was lying on a transport gurney rolling straight toward the operating room.

Clutching the phone she hadn't handed over yet on the gurney, Kita typed frantically into her band group chat—'HELP!! I only came in for stomach medicine, and now the hospital says there's a safety pin in my belly and I need emergency surgery right now?! I might have to miss rehearsal tonight boohoo!!'
The instant the message went through, Rumi Iwasaki cheerfully collected her phone into the personal belongings bag.

Watching the corridor ceiling lights glide past overhead one after another while the gurney wheels clicked crisply beside her ears, Kita—who could chat and laugh effortlessly at any party—finally swallowed hard as reality caught up with her:
"...N-No way, is this for real...? Just this morning I was taking outfit selfies before leaving the house—how am I suddenly getting wheeled in to have my stomach cut open...?"
The automatic doors slid shut behind them, greeting her with the cool air peculiar to an operating room and the crisp clinking of surgical instruments being counted.

Not far away beneath the shadowless lamps, Ryuji Sakaguchi and Kaori Miyama—already changed into green scrubs with surgical caps and masks—were double-checking the imaging, while scrub nurse Mika Nakai stood before the instrument table methodically counting hemostats and retractors from the laparotomy pack.
Standing beside the black leather operating table, Rumi Iwasaki held out an empty clothing basket and spoke briskly to Kita as she stepped off the gurney:
"Ms. Kita, we came through the emergency lane in a rush just now—go ahead and take off everything you're wearing and hand it to me."

Clutching the front of her transport gown with both hands, Kita glanced reflexively at the male lead surgeon Sakaguchi a few paces away; her cheeks flared crimson as she tried politely in a tiny voice to negotiate:
"U-Um, Nurse... taking off the outer gown is enough, right? Can I at least keep my underwear on underneath...?"
Rumi shook her head with a smile, her tone light and natural, leaving no awkward pause for the patient's imagination to run wild:

"Emergency abdominal surgery requires full exposure of the entire abdomen and perineal prep zone, so nothing close-fitting can stay on. Don't worry—both doctors are busy checking the pre-op setup over there. Slip everything off and lie down on the table."

Looking at the gleaming rows of stainless-steel instruments under Mika Nakai's hands nearby, it truly sank in for Kita—she was no longer a band vocalist standing beneath stage spotlights, but a real patient seconds away from lying on an operating table under the knife.

Biting her lip, she turned half away, ears burning red as she untied the transport gown and handed it to Rumi; then she took a deep breath, bent down to slide her last pair of light-colored cotton panties down her legs, balled them up in her hand, and passed them into the basket.
"All right, watch your step on the footstool—just climb onto the operating table and lie flat on your back."

Shielding her chest with one arm, Kita stepped barefoot onto the stool and climbed tensely onto the cool operating table to lie flat. Nearby, Mika Nakai smoothly picked up a thin warming sheet and draped it steadily over her bare lower body.
At the exact second Kita let out a long breath and prepared to close her eyes and resign herself to fate—
Beside the table, Rumi casually shook out the panties Kita had just taken off to fold them into the clothing basket, flipping the folded hem of the front elastic waistband.
A crisp, tiny, yet impossibly clear metallic clink rang out against the terrazzo floor in the quiet operating room.

Sharp-eyed Mika Nakai swept her gaze toward the floor at once, crouched down with a pair of pre-sterile utility forceps to pick up the shiny little object steadily, and reported in a calm, crisp voice:
"Dr. Miyama, Dr. Sakaguchi. A clasped safety pin just fell onto the floor—judging from where it landed, it slipped out of the folded front waistband hem of the underwear the patient just removed."
Just about to head out to scrub and gown, Kaori Miyama stopped dead in her tracks and strode briskly back to the operating table, with Sakaguchi right behind her.

Every pair of eyes in the operating room swept back and forth in unison between the safety pin at the tip of Mika Nakai's forceps, the X-ray on the lightbox, and Ikuyo Kita lying on the operating table.
Kita froze for two seconds, craned her neck to get a clear look at the familiar little silver pin, and bolted wide-eyed as if jolted by electricity:
"AAAH—!! That's the safety pin from last night!!"
So excited she nearly sat straight up off the operating table, Kita slapped the edge of the pad and explained at breakneck speed:

"I do, I do!! Last night at home I was taking in the skirt waist of my band stage outfit for tonight with a bunch of safety pins, and afterward one went missing and I couldn't find it anywhere—it must have dropped into the folded waistband of the clean underwear stacked by my bed and gotten stuck!! When they took the X-ray earlier I only pushed my outer skirt with the metal zipper down past my knees while still wearing these panties underneath—no wonder it showed up lying right across the middle of my stomach!!"

In an instant, the sheer euphoria of surviving a brush with the scalpel swept away every shred of embarrassment and fear. Kita's whole face burst back into a dazzling smile, her voice practically chirping as if she'd just won a music festival championship:

"Thank goodness—!! Case closed, case closed! I never swallowed it at all! Haha, that scared me half to death—sorry for making both doctors and nurses panic for nothing, that's super embarrassing! Does that mean I can put my clothes back on now? If I catch a cab to Shimokitazawa right now, I can still make our seven o'clock band rehearsal—!"

Beaming like sunshine, she reached out toward the clothing basket by Rumi's hand—only to realize that Kaori Miyama, standing beside the operating table, wasn't smiling at all; instead, her brows knit slightly as she stepped half a pace closer.
Kita's hand froze in midair as she blinked:
Looking down at her, Miyama cut straight to the heart of the problem with clear, composed eyes:
"The pin was indeed found in your clothing. Since you never swallowed a pin at all—then what on earth caused the abdominal pain that brought you clutching your stomach into the ER this afternoon?"
On the operating table, Kita went blank.
Standing beside the table, Miyama spoke so earnestly there was even a trace of urgency in her voice:

"The metallic shadow on the X-ray was a false alarm—I admit that. But you didn't come to the hospital because you saw a pin; you came because your stomach hurt too much to go to rehearsal. So—does it still hurt right now?"
Surrounded beneath the shadowless lamp by an entire room of staff in green scrubs staring at her, Kita's mind went completely blank for half a second.
The instant the words left her mouth she stopped abruptly, looking down to feel her pounding heart and tight stomach:
"...Wait, no, maybe it doesn't hurt...? Eh... I-I don't know..."
Kita's fingers gripped the pad sheet beneath her as her eyes darted around in a panic:

"B-Because when I saw the pin fall out just now, I was so happy it suddenly felt like my stomach didn't hurt at all anymore... b-but the moment you asked so seriously, Dr. Miyama, it started feeling all twitchy and weird inside my lower belly again..."
"Then we cannot treat it as nothing."

At those words, alarm bells went off wildly inside Kita's head as survival instinct and twenty-two years of finely honed social reflexes fired at once—craning her neck up, she forced out a picture-perfect smile ten times brighter than before:

"Ahaha! It doesn't hurt! I've thought it through—it really doesn't hurt one bit anymore!! Just now was definitely an illusion from being too nervous! My stomach feels super great right now, honestly! Nothing's wrong at all, Dr. Miyama, Dr. Sakaguchi!"
"Five seconds ago, you just said 'I don't know.'"
Kita's smile stiffened, sweat nearly beading on her forehead:
"That was just a slip of the tongue! Anyone gets a little dazed when they suddenly breathe a sigh of relief—"
"Why did you suddenly change your answer?"
"Do you even have to ask?! Obviously because I don't want to get cut open!!"
Miyama replied without missing a beat:

"Then we can rely on your current answer even less. Because right now you aren't describing your symptoms at all—you're picking whichever answer you think will get you off this table to avoid surgery."
"Ugh...?! How could you say that—I'm telling the truth! Probably?!"

Watching one trying desperately to bluff her way off the table with a dazzling smile while the other refused to yield half an inch of clinical logic, Sakaguchi raised a hand to signal both sides to pause:

"Let's not jump to conclusions yet. Now that the foreign-body artifact is ruled out, while she's still on the operating table, let's perform a systematic abdominal palpation to verify her physical signs."
"Right—let's do as you say and re-examine her abdomen."
Hearing she had to lie back down to have her belly palpated again, Kita hunched her shoulders tight in a flash:
"W-What else do you still have to check...?"

Pulling on warm sterile exam gloves, Miyama signaled Rumi Iwasaki to fold the thin sheet over Kita's belly down above the pubic symphysis, exposing flat, fair abdominal skin rising and falling rapidly with her shallow breaths.
"We're palpating your abdomen once more to check for peritoneal irritation signs. Lay your shoulders flat, breathe deeply, and relax your stomach."
Gripping both edges of the operating table for dear life, Kita still clung to a stiff social smile:
"O-Okay! I'm super relaxed! Totally relaxed—look, I'm even smiling—!"
The moment Miyama laid her palm gently against her abdominal wall, her brows furrowed:
"Ms. Kita, your entire abdominal wall is as stiff as a wooden board."
Kita looked ready to cry without tears:
"Because five minutes ago you just told me you were going to slice my stomach open!! How is any normal person supposed to relax lying half-naked on an iron table like this?!"
Lightening the pressure of her wrist, Miyama began with gentle, probing palpation using the pads of her fingers around Kita's flat upper abdomen and umbilicus.
"Let's start lightly. How does it feel here?"

As the cool gloved fingertips brushed across her taut, ticklish belly, Kita gave a full-body shiver, sucked her stomach in with a tiny snort, and shook her head frantically with scarlet cheeks while stifling a giggle:
"Kya! Haha—sorry, sorry! It doesn't hurt, it doesn't hurt—having someone suddenly touch right next to my belly button just tickles! Look, I can even laugh, so I'm definitely not sick, right?"
Watching her rectus abdominis clench defensively, Miyama shook her head:
"She keeps pulling her stomach in reflexively; superficial light palpation can't pick up deep reactions at all."
Taking a breath, Miyama brought four fingers together over the right lower quadrant ileocecal region and pressed down steadily to standard clinical palpation depth.
"Don't laugh—focus on what you feel. How about here?"
The smile froze on Kita's lips as her brows pinched slightly:
"W-Wait a sec... it feels a tiny bit sore and bloated here... no, wait, maybe I just pulled a muscle jumping too hard at rehearsal the day before yesterday...?"
Miyama immediately shifted her hand to press the symmetrical left lower quadrant:
"Then what about this side? Is it the same as the right side just now?"
Fine sweat broke out at Kita's temples, her gaze completely scrambled:

"Eh?! Pressing the left side feels kinda weird too! Wait, no, maybe the right side was clearer? Or maybe my stomach just got chilled from the iced coffee at lunch... Ugh, Dr. Sakaguchi, my whole belly is thumping everywhere right now—even I can't tell whether it's pain or nerves anymore!!"

Unable to get a reliable answer across several regions in a row, Miyama grew ever more intent on ruling out an occult acute abdomen. Determined to press past the tense abdominal muscles and confirm whether true deep tenderness was present, her hand unconsciously sank in a fraction heavier, pressing firmly down into the deep quadrant—
This time Kita genuinely cried out aloud, a drop of physiological tears squeezing from the corner of her eye.
Miyama's eyes sharpened as she pressed immediately:
"Is it definitely deep pain right here?!"
Panting, Kita looked up at her in aggrieved meltdown:
"Dr. Miyama, if you mash my stomach down that hard with all your strength, even an ironclad healthy person is gonna hurt!!"
"I have to verify whether there's rebound tenderness when I release—one more time: was that pressure pain from my hand, or pain coming from inside?"
Clutching her head, Kita was on the verge of tears:

"I don't know, I really don't know anymore!! The more you ask, the more my whole stomach feels like it hurts, and when you don't ask it feels like it doesn't... Boohoo, why can't I even tell whether my own stomach hurts or not?!"
Glancing from across the table at the heart rate spiking on the monitor, Sakaguchi reached out gently to stay Miyama's wrist just as she prepared to press again:
"Dr. Miyama, let's stop here. She's extremely tense and guarding across her entire abdominal wall—pressing any further won't yield reliable clinical information anymore."
Looking down at Kita—flushed crimson, breathing fast, barely able to string a coherent sentence together—she fell silent for a second, then gently withdrew her hand.

She knew better than anyone: the harder she pressed to wring a black-and-white certainty out of the patient, the less capable this girl—desperate to please her doctors and escape the operating table—became of giving a single trustworthy answer.
Holding up the safety pin sealed inside a clear evidence bag, Rumi Iwasaki looked to both surgeons for instructions:
"Dr. Sakaguchi, Dr. Miyama, now that the foreign body is confirmed to have been outside in her clothing... should we cancel this emergency surgery?"
On the operating table, Kita immediately held her breath, her dewy eyes wide with hope as she looked toward Sakaguchi at the lead surgeon's position.
"Since we found the pin, let's cancel the surgery for now and pack up."
"Finding the pin outside her body actually leaves her original abdominal pain unexplained."
Glancing at the safety pin in the evidence bag, Sakaguchi spoke:
"Since the pin was found outside her body, our initial foreign-body perforation hypothesis no longer holds. Let's cancel the surgery for now and pack—"
Miyama spoke up at once to stop him:
Sakaguchi turned to look at her:
Meeting his gaze, Miyama spoke without a shred of stubborn pride—only the cool, rigorous logic of an emergency and surgical physician:

"Her verbal answers are completely unreliable now, and the operating-table palpation just now couldn't establish a clean bill of health through her abdominal guarding. At best, that pin explains the white shadow on the X-ray—it does not explain why her stomach hurt too badly to go to rehearsal."
She paused, looking straight at Sakaguchi word by word:
"Until we've ruled out atypical appendicitis, diverticulitis, or an early bowel lesion, I still cannot guarantee she is safe—and I certainly cannot send her back out onto the street on luck alone."
Looking between the X-ray film and the patient on the table, Sakaguchi considered thoughtfully:
"Now that the pin turned out to be caught in her waistband, it actually leaves the acute abdominal pain that brought her into the ER completely unexplained."
Miyama gave an immediate, emphatic nod, a flash of kindred professional recognition crossing her eyes:

"Exactly—that's what I'm thinking too. Resolving the misleading X-ray actually turns her acute abdominal pain into a clinical blind spot with zero reliable signs backing safety: she's changing her verbal answers to dodge surgery, and her abdomen guarded through the entire exam. If we let her walk out to rehearsal right now and it really is an early atypical acute abdomen, waiting until it perforates at midnight will be too late."
Listening to their exchange from the operating table, every trace of color drained visibly from Kita's face:
"W-Wait a second... Doctors?! Didn't the safety pin already fall on the floor?! Why does it sound like... you're still going to operate on me?!"
Turning toward her, Miyama explained earnestly:

"Because finding the pin proves your stomachache wasn't caused by the pin. Right now we can neither rule out intra-abdominal pathology nor confirm safety by palpation, so the safest course is to proceed directly with a lower abdominal exploratory laparotomy and check inside clearly."
Kita panicked so hard her voice cracked:
"B-But I can really swear right now that it doesn't hurt anymore—!"
"You just demonstrated firsthand that your 'it doesn't hurt' right now cannot serve as medical evidence."

For the first time in her life, this social natural—whose quick tongue could charm her way through school, part-time shifts, and livehouses alike—learned what it felt like to have her own words seal off every last escape route.
Standing behind the instrument table, Mika Nakai looked toward Ryuji Sakaguchi, confirming in a steady, capable tone:
"Dr. Sakaguchi, shall I continue setting up the instrument table?"
Miyama looked to Sakaguchi as well, quiet determination in her eyes as she awaited the primary surgeon's final call.
Sakaguchi studied Miyama for two seconds; seeing that she wasn't acting out of pride, but genuinely taking responsibility for that 'unexcluded what-if,' he gave a slow nod:
"We follow Dr. Miyama's call and rule out the risk completely. Prep for an emergency exploratory laparotomy under spinal anesthesia—proceed."
Lying dazed on the operating table, Kita felt a buzz go off inside her head:
"S-Spinal anesthesia...?! You won't even put me to sleep?! All I came in for was a box of painkillers...!"

Guided by Rumi Iwasaki's gentle voice and steadying hands on her shoulders, Kita curled onto her side in position while Sakaguchi personally administered the spinal anesthesia cleanly and briskly. By the time Kita lay flat on her back again and Rumi deftly completed local skin prep and catheterization readiness, Sakaguchi and Miyama had stepped out to scrub, donned sterile green surgical gowns and gloves with Mika Nakai's assistance, and returned to the table ready to operate.

Within just a few minutes, a warm, heavy numbness spread swiftly from her lower back across her lower abdomen and down both legs. Kita's mind remained wide-awake—her eyes could clearly see Sakaguchi and Miyama standing gowned on either side, and her ears caught every crisp metallic clink as Mika Nakai arranged stainless-steel instruments onto the tray, yet everything below her waist felt muffled beneath a thick layer of cotton, heavy and unfamiliar.
Picking up sterile toothed forceps, Miyama pinched gently twice along the planned lower abdominal incision line and looked up to verify:
"Ms. Kita, does it hurt where I'm touching you right now?"
Startled, Kita squeezed her eyes shut by reflex, waited two seconds, and blinked them open blankly:
"...Eh? Did you pinch already? It didn't hurt at all... My lower belly just feels numb and heavy, like it doesn't belong to me anymore..."
"Anesthetic level and pain blockade are completely adequate. Beginning skin disinfection."
With a sharp click, the main shadowless lamp switched to full brightness, bathing the entire operating table in a stark white beam.

Kita's bare arms rested flat along the padded armboards on either side while the thin lower sheet was folded down to the edge of her pubic symphysis. Sponge forceps lifted a large cotton ball soaked in amber-brown povidone-iodine and touched down steadily right at the center of her flat, fair navel.

Centered on her umbilicus and the lower midline incision site, the wet swab swept outward in expanding concentric circles without leaving a single gap—painting the pale, smooth skin of her abdomen beneath the surgical lamp in a glistening coat of golden-brown iodine.

Because spinal anesthesia had completely blocked pain and temperature sensation below her waist, Kita couldn't even feel the chill of the antiseptic on her skin. Yet watching wide-awake as the surgeon painted pre-incision iodine across her unfeeling bare belly to the metallic clink of surgical counts only made the surreal helplessness of lying conscious on the chopping block all the more overwhelming.
With a tear of sheer helplessness clinging to the corner of her eye, Kita stared up at the massive lamp housing overhead, unable to hold onto even a trace of her social smile:

"Boohoo... If I'd known this would happen, you couldn't have paid me to pin that skirt hem last night... Gotoh-san, Nijika-senpai, Ryo-senpai... your vocalist is really about to get her stomach cut open wide awake today..."

Sterile green surgical drapes were then unfolded and secured layer by layer, raising a neat cranial anesthesia screen above Kita's chest—completely blocking her view of her own abdomen while leaving her face uncovered.
Taking his place as primary surgeon, Sakaguchi spoke gently across the sterile screen to reassure her:
"Take it easy, Ms. Kita. The block is working thoroughly—you won't feel any pain at the incision, and if anything feels uncomfortable, tell us anytime."
The patient monitor ticked in a steady, even rhythm.

From the lead position, Sakaguchi accepted the scalpel from Mika Nakai and made a clean, controlled lower midline exploratory incision. Opening subcutaneous tissue, fascia, and peritoneum layer by layer, he worked across from Miyama, whose retraction and suction as first assistant were crisp, precise, and completely free of wasted motion.

Behind the cranial sterile screen, Kita gripped the edges of the armboards tight, staring wide-eyed at the OR ceiling. Hearing the faint clicks of hemostats ratcheting and gauze dabbing on the other side of the drape, she gulped and spoke in a tiny, trembling voice:
"U-Um... Dr. Sakaguchi, Dr. Miyama? Before you make the first cut, could you count 'one, two, three' for me so I can brace myself...?"
Steadily retracting the abdominal wall incision, Miyama answered calmly without even looking up:
"No need for a countdown—we've already incised and entered the peritoneal cavity. Keep your shoulders still."
Kita sucked in a sharp breath, her voice nearly pitching off-key:
"EEEH—?!! Y-You already cut my stomach open?!! It really didn't hurt at all... wait no, knowing my belly is wide open right now makes it ten times scarier!!"
Sakaguchi offered a steady reassurance across the drape:
"That means the spinal block is working well. Right now we're systematically checking your lower bowel loops, appendix, and pelvis—we'll be finished looking shortly."
Beneath the shadowless lamp, laparotomy pads moistened with warm saline gently swept aside the greater omentum, exposing the right lower quadrant ileocecal field first.
Miyama leaned in to inspect the exposed structures closely:
"Ileocecal serosa is smooth; appendix is slender and supple, with no congestion, edema, fecalith impaction, or sign of perforation."
Following the anatomical planes unhurriedly, Sakaguchi gently ran the terminal ileum and adjacent lower small-bowel segments centimeter by centimeter:
"Right. Let's inspect each segment in order and make sure we don't miss an occult diverticulum."

Though she felt zero sharp pain, the subtle, muffled tugging deep inside her abdomen—the unmistakable sensation of gloved hands gently sliding and drawing things aside inside her own belly—made Kita's skin prickle behind the drape as she strained her ears to eavesdrop on the two surgeons:

"Ugh... feeling something gently pulling back and forth inside my stomach is so weird... U-Um, Dr. Miyama, if my appendix isn't swollen and my small intestine isn't torn, don't tell me there's really nothing wrong inside me at all...?"
Sakaguchi's tone remained warm and unhurried:
"Don't rush to call the findings for us yet, Ms. Kita. We still need to finish checking the sigmoid colon and pelvis—slow your breathing down a little."
Holding the abdominal wall retractor at a steady angle, Miyama glanced at Sakaguchi above her surgical mask and lowered her voice a fraction toward her partner:
"...You really don't rattle easily. Even after I framed the case so urgently earlier, you didn't rush the exploration."

"Once we commit to opening the abdomen, we owe it to her to inspect the lower abdomen and pelvis thoroughly—missing a hidden corner is what would truly make the incision pointless. Help me expose the sigmoid colon and deep pelvis."
Lower small intestine and ileocecal region—bowel wall pink and supple, without a trace of puncture or perforation.
Sigmoid colon and rectouterine pouch—serosa smooth and intact, free of inflammatory adhesions or diverticulitis.
Bilateral pelvic adnexa—spotless, without even a drop of abnormal effusion or exudate.
For a moment the operating room fell quiet save for the steady pulse of the monitor.
Pausing his exploration, Sakaguchi looked up across the table at his first assistant:
"Exploration of the lower bowel loops, appendix, and pelvis is complete. Zero organic pathology identified—a textbook negative laparotomy."
Miyama gazed down beneath the surgical light at the impeccably healthy abdominal viscera, silent for two seconds.
There was no wounded pride, nor any awkwardness over losing face. Shoulders that had been taut all afternoon slowly settled as, behind her mask, she let out a quiet, genuinely relieved breath:
Miyama raised her clear, earnest eyes, her voice completely free of pretense:
Hardly had the words fallen when dead silence held behind the cranial drape for one full second—followed by an outraged protest loud enough to nearly knock her blue surgical cap askew—

"WAIT JUST A SECOND—!! What do you mean 'Thank goodness, she's completely healthy'?! My stomach is still cut wide open right now, isn't it?! Did you seriously open up my belly, rummage around inside, and say 'Thank goodness, completely healthy' straight to my internal organs in front of me?!!"

Faced with the patient's on-the-spot meltdown, Miyama showed zero guilt; instead, she answered across the drape in a tone of a hundred percent sincere relief, as if nothing could be more self-evident:

"Would you rather we had found a bowel perforation or suppurative appendicitis inside you? Confirming with our own eyes that there is no organic lesion at all is obviously the best possible news today."
Tears glistening at the corners of her eyes, Kita wailed:

"W-Well, when you put it like that, sure... but I was just a healthy band vocalist who came in for painkillers to begin with!! Boohoo... now that you've confirmed I'm super healthy, please sew me back up quick, both of you!!"

Looking at Miyama's utterly earnest relief while listening to the spirited protest from behind the drape, Sakaguchi couldn't help letting out a quiet chuckle as he accepted the needle holder from Mika Nakai:
"You heard the patient hurrying us along. Come on, First Assistant—sponge and instrument count, let's prepare to close."

As the numbness of the spinal block gradually wore off from her lower body, Kita lay flat in bed changed back into a light-colored hospital gown. Though sterile dressings covered her lower abdomen and she couldn't twist around yet, her spirits were visibly livelier than before surgery—holding her freshly returned smartphone up with both hands and sighing dramatically over the exploding '99+' unread messages in her band group chat.
The instant she spotted Kaori Miyama and Ryuji Sakaguchi pushing open the ward door, Kita turned her head and puffed out her cheeks in plaintive protest:
"Aaah—Dr. Miyama, Dr. Sakaguchi! You two really have the nerve to walk in for rounds looking completely calm!"
Stepping up to the bedside, Miyama carefully checked her post-op pulse, lower-limb sensory recovery, and incision dressing before delivering a composed clinical update:

"Your vital signs are steady, and the incision dressing is clean and dry. Since organic pathology was thoroughly ruled out intraoperatively, this afternoon's abdominal pain was most likely a transient intestinal spasm triggered by drinking an iced Americano on an empty stomach plus pre-rehearsal tension."
Lowering her phone, Kita stared up at the ceiling half-laughing, half-crying:

"I lay on that operating table with my eyes wide open listening to every single word from start to finish!! First I got wheeled into the OR over a safety pin stuck in my underwear waistband, then I didn't even get put to sleep—I just lay there wide awake behind a green cloth listening to you rummage through my stomach and cheerfully announce 'Thank goodness, she's completely healthy'! Where on earth do you find an ER experience that absurd?!"
Miyama mulled that over with utmost seriousness for half a second:
"Compared with sleeping through everything in a haze, doesn't hearing with your own ears while wide awake that you're completely healthy put your mind at ease right on the spot—"
Quick on the uptake, Sakaguchi cleared his throat lightly to cut that line of reasoning short:
"Dr. Miyama, there's no need to elaborate on that particular reassurance."

"It doesn't put my mind at ease ONE BIT!! How am I supposed to explain this in our band group chat?! Gotoh-san was already so terrified in the chat earlier she offered to fold a thousand paper cranes for me—if I text them 'Sorry, the safety pin was actually stuck in my underwear, but I stayed wide awake listening to the doctors cut my belly open to confirm I'm super healthy,' everyone at the livehouse next week is gonna laugh at me for the rest of my life!!"
"Just tell everyone you were kept overnight for observation with acute intestinal spasms. Rest flat tonight, and you'll be back at rehearsal before long."

Though Kita still muttered under her breath about how 'hardcore this hospital's checkups are,' remembering the unmistakable sincerity in Miyama's quiet 'Thank goodness' at the operating table soon brought a bright, sunny smile back to her face as she waved at them both:

"All right, all right—hearing Dr. Miyama breathe that sigh of relief behind the curtain earlier, I could tell both of you were genuinely worried something bad might happen to me! Just remember to help me come up with a cooler-sounding excuse for missing rehearsal during morning rounds tomorrow, okay!"

Shortly after leaving the ward, while Sakaguchi stopped by the nurses' station to sign post-op orders, Asuka Shiromiya walked down the quiet early-evening hallway cradling a stack of administrative folders and paused beside Kaori Miyama at the vending machines.
With nobody else around, Asuka dropped the hospital director formalities, her tone as familiar as if they were back in a university clubroom:
"I heard you performed an emergency exploratory laparotomy this afternoon on a band vocalist who turned out to be completely healthy?"
Pressing the button for a warm canned tea, Miyama didn't even turn around:
"There were clinical grounds at the time. The X-ray had a foreign-body artifact, and the patient couldn't give a coherent account of her pain."
"I didn't say your judgment was wrong."
Miyama turned her head to cast a sidelong look at her old classmate:
"Then why did Madam Director come all the way over here?"
"To check whether a certain someone was spiraling into self-criticism and hiding in a corner skipping dinner."
Holding the warm can, Miyama gave a quiet huff:
Asuka chuckled, patted the back of her hand, and softened her voice a touch:
"Good. ...The patient is safe and sound, and nothing matters more than that. Go get dinner once you wrap up, Kaori."
A few minutes later, Asuka headed off, and Sakaguchi walked down the hallway after finishing the post-op orders.

Dusk was deepening outside the window. Standing by the glass with the unopened warm tea can still in her hand, Miyama seemed to be quietly reviewing every step at the operating table that afternoon—from that crisp 'Ding.' to the moment she had pressed too hard in her urgency to get a clear palpation answer.
Seeing Sakaguchi approach, Miyama turned toward him and spoke up first:
Looking him straight in the eye, Miyama spoke calmly and candidly:

"This afternoon at the operating table, the moment that safety pin dropped out—if you had used your authority as primary surgeon to overrule me and cancel the operation on the spot, I would have tried to stop you."
"I know. That's why I wanted to hear your reasoning all the way through."
Miyama blinked slightly, then pressed the corner of her lips together ever so faintly.
She glanced down at the tea can in her hand before raising her eyes squarely to Sakaguchi again. The aloof, appraising edge she usually carried softened, replaced by genuine professional recognition:

"Plenty of surgeons more worried about liability would have jumped at the excuse to send the patient home the moment the pin turned up in her clothes—and written me off as overreacting. ...Thank you for not brushing me off today, and for listening to the full clinical reasoning behind my call."
"Whenever you have solid clinical grounds, of course I'll listen seriously."
"Next time you palpate, go easy on the pressure—you pressed her completely dizzy."
"Confirming she's completely healthy in the end is hardly a bad outcome."
Sakaguchi's expression was warm and steady:
"You were the attending physician who examined her first, and the blind spot you pointed out was real. Whenever you have solid clinical grounds, of course I'll listen seriously."
Miyama paused for a heartbeat before a faint, clear smile touched the corner of her lips:
"...Right. With your word on that, the next time a thorny case comes into the ER, I'll call you straightaway."
Sakaguchi smiled with a touch of light teasing:

"Of course I'll listen. Next time we palpate on the operating table, though, remember to hold back a little before pressing deep—even the chattiest patient can't tell what hurts anymore once you press like that."
The tips of Miyama's fair ears warmed almost imperceptibly, yet instead of bristling, she nodded frankly:
"...I really was too impatient for a definitive answer on that press. Noted—I'll do better next time."
Looking out at the night sky beyond the window, Sakaguchi spoke gently:
"The path there took a few twists, sure, but confirming with our own eyes that she's completely healthy is hardly a bad outcome."
Miyama let out a soft breath, a rare, relaxed smile touching her lips:
"True enough. Far better than letting her go sing halfway through a set only to come back in an ambulance."
Popping the tab on her warm tea can, Miyama gave Sakaguchi a composed, respectful nod:
"Thank you for taking the lead at the table today, Dr. Sakaguchi. It seems the Director's praise for your surgical record wasn't mere politeness after all—see you in the OR next time."

Watching her brisk figure turn down the hall toward the on-call room, Sakaguchi could tell unmistakably that this eminent surgeon's daughter—who had kept a cool, appraising distance since their very first meeting—had for the first time genuinely placed him on her list of clinical partners she could debate seriously and share responsibility with.
“That is an endoscopically confirmed gastric lesion, not a safety pin lost while altering a stage outfit.”
“Besides, this patient completed admission yesterday, and she isn't rushing off to an evening rehearsal in Shimokitazawa.”
Miyama closes the folder, her usually poised and cool tone carrying a faint trace of dry self-mockery that only a familiar partner would catch.
“Rest assured. At the very least, whoever lies down on the operating table today cannot possibly turn out to have nothing wrong at all once we open up.”
“In an operating room, it's probably best not to tempt fate like that.”
“Save the jinxing. Quarter past eleven—see you in the OR.”

Only after Miyama turns and walks out of the work area does Sakaguchi look away.

In that absurd safety-pin emergency last time, Miyama voluntarily handed the primary surgeon's spot over to him; today is the first time she has asked for him by name to stand across the table in a formal operation where she holds the scalpel herself.

“That concludes the formal review for now. Ren, Asakura, head back and compile the OR handover timeline for the file; Dr. Sakaguchi, please go check Ms. Katagiri's current postoperative vitals first—at five-thirty we will go to her room together to apologize formally.”
Everyone rises and files out one after another. As the conference room door clicks shut, only Asuka Shiromiya and Kaori Miyama remain inside.
The latch clicks into place, and the conference room falls quiet for two seconds.

Asuka closes the thick incident report binder in front of her, rises from the head of the long table, walks around to Miyama's side, and pulls out a chair to sit down. The brisk, unyielding edge she wore as hospital director vanishes the instant no outsiders are left.
“...Everyone's gone now. Kaori, are you holding up?”
Miyama's ramrod-straight posture eases by a fraction of an inch, her gaze still resting on the photocopy of the operative record on the table.
“Director Shiromiya certainly didn't spare any feelings a moment ago when going down the list at the table.”
“That is what a director is supposed to do. If I had tried to smooth things over for you in front of everyone in that room, wouldn't you have been the very first person to get upset on the spot?”
Miyama stays silent for half a second, letting out an almost imperceptible breath.

“...True enough.”

“I'm fine. Ms. Katagiri's postoperative vitals are steady, and nothing happened to the gastric patient who ran off either... It just feels utterly absurd.”
She glances down at her hands resting on her lap. Those hands that held a scalpel this morning remain steady, save for knuckles still faintly pale.

“At least that band vocalist with the safety pin last time really did walk into the ER on her own with stomach pain.”

“Today's case... the chart, the wristband, the preoperative time-out—every single step was checked by the book. Yet when I stood at the primary spot, opened the peritoneum, and saw a completely healthy stomach, liver, gallbladder, and bowel inside—for one second, I nearly thought I still hadn't woken up from that last operating table.”

“This wasn't carelessness on your part alone, Kaori. Someone handed a visitor a genuine wristband that scanned with a full set of matching records, contaminating the entire identity chain at the very source—if I had been the one standing at primary today, there is no way I could have known by clairvoyance before opening the abdomen and seeing the stomach with my own eyes either.”
“I understand every point where the system failed. ...Still, I was the one holding the scalpel, and I was the one who cut open an innocent visitor's abdomen.”
Watching the tight line of her old classmate's lips, Asuka reaches out and rests her hand lightly over the back of Kaori's, just as she used to during their university clerkships.

“And the person who carefully re-verified everything the moment the operative field didn't match the chart, halted the planned resection as soon as the mistake was confirmed, and sent her back to the ward safe and sound—that was you too.”

“We've known each other since our first year of medical school, Kaori. Nobody knows what caliber of surgeon you are better than I do—so you are not allowed to go home tonight and sit staring at this review report until dawn, do you hear me?”
Miyama lifts her eyes to look at her closest friend for a moment, and the furrow locked between her brows all afternoon finally loosens a fraction.
“...I heard you, Asuka. I'm not quite that fragile.”
Asuka withdraws her hand, adding an offhand remark in a gentler tone.

“Speaking of which, though, the first assistant you picked today really left an impression. Back in the conference room, he stepped forward on his own to shoulder responsibility for the identity check without a single word of excuse.”
“...Yes. From the moment we found no lesion on the stomach, he stayed calm the entire time. And he didn't shy away from his share of responsibility in the report either.”
Asuka lets a knowing faint smile cross her lips as she picks the folder back up from the table and rises to her feet.
“Looks like your eye for choosing a partner, at least, didn't fail you one bit. Come on, take a breather—at five-thirty we'll head to the ward to see our manga artist.”
Under the overhead corridor lights on her slightly weary profile, her voice suddenly takes on an odd, half-serious, half-self-mocking note.
“Last time, a safety pin caught in the waistband of a pair of underwear had us open up a completely healthy band vocalist just to take a look around.”

“This morning I practically guaranteed you that the person on the table couldn't possibly have nothing wrong again—and then turned right around, mistook a healthy manga artist here for research for a runaway patient, and opened her abdomen.”
She lets out a quiet sigh, eyes lingering on the operating room doors.

“Once can be called a coincidence, but opening up two completely lesion-free, healthy abdomens in a row on the table... almost feels like a pattern. Tell me, if some kind of ‘OR God’ really does live inside that suite, has it been going out of its way to pick on me lately?”
“Even Dr. Miyama, the strictest believer in objective evidence here, is starting to believe in an ‘OR God’ now?”
Miyama shoots him a sidelong glance and tips her head back to finish the last swallow of coffee in the can.
“...Just a passing bit of self-mockery. As if I would ever be superstitious about something like that. Come on, let's clock out.”

strings.collections.special_event_steps.ayako_re: Just past nine in the morning, the hallways gradually quieted down after morning handover.

In the doctors' lounge, Ryuji Sakaguchi had just handed an interdepartmental follow-up record back to Shiori Fujisaki, setting two freshly poured cups of warm black tea onto the small round table while he was at it.
Shiori Fujisaki accepted her teacup and neatly closed the folder, a gentle, unhurried smile touching her lips:
"Thank you, Dr. Sakaguchi. With those postoperative observation points you just added, following up this afternoon will be so much smoother."
"Think nothing of it. It's rare to see your schedule with breathing room today—no morning outpatient clinic?"
"Mm, I deliberately kept this little window around nine open. A guest with an advance appointment is coming by the hospital today to complete some paperwork—"
Before she even finished speaking, the smartphone resting on the table buzzed softly twice.
Shiori Fujisaki glanced down to tap the screen awake, then looked back up, her eyes curving warmly:
"Speak of the devil—she says she's already entered the first-floor lobby and is heading up in the elevator."
Ryuji Sakaguchi picked up his teacup and asked casually:
Just then, Kaori Miyama—who was passing the doorway with an armful of ER observation charts—paused slightly, stopping beside the half-open door to chime in:
"A visitor heading this way at nine o'clock... Don't tell me some pharmaceutical rep wandered onto the wrong floor?"
Shiori Fujisaki turned toward Dr. Miyama and blinked, her tone as calm as if she were reading the weather forecast:
"Not a pharmaceutical rep. Both Dr. Miyama and Dr. Sakaguchi should still remember her—it's Ayako. Ayako Katagiri."
Visibly, the air inside the lounge froze for a full second.
The teacup in Ryuji Sakaguchi's hand stopped midair:
Kaori Miyama's relaxed shoulders stiffened on the spot. Almost by pure reflex, she flipped open today's schedule sheet in her hands, her brows snapping tightly together:
"Hold on. I don't have a single gastric surgery scheduled this morning or afternoon, and the ER hasn't admitted any patient named Ayako Katagiri—what is she doing at the hospital?"
Ryuji Sakaguchi set his teacup down, a complicated expression crossing his face:

"It's been over half a year since that incident... She actually dares set foot inside Hoshimi Hospital again? Don't tell me she ran into another 'super helpful person' downstairs and is getting changed right now for some new brand of immersive research."
Kaori Miyama's gaze sharpened, and she turned on her heel to head straight out the door:

"I'm calling the fourth-floor nurses' station on the internal line right now and telling Nanase to lock down the changing rooms and surgical corridor—under no circumstances can we let her get her hands on a patient wristband again."
Watching the two of them go on red alert as if bracing for an invasion, Shiori Fujisaki couldn't help lifting a hand to her lips with a soft laugh:

"Please calm down, you two. Ayako isn't here as an outpatient today, and she isn't sneaking in either—she submitted a formal application to the Director's Office through me a week ago, and she's coming in openly through proper channels today."
"A formal application? After we opened her up by mistake, it's already miraculous enough that she didn't blacklist Hoshimi Hospital for life—what is she applying to come back for?"
A bright, spirited woman's voice brimming with energy suddenly rang out from beside the half-open lounge doorframe.
All three of them turned to look at the same time.

Peeking around the doorframe was a head crowned with a signature high ponytail of silvery-violet hair. Twenty-five-year-old Ayako Katagiri had a bulging canvas art bag slung over her shoulder, her sparkling eyes curved into crescents as she waved enthusiastically at the three people inside:
"Good morning, Shiori! And Dr. Sakaguchi, Dr. Miyama—long time no see! I heard every word from out in the hall about locking up the fourth-floor changing rooms, you know!"

Kaori Miyama stared at the lively Ayako in the doorway, sizing her up from head to toe for two full seconds. Only after confirming she was wearing a normal pale-purple cardigan and trousers, with sneakers properly on her feet, did Dr. Miyama slowly let out a breath:
"...At least you're wearing your own clothes today."
Ayako Katagiri puffed out her chest and strolled grinning into the lounge:
"Well, obviously! Give me some credit—even I wouldn't trip over the exact same spot twice!"
"It's been half a year—seeing you so full of energy puts my mind at ease."
"Just to check first—you don't have any strange barcode wristbands on, right?"
Looking at Ayako beaming with vitality, Ryuji Sakaguchi couldn't help chuckling:
"It's been half a year—seeing you so full of energy puts my mind at ease. That incision on your abdomen has completely healed up by now, right?"
Ayako Katagiri patted her flat midriff, grinning from ear to ear:
"Completely healed! Even the scar has pretty much faded away—now I can pull an all-nighter drawing thirty pages of storyboards straight without even getting winded!"
Ryuji Sakaguchi let his gaze settle on her wrists and asked with deadpan seriousness:
"Welcome back, Ms. Katagiri. Just to be on the safe side, though, let me verify first—you aren't wearing any mysterious barcode wristbands today, are you?"
Ayako Katagiri burst out giggling and obligingly rolled up both sleeves, turning her wrists all the way around:
"Squeaky clean! Nothing here except a wristwatch and a hair tie—inspect away to your hearts' content, Doctors!"

Once the pleasantries were out of the way, Ayako Katagiri set her heavy canvas bag beside the round table, unzipped it with a loud zip, and—like someone showing off buried treasure—pulled out a finely printed sample issue of a shoujo manga magazine, sliding it in front of the three of them.

"Ta-daaa—! After I was discharged last time, I wove my operating-table perspective and recovery experience from those hospital days into a fictional hospital one-shot. It ran just last month, and guess what—it took second place in the reader survey for that issue!"
Mildly surprised, Ryuji Sakaguchi picked up the sample issue:
"Oh? Congratulations. Here I was worrying you'd turn 'Researching Manga Artist Suffers Botched Laparotomy' into an investigative expose series."
Ayako Katagiri waved her hands furiously:

"No way would I draw it like that! If I actually drew a patient mix-up, not only would the editorial legal team get a massive headache, it'd cause trouble for Shiori and all of you too, right? What I drew is a classic shoujo manga one-shot—the heroine is an ordinary girl rushed into the OR with an acute abdomen!"
Standing beside them, Kaori Miyama had just breathed a quiet sigh of relief when she leaned over for a casual glance at the page Sakaguchi had flipped open.
The very next second, Kaori Miyama's expression froze solid.

Right in the center of the double-page spread loomed a massive operating room surgical lamp. Beneath it stood a young dark-haired female surgeon in a surgical mask, her gaze as cold as frost, holding a gleaming scalpel steady in her fingers—while the speech bubble above her head reproduced a chilling line word for word:
"Panicking right now has zero medical value."
And in the panel right beside it stood a composed young male assistant, delivering a follow-up line to the heroine on the table in an utterly placid tone:
"Let's get you safely stitched back up first."
Ryuji Sakaguchi went silent for two seconds:
"...Why does that line look so awfully familiar?"
A vein at Kaori Miyama's temple gave a barely perceptible twitch. Pressing a slender finger down onto the magazine page, she lifted a cool gaze to Ayako:
Ayako Katagiri clapped her hands together in a plea, beaming brightly as she tried to smooth things over:

"Come on, call it touched-up details—artistic license! Besides, Dr. Miyama, you have no idea: the single most popular character in the fan mail was this 'deadpan ice-queen surgeon with the scalpel'! Several readers wrote in saying, 'A cool older-sister doctor who wouldn't bat an eye if the sky fell is just beyond cool—totally breathtaking!'"
Holding her teacup nearby, Shiori Fujisaki could barely contain her amusement:

"It startled me when I got my sample copy, too. Even without naming names, anyone who knows Dr. Miyama would probably recognize her within three seconds just from that look in her eyes while holding a scalpel."
Kaori Miyama shifted her gaze half an inch away and let out a quiet huff:
"...I was simply stating basic clinical common sense at the time. I had no intention of supplying you with flashy shoujo manga catchphrases."

With a sheepish giggle, Ayako Katagiri tucked the magazine away and promptly hauled out a hardcover sketchbook fully three fingers thick, its edge freshly lined with blank colored index tabs, slapping it down onto the table.

"Anyway, seeing how well the one-shot was received, my magazine editor asked if I wanted to strike while the iron's hot and expand it into a full-fledged long-form hospital serialization—preferably with some bizarre, over-the-top major surgery every single chapter!"
Ryuji Sakaguchi raised a brow at her:
"Sounds right up a commercial magazine's alley. Did you agree to draw it that way?"
Ayako Katagiri shook her head, tapping the sketchbook's cover lightly as the keen expression of a seasoned creator settled over her face:

"I went home, drafted two pages of an outline, and stopped right there. If you rely purely on gimmicky spectacle surgeries, readers get tired of it after two or three chapters once the novelty wears off. That can never carry a real long-running series—and it wouldn't be satisfying for me to draw, either."

She flipped the sketchbook open with a crisp rustle—nearly every page inside was still pristine white, save for the center of the flyleaf, where a tentative project title was written bold and proud in vivid purple marker:
Bracing both hands on the edge of the table, Ayako Katagiri looked around at the three of them with shining eyes:

"As for what the true centerpiece of a long-form series ought to be... honestly, I'm still figuring that out myself! After all, the last time I came to Hoshimi Hospital, I spent the first half groggy and knocked out on an operating table, and the second half obediently flat on my back nursing stitches—I didn't even make it halfway down the inpatient hallway."
She pointed to the rough few-stroke impression doodles sketched beneath the title on the flyleaf, her voice growing more excited by the second:

"Even so, just from the sounds I heard through my ward door during those few days and the way you all took turns coming in on rounds, my manga-artist intuition kept setting off sirens nonstop—this hospital is definitely hiding tons of treasure-trove material I never got the chance to see! So instead of locking myself in my studio making things up out of thin air, I applied to my editorial department for a one-month field research period and came running back to see everything from top to bottom!"
Kaori Miyama glanced down at the handful of stick-figure first-impression doodles tucked in the corner of the flyleaf, her brows furrowing again:
"...Hold on. Even if it's just an initial-impression memo, why does the little stick figure representing me have three shards of ice drawn floating over its head?"
Ayako Katagiri answered with unapologetic conviction:

"That's my first-impression icon left over from my hospital stay! Look at Dr. Sakaguchi's little figure right next to yours—I even tagged him with an unverified note saying 'Looks like a normal person, but surprisingly savage with dry remarks'! Who knows, after a month of observation it might even get an upgrade!"
"...Thanks for the glowing review, though that note really doesn't need any upgrading."
Smiling, Shiori Fujisaki glanced at her wristwatch and gently reminded her old classmate:

"All right, Ayako—keep flipping past the flyleaf and Dr. Miyama might confiscate your brand-new sketchbook on day one. It's almost time for our appointment with Director Asuka, so why don't we head to the Director's Office to take care of the formal paperwork first?"
Ayako Katagiri clapped a hand to her forehead:
"Ah, right, right! Today's number-one mission is picking up Director Shiromiya's official permit!"
Kaori Miyama set her stack of ER folders neatly onto the table and stood up crisply:
Expressionless, Kaori Miyama pulled open the door:

"Getting from here to the Director's Office means passing two stairwells and an elevator with direct access to the fourth-floor surgical wing. Until I watch you finish registering as an official visitor with my own eyes, I don't trust leaving you to roam the corridors unsupervised."
Ryuji Sakaguchi rose to his feet with a smile as well:
"In that case, I'll tag along and bear witness too."
Sunlight poured generously into the Director's Office.

Seated behind her wide desk, twenty-three-year-old Hospital Director Asuka Shiromiya held the "Long-Term Manga Research Residency Proposal" Ayako had sent ahead. After turning the final page with focused attention, she looked up at the four people standing neatly before her desk.

"Welcome back to Hoshimi Hospital, Ms. Katagiri. Seeing how tightly Dr. Miyama and Dr. Sakaguchi are escorting you today, I take it you didn't run into any unidentified 'helpful direction-givers' along the way?"
Sheepishly, Ayako Katagiri stuck out the tip of her tongue:
"Haha... I really caused you colossal trouble last time, Director Shiromiya! That's why I dutifully applied through proper channels a whole week in advance this time!"
The corners of Asuka Shiromiya's lips curved upward. Picking up the Director's seal from her desk, she stamped a crisp red impression onto the bottom of the application form:
"I've read through your proposal—it's fascinating. Effective today, I officially approve your thirty-day research residency here at Hoshimi Hospital."
